x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: Alif, Lam, Meem.

Some of them said: It means: I am God, I decide. Mentioned after that: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Alif, Lam, Meem, I am God, the most distinguished.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Ammar bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement: For the sake of God, I am God, the most detailed.

x: Others said: It is the spelling of the letters of the name of God Almighty, who is the Creator.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Al-Masr, he said: It is a satire of the photographer.

x: Others said: It is one of the names of God, by which our Lord swore. Mentioned after that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: Alif, Lam, Meem, is an oath that God swore, and it is one of the names of God.
Others said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Alif, Lam, Meem, he said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

x: Others said: It is a series of disconnected letters of the alphabet.
Others said: It is from the abjad calculation.
Others said: They are letters that contain many meanings, through which God guided His creation to His intention in all of that.

Others said: They are the letters of the greatest name of God. We have mentioned all of that with the narration in it, and the reasoning of each group that said something about it, and what is correct in our opinion regarding that, with its evidence and proofs in what has passed, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
God Almighty means: This Qur’an, O Muhammad, is a book that God has revealed to you. And He raised the book with the interpretation: This is a book.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do not be distressed by the warning of it from the One I sent you to warn him of it, and by conveying it to the One I commanded you to convey it to, and do not doubt that it is from Me, and be patient in carrying out God’s command and following His obedience in what He has charged you with and burdened you with of the burden of the heavy burdens of prophethood, just as the resolute messengers were patient, for God is with you. In Arabic, hardship means distress. We have explained the meaning of this with evidence and proof in His statement: a tight tightness, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.
The interpreters said about this:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: So let there not be in your breast any difficulty concerning it, he said: Do not be in doubt about it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: In it, let there not be in your breast any difficulty concerning it, he said: Doubt.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So let there not be in your heart any discomfort from it, he was doubtful about it.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So let there be no distress in your heart about it, he said: As for distress, then there is doubt.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad Al-Madani told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid regarding his statement: So let there not be in your breast any discomfort therefrom, he said: Doubt about the Qur’an.

x: What I have mentioned of the interpretation from the people of interpretation is the meaning of what we said about the difficulty, because doubt about it only comes from the narrowness of the chest about it, and the lack of room to direct it in the direction that is its correct direction. And we chose to express it in the meaning of narrowness, because that is the most common meaning of it in the speech of the Arabs, as we have explained before.
By that, the Most High means: This is a book that We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, so that you may warn with it those whom I have commanded you to warn,
h
and a reminder
for the believers, which is from the word mukhdhir which means to bring forward. Its meaning is: A book that has been revealed to you so that you may warn with it,
h
and a reminder
for the believers, so let there be no difficulty in your heart regarding it. If that is what it means, then the position of his saying:
h
and a reminder

is in the accusative case, meaning: We sent down this book to you so that you may warn with it and remind the believers with it. If it was said that the meaning of this is: This is a book that has been revealed to you, so let there be no difficulty in your heart regarding it, that you warn with it and remind the believers with it, then it would be a statement whose authenticity is not proven. If the meaning of the speech is directed to this aspect, then there are two aspects to the parsing of his statement:
h
And a reminder
: One of them: the accusative case in response to the position of to warn with it. The other: raising, in apposition to the book, as if it was said: “Alif, Lam, Meem. A book revealed to you,”
h
and a reminder
for the believers.

God, the Most High, says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people who worship idols and statues: Follow, O people, what has come to you from your Lord with clear proofs and guidance, and do what your Lord has commanded you, and do not follow anything other than it, meaning: anything other than what your Lord has revealed to you. He says: Do not follow the command of your allies who command you to associate partners with God and worship idols, for they will lead you astray and not guide you.
How did you say: The meaning of the statement is: Say, follow, and there is no mention of the statement in the statement?

Even if it was not explicitly mentioned, there is evidence for it in the speech, and that is His saying: So let there not be in your breast any discomfort from it, that you may warn thereby. In His saying that you may warn thereby, there is a command to warn, and in the command to warn, there is a command to speak, because warning is speaking. So the meaning of the speech is: Warn the people and tell them: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord.

If it was said: Its meaning is: To warn with it and remind the believers with it, and say to them: Follow what was revealed to you, it would not be refuted. Some Arab scholars used to say: His statement, Follow, is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its meaning is: A book revealed to you, so let there be no difficulty in your heart regarding it. Follow what was revealed to you from your Lord. He saw that this is similar to God’s statement, O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period, as He began by addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then made the action for everyone, as God’s command to His Prophet with a command was a command from Him to all of his nation, just as it is said to a man who is addressed alone and what is meant by it is him and a group of his followers or his clan and tribe: Do you not fear God?

Do you not feel ashamed before God! And similar statements. Even if this is an unproven view, the statement we have chosen is more deserving of the meaning of speech, due to the apparent meaning we have described. His saying: You remember little, means: You learn little and take heed and then review the truth.

God Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Warn those who worship other than Me, and those who equate gods and idols with Me. I will not inflict My punishment upon them and destroy them, just as I destroyed those nations who followed their path before them. I have often destroyed before them the people of villages who disobeyed Me, denied My messengers, and worshipped other than Me. So Our punishment came to them by night, meaning: So Our punishment and vengeance came to them by night before morning, or it came to them while they were asleep, meaning: during the day at noon. It was said: And how many because what is meant by the speech is what I described of the report about the large number of things that happened to the previous nations of the triad, by their denial of his messengers and their disagreement with him. And the Arabs do the same when they want to report about the large number, as Al-Farazdaq said: How many aunts do you have, Jarir, and how many maternal aunts have you milked for me?
God Almighty only informed us that He destroyed villages, so what evidence is there in His report about His destruction of villages that He destroyed their people?

Villages are not called villages! And no village is a village, unless it has dwellings for its people and residents from among them, so in its destruction is the destruction of its people. Some Arabists believed that the speech was taken as report about the village, and that its people were its victims.
What we said about that is more deserving of the truth, because it is in agreement with the apparent meaning of the recited revelation.

How was it said: And how many a town have We destroyed, and Our punishment came upon it by night, or while they were asleep? Has a town been destroyed except by the coming of God’s punishment and the befalling of His wrath and anger upon it? How was it said: We destroyed it, and Our punishment came upon it? And if the coming of God’s punishment upon it was after its destruction, then what is the reason for that coming to a people who had perished and disappeared, and who were unaware of what was befalling them or their dwellings?

There are two interpretations of this, both of which are correct and clear in their approach: One of them: that its meaning is: And how many a town have We destroyed, by abandoning it from following what We sent down to it of clear proofs and guidance, and its choosing to follow the command of its guardians who led it astray from obeying its Lord, so Our punishment came upon it, when it did that, at night or while they were asleep, so God’s destruction of it is His abandoning it from obeying Him, and God’s punishment coming upon them is a punishment for their disobedience to their Lord by abandoning them. The other of them: that the destruction is the hardship itself, so the mention of the destruction indicates the mention of the coming of the hardship, and the mention of the coming of the hardship indicates the mention of the destruction. If this is the case, it would be the same to the Arabs whether one begins with destruction and then follows it with violence, or begins with violence and then follows it with destruction. This is like their saying: You visited me and honored me, since the visit is the honor, so it is the same to them whether one brings forward the visit and delays the honor, or brings forward the honor and delays the visit and says: You honored me and then visited me. Some Arab scholars claim that there is something omitted in the statement, otherwise the statement would not be correct, and that the meaning of this is: How many a town have We destroyed, so Our punishment came to them before Our destruction.

This is a statement that is not proven to be correct by the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor by a report that must be accepted. If the statement is devoid of proof of its correctness in some aspects that must be accepted, its corruption is clear. Another of them also said: The meaning of the letter fa’ in this place is the meaning of the letter waw. He said: The interpretation of the statement is: How many a town have We destroyed, and Our punishment came to it at night. This is a statement that has no meaning, since the fa’ has a ruling among the Arabs that the letter waw does not have in speech, so diverting it to the most common meaning among them, when there was no way to do so, is more appropriate than diverting it to something else.

How was it said: Our punishment came upon them at night, or while they were still asleep, when you know that the most common use of or in speech is to bring about doubt, and it is not permissible for there to be doubt in God’s report?

The interpretation of that is contrary to what I have adopted. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: And how many a town have We destroyed, some of which Our punishment came at night, and some of them while they were still asleep. If the or had been replaced in this place by the waw, the statement would have been impossible, and the most likely meaning of the statement would have been: That the town that God destroyed, His punishment came to it at night and at the time of noon. And that is report about the punishment, that it destroyed those who had already perished, and annihilated those who had already perished. And that is from the contradictory statement.

But the correct statement is what the revelation came with, since it did not separate the towns that the punishment came to at night from the towns that it came to while still asleep. And if it had been separated, it would not have been reported about them except with the waw. It was said: Our punishment came to it is report about the village that the calamity came to it, and the speech continued as it began in the beginning of the verse. If it had been said: Our punishment came to it at night, it would have been correct and eloquent, returning the speech to its meaning, since the calamity was only intended for the inhabitants of the village and not its buildings, even though its buildings and dwellings had been destroyed by the calamity, similar to what happened to its inhabitants. And in his saying: Or they are saying, he returned to the specific report about its inhabitants and not its dwellings, because of what we described that the intended purpose of the calamity was the inhabitants, even though in their destruction was the destruction and ruin of their dwellings.
If it was said: Or she is the speaker, it would be correct, since the listeners would have understood what was meant by the words.
Is not his statement, Or are they saying, report about the time during the day when God’s wrath came to them?
Yes!
Are not the times in such a case in the speech of the Arabs with the letter waw indicating the time?

Even if that is the case, they may delete from such a place, due to the difficulty of combining two conjunctions, since aw is among the conjunctions, as is the waw, so they say: laqatani mamlaqan or ana musafer, meaning: or I am a traveler, so they delete the waw and they want it in speech, because of what it described.

God Almighty says: The only claim of the people of the town which We destroyed, when Our punishment and might came to them by night or while they were asleep, was their admission against themselves that they were wrongdoers to themselves, sinners to their Lord, and disobedient to His commands and prohibitions. And what He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: their supplication, in this place is their supplication. In Arabic, the word claim has two meanings: one is supplication, and the other is claiming the truth. Among the meanings of claim is the statement of God Almighty: And that was their claim, and from it is the statement of the poet: If my feet are humiliated, I will call upon you. I will seek relief through your call from the one who is humiliated and degraded by it. We have previously explained that ba’s and asa’ are severity, with evidence indicating its correctness, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in the same place.
This verse clearly indicates the validity of what was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said: A people will not perish until they excuse themselves.
Some of them interpreted this as well.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Maysarah Al-Zarrad, he said: Abdullah bin Masoud said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No people perished until they excused themselves. He said, “I said to Abdul Malik: How could that be?” He said: So he recited this verse: So what was their plea when Our punishment came to them? The verse.

x: How was it said: Their only claim when Our punishment came to them was that they said, ‘Indeed, we were wrongdoers’? How was it possible for them to claim that, when the punishment of God came to them with destruction? Did they say that before the destruction? If they said it before the destruction, then they said it before the punishment came, and God informs us that they said it when it came to them, not before that? Or they said it after it came to them, so that was a state in which they were destroyed, so how can it be permissible to describe them as having said that when they witnessed the punishment of God, and the reality of what the messengers promised them of God’s wrath?

Not all nations perished in a moment, with no respite between its beginning and its end. Rather, some of them were drowned in the flood. So between the first appearance of the reason by which they knew they were doomed, and its final appearance, they all swam towards their doom, a period that is not hidden from any rational person. And some of them enjoyed life after the sign of doom appeared to their eyes for three days, like the people of Salih and their likes. Then, when they witnessed the beginnings of the punishment of God that the messengers of God had threatened them with, and were certain of the truth of the descent of God’s wrath upon them, they cried out: Woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers.

So their faith did not benefit them despite the coming of God’s threat and the arrival of His vengeance upon their court. So our Lord, may His praise be glorified, warned those to whom He sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of His wrath and punishment for their disbelief in Him and their denial of His Messenger, as happened to the nations before them when they disobeyed His messengers and followed the command of every stubborn tyrant.

evidence.text: He said: So he recited this verse: So what was their plea when Our punishment came to them?

x: God Almighty says: We will surely ask the nations to whom I sent My messengers: What did you do with regard to what the messengers brought to them from Me of My commands and prohibitions? Did they do what I commanded them to do, and abstain from what I prohibited them from, and obey My commands, or did they disobey Me and go against that? And We will surely ask the messengers, meaning: We will surely ask the messengers whom I sent to the nations: Did you convey My messages to them, and deliver to them what I commanded them to deliver to them, or did they fall short in that and neglect it and not deliver it to them? And so did the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent
, and We will surely question the messengers, he said: God will ask the people about what they answered the messengers, and He will ask the messengers about what they conveyed.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent
, to His statement: absent, he said: The book will be placed on the Day of Resurrection, and it will speak about what they used to do.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent

, and We will surely question the messengers, meaning: We will surely ask the nations: What did they do with what the messengers brought? And We will surely ask the messengers: Did they convey what they were sent with?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad Al-Madani told us, he said, Mujahid said:
m: Then we will ask those to whom the message was sent, meaning the nations, and we will ask those to whom we were sent about what we entrusted them with: Did they convey it?

x: God Almighty says: We will surely inform the messengers and those to whom You sent them with certain knowledge of what they did in this world, in what I had commanded them to do and what I had forbidden them from doing. And We were not absent, from them and from the actions that they used to do.
How can he ask the messengers and those to whom he is sent, when he informs them that he is telling them about their actions and deeds in this regard?

That from Him, the Most High, is not a matter of seeking guidance, nor a matter of knowing from them what He does not know, but rather it is a matter of rebuke and confirmation, the meaning of which is information, as a man says to another: Did I not do good to you and you did wrong? And did I not connect with you and you were cut off? So is the question of God to those sent to them, by saying to them: Did not My messengers come to you with clear proofs? Did I not send to you the warners to warn you of My punishment and chastisement on this day for whoever disbelieves in Me and worships other than Me? As He, the Most High, has informed us that He will say to them on that day: Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - for indeed, he is to you a clear enemy - and that you worship Me - this is a straight path.

And this is from the statement whose appearance is the appearance of the question, and its meaning is bread and stories, and it is after rebuke and confirmation. As for the issue of the messengers, which are stories and bread, when the polytheistic nations are asked on the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to them: Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord? Many of them denied that and said: No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us. So it will be said to the messengers: Did you convey what you were sent with? Or it will be said to them: Did you not convey to these people what I sent you with? Just as the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and just as God, the Most High, said to the nation of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you.

All of that is a question from God to the messengers in order to bear witness for them against the nations to which they were sent, and to those to whom they were sent in order to report and rebuke, and all of that is in the sense of stories and report. As for that which is denied from God in His questioning of His creation, it is the question that is a question of guidance and confirmation in what the questioner does not know about it and the one being asked knows, so that the questioner may know that knowledge of that is from him, then that is not permissible to describe God with, because He is the Knower of things before they exist, during their existence, and after their existence, and it is the question that He, the Most High, denied from Himself by His saying: Then on that Day no man or jinn will be asked about his sin, and by His saying: And the criminals will not be asked about their sins, meaning: He will not ask any of them about that by a question of confirmation, so that he may know that knowledge is from the one who asked from Him, because He is the Knower of all of that and of everything other than Him.
We have mentioned what was narrated in the meaning of that from the report of another place, so we disliked repeating it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to say about the meaning of his saying: Then We will narrate to them with knowledge, that the book of their deeds will speak to them about their deeds. This statement is not far from the truth, but the correct report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that he said: There is not one of you but his Lord will speak to him on the Day of Resurrection, with no interpreter between him and Him. He will say to him: Do you remember the day you did such and such? Until He reminds him of what he did in the world. And submission to the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more appropriate than submission to anyone else.

x: Weight is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: I weighed such and such, I weigh it weight, weight, like: I promised him, I promised him a promise and a promise. It is raised by the truth, and the truth is by it. The meaning of the words: And the weighing on the Day when We will question those to whom it was sent and the messengers, is the truth, and by the truth he means justice. Mujahid used to say: The weight, in this place, is the judgment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And the weight on that day is the judgment. He also used to say: The meaning of right here is justice. The novel mentioned that:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the weighing on that Day will be the truth
, he said: justice.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying:
h
And the weighing on that Day will be true
, is the weighing of deeds.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
And the weighing on that Day will be the truth
, deeds will be weighed.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And the weighing on that Day will be true
, he said: Ubayd bin Umair said: The great, tall, gluttonous, and drunk man will be brought, but he will not weigh as much as the wing of a mosquito.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the weighing on that Day will be the truth
, he said, Ubayd ibn Umair said: The great man will be brought, but he will not weigh as much as the wing of a mosquito.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Yusuf bin Suhaib told us, on the authority of Musa, on the authority of Bilal bin Yahya, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said:
m: The owner of the scales on the Day of Resurrection will be Gabriel, peace be upon him. He said: O Gabriel, weigh them! Then weigh some on others. He said: There will be no gold or silver there. He said: If the oppressor has good deeds, some of his good deeds will be taken and returned to the oppressed. If he has no good deeds, some of the evil deeds of his companion will be placed on him, and the man will return with a burden like mountains on him. This is what He said:
h
And the weighing on that Day will be true

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His statement:
h
So whoever’s scales are heavy
Some of them said: It means: He whose good deeds are many.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
So whoever’s scales are heavy
, he said: his good deeds.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: So whoever has a heavy scale on which his good and bad deeds are weighed. They said: This is the scale that people know, it has a tongue and two pans.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar told me
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the weighing on that Day will be true
, he said: We see a balance and two pans. I heard Ubayd ibn Umair say: A great, tall man will be placed in the balance, then he will not be worth the weight of a fly’s wing.

x: The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is the statement we mentioned on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Dinar, that this is the well-known scale by which things are weighed, and that God, the Most High, weighs the deeds of His creation, both good and bad, as He, the Most High, said: But those whose scales are heavy, the scales of his righteous deeds, they are the successful ones, meaning: they are the ones who attain success, and attain the attainment of their requests, and eternity and remaining in Paradise, because of the clear reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he said: Nothing heavier than good character has been placed in the scale, and similar reports that confirm that this is a scale by which deeds are weighed, as I have described. If someone denies this out of ignorance of the meaning of God’s statement about the scale and the statement of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, then I will explain it to him and say: Surat al-A’raf 7:8
h
And the weighing on that Day will be the truth

So those whose scales are heavy - it is those who will be the successful. Does God have a need to weigh things, while He knows the amount of everything before and after His creation of it, and in every situation? Or he said: How are deeds weighed, when deeds are not bodies described as heavy or light, but rather things are weighed to know their heaviness from their lightness, and their abundance from their scarcity, and that is not permissible except for things described as heavy or light, and abundance and scarcity? It was said to him regarding his statement: And what is the aspect of weighing the deeds, while He is the Knower of their amounts before they come into being?: The weighing of that, is similar to His establishing it in the Mother of the Book and His copying it in the books, without any need for it, and without fear of forgetting it, and He is the Knower of all that in every state and time before its existence and after its existence, but rather so that it may be an argument against His creation, as He, the Most High, said in His revelation: “Every nation will be called to its book.

Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do. This is Our book that speaks against you with truth.” The verse. Likewise, His, the Most High, weighing the deeds of His creation with the scale, is an argument against them and for them, either by falling short in obeying Him and wasting it, or by completing and perfecting it.
As for the reason for its permissibility, it is as follows:

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said, Jaafar bin Awn told us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Ziyad Al-Ifriqi told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said:
m: A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection to the scales, and he will be placed on the pan, and ninety-nine records will be taken out for him in which are his sins and transgressions. He said: Then a book the size of a fingertip will be brought out for him, in which is the testimony that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Then it will be placed on the scale, and it will outweigh his sins and transgressions. Thus God will weigh the deeds of His creation, by placing the servant and his good deeds on one scale of the scales, and his bad deeds on the other scale, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, will create heaviness and lightness in the scale on which the weight is more deserving, as an argument from God to His creation with that, as He did with many of them: by making their hands and feet speak, as evidence against them, and other similar arguments. And the one who denies this is asked, and it is said to him: Verily, God, the Most High, has informed us that He will make the scales of some people heavy on the Day of Resurrection, and will make the scales of others light, and the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have all confirmed this, so what made you deny that the scale is the scale whose description we have described, which people are familiar with? Is it an argument of reason that is far from being attained from the aspect of reason? And in God, the Most High, weighing His creation and writing down their deeds to inform them of the heaviest of the two parts of it by the scale, there is no departure from wisdom, nor does it enter into injustice in a judgment, so what made this, in your opinion, a rational argument or a report? Since there is no way to the truth of the statement of the corruption of what reason cannot refute except from one of the two aspects that you mentioned, and there is no way to that. And in the lack of proof of the correctness of his claim from these two aspects, the corruption of his statement is clear, and the correctness of what the people of truth have said about it. This is not a place to dwell on this meaning for those who deny the scale whose description we have described, since our intention in this book was to explain the interpretation of the Qur’an and nothing else. If it were not for that, we would have turned to what we have mentioned similar examples, and what we have mentioned of that is sufficient for whoever is guided to understand it, God willing.

x: God Almighty says: And whoever’s scales of righteous deeds are light, and they are not heavy because of his acknowledgement of the Oneness of God, and belief in Him and His Messenger, and following His commands and prohibitions, then those are the ones who have deprived themselves of their share of the great reward of God and His honor, because they were unjust to Our signs, meaning because they were denying God’s proofs and evidence, so they do not acknowledge their validity, nor are they certain of their truth, like the one who:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And those whose scales are light, he said: his good deeds. And it was said: Then those, and it is safe in the singular form, because its meaning is the plural. If it had come in the singular form, it would have been correct and eloquent.

x: God Almighty says: And We have certainly established for you, O people, the earth, and made it a resting place for you in which you settle, a resting place for you to lie down on, and a bed for you to spread out on, And We have made for you therein means of livelihood, in which you live the days of your lives, from food and drink, as a blessing from Me to you, and a kindness from Me to you, little do you give thanks, meaning: And you are little thankful for these blessings that I have bestowed upon you because of your worship of other than Me, and your taking a god other than Me. And livelihood is the plural of livelihood. The reading differed in its reading. The majority of the people in the countries read it as Ma’aish without a hamza. Abdul Rahman Al-Araj read it: Ma’aish with a hamza.

The correct reading in this regard according to us is: Maʿaish without a hamza, because it is a mafʿil from the saying of the speaker ʿisht taʿish, so the mim in it is extra, and the ya’ in the rule is mobile, because its singular is mafʿilah, maʿishah, and the ya’ is mobile, and the movement of the ya’ was transferred from it to the ʿayn in its singular. So when it was made plural, its movement was returned to it because of the sukoon of what preceded it and its movement. And this is what the Arabs do with the ya’ and the waw if what preceded them is sukoon and they have movement, in similar cases to what we described of the plural that comes in the form of mafʿil. This is contrary to what came in the form of faʿa’il in which the ya’ is extra and not original. If the plural is in this example, the Arabs pronounce it with a hamza, like their saying: these are cities and newspapers and their likes, because cities is the plural of city and city is a fa’ila from their saying: I made the city city, and likewise, newspapers is the plural of newspaper, and newspaper is a fa’ila from your saying: I made the newspaper, so the ya’ in the singular is an additional silent letter, so when it is pluralized, it is hamzat, because it is different in the plural from the ya’ that was in the singular, and that is because it was silent in the singular, and it is moving in the plural.

If you made city a mafa’il from dan yadayn, and pluralized it with mafa’il, the eloquent would be to leave the hamza in it and move the ya’. The Arabs may have hamzated the plural of mafaʿala in words with yaʿ and waw, although the eloquent form of their speech leaves the hamzah in it, if it comes in mafaʿil, as they liken its plural to the plural of faʿilah, just as they liken mafaʿlan to faʿil, so they say: masil al-maʿ min: sala yaseel, then they pluralize it in the plural faʿil, so they say: hiyya amsala, in the plural, as they liken it to the plural of baʿir, which is faʿil, since its plural is abʿara. Likewise, the plural of al-masir, which is mafaʿil, is misran, as they liken it to the plural of baʿir, which is faʿil, since its plural is baʿran. Based on this, al-Aʿraj hamzated maʿaish. This is not eloquent in their speech, and the most appropriate way in which the Book of God is recited from tongues is the most eloquent and well-known, not the most strange and unusual.

evidence.text: The reading differed in its reading.
The majority of the people in the countries read it as Ma’aish without a hamza.
Abdul Rahman Al-Araj read it: Ma’aish with a hamza.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard according to us is: Maʿaish without a hamza, because it is a mafʿil from the saying of the speaker ʿisht taʿish, so the mim in it is extra, and the ya’ in the rule is mobile, because its singular is mafʿilah, maʿishah, and the ya’ is mobile, and the movement of the ya’ was transferred from it to the ʿayn in its singular.
This is not eloquent in their speech, and the most appropriate way in which the Book of God is recited from tongues is the most eloquent and well-known, not the most strange and unusual.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The interpretation of that is:
h
And We created you
, in the back of Adam, O people, then We formed you, in the wombs of women. A created creation and an example represented in the image of Adam.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We created you
, then We shaped you. His statement:
h
We created you
, refers to Adam, and as for We shaped you, it refers to his offspring.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We created you
, then We shaped you verse, he said: As for
h
We created you
, it is Adam. As for We shaped you, it is the descendants of Adam after him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
And We created you
, meaning Adam, then We formed you, meaning in the wombs.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We created you
, then We formed you, he said:
h
We created you
as Adam was created, then We formed you in the wombs of your mothers.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And We created you
, then We formed you, meaning: We created Adam, then We formed the offspring in the wombs.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We created you

, then We shaped you, he said: God created Adam from clay, then We shaped you, in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation: a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then He covered the bones with flesh, then We developed him into another creation.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: God created Adam, then He created his offspring after him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Omar bin Harun told us, on the authority of Nasr bin Musharis, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
We created you
, then We formed you, he said: his offspring.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
And We created you
, meaning Adam, then We formed you, meaning his offspring.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
h
And We created you
, in the loins of your fathers, then We formed you, in the wombs of your mothers.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And We created you
, then We formed you, he said:
h
We created you
in the loins of men, and formed you in the wombs of women.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us,
m: I heard Al-A’mash recite:
h
And We created you
, then We formed you, he said:
h
We created you
in the loins of men, then We formed you in the wombs of women.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
h
We created you
, meaning Adam, then We formed you, meaning: on his back.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And We created you
, he said: Adam, Then We formed you, he said: in the back of Adam.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shabl narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We created you
, then We formed you, on the back of Adam.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We created you
, then We formed you, he said: We formed you on the back of Adam.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad Al-Madani told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid regarding his statement:
h
And We created you
, then We formed you, he said: In the back of Adam, for what you will attain of reward in the Hereafter.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
And We created you
in your mothers’ wombs, then We formed you in them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned him, he said:
h
We created you
, then We formed you, he said: God created man in the womb, then formed him, and split his hearing, sight, and fingers.

x: The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: Its interpretation is:
h
And We created you

, and We created Adam, Then We shaped you, by Our sculpting of Adam, as we have previously explained of the Arabs addressing men with actions that they attribute to them, and the one being rebuked in that is his predecessor, and as the Most High said to those among the believing Jews during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And when We took your covenant and raised the mountain over you, [saying], ‘Take what We have given you with strength.’ And what is similar to that of the speech directed to the living, existing one, and what is meant by it is the non-existent predecessor, so it is the same in His saying:
h
And We created you

, then We shaped you, meaning: And We created your father Adam, then We shaped him. We said that this statement is the most correct of the statements on this matter, because what follows it is His statement:
h
Then We said to the angels

, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ and it is known that God, Blessed and Exalted be He, commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam before He formed his offspring in the wombs of their mothers, and even before He created their mothers.
Then, in the speech of the Arabs, it does not come except with an indication of the separation of what comes after it from what comes before it, and that is like the saying of the speaker:
h
I stood up
, then I sat down. The sitting, if he connects it with then to his saying:
h
I stood up

, does not occur except after the standing, and likewise in all speech. If the connection in that was with the letter waw, it is possible that what comes after it came before what came before it, and that is like the saying of the speaker:
h
I stood up

and sat down. So it is possible that the sitting in this speech came before the standing, because the letter waw enters the speech if it is a connection, to require for what comes after it the same meaning as what came before it, without indicating by itself that that was at one time or two different times, or if they were at two times, which of them came first and which of them came last.
So when we described, we said that his saying:
h
And We created you

, then We formed you, cannot be interpreted except in the way we mentioned. If someone thinks that the Arabs, since they may have pronounced thumma in place of waw in their poetry, as some of them said: Rabia asked: Who is better, a father or a mother?

i: She said:
x: Why?

Meaning: father and mother, then it is possible that it is its counterpart, because that is contrary to what was thought. This is because the Book of God, may He be glorified and praised, was revealed in the most eloquent of the Arab languages, and it is not permissible to direct any of it to the irregular of its languages, and it has an understood meaning and a known aspect in the most eloquent and well-known. Some of those who have extensive knowledge of the Arabic language have attributed this to the fact that it is from the word mu’akhir which means to bring forward, and they have claimed that its meaning is:
h
And We created you
h
then We said to the angels

, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ then We formed you. This is not permissible in the Arabic language, because then does not enter into the speech and it is intended to bring forward what precedes it from the report, even though they may bring it forward in the speech if there is evidence that its meaning is to delay, such as their saying: Then Abdullah stood up, then Amr sat down.

But if it is said: Then Abdullah stood up, then Amr sat down, then it is not permissible for Amr’s sitting to have happened except after Abdullah stood up, if the report is true. So the statement of God, the Most High:
h
And We created you
, then We formed you,
h
then We said to the angels

, ‘Prostrate to you,’ is similar to the statement of the one who says: Then Abdullah stood up, then Amr sat down, in that it is not permissible for God’s command to the angels to prostrate to Adam to have happened except after the creation and formation, for what we have described before. As for His saying to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, He, the Most High, says: So when We formed Adam, and made him a well-proportioned creation, and breathed into him of Our spirit, We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, as a trial from Us and a test for them with the command, to know the obedient among them from the disobedient.

So they prostrated, meaning: So the angels prostrated, except for Iblis, for he was not among those who prostrated to Adam, when God commanded him with those other angels whom He commanded to prostrate. We have previously explained the meaning for which He, the Most High, tested His angels by prostrating to Adam, and commanded Iblis and his stories, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
This is report from God, the Most High, about what He said to Iblis, when he disobeyed Him and did not prostrate to Adam when He commanded him to prostrate to him. He says: God said to Iblis:
h
What prevented you
, that is,
h
what prevented you
, from not prostrating, from abandoning prostration to Adam, when I commanded you, to prostrate, He said,
h
I am better than him
, that is, Iblis said: I am better than Adam,
h
You created me from fire and created him from clay
Tell us about Iblis, was he blamed for prostrating, or for not prostrating? If he was blamed for not prostrating, then how was it said to him:
h
What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you
? And if the denunciation was for prostrating, then that is contrary to what came in the revelation in the rest of the Qur'an, and contrary to what Muslims know!

The blame did not fall on Iblis except for his disobedience to his Lord by not prostrating to Adam when He commanded him to prostrate to Him. However, there is a difference of opinion among those who are knowledgeable about the speech of the Arabs regarding the interpretation of his statement:
h
What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you
? I will begin by mentioning what they said, then I will mention what is most correct.
Some Basra grammarians said: The meaning of this is:
h
What prevented you
from prostrating?

i: La here is redundant, as the poet said:
x: My father is generous, not stingy, and I hastened it, yes, from a young man who does not prevent hunger from killing him He said: The Arabs interpreted it as: Abba Jawdah Al-Bukhl, and they made La an extra filler here, and connected the speech with it.

He said: Yunus claimed that Abu Amr used to drag Al-Bukhl and make La an addition to it, he meant: Abba Jawdah Al-Bukhl which is for miserliness, and he made La an addition, because La can be for generosity and miserliness, because if he had said to him: Withhold the right and do not give to the poor and he had said: No, this would have been generosity from him. Some grammarians of Kufa said something similar to what we mentioned from the Basrans, regarding its meaning and interpretation. However, he claimed that the reason for the inclusion of except in his statement: that you do not prostrate is that at the beginning of the speech there is a denial, meaning by that his statement: he was not among those who prostrated, for the Arabs sometimes repeat the denial in speech that contains a denial, such as to confirm and affirm it. He said: This is like their saying: We have never seen anything like them among the black-headed, greedy and greedy.

So he repeated the denial, which is what he denied, which is his saying: If, so he combined them for emphasis. Another of them said: It is not a filler in this place nor a connection, but the prohibition here means the saying. The interpretation of the speech is: Who told you not to prostrate when I ordered you to prostrate? But the word an entered into the speech, since the prohibition was in the meaning of the saying, not in its wording, as it does in all speech that resembles the saying, and it is different in wording, like their saying: I called out that you not stand up and I swore that you would not sit down, and similar speech. He said: The word al-Bukhl was lowered by the one who narrated: Abi Judeh, not al-Bukhl, meaning: the word of miserliness, because la is the word of miserliness, so it is as if he said: the word of miserliness.

Some of them said: The meaning of prevention is the barrier between a person and what he wants. He said: The one who is prevented is compelled to do something other than what he is prevented from doing, like the one who is prevented from standing while he wants to do it. He is compelled to do something that is contrary to standing, since the one who chooses the action is the one who has the way to it and to its opposite, so he influences one of them over the other and does it. He said: So since the description of prevention was that, Iblis was addressed with prevention and it was said to him:
h
What prevented you
from prostrating? Its meaning was as if it was said to him: Is there something that compelled you not to prostrate?
The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that there is something omitted in the speech, and the apparent evidence of it is sufficient, which is that its meaning is:
h
What prevented you

from prostrating, so that you needed not to prostrate? So he omitted mentioning most needy, so that the listeners would be satisfied with his statement: Except Iblis, he was not among those who prostrated, that this is the meaning of the speech, from mentioning it. Then he worked on his statement:
h
What prevented you

, in that, what was working in it before most needy, had it appeared, since it had taken its place. We said that this statement is more correct, because we have previously demonstrated that it is not permissible for there to be something in the Book of God that has no meaning, and that every word has a correct meaning. Thus, the corruption of the statement of those who said: No, there is superfluity in speech and no meaning to it is clear.

As for the statement of the one who said: The meaning of prevention here is speech, therefore it was included with that because prevention, even though it may be speech and action, it is not known among people to use prevention in ordering to leave something, because the one who is ordered to leave an action, if he is able to do it and leave it, then he does it, it is not said: he did it, and he is prevented from doing it, except in the case of a forced speech. This is because prevention from the action is a barrier between him and it, so it is not permissible for him, while he is a barrier between him and it, to be the doer of it, because if that were permissible, then it would be necessary for him to be a barrier between him and it, not a barrier, and prevented, not prevented. And then, Iblis did not obey the command of God Almighty to prostrate to Adam out of arrogance, so how could he have obeyed someone else in abandoning the command of God and obeying Him by not prostrating to Adam?
It is permissible to say to him: What told you: Do not prostrate to Adam when I commanded you to prostrate to him? But its meaning, God willing, is what you said:
h
What prevented you
from prostrating to him that made you needy, or: brought you out, or: forced you not to prostrate to him, as I explained. As for his saying: “
h
I am better than him
h
You created me from fire and created him from clay

,” it is a report from God, the Most High, about the answer of Iblis to him when he asked him: What prevented him from prostrating to Adam, which made him need not to prostrate to him, and forced him to disobey his command, and to abandon his obedience? The reason for preventing him from prostrating, and the reason for him to disobey his Lord’s command in that, was that he was stronger than him in support, more powerful than him in strength, and better in virtue than him, due to the superiority of the species from which he was created, which is fire, over that from which Adam was created, which is clay.

So the enemy of God was ignorant of the truth, and erred in the right path. For it was known that the essence of fire includes lightness, rashness, turmoil, and rising high, and what is in its essence of that is what led the wicked one, after the misery that God had previously decreed for him in the previous Book, to be arrogant about prostrating to Adam, and to belittle the command of his Lord, which caused him to be ruined and destroyed. It was known that the essence of clay is sobriety, patience, forbearance, modesty and piety, and that which is in its essence from that, was the motive for Adam after the happiness that had preceded for him from his Lord in the previous Book, to repent from his sin, and to ask his Lord for pardon and forgiveness. Therefore, Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin used to say: The first to make an analogy was Iblis, meaning by that: analogy and error, which is what we mentioned of the error of his statement, and after it from hitting the truth, in the favor that God distinguished Adam with over the rest of His creation: from His creation of him with His hand, and breathing into him from His spirit, and His making the angels prostrate to him, and teaching him the names of everything, along with the rest of the honor that He distinguished him with.

So the ignorant one ignored all of that, and intended to argue that he was created from fire and Adam was created from clay!! And in that also he is not equal to him, if Adam had not had from God Almighty honored anything other than him, so how is it that what He distinguished with from His honor is too numerous to count, and it becomes boring to enumerate.

c: Amr bin Malik told me, he said, Yahya bin Salim Al-Ta’ifi told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: The first one to make an analogy was Satan, and the sun and moon were not worshipped except by analogy.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Muhammad bin Katheer told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Matar Al-Warraq, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You created me from fire and created him from clay
, he said: Iblis made a comparison, and he was the first to make a comparison. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said.

x: Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Uthman bin Saeed narrated, he said: Bishr bin Ammarah narrated, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When God created Adam, He said to the angels who were with Iblis specifically, excluding the angels who were in the heavens: Prostrate to Adam. So they all prostrated together except Iblis, who was arrogant, because of what he had thought of himself, out of his arrogance and conceit, so he said: “I should not prostrate to him, and
h
I am better than him
, older in age, and stronger in creation.
h
You created me from fire and created him from clay
.” He said: Fire is stronger than clay.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You created me from fire
, he said: Then He made his offspring from water.

x: What the enemy of God said was not an answer to what he asked him about, because God Almighty said to him:
h
What prevented you

from prostrating? He did not answer that what prevented him from prostrating was that he was created from fire and Adam was created from clay, but he began by telling a story about himself, in which there is evidence of the place of the answer, so he said: “
h
I am better than him
h
You created me from fire and created him from clay

By that, may His praise be glorified, He meant: God said to Satan at that time: Then get down from it. We have explained the meaning of descent previously, so there is no need to repeat it. So it is not for you to be arrogant therein, God Almighty says: So God said to him: Descend from it, meaning from Paradise. So it is not for you, He says: It is not for you to be arrogant in Paradise about obeying Me and My command.
Can anyone be arrogant in Paradise?

The meaning of this is different from what you have gone to, and the meaning of this is: So descend from Paradise, for Paradise will not be inhabited by one who is arrogant towards the command of God. As for other than it, then the one who is arrogant towards the command of God and humble towards His obedience will inhabit it. And his saying: Then get out, for you are among the humiliated, means: Get out of Paradise, for you are among those who have been afflicted by humiliation, humiliation, and disgrace from God.
It is said: He became small, he becomes small, smallness, smallness, and smallness. It has also been said: He became small, he becomes small, smallness, smallness. Al-Suddi said something similar.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then go out, for you are among the debased. Debased means humiliation.

x: This is also another lapse of his malicious ignorance. He asked his Lord for something that he knew no one of God's creation could attain. That is, he asked for a respite until the Day of Judgment, which is the day on which creation will be resurrected. If he had been given what he asked for of a respite, he would have been given immortality and an everlasting life without annihilation, because there is no death after the resurrection. So God Almighty said: Indeed, you are of those granted respite * Until the Day of the Appointed Time, that is until the day on which God has decreed for him destruction, death, and annihilation, because nothing remains and does not perish, except our Lord, the Ever-Living Who does not die. God Almighty says: Every soul will taste death. In Arabic, respite means delay. It is said: I gave him respite by My right over him, I gave him respite.
God said to him when he asked him for respite until the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Indeed, you are among those granted respite, in this place, so did He answer him to what he asked?

The matter is not like that, but rather He would have answered him to what he asked if He had said to him: Indeed, you are among those granted respite until the time you asked or: until the Day of Resurrection - or: until the Day of Resurrection, or something similar to that, which indicates His answer to what he asked of respite. As for his saying: Indeed, you are among those granted respite, there is no evidence for it except for the other verse in which He explained the period of His respite for him, and that is His saying: Indeed, you are among those granted respite * Until the Day of the Appointed Time, how much period did He grant him respite, because if He granted him respite for one day or less than that or more, then he has entered the number of those granted respite, and the promise of God the Truthful has been fulfilled, but He explained the amount of that period by what we mentioned, so he knew by that the time for which He granted him respite. And in a similar vein, Al-Saddī used to say:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He said, ‘Respite me until the Day they are resurrected.’ He said, ‘Indeed, you are among those granted respite.’ “Until the Day of the Appointed Time.” Verily, He did not grant him respite until the Day of Resurrection, but He granted him respite until the Day of the Appointed Time, which is the Day when the first blast is blown into the Trumpet, and all who are in the heavens and on the earth will burst into tears and die.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: Iblis said to his Lord: Give me respite, meaning, delay me, postpone my lifespan, and postpone my death, until the Day they are resurrected, meaning, until the Day when creation is resurrected. So God Almighty said: Indeed, you are among those granted respite, until the Day when the Trumpet is blown, and all those in the heavens and on the earth will be stunned, except whom God wills.
Is there anyone who will see anything until that day except Satan, and it will be said to him: You are one of them?

Yes, whoever God has not taken the soul of from among His creation until that day, among those upon whom the Hour will come, they are among those whose appointed times are respite until that day. Therefore, it was said to Iblis: You are among those who are respite, meaning: You are among those whom God will not kill until that day.
God Almighty says: Iblis said to his Lord:
h
Then why did you mislead me
? He says: Then why did you lead me astray?

c: Just as Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said: Muʿawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then why did you mislead me
? He says: Then why did you lead me astray?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Because you misled me
, he said: Because you led me astray.

i: Some of them interpreted his saying:
h
Because you have led me astray
, as meaning because you have destroyed me, from their saying: The young camel has gone astray, it goes astray, it goes astray, which is when it loses its milk and dies, from the saying of the poet:
x: The coat of arms is not its faction, its prey is not its dung beetle, nor its plunder is its seduction The origin of seduction in Arabic speech is: a man embellishing something for another man until he finds it good, out of jealousy of him.
It was narrated that some of the tribes of Tayyi’ used to say: So-and-so has become misguided, meaning: He has become ill.
Some of them interpreted this to mean an oath, and to them it meant:
h
Because you misled me
, I will ambush them on your straight path, just as one would say: By God, I will do such-and-such.
Some of them interpreted it as a recompense. For them, it meant: Because you led me astray - or: Because you led me astray - I will sit in wait for them on your straight path.

This is a clear statement of the corruption of what the Qadarites say, that whoever disbelieves or believes, then it is by God’s entrusting of the reasons for that to him, and that the reason by which the believer reaches faith is the same reason by which the disbeliever reaches disbelief. This is because if that were as they said, then the wicked one would have said in his statement:
h
Then because you have misled me

, “Then because you have reformed me,” since the reason for misleading is the reason for reforming, and in his telling of misleading there was telling of reforming. But since their two reasons were different, and the reason by which he was misled and destroyed was from God, he added that to it and said:
h
Then because you have misled me
Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi said the same, in what:

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, he said: Abu Mawdud told us:
m: I heard Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi say: May God curse the Qadarites, for Iblis knows God better than they do. As for His statement:
h
I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path

, he is saying: I will surely sit in wait for the children of Adam on Your straight path, meaning: Your straight path, and that is the true religion of God, which is Islam and its laws. The meaning of the statement is: I will turn the children of Adam away from Your worship and obedience, and I will mislead them as You misled me, and I will lead them astray as You led me astray. This is as narrated on the authority of Sabra bin Abi Al-Fakih: He heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The devil sits in wait for the son of Adam in all his ways. He sits in wait for him in the way of Islam and says: Will you submit and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers? So he disobeyed him and became a Muslim. Then he sits in wait for him in the way of migration and says: Will you migrate and abandon your land and sky, while the migrant is like a horse in height? So he disobeyed him and migrated. Then he sits in wait for him in the way of jihad, which is the effort of the soul and money, and says: Will you fight and be killed, and the woman be married, and the money be divided? So he disobeyed him and fought.”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah
m: regarding this matter as follows: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Habawiyah Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Bakir, on the authority of Muhammad bin Suqah, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah: I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path, he said: The road to Mecca. What Aoun said, even if it is from the straight path of God, is not the whole path. Rather, the enemy of God informed that he would sit for them on the straight path of God, and he did not specify one thing from it over another. So what was narrated about that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation, and more deserving of interpretation, because the wicked one does not spare any effort in turning God’s servants away from everything that brings them closer to God. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said about the meaning of straight in this place.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Your straight path, he said: the truth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. Surat al-A’raf 7:16 He said, "Then because You have put me in error,
h
I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad Al-Madani told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say: I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path, he said: The path of truth, so I will lead them astray except for a few.

x: The Arab scholars differed on this.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its meaning is: I will sit for them on your straight path, just as it is said: He headed towards Mecca, meaning: towards Mecca, and as the poet said: As if I am trying to catch a bird with the star, aiming from the sky Meaning: To catch a bird, so he threw the baa, and as he said: Have you hastened the matter of your Lord? meaning: Have you hastened regarding the matter of your Lord. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The meaning, and God knows best, is: I will sit for them on their way, and in their way. He said: It is permissible to throw the description from this, as you say: I sat for you on the face of the road, and on the face of the road, because the road is a description in meaning, so it is possible for what the day, the night, and the year are possible for, if it is said: I will come to you tomorrow, and I will come to you in the tomorrow.

This statement is the more correct of the two statements in my opinion, because: sitting requires a place to sit in, so just as it is said: I sat in your place, it is said: I sat on your path, and on your path, as the poet said: He is lean with the palm, his back is honeyed in it, as the fox honeys the road. Arabs hardly ever say that in the names of countries. They hardly ever say: Mecca sat down, and Baghdad stood up.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The meaning of his saying:
h
I will come to them from before them

, from the direction of the Hereafter, and from behind them, from the direction of this world, and from their right, from the direction of the truth, and from their left, from the direction of falsehood.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then I will come to them from before them

, meaning, I will make them doubt their afterlife, and from behind them, making them desire their worldly life, and on their right, making them desire their religious affairs, and on their left, making them forgive their sins. And it has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas with this chain of transmission regarding the interpretation of that, which is different from this interpretation, and that is what:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then I will come to them from before them

, meaning from this world, and from behind them, from the Hereafter, and from their right, from their good deeds, and from their left, from their bad deeds. And this narration is confirmed, as is the other one which:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left
, he said: As for before them, it is
h
from before them
, and as for from behind them, it is the matter of their afterlife, and as for their right, it is from before their good deeds, and as for from their left, it is from before their bad deeds.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Then I will come to them from before them the verse
, He came to them
h
from before them

and informed them that there is no resurrection, nor Paradise, nor Hell, and from behind them, from the affairs of this world, so He made it attractive to them and called them to it, and from their right, from their good deeds, turning them away from them, and from their left, He made evil deeds and transgressions attractive to them, and called them to them, and commanded them to them. He came to you, O son of Adam, from every direction, except that He did not come to you from above you. He was not able to stand between you and the mercy of God.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of his saying:
h
from before them
is from their worldly life, and from behind them is from their afterlife.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them
, he said:
h
From before them
, from their worldly life, and from behind them, from their afterlife, and from their right, from their good deeds, and from their left, from their bad deeds.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
m: h
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them
and from their right and from their left, he said:
h
From before them

means from their worldly life, and from behind them means from their afterlife, and from their right means from their good deeds, and from their left means from their bad deeds. - Sufyan told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
h
Then I will come to them from before them

, he said: from the direction of this world, making it seem attractive to them, and from behind them, from the direction of the Hereafter, making them slow down from it, and from their right, from the direction of the truth, turning them away from it, and from their left, from the direction of falsehood, making them desire it and making it seem attractive to them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left
. As for
h
from before them

, it is the world, I will call them to it and make them desire it. And from behind them, it is the Hereafter, I will make them doubt it and make it distant from them, I will make it difficult for them, meaning the truth, so I will make them doubt it, and from their left, meaning falsehood, I will make it easy for them and make them desire it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, his statement:
h
From before them

, from their worldly life, the most desirable for it, and behind them, their afterlife, the most ungrateful for it and the most uninterested in it, and from their right, their good deeds, the most uninterested in them, and from their left, the faults of their deeds, the best of them to them. Surat al-A’raf 7:17
h
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left
h
and You will not find most of them grateful

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: from where they see and from where they do not see.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: God’s statement:
h
From before them and from behind them and on their right
, he said: where they can see, and from behind them, “and on their left,” where they cannot see.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said:
m: We discussed with Mujahid his statement:
h
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left
, so Mujahid said: It is as he said: He will come to them
h
from before them and from behind them and on their right
and on their left. Ibn Hameed added: He said: He will come to them from there.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Abdul Aziz told us, he said: Abu Saad Al-Madani told us, he said:
m: Mujahid said, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Muhammad Ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Asim.

x: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: Then I will come to them from every direction of truth and falsehood, and turn them away from the truth, and make falsehood seem good to them.
