That is because that follows His statement: I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path, so He informed that He will sit in wait for the children of Adam on the path that God has commanded them to follow, which is what we have described of the religion of God, the religion of truth. So He will come to them in that from every direction, from the direction that God has commanded them to take, and turn them away from it, which is
h
from before them and from behind them and on their right
, and from the direction that God has forbidden them from, and He will make it seem good to them and call them to it, which is from behind them and from their right and from their left.
It was said: He did not say: from above them, because the mercy of God descends upon His servants from above them.
Who said that?

c: Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam Al-Masry narrated to us, he said: Hafs bin Omar narrated to us, he said: Al-Hakam bin Abaan narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left
, and He did not say: from above them, because mercy descends from above them. As for His statement:
h
And You will not find most of them grateful

, he is saying: And You will not find, O Lord, most of the children of Adam grateful to You for Your favor that You bestowed upon them, like Your honoring of their father Adam with what You honored him with, from Your angels prostrating to him, and Your preferring him over me, and their gratitude to him, their obedience to him by acknowledging His Oneness, and following His commands and prohibitions. Ibn Abbas used to say about this:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you will not find most of them grateful
, he said: monotheists.

x: This is report from God Almighty about His bringing upon the wicked enemy of God what He brought upon him of His vengeance and curse, and His expulsion of him from His Paradise, because he disobeyed Him and went against His command, and returned to Him an answer that he had no right to return to Him with. He says: God said to him at that time:
h
Get out of it

, meaning from Paradise, disgraced and banished, meaning: disgraced. And blame, defect. It is said: he blamed him, he blames him, he is blameworthy, and he is blameworthy. And they leave out the hamza and say: I blame him, I blame him, dhimman and dhaman. And blame and dhim are more expressive of the defect than blame. And some of them recited this verse: I kept you company while my eyes were covered with a veil, but when it lifted, I cut myself off from hurting myself. Most narrators recite it as: I blame her. As for the defeated, it is the one who is cut off.

It is said: he defeated him, he defeats him, defeating him, if he pushed him away and expelled him. From this comes their saying: Defeat the devil from you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Get out of it
, disgraced and banished, meaning:
h
Get out of it
, cursed and banished.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: condemned, hated.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: He said, ‘
h
Get out of it

, disgraced,’ meaning: young and banished. 14392 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement:
h
Get out of it
, disgraced and banished. As for disgraced, it means banished, and as for banished, it means expelled.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Reprehensible, he said: banished, repelled, he said: expelled.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Get out of it
disgraced, he said: banished. And the one who has been driven out, he said: diminished.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Yunus La Isra’il, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Get out of it
, disgraced, he said: banished.

c: Abu Amr Al-Qarqasani Uthman bin Yahya told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi:
m: Ibn Abbas was asked: What is He was brought out from it, disgraced and expelled, he said: Abhorred. 14397 - Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement:
h
Get out of it

, disgraced and banished, he said: We do not know the disgraced and the blameworthy as anything but one, but there are defective letters, and the poet said to Amer: Oh, Aam, and to Harith: Oh, Harith, the Qur’an was revealed in the language of the Arabs.

x: This is an oath from God, may He be glorified: He swears that whoever among the children of Adam follows the enemy of God, Satan, and obeys him... And his assumption of Him was true, that He would fill Hell with all of them, meaning: from the disbelievers of the children of Adam, the followers of Iblis, and from Iblis and his offspring. So may God have mercy on the man who belies the assumption of the enemy of God about himself, and disappoints his hope and desire in it, and does not enable the desire of his enemy in it, and deceives him and does not seek his advice, for God, the Most High, mentioned Him, only alerted His servants with these verses to the long history of the enmity of His enemy and their enemy Iblis towards them, and the past of what preceded of his envy of their father, and his aggression against him and them, and He made them know the locations of His blessings upon them in the past in themselves and their father so that they may ponder His verses, and so that those of understanding may remember, so that they may Surat al-A’raf 7:18 He said, "
h
Get out of it
, disgraced and expelled.
Whoever of them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with you, all together." refrain from obeying His enemy and their enemy and turn to His obedience and repent to it.

evidence.text: And some of them recited this verse: I kept you company while my eyes were covered with a veil, but when it lifted, I cut myself off from hurting myself.
Most narrators recite it as: I blame her.

x: God Almighty says: And God said to Adam: O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you wish. So God Almighty settled Adam and his wife in Paradise after He had brought down Satan from it and expelled him from it, and He permitted them to eat from its fruits from wherever they wished, and He forbade them from approaching the fruit of a particular tree. We have mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding this, and what we see as correct in saying about it, in a place other than this, so we disliked repeating it. Then you will be among the wrongdoers, meaning: you will be among those who disobeyed the command of their Lord and did what they had no right to do.
What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying:
h
So He whispered to them

, is that He whispered to them, and that whispering was His saying to them: Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you should become angels or become of the immortals, and His swearing to them on that. It was said: He whispered to them, and the meaning is what I mentioned, just as it was said: I longed for him, meaning: I yearned for him, but it means: I longed for him from these people. So the meaning of that is the same. So Satan whispered to them from himself with lies of speech, to reveal to them what was hidden from them of their private parts, just as Ru’bah said: Whispers calling the Savior, Lord of the dawn The meaning of the words: So Satan drew Eve to Adam and said to them: Your Lord did not forbid you from eating the fruit of this tree unless you became angels or became immortals, so that he could show them what God had hidden from them of their private parts and covered it with the veil that He had veiled over them.
Wahb ibn Munabbih used to say about the veil that God had veiled them with, what:

c: Hawthara bin Muhammad Al-Manqari told me that Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ibn Munabbih,
m: regarding his statement: Then their private parts became apparent to them, he said: It was as if there was a light upon them, and their private parts could not be seen.

x: God Almighty says: And Satan said to Adam and his wife Eve: Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree, that you should eat its fruit, except lest you become angels. And the word la was dropped from the statement, because of the indication of what appeared on it, just as it was dropped from His statement:
h
God makes clear to you
, lest you go astray An-Nisa’. The meaning is:
h
God makes clear to you
, lest you go astray.

Some of the Arab scholars from Basra claimed that the meaning of the statement was: Your Lord forbade you from this tree only out of aversion to becoming angels, just as one says: Beware of doing something out of aversion to doing something. Or you will be among the immortals, in Paradise, remaining there forever, so you will not die. Reading with the opening of the lam, meaning: two angels.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: what: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, he said, Isa Al-Ama narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: Unless you two are angels, with a kasra on the lam. On the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, what:

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said, Ya’la bin Hakim told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer:
m: that he read it: two angels, with a kasra on the lam. Ibn Abbas and Yahya interpreted the statement to mean that Satan said to them: Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you should become two kings among the kings, and they interpreted in that the statement of God in another place: He said, O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of immortality and a kingdom that will not decay?

x: The correct reading is that I do not permit reading in this regard with anything other than it, the reading that the regions have read, which is the opening of the lam of two angels, meaning two angels, from the angels, because of what we have previously stated in our statement that everything that is widespread in the reading of Islam from the reading is the correct reading that it is not permissible to contradict it.

evidence.text: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said, Ya’la bin Hakim told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer: that he read it: two angels, with a kasra on the lam.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading is that I do not permit reading in this regard with anything other than it, the reading that the regions have read, which is the opening of the lam of two angels, meaning two angels, from the angels, because of what we have previously stated in our statement that everything that is widespread in the reading of Islam from the reading is the correct reading that it is not permissible to contradict it.

x: He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying:
h
And He swore to them
h
and He swore to them

, as He said in another place: They swore by God that we would spend the night with him, meaning they swore by God, and as Khalid bin Zuhair, the cousin of Abu Dhuʿayb, said: I swear by God that I will do my best for you, for you are sweeter than quails when they are raised. Meaning: And he swore to her by God, as A’sha of Banu Tha’laba said: My baby is milk, my mother's breast is shared with me, Basham Dag Awad, we will not be separated Meaning: they made an alliance.

And his saying: I am indeed among your sincere advisers means: among those who advise you in his advice to you, and his command to you to eat the fruit of the tree whose fruit you were forbidden to eat, and in my informing you of what he informed you of, that if you eat it you will be kings or you will be among the immortals, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he swore to them

, ‘Indeed, I am to you one of the sincere advisers.’ So he swore to them by God until he deceived them, and the believer may be deceived by God, so he said: I was created before you, and I am more knowledgeable than you, so follow me, and I will guide you.

x: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: Whoever deceives us with his words, deceives us.

He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: So He led them astray with deception, that is, He deceived them with deception. It is said: So-and-so continued to deceive so-and-so, meaning: he continued to deceive him with deceit, and speak to him with false and vain words.
h
So when they tasted of the tree
, meaning: when Adam and Eve tasted the fruit of the tree, meaning: they ate it,
h
their private parts became apparent to them

, meaning: their private parts were exposed to them, because God stripped them of the clothing that He had clothed them with before the sin and wrongdoing, so He took that away from them because of the sin that they committed and the transgression that they committed, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise, meaning: they came and began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise, to cover their private parts, as:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they began to cover themselves with leaves of Paradise. He said: They began to take leaves of Paradise and put them on their private parts. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Adam was like a palm tree with abundant hair, but when he committed the sin, his private parts became apparent to him, although he could not see them. So he set off fleeing, but a tree came across him and held him back by his hair. So he said to it: Let me go! It said: I am not the one who sent you! So his Lord called out to him: O Adam, are you fleeing from me? He said: No, but I felt shy of you. - Al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Ishaq narrated, he said:

c: Abd Al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and Ibn Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Umarah, on the authority of Al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The tree from which God forbade Adam and his wife was the ear of wheat. So when they ate thereof,
h
their private parts became apparent to them

, although what had concealed them of their private parts were their fingernails. And they began to fasten together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise, the leaves of figs, sticking them together. Then Adam went on turning away in Paradise, and a tree from Paradise took hold of his head and called out to him, O Adam, are you fleeing from Me? He said, No, but I am ashamed of You, O Lord! He said: Did you not have in what I granted you of Paradise and permitted you from it an alternative to what I forbade you? He said: Yes, O Lord, but by Your glory, I did not think that anyone would swear by You falsely! He said: And this is the saying of God: And he swore to them, ‘I am to you both of you,’ 1:17. He said: By My glory, I will send you down to the earth, and you will not live except thus. He said: Then descend from Paradise. They used to eat there in comfort, so they descended in a state of no comfort in food and drink. So he learned the craft of iron and was ordered to plough. So he ploughed and planted, then watered, until when it was ripe he harvested. Then he trampled it, then crushed it, then kneaded it, then baked it, then ate it, and did not swallow it until he had swallowed from it what God willed him to swallow.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: They patch, he said: They patch, like the shape of a garment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They sewed together paper over themselves like a garment.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
So when they tasted of the tree
h
their private parts became apparent to them

, and before that they had not seen them, and they began to fasten together, He said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said, Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b: That Adam, peace be upon him, was a tall man, like a tall palm tree, with much hair on his head. When he committed the sin that he committed, his private parts became apparent to him, but he could not see them. So he set off fleeing into Paradise, and a tree from the trees of Paradise caught hold of his head, so he said to it: Let me go! It said: I will not let you go! So his Lord called to him: O Adam, are you fleeing from Me? He said: My Lord, I am ashamed of You.

c: Ibn Rakiʿ told us, he said, Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn ʿAmr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they began to fasten together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise, he said: fig leaves.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they began to fasten together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise, he said: fig leaves.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Hisam bin Musak, on the authority of Qatada and Abu Bakr, on the authority of someone other than Qatada, who said:
m: Adam’s clothing in Paradise was all fingernails. But when he committed the sin, it was peeled off and his private parts were exposed. Abu Bakr said, someone other than Qatada said: And they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise, he said: fig leaves.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their private parts became apparent to them
, he said: They did not see their private parts.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Amr told us, he said:
m: I heard Wahb bin Munabbihah say: Their clothing will be removed from them. He said: The clothing of Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, was a light upon their private parts. This one could not see the private parts of this one, nor could this one see the private parts of this one. But when they committed the sin,
h
their private parts became apparent to them

x: God Almighty says: And Adam and Eve called to their Lord: Did I not forbid you from eating the fruit of the tree whose fruit you ate, and inform you that Satan is to you a clear enemy? He says: He made his enmity towards you clear, by not prostrating to Adam out of envy and malice, as: Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays, his saying: “
h
And their Lord called to them

, ‘Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?’ Why did you eat it when I forbade you from it? He said: O Lord, Eve fed me! He said to Eve: Why did you feed him? She said: The serpent commanded me! He said to the serpent: Why did you command her? She said: Satan commanded me! He said: Cursed and banished! As for you, Eve, just as you made the tree bleed, you will bleed every month. As for you, serpent, cut off your legs and you will walk on your face, and your head will be smashed by whoever meets you.
Go down, some of you enemies to others.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Ibad bin Al-Awam narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Hussein, on the authority of Ya’la bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When Adam ate from the tree, he was asked: Why did you eat from the tree that I forbade you from? He said: Eve commanded me! He said: Then I have made her do not conceive except with difficulty, and she does not give birth except with difficulty. He said: Eve was alarmed at that, and it was said to her: May the alarm be upon you and your child.

x: This is report from God, may He be glorified, about Adam and Eve in what they answered Him with, and their admission of their sin, and their asking Him for forgiveness and mercy, contrary to the answer of the accursed Iblis to him. The meaning of His statement: They said, ‘Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves,’ is that Adam and Eve said to their Lord: “Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves by disobeying You and going against Your command, and by obeying our enemy and Your enemy in that which we should not have obeyed, by eating the tree from which You forbade us to eat. ‘And if You do not forgive us,’” meaning, if You do not cover up our sin for us, and do not leave us disgraced by it by punishing us for it, and have mercy upon us, by being kind to us and not taking us by it, we will surely be among the losers, meaning, we will surely be among the perishing. We have already explained the meaning of the loser with its evidence and the narration of it, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Adam, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, what do you think if I repent and seek Your forgiveness? He said: Then I will admit you to Paradise. As for Satan, he did not ask Him for repentance, but asked for a look, so He gave each of them what he asked for.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us, the verse, he said: They are the words that Adam received from his Lord.

x: This is report from God Almighty about what He did to Iblis and his offspring, Adam and his son, and the serpent.
God Almighty says to Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, and to Iblis and the serpent: Descend from the sky to the earth, some of you enemies to one another, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr ibn Talhah told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Go down, some of you as enemies to others. He said: So he cursed the snake, cut off its legs, and left it to walk on its belly, and made its sustenance from the dust, and they descended to the earth: Adam, Eve, Satan, and the snake.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Ismail bin Salem, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: Go down, some of you enemies to others, he said: Adam, Eve, and the serpent. And his saying:
h
And for you on earth is a place of settlement
, he says: And for you, O Adam and Eve, for Satan and the serpent, on earth is a place of rest for you to settle in, and a bed for you to lie on, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And for you on the earth is a place of settlement
, he said: It is his statement,
h
Who made the earth a bed for you

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas in this regard:
m: -It was narrated on the authority of Ubaid God, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of someone who narrated to him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And for you on earth is a place of settlement
, he said: the graves.

x: The correct statement about that is to say: God, the Most High, informed Adam and Eve, to Satan and the serpent, when they were sent down to the earth, that they were enemies to one another, and that they would have a place to settle in it. He did not specify that they would have a place to settle in it during their life and not during their death. Rather, the information about it was general, that they would have a place to settle in it. This is general, just as God’s information was general, and they would have a place to settle in it during their life on its surface, and after their death in its belly, as He, the Most High, said: Have We not made the earth a receptacle * for the living and the dead?
As for His saying:
h
And provision for a time
, He, the Most High, says: And therein you will have provision, which you will enjoy until the end of the world, and that is the time that He mentioned, as:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ubayd God bin Musa,
m: who said: Israel told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And provision for a time

, he said: until the Day of Resurrection, and until the end of the world. And the same time: time, but its amount is unknown, as indicated by the poet’s saying: What are your stages after dreaming and religion, when gray hair has covered you at a time when there is no time? Meaning: time, no time.

x: God Almighty says: God said to those whom He sent down from His heavens to His earth: Therein you shall live, meaning: on the earth you shall live, meaning: you shall be there during the days of your life, and therein you shall die, meaning: on the earth your death will be, and from it you shall emerge, meaning: from the earth your Lord will emerge you and gather you to Him for the resurrection of the Day of Resurrection alive.

God, the Most High, says to the ignorant Arabs who used to strip for the Tawaf, following the command of Satan, and abandoning the obedience of God, so He made them aware of their deception by his deception of them, until he gained control over them and robbed them of the covering of God that He had bestowed upon them, until He exposed their private parts and made them apparent to one another, despite God’s favor upon them by enabling them to cover them with what they used to do, and that He had led them as He had done with their parents Adam and Eve, whom He had led astray by deception until He robbed them of the covering of God that He had bestowed upon them until He exposed their private parts to them and stripped them of it:
h
O children of Adam

, We have bestowed upon you clothing, meaning by sending it down upon them, He created it for them and provided for them, and clothing is what they wear of clothes, to conceal your private parts, meaning: It conceals your private parts from your eyes, and He used the word private parts as a metaphor for private parts.

i: Its singular is su’ah, and it is an action from su’, because it is called su’ah because its owner finds it unpleasant to have it exposed from his body, as the poet said:
x: They tore their girl's pocket, they didn't care about the man's misdeeds And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: clothing to cover your private parts, he said: There were some Arabs who would circumambulate the House naked, and none of them would wear a garment in which to circumambulate.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Asaad Al-Madani told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say about His statement:
h
O children of Adam

, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and adornment, he said: Four verses were revealed about the Quraysh. In the pre-Islamic era, they would not circumambulate the House except naked.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Awf, he said:
m: I heard Ma’bad Al-Juhani say regarding His statement:
h
O children of Adam
, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and adornment, he said: The clothing that you wear.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
O children of Adam

, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts. He said: The Quraysh used to circumambulate naked, and none of them would wear a garment to circumambulate in. And some of the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar and Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Maʿbad al-Juhani:
m: h
O children of Adam
, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts. He said: The clothing that conceals your private parts, and it is this clothing of yours.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: A garment that covers your private parts, he said: It is the clothes.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us,
m: he told me who heard Urwah bin Al-Zubayr say: Clothing: garments.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: We have sent down upon you clothing to conceal your private parts, he said: He means the clothes that a man wears.

x: There are different readings of this. So, the majority of the people in the region read it as warishan, without an alif. It was mentioned on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaysh and al-Hasan al-Basri that they used to read it as warishan.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, on the authority of Aban al-Attar, he said, Asim told us:
m: that Zur ibn Hubaish read it: And feathers.

x: The correct reading in this regard is Surat al-A’raf 7:26
h
O children of Adam

, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of God that perhaps they will remember. the reading of those who read: Wa-Risha without an alif, because the evidence from the readings agrees on it. A report was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission that is questionable: that he read it: Wa-Risha. Whoever reads it as: and feathers, it is possible that he meant by it the collection of feathers, just as the wolf gathers wolves, and a well gathers wells. It is possible that he meant a source, from the saying of the speaker: May God sprinkle him, may He sprinkle him with feathers and feathers, just as it is said: May He dress him, may He dress him with clothing and clothing.

i: Some of them recited:
x: When they removed the blemish from him, they wiped him with the tips of a tattooed, adorned child.

With a broken lam from the word al-labis. And al-rayash, in the speech of the Arabs, is the furniture, and what is visible of the clothes of the goods that are worn or stuffed with a mattress or blanket. And feathers are only goods and money for them. And they may use them for clothes and clothing without other money. They say: He gave a saddle with its feathers, and a saddle with its feathers, meaning with its clothing and equipment. And they say: It is for the beauty of the feathers of clothes, and feathers may be used for fertility and a comfortable life. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said: feathers, money.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: and feathers, he said: money.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And feathers, he said: money.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And riyasha, he said: As for riyasha, it is the furnishings of money.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saeed Al-Madani told us,
m: he told me who heard Urwah bin Al-Zubayr say: Al-Riyash is money.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And luxuries, meaning money. It was mentioned that it is clothing and a comfortable life.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And ostentatious garments
, he said: The ostentatious garments are clothing, living, and comfort.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar and Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Ma’bad Al-Juhani:
m: And riyasha, he said: riyasha means livelihood.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Aouf told us, he said, Ma’bad Al-Juhani said:
m: And feathers, he said: And livelihood. And others said: Feathers, beauty.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: and feathers, he said: feathers are beauty.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: The garment of piety is faith.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the clothing of piety
means faith.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And the clothing of piety
means faith.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And the clothing of piety
means faith.

x: Others said: It is modesty.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar and Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Maʿbad al-Juhani,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the clothing of piety
, which God mentioned in the Qur’an, is modesty.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Aouf told us, he said,
m: Ma’bad Al-Juhani said, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Ma’bad,
m: something similar. And others said: It is righteous work.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And the clothing of piety
- that is best. He said: The clothing of piety is righteous deeds.

x: Others said: Rather, that is the good character.
Who said that?

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said, Abdullah bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Musa, on the authority of Ibn Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And the clothing of piety
, he said: The good appearance on the face.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Ishaq bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Arqam, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: I saw Uthman bin Affan on the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wearing a brown shirt with the button unbuttoned, and I heard him order the killing of dogs and forbid playing with pigeons. Then he said: O people, fear God in these secrets, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one has ever done anything in secret except that God will clothe him in a robe of publicity, if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil. Then he recited this verse: And feathers - and he did not read it: and feathers - “And the garment of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of God.” He said: The good appearance.

x: Others said: It is the fear of God.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad Al-Madani told us,
m: he told me who heard Urwah bin Al-Zubayr say: The clothing of piety is the fear of God.

x: Others said: The clothing of piety, in these situations, is covering the private parts.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And the clothing of righteousness

, he fears God and covers his private parts, that is the clothing of righteousness. And the reciters differed in the recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Mecca, Kufa, and Basra recited it:
h
And the clothing of righteousness
, that is best, raising clothing. And the majority of the reciters of Medina recited it:
h
And the clothing of righteousness

, lowering clothing, and that is the recitation of some of the reciters of Kufa. Whoever puts clothing in the accusative case and dressing in the accusative case is in apposition to feathers, meaning, We have sent down upon you clothing to cover your private parts and feathers, and We have sent down the clothing of piety. As for the nominative case, the Arab scholars differed on the meaning by which the word clothes was raised.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is a subject, and its predicate is in his statement:
h
That is better
. Some Arab scholars found fault with him in that and said: This is a mistake, because there is no reference to the word clothes in the sentence, so if the word clothes is raised as a subject,
h
that is better
is made the predicate. Some grammarians of Kufa said: And clothing is raised by saying:
h
And the clothing of piety
is better, and he made that one of its descriptions.

This statement, in my opinion, is more correct in the case of the one who raises the garment, because there is no reason for raising it except that it be raised by good, and if it is raised by good, then there is no reason for that except that the garment be made an attribute, not that it refers back to the garment from its mention in His statement:
h
That is better
, so good would be raised by that, and that, by it. So since that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement - if the garment of piety is raised:
h
And the garment of piety
is that which you have learned, better for you,
h
O children of Adam

, than wearing the garments that cover your private parts, and than the feathers that We have sent down to you, so wear it like this. As for the interpretation of those who read it in the accusative case, it is:
h
O children of Adam
, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and plumage,
h
and the clothing of righteousness
This that We have bestowed upon you of clothing to conceal your private parts and plumage,
h
and the clothing of righteousness

is better for you than being naked and stripped of clothing during your circumambulation of the House, so fear God and wear what God has provided you of plumage, and do not obey Satan by stripping and stripping of clothing, for that is a mockery of you and a deception from him, as he did with your parents Adam and Eve, so he deceived them until he stripped them of the clothing of God that He had clothed them with because of their obedience to Him, in eating what God had forbidden them to eat of the fruit of the tree that they disobeyed Him by eating.
This reading is the more correct of the two readings in my opinion, I mean the accusative of his statement:
h
and the clothing of piety

, because its meaning is correct in interpretation as I have explained, and that God only began the report of His sending down the clothing that covers our private parts and the feathers, as a rebuke to the thieves who used to strip off while circumambulating the House, and He commands them to take their clothes and cover themselves with them in every situation, while believing in Him and following His obedience, and He teaches them that all of
h
that is better

than everything they are doing of their disbelief in God and their stripping, except that He informed them that some of what was sent down to them is better than some. What indicates the correctness of what we have said about that are the verses that come after this verse, and that is His saying:
h
O children of Adam

, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts, and the verses that come after that until His saying: And that you say about God that which you do not know, for He, may He be glorified, commands in all of that to take on adornment of clothing, and to use clothing, and to leave off stripping and nudity, and to believe in Him, and to follow His command and to act in obedience to Him, and He Surat al-A’raf 7:26
h
O children of Adam
, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment.

But the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is from the signs of God that perhaps they will remember. forbids associating partners with Him and following the command of Satan, confirming in all of that what He has summarized in His saying:
h
O children of Adam
, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and adornment. But the clothing of righteousness - that is best.

The most correct interpretation of his statement, the clothing of piety, is the soul’s awareness of piety towards God, in refraining from what God has forbidden of His sins, and doing what He has commanded of obedience to Him. This combines faith, righteous deeds, modesty, fear of God, and good conduct. Because whoever fears God is a believer in Him, and acts according to what He has commanded him, and fears Him, and watches Him, and is ashamed to be seen when He dislikes one of His servants. And whoever is like this, the effects of goodness appear in him, so his conduct and guidance are good, and the joy and light of faith are seen upon him. We said that by the clothing of piety we mean the soul and heart’s perception of that, because clothing is nothing but the armour of what is worn, the selection of what is clothed, or the covering of one’s body or part of it with it.

So whoever puts on something and selects it until he sees with his own eyes or its traces its place, then it is its wearer. For this reason, the Most High made men a garment for women, and they a garment for them, and He made the night a garment for His servants. It was mentioned that whoever interpreted it with the meaning we mentioned of its interpretation, if his saying is read:
h
And the garment of piety
, in the nominative case.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And the clothing of piety
means faith,
h
that is better
, he says:
h
That is better
than finery and clothing that covers your private parts.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the garment of piety
, he said: The garment of piety is faith.

x: God Almighty says: That which I have mentioned to you that I have sent down to you, O people, of clothing and riyals, is from the proofs and evidence of God by which He knows from the disbelievers the truth of the oneness of God, and the error of what they are persisting in of misguidance, so that they may remember, God Almighty says: I made that for them a proof of what I have described, so that they may remember and take heed and turn to the truth and abandon falsehood, as a mercy from Me to My servants.

evidence.text: So, the majority of the people in the region read it as warishan, without an alif.
It was mentioned on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaysh and al-Hasan al-Basri that they used to read it as warishan.
Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, on the authority of Aban al-Attar, he said, Asim told us: that Zur ibn Hubaish read it: And feathers.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard is Surat al-A’raf 7:26 O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment.
That is from the signs of God that perhaps they will remember. the reading of those who read: Wa-Risha without an alif, because the evidence from the readings agrees on it.
A report was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission that is questionable: that he read it: Wa-Risha.
Whoever reads it as: and feathers, it is possible that he meant by it the collection of feathers, just as the wolf gathers wolves, and a well gathers wells.
Then he recited this verse: And feathers - and he did not read it: and feathers - “And the garment of righteousness - that is best.
And the reciters differed in the recitation of that.
The majority of the reciters of Mecca, Kufa, and Basra recited it: And the clothing of righteousness, that is best, raising clothing.
And the majority of the reciters of Medina recited it: And the clothing of righteousness, lowering clothing, and that is the recitation of some of the reciters of Kufa.

As for the interpretation of those who read it in the accusative case, it is: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and plumage, and the clothing of righteousness.

Abu Jaʿfar said: This reading is the more correct of the two readings in my opinion, I mean the accusative of his statement: and the clothing of piety, because its meaning is correct in interpretation as I have explained, and that God only began the report of His sending down the clothing that covers our private parts and the feathers, as a rebuke to the thieves who used to strip off while circumambulating the House, and He commands them to take their clothes and cover themselves with them in every situation, while believing in Him and following His obedience, and He teaches them that all of that is better than everything they are doing of their disbelief in God and their stripping, except that He informed them that some of what was sent down to them is better than some.
It was mentioned that whoever interpreted it with the meaning we mentioned of its interpretation, if his saying is read: And the garment of piety, in the nominative case.

x: God Almighty says: O children of Adam, do not let Satan deceive you and expose your private parts to people by your obedience to him when he tests you, as he did with your parents Adam and Eve when he tested them, so they obeyed him and disobeyed their Lord, so he expelled them from Paradise because of his deception and trickery, and took away from them the clothing that he had worn, in order to show them their private parts by uncovering their private parts, to expose them to their eyes after they had been hidden. We have previously explained that the meaning of temptation is testing and trial, so there is no need to repeat it.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the clothing that God Almighty said He removed from our parents, and what it was.
Some of them said: It was nails.
Mention of what was not mentioned in the previous part of our book regarding this:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
He will strip them of their clothing
, he said: The clothing of every animal, and the clothing of man is the nail, so Adam’s repentance overtook him when he had his nails, or he said: his nails.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdul Hamid Al-Hamani told us, on the authority of Nadr bin Abi Omar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: His nails were left on him as an adornment and benefit, in His statement:
h
He will strip them of their clothing

c: Ahmad bin Al-Walid Al-Qurashi told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Abi Al-Wazir told us, he said, Mukhallad bin Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Their clothing will be stripped from them, he said: Their clothing was nails, but when they committed the sin, they were stripped from them, and the nails were left as a reminder and an adornment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He will strip them of their clothing
, he said: His clothing was nails, so his repentance ended at his nails.

x: Others said: Their clothing was light.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
m: h
He will strip them of their clothing

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said, Amr told us, he said:
m: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih say about His statement,
h
He will strip them of their clothing

to show them their private parts, he said: The clothing of Adam and Eve was a light upon their private parts, so that this one would not see the private parts of this one, nor that one the private parts of this one.

x: Others said: What God meant by His statement,
h
He will strip them of their clothing
, is that He will strip them of their fear of God.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Mutalib bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He strips them of their clothing, he said: piety.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He strips them of their clothing, he said: piety.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: The correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is that God Almighty warned His servants lest Satan tempt them as he tempted their parents Adam and Eve, and that He should strip them of the clothing of God that He sent down to them, just as He stripped their parents of their clothing. Clothing is the absolute meaning of speech without any relation to anything in common usage among people, and it is what the wearer chooses from the types of clothing, or covers his body or part of it. Since this is the case, it is true to say that what God told about Adam and Eve, regarding their clothing that Satan took off from them, was some of what they used to cover their bodies and private parts with. It may be possible that this was a nail, or it may be possible that this was light, or it may be something else, and we do not have any information on which of these two things the proof is established with, so there is no more correct statement about this than to say as God Almighty said: He will take off their clothing.

And He, the Most High, added to the expulsion of Adam and Eve from Paradise, and the stripping of the clothing they were wearing, even though God, the Most High, was the one who did that to them as Surat al-A’raf 7:27 O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe. punishment for their disobedience to Him, since what they did in that was to make it easy for them through his deceit and trickery, so it was sometimes attributed to Him in that sense, and sometimes to God for His doing that to them.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Indeed, Satan sees you, and the ha in indeed, refers back to Satan, and his tribe, meaning: and his type and kind from which he is one, a group of generations, and they are the jinn, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, he and his tribe see you, he said: The jinn and the devils.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, Indeed, he and his tribe see you, he said: His tribe, his offspring. And His statement, from where you do not see them, he said: from where you, O people, do not see Satan and his tribe. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe, he said: We have made the devils supporters of the disbelievers who do not believe in the Oneness of God and do not believe in His Messengers.

x: It was mentioned that the meaning of obscenity, in this context, is:

c: Ali bin Saeed bin Masruq Al-Kindi told me, he said, Abu Muhyiah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when they commit an immorality

, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it.’ He said: They would circumambulate the House naked, saying, We circumambulate as our mothers bore us. Then the woman would place a piece of cloth or something on her private parts and say: Today some or all of it appears, so whatever appears of it I do not permit.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when they commit an immorality
, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it.’ Their immorality was that they used to circumambulate the House naked.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Mufadhal, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Imran bin Uyaynah narrated, on the authority of Ata’ bin As-Saazib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Ash-Sha’bi: “And when they committed an immorality, they said: ‘We found our fathers doing it.’” They said: They used to circumambulate the House naked. Muhammad bin Al-Husayn narrated, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal narrated, he said: Asbat narrated, on the authority of As-Suddi: “And when they committed an immorality, they said: ‘We found our fathers doing it, and God commanded us to do it.’” He said: There was a tribe of Arabs from Yemen who used to circumambulate the House naked. If it was said: Why do you do that? They said: We found our fathers doing it, and God commanded us to do it.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when they commit an immorality
, he said: their circumambulation of the House naked.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when they commit an immorality

, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it.’ He said: During the circumambulation of the Kaʿbah in clothes, while others are naked. 14464 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And when they commit an immorality

, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it.’ He said, their women used to circumambulate the House naked, and that was the immorality that they found their fathers doing: Say, ‘Indeed, God does not command immorality.’ The verse.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: And if those who do not believe in God, whom God has made devils their guardians, do an ugly act, which is immorality, and that is their undressing for circumambulation of the House and their stripping off for it, then they change their ugly act and are rebuked for it, saying: We found our fathers doing what we did, so we do what they did, and we follow their guidance and their Sunnah, and God has commanded us to do it, so we follow His command in it. God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to them: Indeed, God does not command immorality, meaning: He does not command His creation to do ugly and wrong actions. Do you say, O people, about God that which you do not know? He says: Do you attribute to God that He has commanded you to undress and strip off your clothes and garments for circumambulation, while you do not know that He has commanded you to do that?

God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to those who claim that God commanded them to commit immorality, lying against God: My Lord did not command what you say, rather my Lord commanded justice, meaning: fairness, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Say, ‘My Lord has commanded justice,’ meaning fairness.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Say, ‘My Lord has commanded justice.’ Justice is fairness. As for his statement,
h
And direct your faces toward every mosque
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And direct your faces toward every mosque
, toward the Kaaba wherever you pray, in the church and elsewhere.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And direct your faces toward every mosque
, he said: When you pray, face the Kaaba, in your churches and elsewhere. Hali Thani Muhammad bin Al-Hussein said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And direct your faces toward every mosque
, meaning the mosque, the Kaaba.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Khalid bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Omar bin Dhir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And direct your faces toward every mosque
, he said: The Kaaba, wherever you are.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And direct your faces toward every mosque
, he said: Direct them toward the qiblah, this qiblah that God has commanded you to do.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that: Make your prostration purely for God, without any other gods or rivals.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And direct your faces toward every mosque
, he said: In sincerity, that you do not call upon anyone other than Him, and that you devote your religion to Him alone.

x: The most appropriate of these two interpretations of the verse is what Al-Rabiʿ said: That the people were commanded to direct their prayers to their Lord, not to anything else of idols and statues, and to make their supplication to God sincere, not whistling or clapping. We said that this is the more correct interpretation of the verse, because God addressed this verse to a group of polytheists from the Arabs who were not people of churches and synagogues. Rather, churches and synagogues belonged to the People of the Book. So it is not reasonable to say to someone who does not pray in a church or synagogue: Turn your face toward the Kaaba in a church or synagogue. As for his saying:
h
And call upon Him
, making your religion sincere to Him, he is saying: And work for your Lord, making your religion and obedience sincere to Him.
Do not mix that with polytheism, and do not make a partner in anything that you work for Him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: h
And call upon Him
, making your religion sincere to Him, he said: That you make your religion, your call, and your work sincere to Him, then head to the Sacred House.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement: As He began you, you will return.
Some of them said: Its interpretation is: How many of you were born miserable and happy, thus you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.
Who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
As He began you

, you will return, “A group He guided and a group upon whom error was decreed,” he said: God Almighty began the creation of the son of Adam as believers and disbelievers, as He, the Most High, said: It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer, then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as He began their creation, believers and disbelievers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, he said, our companions told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return, he said, the believer will be resurrected as a believer and the disbeliever as a disbeliever.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya bin Al-Durais told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Jabir, he said:
m: They will be resurrected as they were, the believer in his faith, and the hypocrite in his hypocrisy.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu al-A’aliyah, who said:
m: They returned to his knowledge of them. Did you not hear the words of God about them:
h
As He began you
, you will return. Have you not heard His saying:
h
A party He has guided and a party upon whom error is due

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah,
m: h
As He began you
, you will return, he said, return to His knowledge of them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Hammam Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b,
m: regarding his statement:
h
As He began you

, you will return, he said: Whoever God began his creation in misery will become as God began his creation, because he will act according to the deeds of the people of happiness, just as Iblis acted according to the deeds of the people of happiness, then he will become as he began his creation. And whoever God began his creation in happiness will become as he began his creation, because he will act according to the deeds of the people of misery, just as the magicians acted according to the deeds of the people of misery, then they will become as they began their creation.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Waqqa bin Iyas Abu Yazid, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return, he said: The Muslim will be resurrected as a Muslim, and the disbeliever as a disbeliever.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Dukayn told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Yazid, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return, he said: The Muslim will be resurrected as a Muslim, and the disbeliever as a disbeliever.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return, he said: As He wrote for you, you will be.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed,
m: similarly, Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
As He began you
, you will return.

x: “A group He guided and a group upon whom error is due.” He says:
h
As He began you
, you will return, as We created you, a group guided and a group astray, thus you will return and emerge from the wombs of your mothers.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir:
m: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every soul will be resurrected according to what it was upon.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Dawood Al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return, he said: As He wrote for you, you will be.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The believer will be resurrected as a believer, and the unbeliever will be resurrected as an unbeliever.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return, miserable and happy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us,
m: reading from Mujahid, similarly. And others said: The meaning of that is: Just as He created you when you were nothing, you will return after annihilation.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return. He said: Just
h
as He began you
when you were nothing and then brought you to life, so He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return. He said:
h
As He began you
in this world, so you will return on the Day of Resurrection alive.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
As He began you
, you will return. He said: He began their creation and they were nothing, then they went away, then He will return them.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
As He began you
, you will return, “a guided group,” meaning: As We created you the first time, so will you return.

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
As He began you
, you will return, He will revive you after your death.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
As He began you
, you will return, he said: As He created them first, so He will return them at the end.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is that of the one who said: Its meaning is: Just as God created you after you were nothing, you will return after your annihilation as a creation like it, and He will gather you until the Day of Resurrection. This is because God, the Most High, commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to teach what is in this verse to a polytheistic people of ignorance who do not believe in the afterlife or in the Resurrection. So He commanded him to call them to acknowledge that God will raise them on the Day of Resurrection, and will reward those who obey Him and punish those who disobey Him. So He said to him: Say to them: My Lord has commanded justice, and that you should turn your faces toward every mosque, and that you should call upon Him, sincerely devoting your religion to Him, and that you should acknowledge that you will return
h
as He began you

So He left out mentioning and and acknowledge that, just as He left out mentioning that with establish, since what was mentioned indicated what was omitted from it. Since this is the case, there is no reason to command someone who denies the resurrection after death to call upon God to acknowledge the attribute by which he will be resurrected. Rather, he who believes in the resurrection is commanded to call upon God to do so. As for he who has… Denying, he is only called to acknowledge it, then he knows how the conditions of resurrection are.
However, in the report that was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Mughirah bin Al-Nu’man told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: People will be gathered naked and uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited: “As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [It is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of al-Mughira ibn al-Nuʿman, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us and delivered a sermon, and he said: O people, you will be gathered before God barefoot and uncircumcised: “As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [It is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.” This clarifies the correctness of what we have said about that, that its meaning is: that creation will return to God on the Day of Resurrection as a living creation, just as He began them in this world as a living creation. It is said: God began the creation, He begins them, and He began them, He begins them, meaning: He created them, two eloquent languages. Then He, the Most High, began the report of what preceded of His knowledge in His creation, and what His judgment was carried out on them, so He said: God guided a group of them and granted them success in righteous deeds, so they are guided, and it was right for a group of them to stray from guidance and right conduct, by taking Satan instead of God as a guardian. Since this interpretation was, the first group was accusative by the actions of guidance in it, and the second group by the occurrence of His saying: it was right upon, referring back to His mention in upon them, as He, the Most High, said: He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment. One of the ways of interpreting this is that: Just
h
as He began you

in this world as two groups, a disbeliever and a believer, so you will return in the Hereafter as two groups, a group that He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was decreed. He made a group Surat al-A’raf 7:30 A party He guided, and a party upon whom error was justly decreed. Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of God and thought that they were guided. the first in the accusative case by saying: you will return, and made the second in apposition to it. We have explained what is correct in our view of what is said about it.

x: God the Almighty says: The group upon whom misguidance is due, only went astray from the path of God and deviated from the straight path, by taking the devils as helpers and supporters instead of God, out of their ignorance of the error of what they were doing. Rather, they did that while they thought that they were on the right path and that what they had done and done was correct. This is one of the clearest indications of the error of the statement of those who claim that God does not punish anyone for a sin he committed or a misguidance he believed in, unless he commits it after knowing that it is correct, so he does it out of his defiance of his Lord. Because if that were the case, there would be no difference between the group of misguidance who went astray while thinking that they were guided, and the group of guidance. God has distinguished between their names and their rulings in this verse.

God Almighty says to those who strip naked when they circumambulate His Sacred House, and show their private parts there, from the polytheists of the Arabs, and those among them who are forbidden to eat what God has not forbidden them from His lawful provision, as a justification to themselves before their Lord:
h
O children of Adam

, take your adornment, of clothing and garments, at every mosque and eat, of the good things that I have provided you and made lawful for you, and drink, of the lawful drinks, and do not forbid except what I have forbidden you in My Book or on the tongue of My Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yahya bin Habib bin Arabi told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The women used to circumambulate the House naked. And he said in another place: Without clothing, unless the woman puts a rag over her private parts, as described, God willing, and says: Today, some or all of it appears, so what started from it, I do not know. He said: Then this verse was revealed:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque

c: Amr ibn Ali told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: They used to circumambulate naked, the men during the day and the women at night. A woman would say: Today some or all of it is visible, so whatever is visible of it I do not permit it. Then God said, Take your adornment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Take your adornment at every mosque
, he said: clothing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar and Wahb ibn Jarir told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said:
m: I heard Muslim al-Batin narrating, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: A woman used to circumambulate the House naked. Ghundar said: And she was naked. Wahb said: A woman used to circumambulate the House and she had exposed her chest and what was there. Ghundar said: And she would say: Who will lend me a circumambulation garment? She would put it on her vagina and say: Today some or all of it appears, and whatever appears of it I do not permit. Then God revealed:
h
O children of Adam
h
take your adornment at every mosque

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O children of Adam
h
take your adornment at every mosque
, he said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, so God commanded them to wear their clothes and not be naked.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me,
m: my father said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque

verse, he said: There were men who would circumambulate the House naked, so God commanded them to adorn themselves, and adornment is clothing, which is what covers the private parts, and other than that of good clothing and goods, so they were commanded to take their adornment at every mosque.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi and Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: Take your adornment. He said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, so they were ordered to wear their clothes.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

c: Amr told me, he said, Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque
, put on your clothes.

c: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Munira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque
, he said: There were people who would circumambulate the House naked, so they were forbidden from doing so.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us,
m: on the Surat al-A’raf 7:31
h
O children of Adam
h
take your adornment at every masjid
h
and eat and drink
, but be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess. authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque
. He said: They used to circumambulate the House naked, so they were ordered to wear clothes.
