c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Take your adornment at every mosque
, he said: What covers the private parts, even an abaya.

c: Amr told us,
m: Yahya bin Saeed, Abu Asim and Abdullah bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Take your adornment at every masjid
, he said: What covers your private parts, even an cloak.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Take your adornment at every masjid
, regarding Quraysh, because they left their clothes on during the circumambulation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Take your adornment at every mosque
, he said: clothing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: h
Take your adornment at every mosque
, he said: The shawl is one of the adornments.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Tawus:
m: h
Take your adornment at every mosque
, he said: clothing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Suwaid and Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: They used to circumambulate the House naked, and a woman circumambulated the House naked and said: Today some or all of it will be exposed, so whatever is exposed of it I do not permit it. - Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque

, he said: There was a tribe from the people of Yemen, one of them, when he came as a pilgrim or a performer of Umrah, would say: I should not circumambulate in a garment that I have soiled, so he would say: Who will lend me a loincloth? If he is able to do that, then he will circumambulate naked, so God revealed about him what you hear:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Qal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: God said:
h
O children of Adam
h
take your adornment at every mosque

, meaning: what covers the private parts at every mosque. 14530 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri: That the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, except for the Hims, the Quraysh and their allies. So whoever came from outside them would take off his clothes and circumambulate in the clothes of the Hims, because it was not permissible for him to wear his clothes. And if he did not find anyone from the Hims to lend him, then he would throw off his clothes and circumambulate naked. Because he circumambulated in his own clothes, he would throw them off when he finished his circumambulation, making them forbidden for him. That is why God said:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque
. And on his authority, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Ibn Tawus said, on the authority of his father: The shawl is an adornment.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Take your adornment at every mosque

, the verse: There were people from Yemen and the Bedouins who, when they performed Hajj to the House, would circumambulate it naked at night, so God commanded them to wear their clothes and not to be naked in the mosque.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Take your adornment, he said: Their adornment, their clothes that they used to throw at the House and undress.

c: And he told me
m: about it again with his chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Zayd regarding his statement: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” He said: When they came to the House and circumambulated it, the clothes in which they had circumambulated were forbidden to them. So if they found someone to lend them clothes, well and good, otherwise they would circumambulate the House naked. So he said: Who has forbidden the adornment of God? He said: The clothes of God which He has produced for His servants, the verse. And as we said, they also said in the interpretation of His saying:
h
And eat and drink
, but be not excessive.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: God has permitted eating and drinking, as long as it is not extravagance or conceit.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And eat and drink
, but be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess,” in food and drink.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Those who circumambulated the House naked were forbidden to eat fat as long as they stayed during the season, so God said to them: Eat and drink, but be not excessive, for He does not like those who commit excess, He said: Do not be excessive in what is forbidden.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say about His statement:
h
And eat and drink
, but be not excessive, he said: He commanded them to eat and drink from what God provided them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: And do not be extravagant, do not eat what is forbidden, that is extravagance. And His saying:
h
He does not love the extravagant

, means that God does not love those who transgress His limits in what is permissible or forbidden, who go to extremes in what God has permitted or forbidden, by permitting what is forbidden and forbidding what is permissible. Rather, He loves to permit what He has permitted and forbid what He has forbidden, and that is the justice that He has commanded.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these ignorant Arabs who strip naked when they circumambulate the House, and forbid themselves the good provisions that have been made lawful for them: Who has forbidden, O people, for you the adornment of God that He created for His servants, that you adorn yourself with it and beautify yourself with its clothing, and the lawful provisions of God that He has provided for His creation for their food and drink.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of good provisions, after their consensus that the adornment is what we said.
Some of them said: good provisions in this context are meat. This is because they did not eat it while in a state of ihram.
Who said that among them:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” It is the fat.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Say, ‘Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?’ that which they forbade for themselves. He said: When they performed Hajj or Umrah, they forbade themselves the sheep and what came out of it.

c: Yunus told me
m: about it another time. He said, Ibn Wahb told us. He said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Say, ‘Who has forbidden the adornment of God?’ to the end of the verse. He said: There were people who forbade what came out of the sheep, its milk, its fat, and its meat. So God said, Say, ‘Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?’ He said: And the adornment is clothing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: When God sent Muhammad and said: This is a prophet, this is my best, follow his example, take his ways and his path, the doors were not closed to him, the barriers were not erected in front of him, he did not bring him bowls in the morning, nor did he bring them back to him. He used to sit on the ground, eat his food on the ground, lick his hand, wear coarse clothing, ride a donkey, and ride behind him. He used to say: Whoever turns away from my way is not of me. Al-Hasan said: How many are those who turn away from his Sunnah and abandon it. Then there are the wicked, usurious and corrupt ones, whom my Lord has deemed foolish and hated. They claim that there is nothing wrong with what they eat and drink and decorate these houses with. They interpret this verse: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” But that was only made for the allies of Satan. He made it a plaything for his stomach and his private parts, from words that Sufyan did not memorize.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that what the pre-Islamic era prohibited of lakes and wild animals.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” This is what the people of ignorance forbade them from their wealth: the bahīrah. And the loose, and the connection, and the welding.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” He said: The people of ignorance used to forbid things that God had permitted, such as clothing and other things, and this is the saying of God: “Say: Have you considered what God has sent down for you of provision, then you made of it lawful and unlawful?” This is what this is, so God revealed: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?”

x: God the Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those to whom I commanded you to say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision? since they were unable to answer and did not know how to answer you: The adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision are for those who believed in God and His Messenger and followed what was revealed to you from your Lord in this world. And those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger and disobeyed the command of their Lord have shared that with them in it. And it is for those who believed in God and His Messenger exclusively on the Day of Resurrection. No one who disbelieved in God and His Messenger and disobeyed the command of his Lord will share that with them on that Day.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Say, ‘It is for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: The Muslims shared with the infidels in the good things, so they ate from its good food, wore from its best clothes, and married from its best women, and they were exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muthanna told me
m: about it again with this same chain of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world,” meaning: Muslims share with polytheists the good things in the life of this world, then God will make the good things in the Hereafter exclusive for those who believe, and the polytheists will have nothing in them.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision? Say: They are for those who believe in worldly life and exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.” He says: Say: They are exclusively for those who believe in Me in this world in the Hereafter, and no one will share them in it in the Hereafter. That is because adornment in this world is for all the children of Adam, so He made them exclusively for His friends in the Hereafter.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Say, ‘It is for those who believe in the life of this world, and exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: The Jews and Christians share it with you in this world, and it is exclusively for those who believe on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: Say, ‘It is for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.’ It is exclusively for the believers in the Hereafter, and the infidels will not share it with them. As for the life of this world, they have shared it with them.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.” Whoever acts according to faith in this world, God’s honor will be exclusively for him on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever abandons faith in this world will come before his Lord with no excuse.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “Say: It is for those who believed in the worldly life,” the polytheists share in it with them, pure on the Day of Resurrection, for those who believed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision? Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world and exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection,” meaning: The polytheists share with the believers in the world in clothing, food, and drink, but on the Day of Resurrection the clothing, food, and drink will be exclusively for the believers, and the polytheists will have no share in any of that.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: The world is enjoyed by both the believer and the unbeliever, and the good of the Hereafter is reserved for the believers, and the unbeliever has no share in it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Say, ‘It is for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: This is on the Day of Resurrection for those who believe. The people of disbelief will not share it with them, and they will share it with them in this world. And when it is the Day of Resurrection, they will have neither little nor much in it. Saeed bin Jubair said about this:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said,
m: Ismail bin Abaan and Habawayh al-Razi, may God be pleased with them, told us, on the authority of Ya’qub al-Qummi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Say, ‘It is for those who believe in the life of this world, exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: They benefit from it in this world, and its sin will not follow them. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: pure.

x: Some of the readers of Medina read it as: Khalasa, in the nominative case, meaning: Say, it is pure for those who believe. The rest of the readers of the regions read it as Khalasa, in the accusative case as a state of for them. It was omitted from the speech, being satisfied with the apparent meaning of it, as I have described in the interpretation of the speech that the meaning of the speech is: Say, it is for those who believe in the life of this world shared, and it is for them Surat al-A’raf 7:32 Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?" Say, "They are for those who believe in worldly life and exclusively on the Day of Resurrection." Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know. exclusively in the Hereafter. And whoever said that in the accusative case made the predicate of it in his statement: for those who believe.

The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of those who read it in the accusative case, because the Arabs prefer the accusative case for the verb if it comes after the noun or adjective, even though the nominative case is permissible, but that is more common in their speech.

God Almighty says: Just as I have explained to you what is obligatory upon you in terms of clothing and adornment, and what is permissible and what is forbidden in terms of food and drink, and I have distinguished between that for you, O people, thus I explain all of My proofs and arguments, and the signs of what is permissible and forbidden and My rulings, for a people who know what is explained to them and understand what is distinguished for them.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: pure.
Some of the readers of Medina read it as: Khalasa, in the nominative case, meaning: Say, it is pure for those who believe.
The rest of the readers of the regions read it as Khalasa, in the accusative case as a state of for them.

Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of those who read it in the accusative case, because the Arabs prefer the accusative case for the verb if it comes after the noun or adjective, even though the nominative case is permissible, but that is more common in their speech.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who strip off their clothes to circumambulate the House, and forbid eating the good things that God has made lawful for them from His provision: O people, God has not forbidden what you forbid, rather He has made it lawful for His believing servants and made it good for them. My Lord has only forbidden the ugly things, which are the obscenities, “what is apparent of them,” so it is public, and what is hidden, of them so it is secret and hidden.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding this matter: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told me, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said: I heard Mujahid say regarding His statement:
h
What is apparent of it and what is hidden

, he said: What is apparent of it is the circumambulation of the people of ignorance naked, and what is hidden is adultery. I mentioned the difference of opinion among the interpreters of this narration in the past, so I hated to repeat it. As for sin, it is disobedience, and transgression is being arrogant toward people. God Almighty says: My Lord has only forbidden immoralities along with sin and aggression against people. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Sin and transgression. As for sin, it is disobedience, and transgression is to transgress against people by transgressing against the truth.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid regarding his statement: What is apparent of it and what is concealed, and sin and oppression, he said: He forbade sin, which is all transgressions, and he informed us that the oppressor’s oppression is against himself.

x: God Almighty says: My Lord has only forbidden indecencies and associating partners with Him, that you worship with God a god other than Him, for which He has not sent down authority, meaning: Your Lord has forbidden you to associate partners with Him in His worship for something for which He has not given you any proof or evidence for associating partners with Him in His worship - and He is the authority - and that you say about God what you do not know, meaning: and that you say that God has commanded you to strip and undress for the circumambulation of the House, and He has forbidden you to eat these animals that you have forbidden and have slaughtered and made into camels and herds, and other than that which you do not know that God has forbidden, or commanded, or permitted, so you attribute to God its prohibition, prohibition, and command, for that is what God has forbidden you, not what you claim that God has forbidden, or you say that God has commanded you to do, out of ignorance of its truth in what you say and attribute to God.

The Almighty says - as a threat to the polytheists about whom the Most High has informed us that when they committed an immorality, they would say: We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it, and as a warning from Him to them for their lying about Him, and for their insistence on associating partners with Him and remaining in their disbelief, and reminding them of what was inflicted on their peers from the nations who were before them -: And for every nation there is a term, meaning: for every group that gathered to deny the Messengers of God, reject their advice, and associate partners with God, while following their Lord’s proofs against them, a term, meaning: a time for the punishments to befall them, and for the punishment to descend upon them for their polytheism, and when their term comes, meaning: when the time that God has set for their destruction comes, and the punishment comes upon them, they will not be. delayed an hour, nor will they be advanced,” meaning: they will not be delayed in remaining in this world, nor will they enjoy life in it beyond the time of their destruction and the time of their annihilation, an hour of the hours of time, nor They advance, he says: And they do not advance with that either beyond the time that God has set for them as a time of destruction.

God Almighty says, informing His creation of what He has prepared for His party and the people of His obedience and faith in Him and His messengers, and what He has prepared for the party of Satan and his allies and the disbelievers in Him and His messengers: O children of Adam,
h
if there come to you messengers from among you

, meaning: if there come to you My messengers whom I have sent to you calling you to obey Me and to adhere to My commands and prohibitions, from among you, meaning: from yourselves and from your clans and tribes, reciting to you My verses, meaning: they recite to you the verses of My Book, and they inform you of My proofs and signs of the truth of what they have brought you from Me, and the reality of what they have called you to of My Oneness, then whoever fears God and does righteousness, meaning: whoever among you believes in what My messengers have brought him of what He has narrated to him of My verses and is truthful, and fears God and fears Him by doing what He has commanded him to do and refraining from what He has forbidden him from on the tongue of His Messenger, and does righteousness, meaning: And he corrected his actions that had been corrupted before by the sins of God by turning away from them, there is no fear for them, meaning: there is no fear for them on the Day of Resurrection from God’s punishment when they come to Him, nor will they grieve, for what they missed of their worldly life that they left behind, and their desires that they avoided, following God’s prohibition of them, if they witnessed of God’s honor what they witnessed there.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham Abu Abdullah told us, he said, Hayaj told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Abu Sayyar al-Salami, he said:
m: God placed Adam and his descendants in His hand and said: “O children of Adam,
h
if there come to you messengers from among you

relating to you My verses - then whoever fears God and does righteous deeds - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.” Then He looked at the messengers and said: “O messengers, eat from the good foods and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing. And indeed, this, your community, is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear God.” Then He sent them forth.

x: What is the answer to his statement:
h
If there come to you messengers from among you
The Arab scholars differed on this.
Some of them said: The answer is implied, and is indicated by what is apparent in the speech, which is His statement:
h
So whoever fears God and does good
. This is because when He said:
h
So whoever fears God and does good
, it is as if He said: So obey them.

Others among them said: The answer is: So whoever fears God, because its meaning is: So whoever among you fears God and does good deeds. He said: And what indicates that this is the case is the partiality of the speech. So in the partiality, it was sufficient to mention of you.

God Almighty says: As for he who denied the giving of My messengers which I sent to him, and denied My Oneness, and disbelieved in what My messengers brought, and was too arrogant to believe in My arguments and proofs, those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally, meaning: they will remain in the fire of Hell and will never come out of it.

God Almighty says: Whoever commits a mistake in action, speaks ignorantly, and goes farthest from the truth and the right path, from among those who invent a lie against God, meaning: from among those who invent falsehood about God, and say when they commit an immorality: God has commanded us to do it, or deny His signs, meaning: or deny His proofs and signs indicating His Oneness and the prophethood of His prophets, and deny their truth and reject their validity, those, meaning: whoever does that, invents a lie against God and denies His signs,
h
those will receive their share of the Book

, meaning: their share of what God has written for them in the Preserved Tablet will reach them. Then the people of interpretation differed about the description of that share that they have in the Book, and what it is?
Some of them said: It is the punishment of God prepared for the people who disbelieve in Him.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Marwan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: his saying:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, meaning: of the punishment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
. He said: What was written for them of punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Katheer bin Ziyad, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: of the punishment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Abu Sahl, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: From the torment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: From the torment.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Those will receive their share of what preceded them of misery and happiness.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: of misery and happiness.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, like Shaqi and Saʿid.

c: Wasil bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amr Al-Faqimi, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: It is what came before.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, what was written for them of misery and happiness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They will receive their share of the Book, what was written for them of misery and happiness, like miserable and happy. He said: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, of misery and happiness.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr and Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Amr, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: What has already been mentioned of the Book.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book

, he said: What was previously mentioned for Surat al-A’raf 7:37 So who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God or denies His signs? Those will receive their portion of the Book until, when Our messengers come to them, taking their souls, they will say, "Where are those you used to call upon besides God?" They will say, "They have gone astray from us," and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers. them in the Book. He said, Suwaid bin Amr and Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed: Those will receive their share, he said: of misery and happiness. He said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: What was decreed or predestined for them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: They will receive their share of the Book, they will receive what was written for them of deeds.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Bakr al-Tawil, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: People who do deeds that they must do.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that those will receive their share of their book that was written for them or against them, based on the good and evil deeds that they did in this world.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: their share of deeds, whoever does good will be rewarded for it, and whoever does evil will be rewarded for it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: From the rulings of the Book, according to the extent of their deeds.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: They will receive their share in the Hereafter from the deeds that they did and benefited from.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, meaning: their deeds, the evil deeds that they did and committed in the past.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Muqaddam told me, he said, Al-Mu'tamir told us, he said, my father said:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, Qatada claimed: from the deeds that they did.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, meaning: They will receive their share of deeds. He said: If he does a good deed from that, he will be rewarded with good, and if he does evil, he will be rewarded with the like of it.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They will receive their share of what they were promised in the Book, whether good or evil.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this verse:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: of good and evil. He said: Zaid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: What they were promised.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: what they were promised.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book

, he said: What they were promised in it of good or evil. He said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: They were not promised anything like it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: What they were promised of good or evil.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: what they were promised in it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: What they were promised of good or evil.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amr, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: They will receive what was previously given to them of the Book.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that they will receive their share of the book that God wrote for everyone who slandered Him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, meaning: What has been written for them will be written. He said: It has been written for whoever invents lies about God that his face will be black.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Those will receive their share of what was written for them of sustenance, lifespan, and work.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas:
m: h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, from what was written for them of provision. He said: Ishaq told us, Muhammad bin Harb told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Al-Qurazi:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: his work, his provision, and his lifespan.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book
, he said: of deeds, provisions, and life spans. Then when these are finished, Our messengers will come to them to take their souls, and they will have finished with all of these things.

x: The most correct of these sayings in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book

, from what was written for them of good and evil in this world, and provision, deeds, and life span. That is because God, the Most High, followed that with His statement: Until, when Our messengers come to them, taking them in death, they say, ‘Where are those you used to call upon besides God?’ So He made clear by following that with His statement:
h
Those will receive their share of the Book

, that what will reach them of that is only what was decreed for them in this world to reach them, because He has informed that that will reach them until the time His messengers come to take their souls. If that was their share of the Book, or what was prepared for them in the Hereafter, it would not have been limited to reaching them until the messengers of God come to take their lives, because the messengers of God will not come to them to take their lives in the Hereafter, and their punishment in the Hereafter has no end or ending, for God has decreed that they will remain in it forever.
Thus, it is clear that its meaning is what we have chosen to say about it.
What God, the Most High, meant by His statement,
h
Until when Our messengers come to them

, is until Our messengers come to them. God, the Most High, says: And those who fabricated lies against God, or denied the signs of their Lord, will receive their portions that God had written for them, and that He had previously known for them of provision, work, life span, good and evil in this world, until Our messengers come to them to take their souls. So when Our messengers come to them, meaning the Angel of Death and his soldiers, they will take their souls, meaning they will complete their number from this world to the Hereafter. They will say, ‘Where are those you used to call upon besides God?’ He says: The messengers said: Where are those you used to call upon as allies besides God and worship them? They will not repel from you what has come to you from the command of God, who is your Creator and their Creator, and what has befallen your court of great affliction?

Why will they not help you from the distress you are in and rescue you from it? The wretched ones answered them and said: Our allies whom we used to call upon besides God have gone astray from us. What He means by go astray is that they have gone astray and taken a path other than ours, and they have abandoned us when we needed them, so they did not benefit us. God Almighty says: And the people will bear witness at that time against themselves that they were disbelievers in God and denied His Oneness.

This is report from God, the Most High, about what He will say to these slanderers against Him, who deny His signs on the Day of Resurrection. God, the Most High, says, He will say to them when they come to Him on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Enter, you slanderers against your Lord, who deny His messengers, with groups of your kind, who have passed away before you, meaning: those who have passed away before you, of the jinn and mankind in the Fire, meaning: Enter with nations who are in the Fire, who have passed away before you of the jinn and mankind - and by nations he means the parties and people of the disbelieving religions - Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister, meaning: whenever a group of people from a religion enters the Fire, it curses its sister, meaning: it curses the other group from the people of its religion, disowning it. What is meant by sister is brotherhood in religion and faith.

It was said: her sister, and he did not say: her brother, because he was referring to a nation and another group, as if it was said: whenever a nation enters, it curses another nation from the people of its faith and religion. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister, meaning: whenever the people of a religion enter, they curse their companions of that religion. The polytheists curse the polytheists, the Jews curse the Jews, the Christians curse the Christians, the Sabians curse the Sabians, and the Magians curse the Magians. The latter curses the former.

x: God Almighty says: Until the nations overtake each other in the Fire, meaning they gather in it. It is said: They overtook and they overtook each other, if they gathered. It is said: The first of the people of the disbelieving religions and the last of them gathered in it.

This is report from God, may He be glorified, about the dialogue of the parties of the people of the infidel religions in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. God, may He be glorified, says: “So when the people of the infidel religions gather in the Fire and overtake each other, the people of every religion that entered the Fire - those who were in this world after them, who preceded it and were its predecessors and leaders in misguidance and disbelief - will say to those who were before them in this world: ‘Our Lord, these led us astray from Your path, and called us to the worship of other than You, and made obedience to Satan seem fair to us, so give them today from Your punishment a punishment greater than our punishment,’ as:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “Their last ones said,” those who were at the end of time, to their first ones, those who prescribed that religion for them, Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire. As for His statement,
h
He said to each
, ‘Weak,
h
but you do not know

,’ it is a report from God about His answer to them. He says: God said to those who call upon Him and say, Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire, for all of you, the first of you and the last of you, those who follow you and those who follow you, weak, meaning the punishment is repeated upon him. The weakness of the thing, like it once. Mujahid used to say about this:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: A double punishment from the Fire, he said, For each double, weak.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: God said: For every double, for the first, and for the last double.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, more than one person told me, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: Weak from the fire, he said: Snakes.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: Then give them a double punishment from the Fire, he said: Serpents and vipers. It was said: In Arabic language, the word muddaf means twice as much, and the word mudaddaf means more than that. And His saying:
h
But you do not know

, means: But you, O people of Hell, do not know the extent of the punishment that God has prepared for you, and that is why you ask. The second disbelieving nation is twice as much for its first sister.

x: God Almighty says: And the first of every nation and religion that preceded in this world said to the last of them who came after them, and spoke after their time in it, so they followed their path and followed their way: You had no superiority over us. And you know what happened to us from the punishment of God Almighty for our disobedience to Him and our disbelief in His guidance, after the messengers and warnings came to us and to you. So did you turn to the obedience of God, and deter from your misguidance and error? So the argument of the people was broken and they argued and could not bear an answer by saying: We had superiority over you because we considered you and believed in God and believed in His messengers. God said to all of them: So taste all of you, O disbelievers, the punishment of Hell, for what you used to earn in this world of sins and transgressions, and what you committed of transgressions and crimes.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir told us, he said,
m: I heard Imran, on the authority of Abu Majlaz: And the first of them said to the last of them, ‘You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.’ He said: He says: So what was your superiority over us, and what was done to us was made clear to you, and you were warned?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the first of them said to the last of them, ‘You had no superiority over us.’ So you have gone astray just as we have gone astray. Mujahid used to say about this:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So you had no favor over us, he said: of lightening the punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So you had no favor over us, he said: of alleviation. This statement that we mentioned from Mujahid is a statement that has no meaning. Because the statement of those who said, You had no favor over us, to those who said that, is only a rebuke from them for what they had done before that situation, and this is indicated by my including was in the statement. If that was a rebuke from them for what they said to their Lord: Give them a double punishment from the Fire, then the rebuke would have been to say: So you have no advantage over us in lightening the punishment for you, and you have suffered the same punishment that we have suffered. And it would not have been said: So you have no advantage over us.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who denied Our proofs and evidence, and did not believe in them, and did not follow Our messengers, and were arrogant towards them, meaning: and were arrogant about believing in them and refused to follow them and submit to them out of arrogance,
h
the gates of heaven will not be opened for them

, for their souls when they leave their bodies, “and no word or deed will ascend to God in their life, because their deeds are evil. Rather, only good words and righteous deeds will ascend to Him, as God Almighty said: “To Him ascend good words, and righteous deeds raise it up.” Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement:
h
the gates of heaven will not be opened for them
Some of them said: Its meaning is: the gates of heaven will not be opened for the souls of these disbelievers.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ya’la told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, he said: He meant the infidels by it, that heaven will not be opened for their souls, and will be opened for the souls of Believers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: The heavens are opened for the soul of the believer, but they are not opened for the soul of the unbeliever.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them

. He said: When the soul of a disbeliever is taken, the angels of the earth beat him until he ascends to the heaven. When he reaches the lowest heaven, the angels of the heaven beat him and he descends. The angels of the earth beat him and he ascends. When he reaches the lowest heaven, the angels of the lowest heaven beat him and he descends to the lowest of the earths. And when he is a believer, his soul is breathed into him and the gates of heaven are opened for him. He does not pass by an angel except that he greets him and salutes him, until he reaches God, who gives him his need. Then God says: Return the soul of My servant to the earth, for I created him from dust, and to dust he returns, and from it he emerges.

x: Others said: This means that no good deed or supplication will ascend to God.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, neither their words nor their deeds will ascend.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them -
h
the gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, meaning: nothing of their deeds will ascend to God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, meaning: they will not be opened for the good they do.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, he said: No words or deeds will ascend to them.

c: Matar bin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told us, he said, Abdullah bin Dawud told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, he said: No deeds or supplications will be raised for them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, he said: No deeds or supplications will be raised for them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, he said: No good deed or supplication will be raised for them.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: The gates of heaven will not be opened for their souls or their deeds.
Who said that? Surat al-A’raf 7:40 Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them -
h
the gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, nor will they enter Paradise
h
until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
. And thus do We recompense the criminals.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, he said: for their souls nor for their deeds.

x: We chose in interpreting that what we chose from the statement, because of the generality of the report of God, may He be glorified, that
h
the gates of heaven will not be opened for them

. And He did not specify the report that it will be opened for them in anything, so that is according to what the report of God, may He be glorified, mentioned that it will not be opened for them in anything is general, with the support of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what we said in that, and that is what: Abu Kuraib narrated, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara': The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the taking of the soul of the wicked person and that it ascends with it to heaven. He said: They ascend with it, and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they say: What is this evil soul?

They say: So-and-so, using the worst of the names he was called by in the world, until they reach heaven and ask permission for him, but it is not opened for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited:
h
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, nor will they enter Paradise
h
until a camel passes through the eye of a needle

. Abu Kuraib narrated that Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi'b on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata' on the authority of Sa'id ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: The angels attend the dead. If it is a righteous man, they say: Come out, O good soul, you were in a good body, come out praiseworthy, and receive good tidings of spirit and fragrance, and a Lord who is not angry. They say that until it ascends to the heaven, and it is asked to be opened for it.

It is said: Who is this? They say: So-and-so. It is said: Welcome to the good soul, you were in a good body, enter praiseworthy, and receive good tidings of spirit and fragrance, and a Lord who is not angry. It is said that to it until it reaches the heaven in which God is. If it is a bad man, they say: Come out, O evil soul, you were in an evil body, come out blameworthy, and receive good tidings of boiling water and pus, and other like-minded spouses. They say that until it comes out. Then it ascends to the heaven, and it is asked to be opened for it. It is said: Who is this? They say: So-and-so. They say: No welcome to the evil soul that was in the evil body. Go back, reprehensible, for the gates of heaven were not opened for you. So you are sent between heaven and earth, and you go to the grave.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told me, he said, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, he said, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. The readings differed in this. The majority of the Kufans read it: La yiftahu lahum abwab al-sama’, with a ya’ from yiftahu, and a light ta’ from it, meaning: All of them will not be opened to them at once and with one opening.

x: Some of the Medinans and some of the Kufians read it: La yiftahu, with a ta’ and a shaddah on the second ta’, meaning: No door will be opened to them after door, and one thing after another.

“The correct thing to say in this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings. This is because the souls of the infidels will not have the doors of heaven opened for them or for their evil deeds at once, nor one time after another, and one door after another.” So both meanings are correct. The same applies to the ya’ and the ta’ in yiftahu and tuftah, because the ya’ is based on the action of the one for monotheism, and the ta’ is because the doors are a group, so it is reported by the report of the group.

God Almighty says: And those who denied Our signs and were arrogant towards them will never enter Paradise, which God has prepared for His believing friends, just as a camel will never pass through the eye of a needle, which is the eye of a needle. Every hole in the eye, nose, or other, the Arabs call it poison and pluralize it as poisons. As-Samām, the plural of poison, is more famous and more eloquent than as-Sumūm. It is more eloquent in the plural of as-Sam, which means hole. Both are widespread among the Arabs. One of the poisons, which are holes, is called sam and sam, with the seen open or closed. From the sam that means the saying of al-Farazdaq: So I relieved him of his thirst until he was breathing and I said to him: Do not fear anything behind him. I mean, pierce his nose. As for the tailor, he is the stitch, which is the needle. It was said: tailor and stitched, just as it was said: mask and masked, and zar and mi'zar, and qaram and muqram, and lahaf and lahaf.

As for the reading from all countries, they read his saying: in the eye of the tailor with the opening of the seen, and they agreed on reading: the camel with the opening of the jim, the mim and the lightening of that. As for Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Saeed bin Jubair, it was narrated from them that they used to read it: al-Jamal, with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim, with a difference in that from Saeed and Ibn Abbas. As for those who read it with the opening of the two letters and the alleviation, they directed its interpretation to the well-known camel, and thus they interpreted it.
Who said that?

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told us, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, he said: The camel is the son of the female camel, or: the husband of the female camel.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, he said: The camel is the female camel’s husband.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mugheera, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: The camel is the female camel’s husband.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Qara told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Hasan say: The camel is the one who stands in the pasture.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Until a camel enters the eye of a needle, he said: Until a camel enters the eye of a needle.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibad bin Rashid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It is the camel! When they asked him a lot, he said: It is Al-Ashtar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Rashid, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Yahya, who said:
m: Al-Hasan used to recite it:
h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
. He said: So some of them went to ask him, and he said: Buy, buy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Al-Nu’man A’rim told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Shu’ayb bin Al-Habhab, on the authority of Abu Al-A’aliyah:
m: Until the camel enters, he said: The camel that has four legs.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin - or:
m: Hasin - on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding his statement:
h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, he said: The female camel’s husband, meaning the male camel.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: that he used to read: The camel, which is the one with four legs.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Ubaid, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Until the camel enters, meaning the one with four legs.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Qura, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Until the camel enters, he said: the one in Al-Marbad.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Masoud:
m: that he used to recite: Until the yellow camel passes.

c: Nasr bin Ali told us, Yahya bin Saleem told us, Abdul Karim bin Abi Al-Mukhariq told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle

, he said: The camel is the son of the she-camel, or: the husband of the she-camel. As for those who disagreed with this reading, they differed. Two narrations were narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this: One of them agrees with this reading and this interpretation. They mentioned the narration about him:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, and the camel has legs. He said that Ibn Masoud said that.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle

, meaning a huge camel, but it does not pass through the eye of a needle, because it is bigger than it. The other story is: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Until the ship’s rudder enters the tailor’s rudder
, he said: It is the rudder of the ship.

c: Abdul A’la bin Wasil told me, he said, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Wasiti, on the authority of Hanzala Al-Sadusi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he used to recite: Until a camel enters through the thread of a needle, meaning a thick rope. So I mentioned that to Al-Hasan, and he said: Until a camel enters, Abdul A’la said: Abu Ghassan said: Khalid said: meaning the camel.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he read: the camel, heavily laden, and he said: it is the rope of the ship.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us,
m: on the Surat al-A’raf 7:40 Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them -
h
the gates of heaven will not be opened for them
, nor will they enter Paradise
h
until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
. And thus do We recompense the criminals. authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mugheerah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The camel is the ropes of ships.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Ibn Mubarak, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, he said: the thick rope.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle

. He said: It is the rope that is on the ship. There is also a difference of opinion regarding this from Saeed bin Jubair, as two narrations were narrated from him: One of them is like the one we mentioned from Ibn Abbas: with a damma on the jim and a heavy mim. He mentioned the narration about it:

c: Imran bin Musa Al-Qazzaz told us, he said: Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us, he said: Hussain Al-Mu’allim told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: that he recited it until the camel entered, meaning the ships’ ropes, meaning: the thick ropes. The other one is with a damma on the jim and a light mim. He mentioned the narration about it:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Amr told us, on the authority of Salim bin Ajlan Al-Aftas, who said,
m: I read to my father: Until the camel enters, so he said: Until the camel enters lightly, meaning the rope of the ship. This is how Saeed bin Jubair taught it to me. As for Ikrimah, he used to read it: The camel, with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim, and he interpreted it as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Isa bin Ubaid, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah read: the camel, heavily laden, and he said: it is the rope by which one ascends the palm trees.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Kaab bin Farukh told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, he said: The thick rope through the hole of a needle.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, he said: The rope of a ship passes through the eye of a needle.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abdullah bin Katheer said:
m: I heard Mujahid say: The rope is from the ropes of ships. It is as if the one who reads it with a light mīm and a damma on the jīm, as we mentioned from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the example of Ḍard and Ḍa’l, directed it to the collection of a group of ropes gathered together in a sentence, just as darkness is gathered together in darkness, and ruin is gathered together in ruins. Some Arab scholars used to reject the emphasis on the letter mim and say: The narrator intended the sentence to be pronounced with a light emphasis, but that was not understood from him, so he stressed it. Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of Al-Kisa’i that he said: The one who narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas was a foreigner. As for the one who stressed the meem and closed the jim, his explanation is that it is one name, which is the rope, or the thick thread.

x: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the regions read, which is: until the camel passes through the eye of the needle, with the jim and mim of camel open and the mim closed, and the seen of the noun open, because this is the widespread reading in the regions’ reading, and it is not permissible to contradict what the agreed-upon proof has brought regarding the reading. The same applies to the opening of the letter seen in his saying: the eye of the tailor. Since this is the correct reading, the interpretation of the statement is: They will not enter Paradise until they enter. And entering is entering, from their saying: So-and-so entered the house, meaning he entered, the camel entered the eye of a needle, which is its hole. And thus do We reward the criminals, meaning: And thus do We reward those who committed crimes in this world, for which they deserved painful punishment from God in the Hereafter.
And like what we said in the interpretation of his saying: the eye of the needle, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said,
m: Abu Usamah, Ibn Mahdi, and Suwaid Al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Yahya bin Ateeq, he said: I asked Al-Hasan about his saying:
h
Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle
, he said: The eye of a needle.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Kaab bin Farukh told us, he said, Qatada told us on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: In the eye of the needle, he said: the eye of the needle.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: In the eye of the needle, he said: the hole of the needle.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: In the eye of the needle, he says: the hole of the needle.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: In the eye of a needle, he said: In its hole.

evidence.text: The readings differed in this.
The majority of the Kufans read it: La yiftahu lahum abwab al-sama’, with a ya’ from yiftahu, and a light ta’ from it, meaning: All of them will not be opened to them at once and with one opening.
Some of the Medinans and some of the Kufians read it: La yiftahu, with a ta’ and a shaddah on the second ta’, meaning: No door will be opened to them after door, and one thing after another.

As for the reading from all countries, they read his saying: in the eye of the tailor with the opening of the seen, and they agreed on reading: the camel with the opening of the jim, the mim and the lightening of that.

As for Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Saeed bin Jubair, it was narrated from them that they used to read it: al-Jamal, with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim, with a difference in that from Saeed and Ibn Abbas.
As for those who read it with the opening of the two letters and the alleviation, they directed its interpretation to the well-known camel, and thus they interpreted it.
Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Yahya, who said: Al-Hasan used to recite it: Until a camel passes through the eye of a needle.
As for those who disagreed with this reading, they differed.
Two narrations were narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this: One of them agrees with this reading and this interpretation.

Imran bin Musa Al-Qazzaz told us, he said: Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us, he said: Hussain Al-Mu’allim told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: that he recited it until the camel entered, meaning the ships’ ropes, meaning: the thick ropes.
As for Ikrimah, he used to read it: The camel, with a damma on the jim and a shaddah on the mim, and he interpreted it as:

It is as if the one who reads it with a light mīm and a damma on the jīm, as we mentioned from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the example of Ḍard and Ḍa’l, directed it to the collection of a group of ropes gathered together in a sentence, just as darkness is gathered together in darkness, and ruin is gathered together in ruins.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the regions read, which is: until the camel passes through the eye of the needle, with the jim and mim of camel open and the mim closed, and the seen of the noun open, because this is the widespread reading in the regions’ reading, and it is not permissible to contradict what the agreed-upon proof has brought regarding the reading.
Since this is the correct reading, the interpretation of the statement is: They will not enter Paradise until they enter.

x: God Almighty says: For those who denied Our signs and were arrogant towards them, a bed of Hell. It is what they used to sit and lie on, such as a mattress that is spread out, or a rug that is spread out. And above them is a covering. It is the plural of ghashiyah, which is what covered them and covered them from above them. The meaning of the statement is: They will have beds of Hell, beneath them are palm fronds, and above them are blankets of it, and they are between that. And the people of interpretation said something similar.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b:
m: For them is a bed of Hellfire, he said: the mattress, and above them is covering, he said: the blankets.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: For them are beds of Hell and over them are coverings. He said: The bed is the mattress, and the coverings are the blankets.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: For them are beds of Hell and over them are coverings. As for the bed, it is like a bed, and the coverings are covering them from above them. As for his saying:
h
And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers

, he is saying: And thus do We reward and recompense the one who wronged himself, and brought upon himself the wrath of God that he could not bear, by his disbelief in his Lord and his denial of His prophets.

x: God Almighty says: And those who believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged what he brought them of God’s revelation and His sending down and the laws of His religion, and did what God commanded them to do and obeyed Him, and avoided what He forbade them from, We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, meaning: We do not charge a soul with more than it can handle, so it does not feel embarrassed by it. Those, meaning: those who believed and did righteous deeds, are the companions of Paradise, meaning: they are the people of Paradise who are its people, not others who disbelieved in God and committed their evil deeds. They will abide therein eternally, meaning: they will remain in Paradise, their abode will be permanent, they will not leave it, nor will they be deprived of its delights.

God Almighty says: We have removed from the hearts of those whose characteristics He described, and informed us that they are the people of Paradise, whatever rancor, resentment, and enmity there was between some of them in this world toward others. So He has placed them in Paradise when He brings them into it on couches facing each other, not envying each other for anything that God has given to some of them and favored them with from His honor over them, and the rivers of Paradise will flow beneath them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, he said: enmity.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, he said: It is the hatred.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Isra’il Abu Musa, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: By God, it was revealed about us, the people of Badr: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] they will be brothers, on thrones facing each other.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Israel, he said:
m: I heard him say: Ali, peace be upon him, said: By God, it was revealed about us, the people of Badr: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [while] they will be brothers, on thrones facing each other.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said,
m: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: I hope that I, Uthman, Talhah, and al-Zubayr will be among those about whom God Almighty said: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, may God be pleased with them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, and rivers will flow beneath them. He said: When the people of Paradise are driven to Paradise and arrive, they will find at its gate a tree at the base of whose trunk are two springs. They will drink from one of them, and whatever is in their breasts of resentment will be removed, and it will be the pure drink. They will wash themselves from the other, and the freshness of bliss will flow upon them, and they will never be disheveled or dirty after that.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, who said:
m: The people of Paradise will be detained from Paradise until judgment is passed for some of them from others, until they enter Paradise when they enter it and none of them will seek revenge for a nail clipping that they wronged him. And the people of Hell will be detained from Hell until judgment is passed for some of them from others, so they will enter Hell when they enter it and none of them will seek revenge for a nail clipping that they wronged him.
