x: God Almighty says: And those whom He, the Most High, described, and they are those who believed and did righteous deeds, said when they entered Paradise and saw what God had honored them with of His honor, and what He had averted from them of the humiliating punishment with which the people of Hell were afflicted because of their disbelief in their Lord and their denial of His Messengers: Praise be to God who has guided us to this, meaning: Praise be to God who has guided us to the work that has earned us this honor and grace of God that we are in, and has averted His punishment from us.
And we would not have been guided had God not guided us, meaning: We would not have been guided to this had God not guided us to it and granted us success with it by His grace and bounty, as:

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone in Hell will see his place in Paradise and say, ‘If only God had guided us.’ That will be a regret for them. And every person in Paradise will see his place in Hell and say, ‘If only God had guided us!’ That is their gratitude.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, Shuʿbah narrated, I heard Abu Ishaq narrating, on the authority of ʿAsim ibn Damrah, on the authority of ʿAli, who said: ʿUmar mentioned - for something I do not remember - then he mentioned Paradise and said: They will enter, and there will be a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs will emerge. He said: They will wash from one of them, and the freshness of bliss will flow over them, and their hair will not be disheveled, nor will their skins be covered with dust. And they will drink from the other, and every impurity, filth, and evil in their bellies will come out. He said: Then the gate of Paradise will be opened for them, and it will be said to them: “Peace be upon you, you have done well, so enter it to abide therein.” He said: The young boys will meet them, and they will surround them as young boys surround a hot water source when it returns from its absence. Then they will come and give the good report to their wives, and they will call them by their names and the names of their fathers. They will say: Did you see him? He said: Joy will overcome them. He said: They will come until they stand on the threshold of the gate. He said: They will come and enter, and behold, the foundations of their houses are of pearls, and there are towers of yellow, green, and red, and of every color, and sparks raised high, and cups placed, and cushions lined up, and carpets spread out. Had it not been that God had decreed them for them, their eyes would have dazzled at what they see therein. They will embrace their spouses, and sit on couches, and say: “Praise be to God, who has guided us to this. We would not have been guided had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord have certainly brought the truth.”

x: God Almighty says, informing about those who believed and did righteous deeds, that they will say when they enter Paradise and see the honor that God has bestowed upon them, which is that the enemies of God are in Hell: By God, the messengers of our Lord came to us in this world, and these are the ones in Hell, with the truth of the report about God’s promise to the people of His obedience and belief in Him and His messengers, and His threat to the people of His disobedience and disbelief in Him. As for His statement:
h
And it will be proclaimed to them

, ‘This is Paradise which you have inherited because of what you used to do,’ its meaning is: A caller will call out to those whom God has described and informed about what He has prepared for them of His honor: “O you people, this is Paradise which My messengers in this world used to tell you about. God has made it your inheritance on behalf of those who denied His messengers, because of your belief in them and your obedience to your Lord.”
And that is the meaning of His statement: because of what you used to do. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in the interpretation of that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And it will be proclaimed to them

, ‘This is Paradise which you have inherited because of what you used to do.’ He said: There is no disbeliever or believer but that he has a home in Paradise and Hell. So when the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, and they enter their homes, Paradise will be raised up for the people of Hell so they will look at their homes therein, and it will be said to them, ‘These are your homes if you had acted in obedience to God.’ Then it will be said, ‘O people of Paradise, inherit them because of what you used to do.’ So their homes will be divided among the people of Paradise.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Amr bin Saad Abu Dawud Al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bakir, on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Agharr:
m: h
And it will be proclaimed to them

, ‘This is Paradise which you have inherited because of what you used to do.’ He said: It will be proclaimed to them, ‘Be healthy and do not get sick, live forever and do not die, and enjoy life and do not grieve.’

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Agharr, on the authority of Abu Saeed:
m: h
And it will be proclaimed to them
, ‘This is Paradise,’ the verse. He said: A caller will call out: You will be healthy and never fall ill again. The Arab scholars differed regarding an that comes with talkum.

x: Some of the Basrans said: It is the heavy one, which was lightened and implied in it, and it is not right to make it the light one, because after it is a noun, and the light one is not followed by nouns.

i: The poet said:
x: In the youths of India, like the swords of India, they have learned that whoever is barefoot and wears shoes will perish.

Another said: I am angry with him, and I know that we are both keen on what hurts the other. He said: Its meaning is: It is both of us. He said: It would be like his saying: That we have found, in the place of which? and his saying: That you stand up, and it is not that that works with verbs, because you say: It angered me that he stood up, and that he went away, so it falls on verbs, even though it does not work with them. And in the Book of God: And the leaders among them set out, saying, ‘Walk,’ meaning: Walk.

Some of the people of Kufa denied this statement of his, saying: It is not permissible for there to be an Surat al-A’raf 7:43 And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, and rivers will flow beneath them, and they will say, "Praise be to God, who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord have certainly come with the truth,
h
and it will be proclaimed to them

, 'This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.' implied ha’ with an in this position, because an entered into the speech to protect what comes after it. He said: And this which is with talakum is the circle in which what is similar to the narration occurs, but is not in the wording of the narration, such as: I called out that you are standing, and that Zaid is standing, and that I stood, so it follows all the speech, and I made an as a protection, because the call occurs on what comes after it, and what comes after an is preserved just as what comes after the statement is preserved.

Do you not see that you say: I said: Zaid is standing, and I said: He stood, so you follow it with whatever speech you want? So since the call has the meaning of suspicion and what is similar to it from speech, what comes after an was preserved, and an entered as a protection. He said: As for ay, it is not on an, ay is not the answer to the statement, and an is sufficient from the name.

God Almighty says: And the people of Paradise will call out to the people of Hell after they have entered it: O people of Hell, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true in this world on the tongues of His messengers, of reward for believing in Him and in them, and for obeying Him. So have you found what your Lord promised on their tongues for disbelief in Him and for disobeying Him of punishment?
So the people of Hell will answer them: Yes, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true, such as that which:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire

, ‘We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?’ They will say, ‘Yes.’” He said: The people of Paradise will find what they were promised of reward, and the people of the Fire will find what they were promised of punishment.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “
h
And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire

, ‘We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?’” That is because God promised the people of Paradise bliss and honor and every good thing that people know or do not know, and He promised the people of the Fire every disgrace and torment that people know or do not know. That is why He said: And other like him [are] pairs. He said: So the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, ‘We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘From disgrace, humiliation, and torment.’ The people of Paradise will say: ‘We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true of bliss and honor.’ Then a crier will proclaim among them: ‘The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.’” There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
They said yes
. The majority of the people of Medina, Kufa and Basra read it as:
h
They said yes
, with the opening of the ‘ayn in yes.

c: It was narrated on the authority of some of the Kufians
m: that he read
h
they said yes
with a kasra on the ‘ayn. He recited a verse by Banu Kalb: Yes, if he says it, it is a sure thing and you will not be disappointed. Yes, I broke it.

x: The most correct reading in our view is Naʿam with the fat-ha on the ʿayn, because it is the widespread reading in the readings of the regions and the well-known language of the Arabs. As for his statement: Then a crier called out among them, he says: A crier called out, and he informed, so he informed among them, that the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers, he says: God’s wrath, anger, and punishment are upon those who disbelieve in Him. We have already explained that if a word accompanies a narration that is similar to a narrative, but not explicitly a narration, the Arabs sometimes stress it, and apply the verb to it, opening it and sometimes lightening it, and working the verb in it, making it accusative with it, and nullifying its work on the noun that follows it, in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. Since this is the case, whether you stress an or not in the recitation, since the meaning of the speech is whichever of these the reciter recites is the same, and they are two well-known recitations in the recitation of the regions.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: They said yes.
The majority of the people of Medina, Kufa and Basra read it as: They said yes, with the opening of the ‘ayn in yes.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct reading in our view is Naʿam with the fat-ha on the ʿayn, because it is the widespread reading in the readings of the regions and the well-known language of the Arabs.

Since this is the case, whether you stress an or not in the recitation, since the meaning of the speech is whichever of these the reciter recites is the same, and they are two well-known recitations in the recitation of the regions.

x: God Almighty says: The muezzin between the people of Paradise and Hell says: The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers, those who disbelieved in God and turned people away from His path, and seek to make it crooked, meaning: they tried to change and alter the path of God - which is His religion - from what God made for it of straightness, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, meaning: and they deny the establishment of the Hour and the resurrection in the Hereafter and the reward and punishment therein. The Arabs say about deviating in religion and the path, ‘awj, with a kasra on the ‘ayn.

i: And about a man’s inclination towards something and his affection for it: ‘ajj ilahi yu’ujju ‘ayjan, wawj, wawj, with a kasra on the ‘ayn and a fatha, as the poet said:
x: Stop, let us ask about the homes of the Layla family, despite their crookedness and bending towards them.
Al-Farra’ mentioned that Abu al-Jarrah recited it to him with a kasra on the ‘ayn from ‘awja. As for what is a natural creation of man, it is said of it: his leg is crooked, with a fatha on the ‘ayn.

evidence.text: Al-Farra’ mentioned that Abu al-Jarrah recited it to him with a kasra on the ‘ayn from ‘awja.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
And between them is a veil

, is that between Paradise and Hell there is a veil. He says: a barrier, and it is the wall that God Almighty mentioned when He said: And a wall was placed between them with a gate, within which is mercy, but outside of it is punishment. It is Al-Aʿraf about which God says:
h
And on the heights are men
, likewise.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: It was reported to me on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Al-A’raf is a veil between Heaven and Hell.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And between them is a veil
, which is the wall, which is Al-A’raf. As for his saying:
h
And on the heights are men

, “the heights” is a plural, the singular of which is arf, and every elevated part of the ground among the Arabs is a arf. The rooster’s crest is called arf because of its elevation above the rest of its body. From this is the saying of Al-Shamakh bin Dirar: And she remained with exaggerated customs, as if they were spears that the wind had blown away. He means by his saying: With heights, with the heights of the earth, and from this is the saying of the other: Every treasure of meat is like a flag of the Mukhi on the customs Al-Suddi used to say: Al-A’raf was called A’raf because its people knew the people.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me that, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi.
m: And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abi Yazid,
m: he heard Ibn Abbas say: Al-A’raf is the elevated thing.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abi Yazid, he said,
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say, the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Al-A’raf is a surah like a rooster’s comb.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Al-A’raf is a veil between Paradise and Hell, a wall with a door. Abu Musa said: Ubayd God ibn Abi Yazid told me that he heard Ibn Abbas say: Al-A’raf is a hill between Paradise and Hell, on which some sinners were detained between Paradise and Hell.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Al-A’raf is a veil between Heaven and Hell, a wall with a door.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Al-A’raf is a wall between Heaven and Hell.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Al-A’raf is a wall between Heaven and Hell.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And on the heights are men
, he means by the heights: the wall that God mentioned in the Qur’an, and it is between Paradise and Hell.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Al-A’raf is a wall with a crest like a rooster’s crest.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us,
m: on the Surat al-A’raf 7:46
h
And between them is a veil
h
and on the heights are men who recognize everyone by their mark

, and they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not yet entered it, while they are still hoping. authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, who said: Al-A’raf is a wall between Heaven and Hell.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told me: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Al-A’raf is the wall between Heaven and Hell.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the men whom God Almighty said were on the heights, and what was the reason for which they were there?

Some of them said: They are a people from the children of Adam, whose good and bad deeds are equal, so they are left there until God decides what He wills regarding them, then He admits them into Paradise by virtue of His mercy towards them.

Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated, Yahya ibn Wadh narrated, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated, Al-Sha’bi said: ‘Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman sent for me, and with him was Abu al-Zinad ‘Abdullah ibn Dhakwan, a freed slave of Quraysh. They mentioned a mention of the people of A’raf that was not as they had mentioned. So I said to them: If you slander me, I will tell you what Hudhayfah mentioned. They said: Bring it. So I said: Hudhayfah mentioned the people of A’raf and said: They are people whose good deeds have made them exceed the Fire, and whose bad deeds have kept them short of Paradise. So when their sight is turned toward the people of the Fire, they say: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people. While they were like that, your Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, looked at them and said: Go and enter Paradise, for I have forgiven you.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, on the authority of Hudhayfah,
m: that he was asked about the people of A’raf, and he said: They are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so their bad deeds kept them from entering Paradise, and their good deeds kept them from entering Hell. He said: So they stood there on the wall until God judged concerning them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, saying: Jarir and Imran ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Husayn, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said:
m: The people of A’raf are people who had sins and good deeds, so their sins kept them from entering Paradise, and their good deeds kept them from entering Hell. They will be like that until God judges between His creation and carries out His command concerning them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so He says: Enter Paradise by My grace and forgiveness. There is no fear for you today, nor shall you grieve.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf are people whose good deeds keep them from Hellfire, and whose bad deeds keep them from Paradise.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, who said:
m: Saeed bin Jubair said, while he was narrating that on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: People will be held to account on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever’s good deeds outnumber his bad deeds by one will enter Paradise, and whoever’s bad deeds outnumber his good deeds by one will enter Hell. Then he recited the words of God: But those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful ones. “And those whose scales are light - it is they who will lose themselves.” Then he said: The scale will be lightened by the weight of a grain and will tip the scales. He said: So whoever's good deeds and bad deeds are equal will be among the people of A'raf. They will stand on the Sirat, then they will recognize the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. When they look at the people of Paradise, they will call out: "Peace be upon you." And when they turn their eyes to their left, they will look at the people of Hell and say: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people. So they will seek refuge with God from their homes. He said: As for the people of good deeds, they will be given a light with which they will walk in front of them and on their right, and every servant will be given a light on that Day, and every nation will be given a light. So when they come to the Sirat, God will take away the light of every hypocrite, male and female. So when the people of Paradise saw what the hypocrites had endured, they will say: Our Lord, perfect our light for us. As for the people of A'raf, the light was in their hands and was not taken away from them. Then God says:
h
They did not enter it while they were hoping

, so hope was an entry. He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: If a servant does a good deed, ten will be written for him, and if he does a bad deed, only one will be written for him. Then he says: He is destroyed who overcomes his tenths alone.

c: Abu Hammam Al-Walid bin Shuja’ told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told me, he said, Isa Al-Hannat told me, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf are people who had deeds by which God saved them from the Fire, and they are the last to enter Paradise. They have known the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so their good deeds do not exceed their bad deeds, nor do their bad deeds exceed their good deeds.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Al-A’raf is a wall between Paradise and Hell, and the people of Al-A’raf are in that place, until when it appears to God to heal them, He takes them to a river called Al-Hayat, its banks are reeds of gold, lined with pearls, and its soil is musk. They throw themselves into it until their colors improve, and a white mole appears on their throats by which they are recognized. When their colors improve, the Most Merciful brings them and says: Wish for whatever you wish. He says, So they wish, until their wish is fulfilled. He says to them: For you is what you wished for, and seventy times the same. Then they enter Paradise with a white mole on their throats by which they are recognized. They are called the poor of Paradise.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, he said:
m: The companions of al-A’raf will be ordered to a river called al-Hayat, its soil is turf and saffron, and its banks are pearl reeds. He said: And I think he said: Crowned with pearls. He said: They will wash in it, and a white mole will appear on their throats. It will be said to them: Make a wish. It will be said to them: You will have what you wished for and seventy banks. And they are the poor people of Paradise. Habib said: A man told me: Their good deeds and bad deeds were equal. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, my father narrated, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, who said: The companions of al-A’raf will be taken to a river called al-Hayat, its banks being reeds of gold. Sufyan said: I think he said: Crowned with pearls. He said: They will wash themselves in it and a white mole will appear on their necks. Then they will return and wash themselves, and their whiteness will increase. Every time they wash themselves, their whiteness will increase. It will be said to them: Wish for whatever you wish, and they will wish for whatever they wish. It will be said to them: You will have whatever you wish for and seventy times over. He said: They are the poor people of Paradise.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said:
m: The people of al-A’raf are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so they are on a wall between Paradise and Hell: They will not enter it while they are hoping.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say: Al-A’raf is between Paradise and Hell, and some people were detained for it because of their deeds. And he used to say: A people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal, so their good deeds did not exceed their bad deeds, nor their bad deeds exceed their good deeds.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal.

c: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf, their deeds are equal.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so they stood there on the wall.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Sufi’ or: Sami’ - Abu Ja’far said:
m: I found this in the book of Sufi’, on the authority of Abu Alqamah, he said: The people of Al-A’raf are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal.

x: Others said: They were killed in the way of God, disobeying their fathers in this world.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Abu Musa’ar, on the authority of Shurahbil bin Sa’d, who said:
m: They are people who went out on a raid without the permission of their fathers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Khalid told me, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Yahya bin Shibl: That a man from Banu Nadir told him, on the authority of a man from Banu Hilal, that his father told him:
m: He asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the people of Al-A’raf, and he said: They are people who fought in the way of God, disobeying their fathers, and they were killed, so God freed them from the Fire because of their killing in His way, and they were kept from Paradise because of the disobedience of their fathers, so they are the last to enter Paradise.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Yahya bin Shibl,
m: a client of Banu Hashim, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the people of Al-Aʿraf, and he said: They are people who were killed in the way of God due to the disobedience of their fathers, so their killing in the way of God prevented them from the Fire, and the disobedience of their fathers prevented them from entering Paradise.

x: Others said: Rather, they are a righteous people, jurists, and scholars.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf are righteous, knowledgeable, and learned people. Surat al-A’raf 7:46
h
And between them is a veil
h
and on the heights are men who recognize everyone by their mark
, and they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not yet entered it, while they are still hoping.

x: Others said: Rather, they are angels, and not human beings.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: his saying:
h
And between them is a veil
h
and on the heights are men
who recognize each by his mark, he said: They are men from the angels, who recognize the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. He said: “
h
And they will call out to the companions of Paradise

, ‘Peace be upon you,’” until His saying: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people. He said: Then the companions of the heights will call out to men in Hell whom they recognize by their mark: Your multitude and your arrogance have not availed you. “These are the ones about whom you swore that God would not grant them mercy,” he said: So this is when the people of Paradise entered Paradise: “Enter Paradise. There is no fear concerning you, nor shall you grieve.”

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, al-Mu'tamir told us, he said,
m: I heard Imran say: I said to Abu Majlaz: God says:
h
And on the heights are men
, and you claim that they are the angels? He said: They are males, not females.

c: Ibn Wakee' told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: h
And on the heights are men
, he said, men from the angels, they know both groups by their features, the people of Hell and the people of Paradise, and this is before the people of Paradise enter Paradise.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: in a similar manner. And he said, Yahya ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, who said: The companions of Al-A’raf are the angels.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yaʿla bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, he said, Al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: h
And on the heights are men
, he said: They are the angels.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: h
And on the heights are men
, he said: They are the angels. I said: O Abu Majlaz, God Almighty says: Men, and you say: Angels? He said: They are males, not females.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And on the heights are men who recognize all by their mark
, he said: The angels. He said: I said: Does God say: men? He said: The angels are males.

x: The correct thing to say about the people of Al-Aʿraf is to say what God Almighty said about them: They are angels who recognize both the people of Paradise and the people of Hell by their marks. There is no report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whose chain of transmission is sound, nor is there any agreement on its interpretation, nor is there a consensus among the nation that they are angels. If that is the case, and if it is not possible to understand it by analogy, and if it is common knowledge among the people of the Arabic language that men is a name that includes the males of the sons of Adam, not their females and not the rest of creation other than them, then it is clear that what Abu Majlaz said, that they are angels, is a statement that has no meaning, and that the correct statement in that is what the rest of the people of interpretation other than him said.

This is with those who said otherwise from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with what was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that of the reports, even if there is what is in their chains of transmission, and:

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told me, he said, Jarir told me, on the authority of Ammarah bin Al-Qaqa’, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the people of Al-A’raf, so he said: They are the last of the servants to be judged, and when the Lord of the Worlds finishes judging between the servants, He says: You are a people whose good deeds have taken you out of the Fire, but have not brought you into Paradise, and you are My freedmen, so go to Paradise wherever you wish.
b.via: Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir

x: God Almighty says:
h
And on the heights are men

who recognize the people of Paradise by their mark, which is the whiteness of their faces and the freshness of bliss upon them, and they recognize the people of Hell by their mark, which is the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes. So when they see the people of Paradise, they call out to them: “Peace be upon you.” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And on the heights are men who recognize everyone by their mark
, he said: They will recognize the people of Hell by the blackness of their faces, and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And on the heights are men who recognize everyone by their mark

, he said: God has placed them in that position, so that they may know who is in Paradise and who is in Hell, and so that they may know the people of Hell by the blackness of their faces, and they seek refuge with God that He should not place them with the wrongdoing people. And in that, they greet the people of Paradise with peace, they have not entered it, and they hope to enter it, and they will enter it, God willing.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: By their mark, he said: By the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And on the heights are men who will recognize everyone by their mark
, the disbelievers by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes, and the mark of the people of Paradise is their white faces.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the people of Al-A’raf see the people of Paradise, they will recognize them by the whiteness of their faces, and when they see the people of Hell, they will recognize them by the blackness of their faces.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The companions of Al-A’raf are men who had committed great sins, and the final decision of their affair was for God, so they were established in that position. When they looked at the people of Hell, they would recognize them by the blackness of their faces, and they would say, Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people. And when they looked at the people of Paradise, they would recognize them by the whiteness of their faces. That is what His statement means: “
h
And they will call out to the companions of Paradise
, ‘Peace be upon you.’ They have not yet entered it, while they were still yearning.”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak regarding His statement,
h
And on the heights are men who will recognize everyone by their mark

, they claimed that the people of the heights are men of sin, who committed sins and the final decision of their matter was for God, so God placed them on the heights. So when they look at the people of Hell, they will recognize them by the blackness of their faces, so they seek refuge with God from the Hellfire. When they look at the people of Paradise, they call out to them, “Peace be upon you,” God said, They will not enter it while they are yearning. He said, This is the statement of Ibn Abbas.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They will know everyone by their mark, they will know people by their mark, they will know the people of Hell by the blackness of their faces, and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They will recognize each other by their mark
, they will recognize the people of Hell by the blackness of their faces, and the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And on the heights are men who will recognize everyone by their mark
, he said: The people of Paradise will be recognized by their mark, white faces, and the people of Hell will be recognized by their mark, black faces. He said: And His statement,
h
They will recognize everyone by their mark
, he said: The companions of Paradise and the companions of Hell,
h
And they will call out to the companions of Paradise
, he said: When they saw their faces had turned white.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
They will recognize each other by their mark

, he said: by the blackness of their faces. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Yahya bin Yaman narrated, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Bismayahim means the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes. Sima’ is the sign indicating something, in the speech of the Arabs. Its origin is from the sign, its waw, which is the fa of the verb, was moved to the place of the ‘ayn, as one says: idhamal, and imdhahal. He mentioned hearing from some of Banu Uqayl: it is a raw land, meaning a thicket. And from this is their saying: he has prestige among the people, meaning face, its waw was moved to the place of the ‘ayn of the verb. And there are three languages for it: sima, shortened, sima, extended, and sima’a, with the addition of another ya after the mim in it, and its extension, like the example of pride, as the poet said: A young man, God shot him with beauty, as he shot him with a beauty that is not difficult for the eye to see. As for his saying: “
h
And they will call out to the companions of Paradise
, ‘Peace be upon you.’
h
They did not enter it while they were hoping
,” meaning: God’s security from His punishment and painful torment has come upon you.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his statement:
h
They did not enter it while they were hoping

Some of them said: This is report from God about the people of A’raf: that they said to the people of Paradise what they said before the people of A’raf entered, except that they said it while they were hoping to enter it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The people of Al-A’raf know the people, so if they pass by a group that is going to Paradise, they say: “Peace be upon you.” God says to the people of al-A’raf 7:They have not entered it, but they hope to enter it.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Surat al-A’raf 7:
m: h
And between them is a veil
h
and on the heights are men who recognize everyone by their mark
, and they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not yet entered it, while they are still hoping. Muammar, he said, Al-Hasan recited:
h
They did not enter it while they were hoping
, he said: By God, He did not put that hope in their hearts except for an honor that He wanted for them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They did not enter it while they were greedy
, he said: May God inform you of their place of greed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, he said,
m: Saeed bin Jubair said, while he was narrating that on the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: As for the people of the A’raf, the light was in their hands, then it was taken away from their hands. God says:
h
They did not enter it while they were hoping
, he said: To enter it. Ibn Abbas said: So God admitted the people of the A’raf to Paradise.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah and Ata’:
m: They will not enter it, and they are hopeful, they said: To enter it.

x: Others said: What is meant by that is the people of Paradise, and that the people of Al-A’raf will say to them before they enter Paradise: “Peace be upon you,” and the people of Paradise are hopeful to enter it, but they have not entered it yet.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: h
And they will call out to the companions of Paradise

, ‘Peace be upon you.’ They have not yet entered it, and they still hope to do so.” He said: The angels will recognize both groups by their appearance. This will be before the people of Paradise enter Paradise. The companions of al-Aʿraf will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘Peace be upon you.’ They have not yet entered it, and they still hope to do so.

x: God Almighty says: And when the eyes of the companions of the Aʿraf are turned toward the companions of the Fire, meaning: in front of them and their faces, and they look at God’s disfigurement of them, They will say, ‘Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people,’ those who wronged themselves, so they earned from Your wrath what caused them to inherit from Your punishment what they are in.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: And when they passed by them, meaning the people of Al-A’raf, with a group that would be taken to the Fire, they said: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the people of al-A’raf look at the people of Hell and recognize them, they will say: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Makin, on the authority of his brother, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire
, he said: Their faces are turned toward the Fire, and when they see the people of Paradise, that will go away from them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire
, and they see their faces blackened and their eyes blue, They will say, ‘Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.’

x: The Most High says: And the companions of the heights will call out to men, from the people of the earth, whom they will recognize by their mark, the mark of the people of Hell, They will say, ‘What availed you was your accumulation,’ that is, what you used to accumulate of wealth and numbers in this world, and what you used to be arrogant, meaning: and your arrogance with which you used to be arrogant in it, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Then some tyrants passed by them, meaning the people of Al-A’raf, and they recognized them by their appearance. He said, he said: The people of Al-A’raf said: Your multitude and your arrogance did not avail you.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the companions of the heights will call out to men, he said: in the Fire, “who will recognize them by their mark. They will say, ‘Your multitude has not availed you, nor was your arrogance,’” and your arrogance.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: And the companions of the heights will call out to men whom they will recognize by their mark, saying, ‘Your multitude and your arrogance have not availed you.’ He said. This is when the people of Paradise entered Paradise, Are these the ones you swore would not be granted mercy by God? The verse. I said to Abu Majlaz: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: No, but on the authority of someone else.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz:
m: h
And the companions of the A’raf will call out to men whom they will recognize by their mark

, he said: The angels will call out to men in the Fire whom they will recognize by their mark, Your multitude and your arrogance will not avail you. “Are these the ones you swore would not be granted mercy by God?” He said: This is when the people of Paradise entered Paradise, “Enter Paradise. There is no fear concerning you, nor will you grieve.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And the companions of the A’raf will call out to men whom they will recognize by their mark

, the men are the great ones from the people of this world. He said: By this description the people of the A’raf will recognize the people of Paradise from the people of Hell. This is because this is mentioned when the leader of the people of good and the leader of the people of evil go on the Day of Resurrection. He said: And Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement,
h
Your gathering will not avail you
, nor will you be arrogant, he said: Against the people of obedience to God.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the two meanings of these words.
Some of them said: This is what God said to the people of Hell, as a rebuke for what they said in this world to the people of A'raf, when He brought the people of A'raf into Paradise.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The people of Al-A'raf are men who had committed great sins, and their decision was for God. They stand on the heights, and when they look at the people of Paradise, they hope to enter it, and when they look at the people of Hell, they seek refuge with God from it, so they enter Paradise. This is what God the Most High said: Are these the ones you swore that God would not grant them mercy? meaning the people of Al-A'raf. “Enter Paradise. There is no fear concerning you, nor shall you grieve.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: God admitted the people of al-A’raf into Paradise because of His saying,
h
In Paradise there is no fear concerning you
, nor shall you grieve.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: God said to the people of arrogance and wealth: Are these the ones you swore that God would not grant them mercy? meaning the people of Al-A’raf. “Enter Paradise. There is no fear concerning you, nor shall you grieve.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Are these, the weak ones, about whom you swore that God would not bestow mercy upon them? Enter Paradise, no fear will there be concerning you, nor will you grieve. Hudhayfah said: The people of al-A’raf are people whose deeds were equal, so their good deeds were too short for Paradise, and their bad deeds were too short for Hellfire. So they were placed on al-A’raf, and people would be recognized by their marks. So when judgment was passed between the servants, permission was given to seek intercession, so they came to Adam, peace be upon him, and said: O Adam, you are our father, so intercede for us with your Lord. He said: Do you know of anyone whom God created with His hand, and breathed into him of His spirit, and whose mercy preceded His wrath, and to whom the angels prostrated, other than me? They will say: No. He will say: I have not done anything about it; I cannot intercede for you. But go to my son Abraham. They will go to Abraham, peace be upon him, and ask him to intercede for them with his Lord. He will say: Do you know of anyone whom God took as a friend? Do you know of anyone whom his people burned in the fire for the sake of God, other than me? They will say: No. He will say: I have not done anything about it; I cannot intercede for you. But go to my son Moses. They will go to Moses, peace be upon him, and he will say: Do you know of anyone to whom God spoke directly and brought him close in private, other than me? They will say: No. He will say: I have not done anything about it; I cannot intercede for you. But go to Jesus. They will go to him and say: Intercede for us with your Lord. He will say: Do you know of anyone whom God created without a father, other than me? They will say: No. He will say: Do you know of anyone who healed the blind and the leper and raised the dead by God’s permission, other than me? He said: They will say: No. He said: He will say: I am my own intercessor. I have not done anything about it. I cannot intercede for you, but go to Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They will come to me, and I will strike my chest with my hand, then I will say: I am up for it. Then I will walk until I stand before the Throne, and I will praise my Lord, and He will open for me praise the like of which the listeners have never heard before. Then I will prostrate and it will be said to me: O Muhammad, raise your head, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. I will raise my head and say: O Lord, my nation. It will be said: They are for you. Then there will not remain a sent prophet or a close angel except that he will envy me on that day for that station, which is the praised station. He said: Then I will bring them to the gate of Paradise, and I will ask to be opened, and it will be opened for me and for them. Then they will be taken to a river called the River of Life, its banks being reeds of gold crowned with pearls, its soil being musk, and its pebbles being rubies. Then they will wash themselves in it, and the colours of the people of Paradise and the fragrance of the people of Paradise will return to them, and they will become like shining stars, and there will remain on their chests white moles by which they will be known, and it will be said to them: The poor people of Paradise.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: God admitted them after the people of Paradise, and this is His saying: Enter Paradise, no fear shall there be concerning you, nor shall you grieve, meaning the people of Al-A’raf, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas.

x: The interpretation of the speech is based on this interpretation that we mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbas, and from those we mentioned, his saying in it: God said to the people who were too arrogant to acknowledge the Oneness of God, and to submit to His obedience and the obedience of His Messengers, who accumulated wealth in this world out of multiplying and hypocrisy: O tyrants, were they in this world? Were these the weak ones whom you were in this world? Did you swear that God would not grant them mercy? He said: I have forgiven them and have had mercy on them by My grace and mercy. Enter Paradise, O people of Al-ʿAʿraf, with no fear upon you after it of a punishment that you will be punished with for what you have done in this world of sins and crimes, nor will you grieve over anything that has befallen them in your world. Abu Majlaz said: Rather, this statement is report from God about what the angels said to the people of Hell, after they entered Hell, as a reproach from them for what they used to say in this world to the believers whom God will admit into His Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.
As for His statement: Enter Paradise, no fear will there be concerning you, nor will you grieve, it is a report from God about His command to the people of Paradise to enter it.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, he said:
m: The angels called out to men in the Fire whom they would recognize by their appearance: Your gathering and your arrogance have not availed you. “Are these the ones you swore that God would not grant them mercy?” He said: This is when the people of Paradise enter Paradise: Enter Paradise, no fear will there be concerning you, nor will you grieve.

x: This is report from God Almighty about the people of Hell calling for help from the people of Paradise, when a great calamity descends upon them from severe thirst and hunger, as a punishment from God for what they did in the past in this world of abandoning the obedience of God, and paying what was imposed upon them in it from their wealth from the rights of the poor from zakat and charity.
God Almighty says: And the companions of the Fire will call out, after they have entered it, to the companions of Paradise, after they have inhabited it, ‘O people of Paradise,
h
pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you
,’ meaning: feed us from the food that God has provided you, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Pour out upon us some water or from what God has provided you, he said: of food.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you

, he said: They ask them for food and they ask them for rain. The people of Paradise answered them: God has forbidden water and food to those who denied His Oneness and denied His Messengers in this world. The ha and mim in His statement:
h
God has forbidden them refer to water and to what is in His statement
: or from what God has provided for you. And the people of interpretation said something similar.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘
h
Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you

.’ He said: A man will call out to his brother and his father and say, I have been burned, pour some water upon me. It will be said to them, Answer them. They will say, God has forbidden it to the disbelievers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Dukayn told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: “And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: ‘
h
Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you
.’” He said: A man will call out to his brother: O my brother, I have been burned, so help me. He will say: God has forbidden them to the disbelievers.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: They said, ‘Indeed, God has forbidden them both to the disbelievers,’ he said: The food and drink of the people of Paradise.

x: This is report from God about what the people of Paradise said to the disbelievers. God the Almighty says: So the people of Paradise answered the people of Hell: God has forbidden them both to the disbelievers, those who disbelieved in God and His messengers, who took their religion that God commanded them as amusement and play, meaning: mockery and play.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding this: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Those who have taken their religion as amusement and play

, the verse, he said: That is because when they were called to faith, they mocked and ridiculed the one who called them to it, being deceived by God. And the life of this world deceived them, meaning: And the immediate life, ease, and comfort they were in deceived them from taking their share of the Hereafter, until death came to them. God Almighty says:
h
So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs

, meaning on this day, and that is the Day of Resurrection, We will forget them, meaning: We will leave them in manifest torment, hungry and thirsty, without food or drink, just as they abandoned work to meet this Day of theirs, and refused to prepare for it because their bodies were exhausted in obeying God. We have explained the meaning of his saying:
h
We forget them
, with evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So today We will forget them, he said: They were forgotten in the punishment.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So today We will forget them, he said: We will leave them as they left the meeting of this day of theirs.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: We will forget them, he said: We will leave them in the Fire.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs
, he said: We will leave them out of mercy, as they left working for the meeting of this Day of theirs.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs
, he said: God forgot them of the good, but He did not forget them of the evil.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid regarding his statement:
h
So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs

, he said: We will delay them in the Fire. As for his saying: And they did not deny Our signs, its meaning is: Today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs, and as they denied Our signs. So what is in his saying: And they were not is connected to what is in his saying: As they forgot?

x: The interpretation of the statement is: Today we leave them in torment, just as they abandoned work in this world in order to meet God on the Day of Resurrection, and just as they used to deny God’s signs, which are His proofs that He used against them, from the prophets, messengers, books, and other things. They deny, they lie and do not believe in any of that.

God Almighty says: I swear, O Muhammad, that We have brought these infidels a Book, meaning the Qur'an that He revealed to him. He says: We have revealed to them this Qur'an, detailed and clear in it the truth from falsehood, with knowledge, he says: with knowledge from us of the truth of what is in it, from falsehood in which He distinguished between it and the truth, guidance and mercy, he says: We explained it so that a people who believe in it and in what is in it of God's commands and prohibitions, His report, His promise and His threat may be guided and shown mercy, so that He may save them by it from misguidance to guidance. This verse is a response to His statement: A Book revealed to you, so let there not be in your breast any discomfort therefrom, that you may warn thereby and as a reminder to the believers. “We have brought them a Book which We have detailed with knowledge.” Guidance is in the accusative case, as a result of the separation of the ha’ in the word We detailed it. If it were in the accusative case, based on the verb We detailed it, then the meaning would be: We detailed the Book. This would be correct. If it had been read: Guidance and mercy, it would have been eloquent in grammar, and the genitive case would have been in response to the Book.

evidence.text: If it had been read: Guidance and mercy, it would have been eloquent in grammar, and the genitive case would have been in response to the Book.

x: God Almighty says:
h
Do they await anything but its interpretation

? Do these polytheists who deny God’s signs and reject meeting Him await anything but its interpretation? He says: Anything but what their affair will lead to, from their coming to God’s punishment, their burning in His Hellfire, and things similar to this that God has promised them. We have explained the meaning of interpretation previously with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do they await anything but its interpretation
? meaning: its reward,
h
On the Day when its interpretation comes
, meaning: its reward.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Do they await anything but its interpretation
h
The Day its interpretation comes
. He said: Its interpretation is its outcome.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Do they await anything but its interpretation
? He said: Its recompense. On
h
the Day its interpretation comes

? He said: Its recompense. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Yahya ibn Abi Zaydah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi:
h
Do they await anything but its interpretation

? As for its interpretation, it refers to its consequences, such as the Battle of Badr, the Resurrection, and what was promised therein. Al-Muthanna narrated, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Ja’far, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, regarding His statement:
h
Do they await anything but its interpretation
h
The Day its interpretation comes

, those who had forgotten it before will say, ‘The messengers of our Lord had come with the truth.’ One interpretation after another will continue to occur until its interpretation is completed on the Day of Resurrection. It was about this that the verse was revealed:
h
Do they await anything but its interpretation

? where God, the Blessed and Exalted, rewarded His friends and enemies with the reward of their deeds. On that Day, those who had forgotten it before will say, The messengers of our Lord have brought the truth.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do they await anything but its interpretation
h
The Day its interpretation comes
, he said: The Day of Resurrection.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
The Day its interpretation comes

, he said: The Day its reality comes, and he recited the statement of God Almighty: This is the interpretation of my vision of before, he said: This! Its realization. He read the words of God: None knows its interpretation except God, and said: No one knows its reality and when it will come except God Almighty. As for His statement:
h
On the Day when its interpretation comes

, those who forgot it before will say, its meaning is: On the Day when what their affair will come to of God’s punishment comes, those who forgot it before will say, that is, those who neglected and abandoned what they were commanded to do of the work that would save them from what their affair will come to on that Day of punishment, before that in this world, will say, Indeed, the messengers of our Lord came with the truth, the poor people swore when they witnessed the affliction and the punishment befell them: that the messengers of God who came to them with the warning and conveyed to them the message from God had advised them and believed them on behalf of God, and that was when belief would not benefit them, nor would much talk and gossip save them from God’s wrath and painful punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Those who forgot it before said, ‘The messengers of our Lord have come with the truth.’ As for those who forgot it, they abandoned it, and when they saw what their prophets had promised them, they were certain and said, The messengers of our Lord have come with the truth.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Those who forgot him say, he said: They turned away from him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about these polytheists whose characteristics He described, that they say when God’s wrath descends upon them, and they encounter His painful punishment, and they witness the interpretation of what God’s messengers used to find them: Do we have friends and allies today who will intercede for us with our Lord, so that their intercession with Him may save us from the evil that has befallen us because of our actions in this world, or may we be returned to this world once again, so that we may do in it what pleases Him and that He may forgive us for ourselves? The poor people there said this statement, because they had known themselves in this world to have intercessors who would intercede for them in their needs, so they remember that at a time when they have no friendship or intercession. God Almighty and His names sanctified says:
h
They have lost their souls
, meaning: they have cheated themselves of their fortunes by selling what has no value of the eternal bliss of the Hereafter for the lowly and fleeting worldly goods.

And what they used to invent has vanished from them, meaning: He has surrendered them to God’s punishment, and their guardians, whom they used to worship instead of God, and falsely and slanderously claim that they are their lords instead of God, have departed from them.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They have lost their souls
, meaning: They sold them at a loss. This is because his statement: Or we are returned, was raised and not lowered in apposition to his statement:
h
So they intercede for us

, because the meaning is: Do we have intercessors who will intercede for us, or will we be returned so that we do something other than what we were doing? And it was not placed in apposition to his statement:
h
So they intercede for us

x: God Almighty says: Your master and the reformer of your affairs, O people, is the One who is worshipped and to whom all things are to be worshipped, Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, that is Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday.
Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The beginning of creation was the throne, the water, and the air, and the earth was created from water. The beginning of creation was on Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and the gathering of creation was on Friday, and the Jews converted to Judaism on Saturday. And one of the six days is like a thousand years of what you count. Then He established Himself on the Throne. We have already mentioned the meaning of istiwa’ and the people’s differences of opinion about it, previously, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his statement,
h
He causes the night to cover the day

, pursuing it rapidly, he is saying: He brings the night over the day and covers it with it, until its freshness and light are gone. He causes it to cover, he says, The night pursues the day, “rapidly,” meaning: quickly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He seeks him quickly, he said: quickly.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: The night covers the day, pursuing it rapidly, he said: The night covers the day, taking away its light, and pursues it quickly until it overtakes it.

x: God Almighty says: Your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth, the sun, the moon, and the stars, all of that by His command. God commanded them, so obey His command. Unquestionably, to God belongs all creation, and the command that cannot be contradicted or rejected, apart from all other things, and apart from what the polytheists worshipped of gods and idols that neither harm nor benefit, nor create nor command. Blessed be God, our God, to whom all things are due worship, Lord of the worlds.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Baqiyah ibn al-Walid told us, he said, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Ansari told me, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz al-Shami, on the authority of his father,
m: who was a companion, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who does not praise God for the righteous deeds he has done and praises himself, his gratitude will be reduced and his deeds will be in vain. And he who claims that God has given the servants any part of the matter has disbelieved in what God has revealed to His prophets, because He says: “Unquestionably, His is creation and command. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.”

x: God Almighty says: Call upon your Lord alone, O people, and make supplication sincere to Him, without what we call upon other gods and idols besides Him, in humility, meaning: in submission and submission to His obedience, and in secret, meaning with the humility of your hearts, and the soundness of your certainty in His Oneness between you and Him, not openly and hypocritically, and your hearts are not certain of His Oneness and Lordship, as the people of hypocrisy and deception did to God and His Messenger, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: If a man has collected the Qur’an, and his neighbor does not know. If a man has learned a lot of knowledge, and people do not know about it. If a man prays a long prayer in his house while he is lying, and they do not know about it. We have known people who did not have any work on earth that they could do in secret, but it would always be public. The Muslims used to strive hard in supplication, and no voice from them was heard. It was only a whisper between them and their Lord. This is because God says: Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. This is because God mentioned a righteous servant and was pleased with his action, so He said: When he called upon his Lord a secret call.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a military campaign, and they looked out over a valley, glorifying God and praising Him, and raising their voices. He said: O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent, but rather you are calling upon one who hears and is near, and He is with you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly
, he said: secretly. As for his saying:
h
He does not love the aggressors

, its meaning is: Your Lord does not love the one who transgresses and exceeds the limit that He has set for His servants in his supplication and asking of his Lord, and raising his voice above the limit that He has set for them in their supplication to Him, and their asking, and in other matters, such as:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, he said, Ismail bin Hammad bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Ibad,
m: Alqamah, on the authority of Abu Majlaz: “
h
Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly
. Indeed, He does not love transgressors.” He said: He does not ask about the stations of the prophets, peace be upon them.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Indeed, He does not like transgressors, in supplication or otherwise. Ibn Jurayj said: There is transgression in supplication. Raising the voice, calling out, and shouting in supplication is disliked, and one is commanded to be humble and submissive.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation

, do not associate partners with God on the earth nor disobey Him therein, and that is corruption therein. We have mentioned the narration on that previously, and we have explained its meaning with its supporting evidence. After its reformation, he says: after God has reformed it for the people of His obedience, by sending among them messengers calling to the truth, to clarify His proofs for them, and call upon Him in fear and hope, he says: and be sincere in supplication and action to Him, and do not associate in your action for Him anything other than Him from deities and idols and other than that, and let whatever you do in that be out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward. And whoever supplicates to Him for something other than that, he will be among the liars in the Hereafter, because whoever does not fear the punishment of God and does not hope for His reward, does not care about what he does of a matter that angers God and is not pleased with.

Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. God Almighty says: Indeed, the reward of God, which He promised to the doers of good for their good deeds in this world, is near to them, and that is His mercy, because there is nothing between them and reaching that of His mercy and what He has prepared for them of His honor except that their souls leave their bodies.
