Therefore, the meaning of his saying: near is from the report of mercy, and mercy is feminine, because what is meant by it is closeness in time, not in relation, and times in that meaning, if they occur as report of nouns, the Arabs make them like the state, so they make them singular with the one, the two, and the plural, and they make them masculine with the feminine, so they say: The honor of God is far from so-and-so, and she is close to so-and-so, just as they say: Hind is close to us, and the two Hinds are close to us, and the Hinds are close to us, because the meaning of that is: she is in a place close to us.

So if they delete the place and make the close behind it, they make it masculine and singular in the plural, just as the place was masculine and singular in the plural. But if they make it feminine, they make it dual with the two, and plural with the plural, so they say: she is close to us, and they are close to us, as Urwah ibn al-Ward said: An eve that is not far from you, so come close to it, nor is it far from you The female is close, and the male is distant, as I have described. If the close one was related in lineage, he would only be feminine with the female, and with all of them except a group.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Qarib was mentioned as an attribute of mercy, like the Arabs’ saying: a strong wind, a new blanket, and a six-month-old sheep. He said: If you wish, you can say: The interpretation of mercy here is rain and the like, so it was mentioned, like he said: And if a party of you believed, so he was mentioned because he meant the people. If you wish, you can make it like some of what they mention of the feminine, like the poet’s saying: No land is more fertile than its greenery Some Arabists have denied this statement, and they saw that if it is permissible to mention near, directing mercy to the meaning of rain, he must say: Hind stood, directing D Hind, which is a woman, to the meaning of human being. He saw that what he likened to in his saying: Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good with his saying: And if a party of you believes, is not likened to it.

This is because the party, as he claimed, is a source with the meaning of the specter, just as the cry and the shouting have the same meaning, and therefore it was said: And the cry seized those who did wrong.

God Almighty says: Your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth, the sun, the moon, and the stars, subject to His command. He is the One who sends the winds as a means of spreading His mercy. In Arabic, Al-Nashr, with the opening of the letter nun and the sukoon of the letter shin, is one of the winds, the pleasant, soft blowing wind that creates the clouds. Likewise, every pleasant wind is called Nashr, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: As if the wine, the clouds, the scent of lavender, and the spread of rain And with this reading, most of the Kufi readers read it, except for Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, who used to read it: Bishran, although there was a difference of opinion about it.
Some of them narrated that from him: Bear good tidings, with the b and the damma, and the sun on the shin. He used to interpret that in the same way in his recitation of it, his saying:
h
And among His signs is that He sends the winds as good tidings

, giving good tidings of rain, and that the plural of bashir is yabshri bears good tidings, the plural of bashir, just as nazir pluralizes nadhir. As for the reciters of Madinah and most of the people of Makkah and Basra, they read that: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings, with the nun with the damma, and the shin meaning the plural of nushur, the plural of nushra, just as sabur pluralizes sabr, and ash-Shakur pluralizes shukran.
Some of the scholars of Arabic speech said: Its meaning, if read in this way, is that it is the wind that blows from every direction and comes from every facet.

Some of them said: If it is read with a damma on the noon, then its sheen should be sukun, because in language it means spreading with a fatha. He said: The Arabs sometimes add a damma on the noon in the word nashār, and sometimes open it, with one meaning. He said: The difference in the readings in this is according to the difference in their language regarding it. He used to say: It is similar to khasf and khasf, with a fatha on the kha and a damma on it.

The correct thing to say about that is that the reading of those who read that is: Nashrān and Nashrān, with the opening of the noon and the sukūn of the sheen, and with the damma of the noon and the sheen, are two well-known readings in the reading of the regions. I do not like to read it with this word, because it has a correct meaning and an understandable aspect in meaning and grammar, for the reason we mentioned. As for his saying: in front of His mercy, he is saying: in front of His mercy and in front of it. The Arabs also say for everything that happened in front of something and in front of it: it came in front of it, because that is from their speech that happened in their stories about the sons of Adam, and its use was common among them, to the point that they said that about other than the son of Adam and what has no hand. The mercy that He, the Most High, mentioned in this place is rain.

So the meaning of the statement is: And God is the One who sends the winds, with gentle blowing and pleasant breezes, before His rain which He drives with them to His creation, and He creates with them heavy clouds, until when they have carried them, and carrying them is carrying them, as it is said: the camel carried its load, and (and carrying it, if he carried it and stood up with it, God drove it to revive a dead land, whose farms had rotted, whose watering places had been destroyed, and whose people had become barren, so He sent down rain with it, and brought forth with it all kinds of fruits. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And it is He who sends the winds as a means of spreading forth His mercy, until His saying: Perhaps you will remember. He said: God sends the winds, and they bring the clouds from between the two horizons, the edge of the sky and the earth from where they meet. Then He brings them forth from there, then He spreads them out and extends them in the sky as He wills, then He opens the gates of the sky, and the water flows upon the clouds, then He causes the clouds to rain after that. As for His mercy, it is the rain. As for His statement:
h
Thus do We bring forth the dead

, that you may remember, then the Most High says: Just as We revive this dead land with the water that We send down from the clouds, and with it We bring forth fruits after its death, its drought, and the barrenness of its people,
h
thus do We bring forth the dead

from their graves alive after their annihilation and the obliteration Surat al-A’raf 7:57 And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy until, when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land and send down water thereby and bring forth thereby all kinds of fruits.
h
Thus do We bring forth the dead

that you may remember. of their traces, that you may remember. The Most High says to the polytheists who worship idols, who deny the resurrection after death, and who deny reward and punishment: I have given you, O people, this example that I have mentioned to you: of the revival of the dead land with the drops of rain that the clouds bring, which are spread by the winds whose characteristics I have described, so that you may take heed and remember and learn that whoever has this power, it is easy, in His power is the revival of the dead after their annihilation, and their restoration as a sound creation after their obliteration. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
Thus do We bring forth the dead

that you may remember. And thus you will be brought forth, and thus is the Resurrection, just as We bring forth the plants with water. Abu Hurayrah said: When people die at the first Trumpet, water from under the Throne will rain down upon them for forty years, and they will grow as plants grow from water. Then, when their bodies are fully formed, the soul will be breathed into them, then sleep will be cast upon them and they will sleep in their graves. Then, when the second Trumpet is blown, they will come to life, and they will find the taste of sleep in their heads and eyes, just as a sleeper finds when he wakes up from his sleep. At that time, they will say: Woe to us! Who has raised us from our beds? Then the announcer will call out to them: This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Thus do We bring forth the dead

, he said: When God wants to bring forth the dead, He sends rain from the sky until the earth splits open and reveals them, then He sends the souls, and each soul returns to its body. Thus God brings the dead back to life with rain, just as He brings the earth back to life.

evidence.text: Likewise, every pleasant wind is called Nashr, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: As if the wine, the clouds, the scent of lavender, and the spread of rain And with this reading, most of the Kufi readers read it, except for Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, who used to read it: Bishran, although there was a difference of opinion about it.

He used to interpret that in the same way in his recitation of it, his saying: And among His signs is that He sends the winds as good tidings, giving good tidings of rain, and that the plural of bashir is yabshri bears good tidings, the plural of bashir, just as nazir pluralizes nadhir.

As for the reciters of Madinah and most of the people of Makkah and Basra, they read that: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings, with the nun with the damma, and the shin meaning the plural of nushur, the plural of nushra, just as sabur pluralizes sabr, and ash-Shakur pluralizes shukran.
Some of them said: If it is read with a damma on the noon, then its sheen should be sukun, because in language it means spreading with a fatha.
He said: The difference in the readings in this is according to the difference in their language regarding it.

Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about that is that the reading of those who read that is: Nashrān and Nashrān, with the opening of the noon and the sukūn of the sheen, and with the damma of the noon and the sheen, are two well-known readings in the reading of the regions.
I do not like to read it with this word, because it has a correct meaning and an understandable aspect in meaning and grammar, for the reason we mentioned.

x: God Almighty says: And the land whose soil is good and whose drinking places are sweet, its vegetation comes forth when God sends down rain and sends down rain upon it, by His permission, its fruit being good in its season and proper time. But that which is bad, whose soil is bad and whose drinking places are salty, its vegetation does not come forth except in a bad form. He says: Except for hardship in hardship, as the poet said: Do not fulfill the promise, if you promise and if you give, you give something trivial and unpleasant It means trivial, little, and difficult, annoying. It is said: nakad yankad nakdana, nakdaan, so he is nakad and nakad, and nakad is the source. And among their proverbs: nakada and jahdan, and nakada and nakdaan.

i: And jahdan is severity and narrowness, and it is said if he is sick and asked: they have upset him, they upset him annoyingly, as the poet said:
x: Give what you give in goodness, there is no good in what is rejected and the one who gives in badness There are different readings of this.

Some of the people of Medina read it: Except Nakada, with the kaf open. Some Kufians read it with a silent kaf, as an insult. And the rest of the readings in the countries differed from them, so they read it: Except Nakada, with a kasra on the kaf. Whoever reads it: Natahda with the accusative of the kaf means the verbal noun. Whoever read it with a sukoon on the kaf wanted to break it, so he made it sukoon according to the language of the one who said: this is a thigh and a liver. What he should have done if he wanted to do that was to break the nun from nakad so that he would have hit the mark.

The correct reading of this, according to us, is the reading of those who read it: nakada, with the nun open and the kaf closed, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings of the regions on it. And His statement:
h
Thus do We diversify the signs for a people who are grateful

, meaning: Thus do We explain verse after verse and provide argument after argument, and set forth parable after parable, for a people who are grateful to God for His blessing upon them with guidance, and for His showing them the path of the people of misguidance, by their following what He commanded them to follow, and their avoiding what He commanded them to avoid of the paths of misguidance. This is a parable that God set forth for the believer and the disbeliever. The good land whose vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord is an example for the believer, and the one that is bad, whose vegetation does not come forth except in difficulty, is an example for the disbeliever.
And similar to that which we said about that is what the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord

. But that which is bad - brings forth nothing but vegetation,” this is a parable that God has given for the believer. He says: He is good, and his deeds are good, just as the fruit of a good land is good. Then He gave the parable of the disbeliever like a salty, marshy land from which oozes forth. So the disbeliever is the bad one, and his deeds are bad.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: and the good land, “and that which is bad,” he said: All of that is from the salty land and other than it, like Adam and his descendants, among them is good and bad.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord

. And that which is bad - brings forth nothing but a little bit.” He said: This is a parable that God has given for the disbeliever and the believer. 14798 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad told me - meaning Ibn al-Mufaddal - he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: “
h
And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord

. And that which is bad - is the salt marsh - its vegetation comes forth nothing but a little bit.” A little bit is something that is of no benefit. So it was with the hearts when the Qur’an was revealed. When the Qur’an entered the believing heart, it believed in it and faith was established in it. But when the Qur’an entered the disbelieving heart, it did not cling to anything that would benefit it, and nothing bad of faith was established in it except that which is of no benefit, just as this land did not produce anything of its vegetation except that which is of no benefit.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord

. And that which is bad - nothing comes forth except with difficulty.” He said: The good land is benefited by the rain and grows, and that which is bad is the salt marshland, the rain does not benefit it, its vegetation comes forth only with difficulty. He said: This is a parable that God gave for Adam and all his descendants. They were created from a single soul, so some of them believed in God and His Book, so they were good. And some of them disbelieved in God and His Book, so they were evil.

Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading of this, according to us, is the reading of those who read it: nakada, with the nun open and the kaf closed, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings of the regions on it.

x: Our Lord, may He be glorified, swore to those addressed in this verse: That He sent Noah to his people, warning them of His punishment and frightening them with His wrath, for their worship of other than Him. So He said to those of them who disbelieved: O my people, worship God, to whom worship is due, and humble yourselves before Him in obedience and submit to Him in submission, and abandon the worship of other than Him of rivals and gods, for you have no deity that requires your worship other than Him. So I fear for you, if you do not do that, the punishment of a tremendous Day, meaning: the punishment of a day on which your affliction will be magnified by His coming to you with the wrath of your Lord. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: other than him.
Some of the people of Medina and Kufa read it: You have no god other than Him, with ghair in the genitive case as an attribute of ilah.

A group of the people of Medina, Basra and Kufa read it: You have no god other than Him, with ghair in the genitive case, because it is in the genitive case. If it were removed from the sentence, the sentence would be in the genitive case. It was also said: You have no god other than God. When the Arabs described that the known thing in the sentence was included in it or taken out, and that they sometimes include it in such a sentence and sometimes take it out of it, they return what they described to the noun that they worked on in its wording. So if it is in the genitive case, then it is for one statement, because it is an attribute of ik. But if it is in the genitive case, then it is for two statements: You have no god other than Him, and this is a statement that the people of Arabic consider weak.

A group of the people of Medina, Basra and Kufa read it: You have no god other than Him, with ghair in the genitive case, because it is in the genitive case.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about the response of the polytheists of Noah’s people to Noah, and they were the elite. And the elite is the group of men, not a woman among them, that they said to him when he called them to worship God alone, with no partner for Him: Indeed, we see you, O Noah, in manifest error, meaning in a matter that has deviated from the truth, and its deviation from the intention of truth is clear to whoever contemplates it.

God Almighty says: Noah said to his people, responding to them: O my people, I did not command you with what I commanded you with, of sincere monotheism for God, to single Him out in obedience without rivals and gods, out of my deviation from the path of truth, and my straying from the path of righteousness, and I do not have what you think of misguidance, but I am a messenger to you from the Lord of the worlds with what I commanded you with: of single Him out in obedience, and acknowledging His Oneness, and disavowing rivals and gods.

This is report from God, the Most High, about His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, that he said to his people who disbelieved in God and denied Him: But I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds. He sent me to you, so I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I advise you in my warning you of God’s punishment for your disbelief in Him, your denial of me, and your rejection of my advice. And I know from God what you do not know, that His punishment will not be averted from the criminal people.

This is also report from God, the Exalted, about what Noah said to his people, that he said to them, when they rejected his advice about God, and denied that God had sent him as a prophet, and said to him: “We see you only as a human being like ourselves, and we see that none follow you except those who are the lowest of us in appearance, and we see no superiority over you over us. Rather, we think you are liars.” Or do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord? He says: Or do you wonder that a reminder from God and an admonition has come to you, reminding you of what your Lord has revealed, to a man from among you. It was said: The meaning of his saying: to a man from among you is with a man from among you, to warn you, he says: to warn you of God’s wrath and frighten you with His punishment for your disbelief in Him, and that you may fear God, he says: and so that you may fear God’s punishment and wrath, by making Him One, sincerely believing in Him, and working in obedience to Him, and that you may receive mercy, he says: And that your Lord may have mercy upon you, if God wills. You feared God, dreaded Him, and were wary of His wrath. The waw was opened in His statement, or you were amazed, because it is a waw of conjunction, and an interrogative alif was added to it.
God Almighty says:

c: Noah’s people denied him when he told them that
m: he was a messenger to God, commanding them to renounce rivals to Him, to acknowledge the oneness of God, and to work in obedience to Him. But they disobeyed the command of their Lord and persisted in their transgression, wandering blindly. So God saved him in the ark and those who were with him from the believers in Him, and they were ten souls with Noah, peace be upon him, in what:
b.via: Noah’s people denied him when he

c: Ibn Hamid told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Noah, his three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives, and six people who believed in him. He carried with him in the ark two of each kind, as the Most High said: And those who believed - and none believed with him except a few. And the ark is the ship. And We drowned those who denied Our signs, meaning: God drowned those who denied His proofs, did not follow His messengers, and did not accept His advice to them in God, with the flood. They were
h
a blind people
, meaning: blind to the truth, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: blind, he said: on the truth. 14852 - Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement:
h
A blind people
, he said: Blindness is the one who is ignorant of the truth.

x: God Almighty says: And We sent to ʿAd their brother Hud, and for this reason Hud is in the accusative case, because it is connected to Noah, peace be upon them both. Hud said: O my people, worship God and single out worship for Him, and do not make any god besides Him, for you have no god besides Him. Do you not then fear your Lord, so that you fear Him and fear His punishment by worshipping other than Him, while He is your Creator and Provider, not anything else?

God Almighty says, informing about what Hud answered his people who disbelieved in God: The leaders of those who disbelieved said, meaning: those who denied the oneness of God and rejected the message of God to Hud, Indeed, we see you, O Hud, in foolishness, meaning in error from the truth and righteousness by abandoning our religion and worshipping our gods, and indeed, we think you are among the liars, in your saying: Indeed, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.

He said: O my people, there is no foolishness in me, meaning: any deviation from the truth and right path, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds, He sent me, so I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I deliver them to you as He commanded me to deliver them.
What he means by his saying:
h
I convey to you the messages of my Lord

, is that I convey that to you, O people, and I am your sincere advisor, meaning: I am your sincere advisor in my command to you to worship God without any rivals or gods besides Him, and in calling you to believe in what I have brought to you from God. So accept my advice, for I am trustworthy with God’s revelation and with what God has entrusted me with of the message. I do not lie in it, nor add to it, nor change it. Rather, I convey what I have been commanded as I have been commanded.

Or do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you to warn you? He says: Or do you wonder that God sent down His revelation to remind you and admonish you for what you are persisting in of misguidance, to a man from among you to warn you of God's wrath and frighten you with His punishment,
h
And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah

, He says: So fear God in yourselves, and remember what happened to the people of Noah of punishment when they disobeyed their Messenger and disbelieved in their Lord, for your Lord only made you successors on the earth from among them, when He destroyed them He replaced them with you in it, so fear God lest a similar punishment happen to you, so He destroys you and replaces you with others, His way with the people of Noah before you, for your disobedience to Him and your disbelief in Him, And He increased you in creation abundantly, He increased your bodies in length and size over the bodies of the people of Noah, and in your strength over their strength, This is a blessing from Him upon you, so remember His blessings and favor with which He favored you over them in your bodies and your strength, and thank God for that by sincerely worshipping Him, abandoning polytheism with Him, and abandoning idols and rivals, that you may succeed, meaning that you may succeed and attain immortality and remaining in bliss in the Hereafter, and succeed in your requests with Him.
And in a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah
, said the commentators.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah
, meaning: He took away the people of Noah and made you successors after them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah
, meaning: the inhabitants of the earth after the people of Noah. And similar to what we said, they also said in the interpretation of his saying: Basta.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And He increased you in creation abundantly, he said: What is the strength of the people of Aad. As for the blessings, it is a plural, its singular is to with a kasra on the alif in the sense of with me, and it is said: to in the sense of back with a fatha on the alif. It has been reported that it was heard from the Arabs: to is like my sense. And the blessings are the blessings. And so said the people of interpretation.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So remember the favors of God
, meaning: the blessings of God.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for the blessings of God, they are the blessings of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
So remember the favors of God
, he said: His favors, His blessings.

x: These people whom God described, and to whom He sent Hud to call them to the Oneness of God and to follow what He brought them from Him, are, in what follows:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Ad bin Iram bin Aws bin Sam bin Noah were born, and their dwellings were in Ash Shihr in the land of Yemen and what was adjacent to the land of Hadhramaut to Oman, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: That Ad were a people who were in Yemen, in Al-Ahqaf.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Saeed Al-Khuza’i, on the authority of Abu Al-Tayfil Amir ibn Wathilah, who said:
m: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, say to a man from Hadramaut: Have you seen a red dune mixed with red mud, with many arak trees and lote trees in such and such a region of Hadramaut? Have you seen it? He said: Yes, O Commander of the Faithful, by God, you are describing it as a man who has seen it! He said: No, but I have narrated about it. The Hadrami said: What is the matter with it, O Commander of the Faithful? He Surat al-A’raf 7:69 Or do you wonder that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you to warn you?
h
And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah
and increased you abundantly in creation.
h
So remember the favors of God

that you may succeed. said: In it is the grave of Hud, peace be upon him. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated that Ibn Ishaq said: The dwellings of the people of Ad when God sent Hud among them were Al-Ahqaf. He said: Al-Ahqaf is the sand between Oman and Hadhramaut, and all of Yemen. However, they had spread throughout the earth and subjugated its people with the strength that God had given them. They were idolaters who worshipped them instead of God: an idol called Sada’, an idol called Samud, and an idol called Al-Haba’. So God sent Hud to them, and he was from the most noble of them in lineage and the best of them in position. He commanded them to believe in the oneness of God and not to make any other god with Him, and to refrain from oppressing people. He did not command them, as far as is mentioned, and God knows best, to do anything else. But they refused and denied him, and said: Who is stronger than you? And some of them followed him, but they were few in number, concealing their faith. Among those who believed in him and confirmed his faith was a man from Aad called Marthad bin Saad bin Ufair. He used to conceal his faith, but when they rebelled against God Almighty and denied their prophet, and spread corruption on earth, and were arrogant and built on every high place a sign in vain and without benefit, Hud spoke to them and said: “Do you build on every high place a sign, amusingly? And build for yourselves lofty palaces that you may live forever? And when you strike, you strike like tyrants. So fear God and obey me.” They said, “O Hud, you have not brought us clear proof, nor will we abandon our gods because of your word, nor will we believe you. We only say that some of our gods have afflicted you with evil.” That is, what you have brought us is nothing but madness that some of these gods of ours have afflicted you, which you criticize. He said, “Indeed, I call God to witness, and you to witness, that I am innocent of what you associate with Him. So plot against me all together and then do not give me respite.” Up to His saying, a straight path. When they did that, God withheld the rain from the sky for three years, they claim, until it exhausted them. And when people at that time were afflicted with a calamity or hardship, and they asked God for relief from Him, their request to God was at His Sacred House in Mecca, both Muslims and polytheists. So many people of different religions would gather in Mecca, all of them respecting Mecca, recognizing its sanctity and its place with God. Ibn Ishaq said: At that time, the Kaaba was known in its place, and the sanctuary was still standing, as they say. The people of Mecca at that time were the Amalekites - and they were called Amalek because their father was Amalek bin Lawdh bin Sam bin Noah - and the leader of the Amalekites in Mecca at that time, as they claim, was a man called Muawiyah bin Bakr. His father was alive at that time, but he had grown old, and his son was the leader of his people. The leadership and honor of the Amalekites, as they claim, were in the people of that house. The mother of Muawiyah bin Bakr was Kalhada bint Al-Khaibari, a man from Ad. When the rain dried up in Ad and they were struggling, they said: Prepare a delegation to Mecca so that they may ask for rain for you, for you are doomed! So they sent Qayl bin Anz, Luqaym bin Hazal bin Hazil, Atil bin Sad bin Ad the elder, Murthad bin Saad bin Ufair, who was a Muslim who concealed his Islam, and Jalhamah bin Al-Khaibari, the maternal uncle of Muawiyah bin Bakr, his mother’s brother. Then they sent Luqman ibn Aad ibn so-and-so ibn so-and-so ibn Sad ibn Aad al-Akbar. Each man of these people set out with a group of his people, until the number of their delegation reached seventy men. When they arrived in Mecca, they stayed with Muawiyah ibn Bakr, who was outside Mecca, outside the sanctuary. He accommodated them and honoured them. They were his maternal uncles and his in-laws. When the delegation of Aad came to Muawiyah ibn Bakr, they stayed for a month drinking wine, and the two locusts, Muawiyah ibn Bakr's slave girls, sang to them. Their journey was a month, and their stay was a month. When Muawiyah ibn Bakr saw how long they stayed, and their people had sent them to seek refuge with them from the calamity that had befallen them, he was upset by that and said: My maternal uncles and in-laws are dead! And these are staying with me, and they are my guests and have come to visit me! By God, I do not know what to do with them! I am ashamed to order them to go out to what they were sent for, lest they think that I am fed up with their staying with me, while those of their people who followed them have perished from exhaustion and thirst!! Or something like that. So he complained about their situation to his two slave girls, the locusts, and they said: Recite poetry so that we may sing to them, without them knowing who said it, perhaps that will move them! So Muawiyah ibn Bakr said, when they suggested that to him: Oh Qayl, woe to you! Get up and sleep, perhaps God will make us cloudy in the morning. He waters the land of Ad, for Ad have spent the night not making clear their words. From extreme thirst, neither the old man nor the young man can hope for it. Their women were fine, but now their women are poor. The beasts come to them openly, and they do not fear the arrows of the enemy. And you are here, as you wish, your day and night are complete. Your delegation is worse than the delegation of a people who did not receive greetings and peace. When Muawiyah recited that poem, the two locusts sang it to them. When the people heard what they had sung, some of them said to one another: O people, your people sent you to seek refuge with you from this calamity that has befallen them, and you have delayed bringing it to them! So enter this sanctuary and pray for rain for your people! Then Murthad bin Saad bin Ufair said to them: By God, you will not be given rain by your prayers, but if you obey your Prophet and turn to him, you will be given rain! Then he declared his Islam, and when Jalhamah bin Al-Khaibari, the maternal uncle of Muawiyah bin Bakr, heard his words and knew that he had followed the religion of Hud and believed in it, he said to them: Abu Saad, you are from a noble tribe and your mother is from Thamud. We will not obey you as long as we live, and we will not do what you want. We are ordered to abandon the religion of slander, slavery, and slavery. We leave the religion of our honorable fathers who had a good opinion and follow the religion of Hood. Then they said to Muawiyah bin Bakr and his father Bakr: Detain Murthad bin Saad from us, so that he does not come with us to Mecca, for he has followed the religion of Hud and abandoned our religion! Then they went out to Mecca to pray for rain there for Aad. When they returned to Mecca, Murthad bin Saad left the house of Muawiyah bin Bakr until he caught up with them there, before they could pray to God for anything for which they had gone out. When he reached them, he stood up to pray to God in Mecca, and there was a delegation of Aad gathered, praying, saying: O God, give me what I ask for alone and do not include me in anything for which the delegation of Aad is praying to You! Qayl bin Anz was the head of the delegation of Aad. The delegation of Aad said: O God, give Qayl what he asked of You, and include our request with his request! Luqman bin Aad, the chief of Aad, had stayed behind from the delegation of Aad when he prayed. When they finished their prayer, he stood up and said: O God, I have come to You alone in my need, so grant me what I ask for! Qayl ibn Anz said when he called out: O our God, if Hud is truthful, then give us rain, for we are lost! So God created for them clouds of three types: white, red, and black. Then a caller from the clouds called out to him: O Qayl, choose for yourself and your people from these clouds. He said: I have chosen the black cloud, for it contains the most water! Then a caller called out to him: You have chosen ashes, ashes, and you will not leave anyone from the family of Aad, neither father nor son, except that you will make them Himyarites, except for Banu al-Lawdhiyyah, the guided ones. Banu al-Lawdhiyyah are Banu Luqaym ibn Hazal ibn Hazilah ibn Bakr, and they were residents of Mecca with their maternal uncles, and they were not with Aad in their land, so they are the Aad of the hereafter, and whoever was from their descendants who remained from Aad. And God sent the black cloud, as they say, which Qayl bin Anz chose for its punishment on Aad, until it came out upon them from a valley called Al-Mughith. When they saw it, they were happy about it and said: This is a cloud that will bring us rain. God says: "Rather, it is that which you were hastening - a wind in which is a painful punishment. It destroys everything by the command of its Lord." That is, everything it commanded. The first one to see what was in it and know that it was a wind, as they say, was a woman from Aad called Muhadd. When she was certain of what was in it, she cried out, then fainted. When she regained consciousness, they said: What did you see, Muhadd? She said: I saw a wind in which was like meteors of fire, with men leading it in front of it! So God made it subservient to them for seven nights and eight days, as God said, and the decisive is the permanent, and it did not leave anyone from Aad except that he perished. So Hud and those who were with him of the believers secluded themselves in a pen, and nothing of the wind affected him or those with him except what softened the skins and pleased the souls, and it would pass over the people of Ad with a stabbing between the sky and the earth, and it would crush them with stones. The delegation of Ad left Mecca and passed by Muawiyah ibn Bakr and his father, and they dismounted. While they were with him, a man came on his she-camel on a moonlit night, the third evening of the calamity of Ad, and told them the report. They said to him, Where did you leave Hud and his companions? He said, I left them on the seashore.

c: It seemed that they doubted what he had told them,
m: so Hazaila bint Bakr said, He has told the truth, by the Lord of the Kaaba! Abu Kuraib narrated, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated, Asim narrated, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Hassan Al-Bakri, who said: I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and I passed by a woman in Ar-Rabadha. She said: Will you carry me to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? I said: Yes! So I carried her until I reached Madinah, and I entered the mosque. There was the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the pulpit, and Bilal was wearing a sword, and there were black banners. I said: What is this? They said: Amr bin Al-Aas has returned from his campaign. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came down from the pulpit, I went to him and asked permission, and he gave me permission. I said: O Messenger of God, there is a woman from Banu Tamim at the door, and she asked me to carry her to you. He said: O Bilal, give her permission. I entered, and when I sat down, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: Is there anything between you and Tamim? I said: Yes! And the thorns were on them, so if you see that you can put oil as a barrier between us and them, then do so! He said: The woman said: Where is your harm forced upon you, O Messenger of God? He said: I said: My example is like that of a goat that has carried its death! He said: I said: And you carried it, so you would be an opponent to me! I seek refuge in God from being like the delegation of Aad! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And what is the delegation of Aad? He said: I said: It has fallen upon the expert! Aad suffered a drought, so they sent those who prayed for rain for them. They sent men, and they passed by Bakr ibn Muawiyah, and he gave them wine to drink, and two locusts sang to them for a month. Then he sent a man from him until he came to the mountains of Mahrah, so they called out, and clouds came. He said: And each time a cloud came, it said: Go to such and such! Until a cloud came, and it was called from it: Take it, ashes, blackened, do not leave anyone from Aad. He said: So he heard it and Surat al-A’raf 7:69 Or do you wonder that there has come to you a reminder from your Lord through a man from among you to warn you?
h
And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah
and increased you abundantly in creation.
h
So remember the favors of God

that you may succeed. concealed them until the punishment came to them. Abu Kuraib said: Abu Bakr said after that in the hadith of Ad, he said: So the one who came to them came and came to the mountains of Mahra, so he climbed and said: O God, I have not come to you as a prisoner so that you may ransom him, nor for a sick person so that you may cure him, so give water to Ad that which you have given them! He said: So clouds were raised for him, he said: And it was called from them: Choose! He said: So he began to say: Go to the Banu so-and-so, go to the Banu so-and-so. He said: Then the last of them was a black cloud, so he said: Go to Ad! And it was called from them: Take it, ashes, do not leave anyone from Ad. He said: And he concealed them, and the people were with Bakr bin Muawiyah, drinking. He said: Bakr bin Muawiyah disliked to say that to them, because they were with him, and they were in his food. He said: So he began to sing and mention them. Abu Kuraib narrated, Zaid bin Al-Habbab narrated, Salam Abu Al-Mundhir Al-Nahwi narrated, Asim narrated, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Bakri, who said: I went out to complain to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Al-Ala’ bin Al-Hadrami. I passed by Ar-Rabdhah, and there was an old woman from Banu Tamim who had been isolated there. She said: O Abdullah, I have a need from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Will you deliver my message to him? So I carried her and went to Madinah. Then I saw banners and said: What is the matter with the people? They said: He wants to send Amr bin Al-Aas as an emissary. So I sat until he finished. He said: So he entered his house - or he said: his tent - and I asked permission to enter, and he gave me permission. So I entered and sat down, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Was there anything between you and Tamim? I said: Yes! And the wasp was upon them, and I passed by Ar-Rabdhah, and there was an old woman among them who was lying there, and she asked me to carry her to you, and here she is at the door. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave permission, so I entered, and I said: O Messenger of God, make a barrier between us and the Tamim of Dahna, so the old woman was protected and provoked, and she said: Where will your harm be, O Messenger of God? I said: I am as the first said: A goat that has carried a dead animal! I carried this one and I did not feel that she was an opponent to me! I seek refuge in God and His Messenger from being like the visitor of Ad! He said: What is the visitor of Ad? I said: I have fallen upon the expert! He said: And he was asking me to talk. I said: If Ad had a drought, then they sent a visitor, Qayla, and he stayed with Bakr, and he gave him wine to drink for a month, and two girls called the two jaradates sang to him, so he went out to the mountains of Mahra, and he cried: I have not come to treat a sick person, nor to a traveler to ransom him. O God, avert from Ad what they used to give him to drink! Black clouds passed over him, and a voice was called from them: Take it as ashes, ashes, do not leave a single one of the people of Aad. He said: The woman used to say: Do not be like the visitors of Aad! I have not heard that the wind was sent upon them, O Messenger of God, only as much as would run through my ring. Abu Wa'il said: That is what I heard.
b.via: It seemed that they doubted what he had

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “And to ‘Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him.’” That Hud came to ‘Aad and preached to them and reminded them of what God has related in the Qur’an, but they denied him and disbelieved, and asked him to bring them punishment. So he said to them, Knowledge is only with God, and I will convey to you that with which I have been sent. When ‘Aad disbelieved, they were afflicted with a drought of rain, to the point that they struggled greatly for it. That was because Hud invoked a curse upon them, so God sent upon them the barren wind, which is the wind that does not fertilize the trees. When they looked at it, they said, This is a cloud bringing us rain. When it drew near to them, they looked at the camels and the men being blown about by the wind between the sky and the earth. When they saw it, they rushed to the houses. When they entered the houses, it entered upon them and destroyed them in them. Then it expelled them from the houses, and it struck them on an ill-omened day - ill-omened is ominous - and continuous - continued torment upon them for seven nights and eight decisive days, it ended everything it passed through. When it expelled them from the houses, God said: It will uproot the people from the houses, as if they were trunks of palm trees hollowed out, hollowed out from their roots, empty, collapsed and fallen. When God destroyed them, He sent upon them black birds, which carried them to the sea and threw them into it. That is what He said: So in the morning nothing could be seen except their dwellings. And no wind ever came out except with a measure, except on that day, for it was violent against the keepers and overcame them, so they did not know how much its measure was. That is what He said: So they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind, and the furious is the one with a loud sound.

evidence.text: When Muawiyah recited that poem, the two locusts sang it to them.

x: God Almighty says: ʿAd said to him: Have you come to us threatening us with punishment from God for our religion, so that we worship God alone, and submit to Him with pure obedience, and abandon the worship of the gods and idols that our fathers used to worship, and disavow them? We will not do that, nor will we follow you in what you call us to. So bring us what you threaten us with of punishment and torment for abandoning the sincere monotheism of God, and our worship of what we worship besides Him of idols, if you are among the people of truth in what you say and promise.
God Almighty says: Hud said to his al-Nas 114:A punishment and wrath from God have befallen you.

i: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala - according to what was mentioned to us about him - claimed that rajaz and rajis have the same meaning, and that they are inverted, the seen was changed to a zay, just as the six was changed to a seen, and just as they said qarbus and qarbut, and just as the rajaz poet said:
x: May God curse the sons of Al-Sa’lat, Amr bin Yarbu’, the vile ones They are neither chaste nor pious.
People want, and bags, so the seen was changed to a ta, as Ru’bah said: How many a liar have we seen, until we thwarted his plot with wrath?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to say: Rijs means wrath.

c: Al-Muthanna told me that, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There has fallen upon you an abomination from your Lord

, meaning: wrath. As for his statement: Do you dispute with Me over names which you and your fathers have named? He is saying: Do you dispute with Me over names which you have called idols, which neither harm nor benefit, you and your fathers, for which God has sent down no authority? He is saying: God has not given you any argument to argue with in your worship of them, nor any excuse to make, because worship is only for He who harms and benefits, rewards for obedience and punishes for disobedience, provides for and withholds. As for inanimate objects such as stones, iron, and copper, there is no benefit or harm in them, unless you make a tool out of them, and there is no argument for a worshipper of His servant other than God in his worship of Him, because God did not permit that, so he apologizes to His servant by saying that he worships Him in accordance with God’s command in his worship of Him. Nor is it - since God did not permit His worship - something whose benefit is hoped for, or whose harm is feared, in the immediate or the future, so that one worships Him in the hope of benefiting from Him, or warding off His harm - Then wait, for I am with you among those who wait, meaning: So wait for God’s judgment concerning us and you, For I am with you among those who wait, His judgment and the finality of His judgment concerning us and you.

x: God Almighty says: So We saved Noah and those who followed him, believing in him and believing in him and what he called to, of the oneness of God and abandoning the gods and idols, by mercy from Us,
h
and We cut off the root of those who denied Our signs
, meaning: And We destroyed those who denied from the people of Hud with Our proofs, all of them, to the last of them, so We did not leave a single one of them, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And We cut off the root of those who denied Our signs

, he said: We eradicated them. We have previously explained the meaning of his saying: He cut off the root of the people who did wrong, with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And they were not believers, meaning: they did not believe in God or in His Messenger Hud.

x: God Almighty says: And We sent to Thamud their brother Salih. Thamud is Thamud bin Ghathir bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah, and he is the brother of Jadhis bin Ghathir. Their dwellings were in Al-Hijr, between Al-Hijaz and Al-Sham, to Wadi Al-Qura and its surroundings. The meaning of the statement is: And to the children of Thamud, their brother Salih. And the reason for preventing Thamud from being declined is because Thamud is a tribe, just as Bakr is a tribe, and so is Tamim. He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him.’ Salih said to Thamud: “O my people, worship God alone, with no partner for Him. You have no god other than Him whom you are permitted to worship. And there has come to you an argument and proof of the truth of what I say, and the reality of what I call to, of sincere monotheism for God, and singling Him out for worship without anyone else, and my confirmation that I am His Messenger.

And my proof of what I say and the reality of what I have brought to you from my Lord, and my proof against Him, is this she-camel that God brought forth from this plateau, as proof of my prophethood and the truth of my words. You have known that this is one of the miracles that no one is capable of being like it except God. As far as I have been informed, Salih used the she-camel as evidence of the truth of his prophethood among his people, Thamud, because they asked him about it as a sign and proof of the truth of his words. He mentioned who said that, and he mentioned the reason why Salih’s people killed the she-camel: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, saying: Israel narrated, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, saying: Thamud said to Salih: Bring us a sign if you are of the truthful! Salih said to them: Go out to a hill on the ground!

So they went out, and behold, she was laboring like a pregnant woman, then she parted and the she-camel came out from her midst. Salih said: “This is the she-camel of God as a sign to you, so leave her to graze in God’s land
h
and do not touch her with harm

, lest a painful punishment seize you.” She has a drink and you have a drink on a specified day. When they got tired of her, they hamstrung her. Then he said to them: “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. This is a promise that will not be denied.” Abd al-Aziz said: Another man narrated to me that Salih said to them: The sign of the punishment is that you will become red tomorrow, yellow on the second day, and black on the third day. He said: So the punishment came upon them in the morning, and when they saw that, they embalmed themselves and prepared themselves.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih, he said: God sent Salih to Thamud, so he called them but they denied him, so he told them what God mentioned in the Quran, so they asked him to bring them a sign, so he brought them the she-camel, she had a drink and they had a drink on a specific day. He said: Leave her to graze in God’s land
h
and do not touch her with harm

. So they all acknowledged it, so that is what He said: So We guided them, but they preferred blindness to guidance. They had acknowledged it out of hypocrisy and dissimulation, and the she-camel had a drink, so on the day she drank water she would pass between two mountains and they would have mercy on her, so her traces are in them until this hour, then she would come and stop for them until they milked the milk, so it would satisfy them, but she would pour it out in abundance, and on the day they drank the water she would not come to them. And there was a young camel with her, so Salih said to them: A boy will be born in this month of yours, and your destruction will be at his hands! Nine of them had a son in that month, so they slaughtered their sons. Then a son was born to the tenth, but he refused to slaughter his son, as he had not had any sons before that. The tenth son was blue-eyed and red, and he grew quickly. When he passed by the nine and they saw him, they said: If our sons were alive, they would be like this! The nine became angry with Salih because he ordered them to slaughter their sons. They swore by God that we would surely kill him and his family by night, then we would say to his heir, ‘We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.’ They said: “We will go out so that people will think that we have set out on a journey, so we will go to the cave and stay in it. When night falls and Salih goes out to the mosque, we will go to him and kill him, then we will return to the cave and stay in it. Then we will return and say: We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.” They will believe us, knowing that we have set out on a journey! So they set out, and when they entered the cave, they wanted to leave at night, but the cave fell on Surat al-A’raf 7:73 And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of God, a sign for you, so leave her to graze in the land of God
h
and do not touch her with harm

, lest a painful punishment seize you." them and killed them. That is what He said: And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform. Until He reached here: Then see how was the end of their plot - We destroyed them and their people, all together. The ten-year-old boy grew up and grew amazingly fast. He sat with some people who were drinking. They wanted some water to mix their drink with. That day was the day the she-camel was drinking. They found that the she-camel had drunk the water, which made them very upset. They said about the she-camel: What should we do with the milk? If we could take the water that this she-camel drinks and give it to our livestock and crops, it would be better for us! The ten-year-old boy said: Would you like me to hamstring her for you? They said: Yes! So they showed their religion. The boy came to her, and when she saw him, she ran away from him, so he ran away from her. When he saw that, he went behind a rock on her path and hid behind it. He said: Bring her to me! So they pushed her to him. When she passed by, they called out to him: Are you here? So he grabbed her and hamstrung her, and she fell. That is what He said: So they called their companion, and he seized her and hamstrung her. Then they revealed their affair, and hamstrung the she-camel, and rebelled against the command of their Lord, and said: O Salih, bring us what you promise us.

x: Some of them were alarmed to Salih, and told him that the she-camel had been hamstrung, so he said: Bring me the young foal! So they sought the young foal and found it on a mound of land, so they sought it, and it rose with it until it flew with it in the sky, but they could not find it. Then the young foal roared to God, so God revealed to Salih: Tell them to enjoy themselves in their homes for three days! So Salih said to them: Enjoy yourself in your homes for three days, and the sign of that is that your faces will become yellow on the first day, red on the second, black on the third day, and the fourth day in which is the torment. So when they saw the signs, they shrouded themselves, embalmed themselves, smeared themselves with myrrh, put on blankets, and dug pits and entered them awaiting the shout, until the torment came to them and they perished. That is what He said: We destroyed them and their people, all together.

Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: When God destroyed the tribe of ‘Aad and their matter was completed, Thamud populated after them and they were made successors on earth. They settled there and spread out, then they rebelled against God. When their corruption became apparent and they worshipped other than God, God sent Salih to them - and they were an Arab people, and he was from the most noble of them in lineage and the best of them in position - as a messenger. Their homes were from Al-Hijr to Qarh, which is Wadi Al-Qura, and between them is eighteen miles between the Hijaz and Ash-Sham! So God sent to them a young boy who called them to God until he grew old and disheveled, and none of them followed him except a few weak ones. When Salih insisted on calling them, and warned them a lot, and frightened them with the torment and vengeance of God, they asked him to show them a sign that would confirm what he was saying in calling them to.

He said to them: What sign do you want? They said: Come out with us to our festival - and they had a festival to which they would go out with their idols and what they worshipped besides God, on a specific day of the year - and call upon your god and we will call upon our gods. If your request is answered, we will follow you, and if our request is answered, you will follow us! Salih said to them: Yes! So they went out with their idols to their festival, and Salih went out with them to God. They called upon their idols and asked them not to answer anything that Salih called upon. Then Junda’ ibn Amr ibn Jawas ibn Amr ibn Ad-Damil, who was at that time the master and great one of Thamud, said to him: O Salih, bring us out of this rock - a separate rock in the corner of Al-Hijr, called Al-Kathbah - a she-camel that has been hollowed out and is bare - and the she-camel that has been hollowed out is what resembles a camel.

Thamud said to Salih the same as Junda’ ibn Amr had said, so if you do, we will believe in you and bear witness that what you have brought is the truth! Salih took their covenant from them: If you do and God does, you will believe in me and you will believe in me! They said: Yes! So they gave him their covenants on that. Then Salih called upon his Lord to bring them out from that plateau, as they had described.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yaqub ibn Utbah ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhns: It seems that he told us that
m: they looked at the hill, when Salih called upon God with what he called upon Him, the she-camel was laboring, the she-camel was laboring with her young, so the hill moved, then the she-camel shook, and it split open to reveal a she-camel, as they described, hollow and bare, with a crown, between its sides only God knows what was a bone. So Junda’ ibn Amr and those of his people who were with him in his affair believed in him, and the nobles of Thamud wanted to believe in him and confirm him, but Dhu’ab ibn Amr ibn Labid, and al-Habbab, the owner of their idols, and Rubab ibn Sam’ar ibn Jalhas, who were from the nobles of Thamud, forbade them, so they turned their nobles away from Islam and from entering into what Salih called them to of mercy and salvation, and Junda’ had a cousin called Shihab ibn Khalifah ibn Mukhlah ibn Labid ibn Jawas, so he wanted to convert to Islam, but those people forbade him from that. So he obeyed them, and he was one of the nobles and best of Thamud. Then a man from Thamud called Mahwas bin Anmah bin Ad-Damil, who was a Muslim, said: A group of the Al Amr family followed the religion of the Prophet and called him Shahab. Aziz Thamud, all of them together, understood that he would answer, even if they answered Saleh became dear to us, and they did not treat their companion as equals. But the seducers of the Al-Hajar family turned away after their maturity? Flies The she-camel that God had brought forth for them remained with her father in the land of Thamud, grazing on trees and drinking water. Salih, peace be upon him, said to them: This is the she-camel of God as a sign for you, so leave her to graze in the land of God
h
and do not touch her with harm

, lest a painful punishment seize you. God said to Salih: The water is divided between them, each drink is in its proper place. That is, the water is divided into two halves, one day for them and one day for her, and she is in its proper place. So she does not stop drinking on her day. He said: She has a drink and you have a drink, a specified day. So, as I have heard, and God knows best, whenever she came to drink, and she would come at night, she would put her head in a well in the rock called the Well of the She-Camel. They claim that it was from this well that she would drink whenever she came to drink. She would put her head in it and would not raise it until she had drunk every drop of water in the valley. Then she would raise her head and it would burst open for them, meaning: it would burst open for them, so they would milk whatever they wanted of milk, and they would drink and store it until they filled all their vessels. Then she would leave from a different place from which she came. They could not set out from where they were going because of its narrowness, so they could not return from it. Until the next day, it was their day, so they would drink as much water as they wanted, and save as much as they wanted for the day of the she-camel, so they were at ease. And the she-camel, as they mentioned, would spend the summer if it was hot in the back of the valley, so the livestock would flee from her, their sheep, cows and camels, and go down to the bottom of the valley in its heat and drought - because livestock are scared away from her when they see her - and spend the winter in the bottom of the valley if it was winter, so their livestock would flee to the back of the valley in the cold and drought, so that harmed their livestock, for the sake of the trial and the test. And their pastures, as they claim, were Al-Habbab and Hasma, all of which grazed with Wadi Al-Hijr, so that was difficult for them, so they rebelled against the command of their Lord, and agreed on their opinion to hamstring the she-camel. There was a woman from Thamud called Unayzah bint Ghanim bin Majlaz, nicknamed Umm Ghanim, and she was from Banu Ubayd bin al-Muhal, the brother of Ramil bin al-Muhal. She was the wife of Khawab bin Amr, and she was an old woman, and she had beautiful daughters, and she had wealth in camels, cows, and sheep. There was another woman called Saduf bint al-Muhaya bin Dahr bin al-Muhaya, the master of Banu Ubayd and the owner of their idols in the early days. The valley was called Wadi al-Muhaya, and he is al-Muhaya al-Akbar, the grandfather of al-Muhaya al-Asghar, Abu Saduf. Saduf was one of the most beautiful people, and she was rich, and she had wealth in camels, sheep, and cows. They were the two women from Thamud who were the most hostile to Salih, and the most disbelieving of him. They used to plot to hamstring the she-camel, despite their disbelief in him, because of the harm it caused to their livestock. Saduf was married to her maternal uncle, whose name was Suntum bin Harawa bin Saad bin Al-Ghatrif, from Banu Halil. He converted to Islam and his conversion was good. Saduf had entrusted him with her money, and he spent it on those of Salih’s companions who converted to Islam with him, until the money became scarce. When Saduf learned of his conversion to Islam, she rebuked him for it. He revealed his religion to her and called her to God and to Islam, but she refused him and plotted against him. She took his sons and daughters from him and hid them among Banu Ubayd, her clan to which she belonged. Suntum was her husband from Banu Halil, and he was her maternal uncle. He said to her: Return my son to me! She said: So that I may go to Banu San’an bin Ubayd, or to Banu Junda’ bin Ubayd! Suntum said to her: Rather, I will go to Banu Mirdas bin Ubayd! This is because Banu Mirdas bin Ubayd had hastened to convert to Islam, while others had been slow to do so. She said: I will not go to anyone except the one to whom I have called you! Banu Murdas said: By God, she will give him his son, willingly or unwillingly! When she saw that, she gave him to them. Then Saduf and Unayzah were divided into two camps to hamstring the she-camel, because of the misery that had befallen them. Saduf called a man from Thamud called Al-Hubab to hamstring the she-camel, and offered herself to him if he would do it, but he refused. So she called her cousin called Musad' ibn Muharij ibn Al-Muhaya, and offered herself to him on the condition that he hamstring the she-camel. She was one of the most handsome people, and she was rich and had a lot of money, so he agreed to do that. Unayzah bint Ghanam called out to Qaddar bin Salaf bin Junda', a man from the people of Qurah. Qaddar was a short, red-haired man, and they claimed that he was the son of a fornicator, from a man called Sahyad. His father was not the one called Salaf, but he was born on Salaf's bed, and he was called after him and attributed to him. She said: I will give you any of my daughters you wish, on condition that you hamstring the she-camel! Unayzah was a noble woman from the women of Thamud, and her husband was Dhu'ab bin Amr, one of the noble men of Thamud. Qaddar was powerful and respected among his people. Then Qudar bin Salaf and Musaddaq bin Muharij set out and summoned some of the adventurers of Thamud. Seven men followed them, so that they were nine men. One of the men who followed them was a man called Huwail bin Miligh, the maternal uncle of Qudar bin Salaf, the brother of his mother from her father and mother. He was a noble man from the people of Hajar. He was also Du'air bin Ghanam bin Da'ir, who was from Banu Khalawah bin al-Muhal. He was also Da'ab bin Muharij, the brother of Musaddaq bin Muharij, and five others whose names we have not preserved. They watched the she-camel when it came out of the water. Qudar had ambushed her at the base of a rock on her way, and Musaddaq had ambushed her at the base of another rock. She passed by Musaddaq, so he shot her with an arrow, which pierced her leg muscle. Umm Ghanem of Unayzah went out and ordered her daughter, who was one of the most beautiful people, to uncover her face and show it to Qudar. Then she Surat al-A’raf 7:73 And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of God, a sign for you, so leave her to graze in the land of God
h
and do not touch her with harm

, lest a painful punishment seize you." restrained him, so he attacked the she-camel with his sword and pierced her heel, so she fell down and bellowed once, warning of her hump. Then he stabbed her in the heart and slaughtered her, and her hump ran away until it reached a high mountain, then it reached a rock on top of the mountain in fear and took refuge there. The name of the mountain, as they claim, is Sunu. Then Salih came to them, and when he saw that the she-camel had been hamstrung, he said: You have violated the sanctity of God, so be glad of the punishment and vengeance of God, the Blessed and Exalted! Four men from the nine who had hamstrung the she-camel pursued the hump, and among them was Musad’ ibn Muharij. Musad’ shot him with an arrow, which pierced his heart, then he dragged him by his foot and made him fall, then they threw his flesh with the flesh of his mother. When Salih said to them: Be glad of the punishment and vengeance of God, they said to him mockingly: When will that be, O Salih? And what is the sign of that? They used to name the days among them: Sunday is the first, Monday is the easiest, Tuesday is the last, Wednesday is the tyrant, Thursday is the companion, Friday is the Arabah, and Saturday is the Shiyar. They had hamstrung the she-camel on Wednesday, so Salih said to them when they said that: You will wake up on the morning of the day of Mu’nis meaning Thursday, and your faces will be yellow. Then you will wake up on the day of the Arabah meaning Friday, and your faces will be red. Then you will wake up on the day of the Shiyar meaning Saturday, and your faces will be black. Then the punishment will come to you on the first day meaning Sunday. When Salih said that to them, the nine who had hamstrung the she-camel said: Come, let us kill Salih. If he is telling the truth, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will have caught up with his she-camel! So they came to him at night to spend the night with his family, but the angels struck them with stones. When they delayed their companions, they came to Salih’s house and found them crushed and stoned. They said to Salih: You killed them! Then they intended to attack him, but his clan stood up to protect him and put on their weapons and said to them: “By God, you will never kill him, for he promised you that the punishment would descend upon you in three days. If he is truthful, you will only increase your Lord’s wrath upon you, and if he is lying, then you will be behind what you want!” So they left them that night. The men whom the angels stoned were the nine whom God Almighty mentioned in the Qur’an, saying: And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform until His saying:
h
A sign for a people who know

. That night when they left Salih, their faces were yellow, and they were certain of the punishment, and they knew that Salih had told them the truth, so they sought him out to kill him. Salih fled from them until he took refuge in a tribe of Thamud, Banu Ghanim, and a man from them called Nufayl, who was a polytheist, descended upon their leader, and he hid him, but they could not find him. So they went to Salih’s companions and tortured them to lead them to him. Then a man from Salih’s companions called Mayda’ bin Harm said: O Prophet of God, they torture us to lead them to you, so shall we lead them to you? He said: Yes! So Mayda’ bin Harm led them to him. When they knew where Salih was, they went to Abu Hudb and spoke to him. He said to them: Salih is with me, and you have no way to him! So they turned away from him and left him, and the punishment that God had sent down upon them distracted them from him.

x: Some of them began to tell each other what they saw on their faces when they woke up on Thursday, and that their faces had become yellow, then on Friday they woke up with red faces, then on Saturday they woke up with black faces, until on Sunday night Salih went out from among them and those who had converted to Islam with him to Ash-Sham, and he settled in Ramlat Palestine, and a man from his companions called: Mayda’ bin Harm stayed behind, so he settled in Qurah - which is Wadi Al-Qura, and between Qurah and Al-Hijr there are eighteen miles - and a man called: Amr bin Ghanim stayed with their master, and he had eaten from the meat of the camel and had not participated in killing it, so Mayda’ bin Harm said to him: O Amr bin Ghanim, leave this country, for Salih said: Whoever stays in it will perish, and whoever leaves it will be saved, so Amr said: I had no part in hamstringing it, and I was not pleased with what was done to it!

When Sunday morning came, the cry overtook them, and none of them, young or old, remained who did not perish, except a crippled girl called Al-Zari'ah, who was a dog, the daughter of Al-Salq. She was an unbeliever and a fierce enemy of Salih. So God released her legs after she had witnessed all the torment, and she went out as quickly as anything had ever been seen, until she came to the people of Qurah and told them what she had witnessed of the torment and what had befallen Thamud from it. Then she asked for water and became ill, and when she drank she died.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told me,
m: he heard al-Hasan say: When Thamud hamstrung the she-camel, her foal went until it reached a hill and said: O Lord, where is my mother? Then it roared and roared, and the shout came down and silenced them.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: in a similar manner, except that he said: Ascend, and you will be rewarded.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: That Salih said to them when they hamstrung the she-camel: Enjoy yourselves for three days! And he said to them: The sign of your destruction is that your faces will become yellow, then on the second day they will become red, then on the third day they will become black, and so it became like that. So on the third day and they were certain of their destruction, they covered themselves and embalmed themselves, then the blast overtook them and rendered them indifferent. Qatada said: The one who hamstrung the she-camel said to them: I will not kill her until you are all satisfied! So they would enter upon the woman in her lap and say: Are you satisfied? She would say: Yes! And the child, until they were all satisfied, then he hamstrung her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by al-Hijr, he said: Do not ask for signs, for the people of Salih asked for them, and they would come from this pass and issue from that pass, but they rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung them. One day they would drink their water and one day they would drink their milk, but they hamstrung them, and a blast overtook them, and God extinguished everyone from them under the sky, except for one man who was in the sanctuary of God. It was said: Who is he? He said: Abu Righal. So when he left the sanctuary, what happened to his people happened to him. Abdul Razzaq said, Muammar said, and Ismail bin Umayya told me: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said: Do you know what this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best! He said: This is the grave of Abu Righal? They said: Who is Abu Righal? He said: A man from Thamud, who was in the sanctuary of God, and the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God. When he came out, what happened to his people happened to him, so he was buried here and buried with him a branch of gold! The people came down and rushed to him with their swords, and they searched for him and extracted the branch. Abdul Razzaq said, Muammar said, Al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal, Abu Thaqif.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim, on the authority of Jabir, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the stone, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said in his hadith: They said: Who is he, O Messenger of God? He said: Abu Righal.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was said that the red man of Thamud who hamstrung the she-camel was the son of fornication.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said, Abu Musa said:
m: I came to the land of Thamud, and I measured the length of the camel’s udder, and I found it to be sixty cubits.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, and Ismail ibn Umayya told me
