m: something similar to this - meaning something similar to the hadith of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim, on the authority of Jabir - he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the grave of Abu Righal. They said: Who is Abu Righal? He said: Abu Thaqif. He was in the Haram when God destroyed his people. The Haram of God protected him from the punishment of God. When he came out, what happened to his people happened to him, so he was buried here, and a golden branch was buried with him. He said: The people rushed to search for it until they extracted that branch. Al-Hasan said: The she-camel had one day and they had one day, so it harmed them.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by al-Hijr, he said: Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves unless you are weeping, lest what happened to them befall you! Then he said: This is the Valley of al-Nafar! Then he covered his head and hastened his pace until he crossed the valley. As for his saying:
h
And do not touch her with harm
, he is saying: And do not touch the she-camel of God by hamstringing or slaughtering, or a painful punishment will seize you, meaning: painful.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Salih said to his people, admonishing them: And remember, O people, God’s blessing upon you, when He made you successors, meaning: You succeed the ʿAd tribe on earth after its destruction. And caliphs is the plural of caliph. The plural of caliph is caliphs, and faʿala is the plural of faʿil, just as partners is the plural of partner, and scholars is the plural of ʿalim, and hulamaa is the plural of halim, because he referred to the caliph as a man, so one of them was khalif and then the plural of caliphs. But if you made the plural of caliph, as it is similar to kareema, haleela, and ragheeba, it would be called khalaif, just as you say karaeem, haleela, and raghaeb, since they are female attributes. The word khalifa was pluralized in both ways in the Qur’an, because it was pluralized once in its wording and once in its meaning. As for His statement,
h
And He settled you in the land
, He says:
h
And He settled you in the land
, and made for you therein dwellings and spouses.
You take palaces from its plains and carve out houses in the mountains, He mentioned that they used to carve out dwellings from the rock, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And you carve out houses in the mountains, they used to carve houses in the mountains. And His saying:
h
So remember the blessings of God
, means:
h
So remember the blessings of God
that He bestowed upon you, and do not spread corruption on the earth. Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not commit abuse on the earth

, spreading corruption, meaning: Do not walk on the earth spreading corruption. I have explained the meaning of that with its evidence and the differences of those who differed about it in the past, so that there is no need to repeat it in this place.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
The chiefs of his people who were arrogant said

, he said the group who were arrogant from the people of Salih about following Salih and believing in God and in him, those who were arrogant, meaning: the poor people among the followers of Salih and the believers in him among them, excluding those of them of honor and leadership among them, Do you know that Salih is a messenger from his Lord, that God sent him to us and to you? Those who believed in Salih from among the weak among them said: Indeed, we are believers in what God sent Salih with of the truth and guidance, meaning: believing and acknowledging that it is from God, and that God commanded it, and that it is the command of God that Salih called us to.

Those who were arrogant, about the command of God and the command of His Messenger Salih, said, Indeed, we, O people, in that in which you have believed", meaning: you believed in it from the prophethood of Salih, and that what he brought was the truth from God, "are disbelievers", meaning: deniers and deniers, we do not believe it nor do we acknowledge it.

God Almighty says: So Thamud hamstrung the she-camel that God had made a sign for them, and they were insolent toward the command of their Lord, meaning: they were arrogant and haughty in following God, and they were haughty toward the truth: just as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And they were insolent, they were above the truth, they do not see.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said:
m: They were insolent towards the command of their Lord, they were arrogant in falsehood.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saeed told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they were insolent towards the command of their Lord
, he said: They were insolent towards falsehood and abandoned the truth.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And they were insolent toward the command of their Lord, he said: They were arrogant in falsehood. It is from their saying:جبر َعْت, meaning he is high in his tyranny. And they said, ‘O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with,’ meaning they said: We have come, O Salih, with what you threaten us with of God’s punishment and vengeance, hastening the punishment, If you are one of the messengers, meaning: If you are God’s messenger to us, then God gives victory to His messengers over His enemies. So that happened to them just as they hastened it, God the Most High says: So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their homes fallen down.

x: God Almighty says: Then the earthquake seized those of Thamud who hamstrung the she-camel, which is the shout. And al-Rajfa is the verb from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so was shaken by such-and-such, meaning he moved and shook him, as al-Akhtal said: Either you show me my tenderness, gray hair from old age, trembling like an eagle, and a man exhausted What is meant by the earthquake here is the shout that shook them and moved them to destruction, because Thamud was destroyed by the shout, according to what the scholars have mentioned. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: The earthquake, he said: The shout.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then the earthquake seized them, which is the shout.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then the earthquake seized them, he said: the shout. And His statement:
h
So they became in their homes

, prostrated, meaning: So those whom God destroyed from Thamud became in their homes, meaning in their land in which they were destroyed and their town. For this reason, He made the word home singular, and did not make it plural by saying: in their homes. It may be possible that what was meant by it were the homes, but the singular was directed to all, as it was said: By declining day, indeed mankind is in loss. His saying: submerged means: fallen down, not moving, because there are no souls in them, they have perished. The Arabs say to someone kneeling on his knee: submerged, and from this is the saying of Jarir: I knew the farthest place, and I knew from it the mounts of destiny like the crouching kite And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they became in their homes
, prostrated, he said: dead.

x: God Almighty says: So Salih turned away from them when they hastened the punishment for him and hamstrung God’s she-camel, leaving their land from among them, because God Almighty revealed to him: I will destroy them after a third time. It was said: No nation perished while its prophet was among them. Then God, the Most High, informed us about the emergence of Salih from among his people who rebelled against their Lord when God wanted to bring down His punishment upon them. He said: Then he turned away from them, Salih, and said to his people, Thamud, I have indeed conveyed to you the message of my Lord, and I have conveyed to you what my Lord commanded me to convey to you of His commands and prohibitions, and I have given you sincere advice, in conveying God’s message to you, in warning you of His punishment for your persistence in your disbelief in Him and your worship of idols, but you do not like sincere advisers, in God’s sake, those who forbid you from following your whims and who turn you away from the desires of your souls.
God Almighty says: And We sent Lot. If it was said: Its meaning is: And remember Lot, O Muhammad,
h
when he said to his people
, since there was no connection to the message in the speech, as there was in the mention of Aad and Thamud, it would be a doctrine. And His saying:
h
When he said to his people
, he says:
h
when he said to his people
from Sodom, to whom he had sent Lot, Do you commit an immorality?

And the immorality that they were committing, for which God punished them, was intercourse with males, No one in the worlds has preceded you in doing it, he says: No one in the worlds has preceded you in doing this immorality, and that is like the one who:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar,
m: regarding his statement: No one in the worlds has preceded you with it, he said: No male was seen on a male until the people of Lot.

x: God Almighty informs us of this about Lot, that he said to his people, rebuking them for their actions: You, O people, approach men from behind, out of desire for that, instead of what God has permitted and made lawful for you from women. Rather, you are a transgressing people, meaning: You are a people who do what God has forbidden you, and you disobey Him by doing this. This is extravagance, in this case.

i: Desire is the action, and it is a source from the saying of the speaker: I desired this thing, I desired it with desire, and from that is the saying of the poet:
x: And I, disheveled and yearning for sleep, said to him: Go!
When the stars turn away and become arrogant. He stood up, dragging his feet, as if he had been told: Take it with your two hands! He would have fallen.

God Almighty says: And the response of the people of Lot to Lot, when he rebuked them for their ugly action and their committing what God had forbidden them of evil deeds, was nothing but that some of them said to one another: Bring out Lot and his family. Therefore, it was said: Drive them out, so it was plural, and it happened before mentioning Lot alone without others. It may be possible that the word was pluralized to mean: Expel Lot and whoever follows his religion from your village. So it was sufficient to mention Lot at the beginning of the speech without mentioning his followers, then it was pluralized at the end of the speech as was said: O Prophet, when you divorce women. We have explained similar examples of this previously, so there is no need to repeat it here.
h
They are people who purify themselves
, he says: Lot and those who followed him are people who abstain from what we do, which is having anal intercourse with men.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hani’ bin Sa’d Al-Nakha’i told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They are people who purify themselves
, he said: from the backsides of men and the backsides of women.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They are people who purify themselves
, from the backsides of men and the backsides of women.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
they are people who purify themselves
, he said: They purify themselves from the backsides of men and women.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Hasan ibn Amara told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They are people who purify themselves
, he said: from the backs of men and from the backs of the heavens.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
They are people who purify themselves
, he said: They are cautious.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They are people who purify themselves
, meaning: They criticised them without fault, and they censured them without censure.

x: God Almighty says: When the people of Lot refused - despite Lot’s rebuke of them for the immorality they were committing, and his conveying to them the message of his Lord prohibiting it for them - except to persist in their error, We saved Lot and his believing family, except for his wife, for she was a traitor to Lot and a disbeliever in God. And his saying: of those who have passed on, means: of those who remain. It was said: Of those who have passed away, and he did not say those who have passed away, because it was meant that she was among those who remained with the men. So when her mention was added to the mention of the men, it was said: Of those who have passed away. The verb is: ghabbar, yagbir, ghabbouran, and ghabran, which means to remain, as Al-A’sha said: Bite what the comforter left for him from a nation in the past As the other said: My father who conquered the country with his sword, then humiliated it for the ancient Banu Aban It means: the rest.
Was Lot’s wife among those who escaped the destruction that destroyed Lot’s people?
No, but it was for those who perished.
How is it said: Except his wife was among those who remained behind, and you said that the meaning of who remained behind is who remains? So it is necessary that she remained?

The meaning of that is not what you have gone to, but rather what he meant by that is that his wife was among those who remained before the destruction, and the long-lived ones who had lived a long time and had experienced a great deal of time, until she became old among those who grew old among the people, so she was among those who had passed a long time before the destruction of the people, so she perished with those who perished from the people of Lot when the punishment came to them.
It was said: The meaning of that is: among those who remain in the punishment of God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except an old woman among those who remain behind, in the punishment of God.

x: God Almighty says: And We rained down upon the people of Lot, who denied Lot and did not believe in him, a rain of stones of baked clay, with which We destroyed them. Then see how was the end of the criminals. God Almighty says: So look, O Muhammad, at the end of those who denied God and His Messenger from the people of Lot, so they committed the sins of God, committed indecencies, and made permissible what God had forbidden from the backsides of men. How was it, and what did it lead to? Was it anything but ruin and destruction? For that or something similar to it is the end of those from your people who denied you and were too arrogant to believe in God and confirm you if they did not repent.
God Almighty says: And We sent to the children of Madyan, and Madyan is his children, Madyan, son of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, in what:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq.
m: If the matter is as he said: then Madyan is a tribe of Kutmim. Ibn Ishaq also claimed that Shuʿayb, whom God mentioned that He sent to them, was from the descendants of this Madyan, and that he was Shuʿayb ibn Mikhail ibn Yashjar. He said: His name in Syriac is Jethro.

x: The interpretation of the statement, according to what Ibn Ishaq said: We sent to the sons of Madyan, their brother Shuʿayb ibn Mikail, calling them to obey God, to adhere to His command, and to abandon the pursuit of corruption on earth and to turn people away from His path. Shuʿayb said to them: O my people, worship God alone, with no partner for Him. You have no god who requires you to worship other than the God who created you, and in whose hand is your benefit and harm. There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, meaning: There has come to you a sign and an argument from God regarding the truth of what I say and the truth of what I am calling you to. So give full measure and weight, meaning: Complete the rights of people with the measure you use and the weight you use. And do not deprive people of their things, meaning: Do not wrong people with their rights or diminish them from them.

This includes their saying: You think she is foolish and unjust, meaning: unjust. This includes God’s saying: And they sold him for a cheap price, meaning: bad. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And do not deprive people of their things, he says: Do not wrong people in their things.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And do not deprive people of their due rights, he said: Do not wrong people in their due rights. And His statement:
h
And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation

, meaning: And do not commit acts of disobedience on the earth of God, and what you used to do before God sent His Prophet to you, of worshipping other than God and associating partners with Him, and cheating people in measure and weight, after its reformation, meaning after God had reformed the earth by sending the Prophet, peace be upon him, among you, forbidding you from what is not permissible for you, and what God hates for you, that is better for you, meaning: What I have mentioned to you and commanded you to do, of sincere worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, and fulfilling people’s rights in measure and weight, and leaving corruption on the earth, is better for you in your immediate worldly life and your afterlife with God on the Day of Resurrection, if you are believers, meaning: If you are truthful in what I say to you, and what I convey to you from God of His commands and prohibitions.

x: What he meant by his saying:
h
And do not sit on every path

, threatening, is that you do not sit - on every path - which is the path - threatening the believers with death. They used to, as mentioned, sit on the road of whoever intended to go to Shuʿayb and wanted him to believe in him, and they would threaten him and frighten him, and they would say: He is a liar!
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: On every path you are promised, he said: They were promised to whoever came to Shu’aib and approached him and wanted to convert to Islam.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not sit on every path
, threatening, and the path is the road, frightening the people by saying, Do not go to Shu’aib.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not sit on every path

, threatening and averting from the way of God, he said: They used to sit on the road and tell whoever came upon them: Shu’ayb, peace be upon him, is a liar, so do not let him tempt you away from your religion.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: By every path, he said: a road, you are promised, by every true path.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And do not sit on every path
, threatening, they used to sit on every path, threatening the believers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And do not sit on every path
, threatening, he said: the tax collectors.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Hajjaj told us, Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: or he said - Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi was not sure - he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came on the night of his Isra’ on a piece of wood on the road. No garment passed by it without it tearing it, and no thing without it tearing it. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is like people from your nation who sit on the road and cut it off! Then he recited: ‘
h
And do not sit on every path

, threatening and turning people away.’” This report that we mentioned on the authority of Abu Hurairah indicates that its meaning according to Abu Hurairah was: that the Prophet of God Shuaib only forbade his people by saying:
h
And do not sit on every path
, being threatened, from cutting off the road, and that they were highwaymen. It was also said:
h
And do not sit on every path

, being threatened. If it had been said in a place other than the Qur’an: Do not sit on every path, it would have been permissible and eloquent in speech. It was only permissible because the path is not a known place, so it was permissible just as it was permissible to say: He sat for him in such and such a place, in such and such a place, and in such and such a place. He said, You are promised, and did not say, You are promised, because the Arabs do the same with regard to threats that are vague and not made explicit. You say, I promised him, with the letter alif, and a threat came from me to him. But if you clarify what you threatened and make explicit, you say, I promised him good, and I promised him evil, without the letter alif, as the Most High said, The Fire is what God has promised those who disbelieve. As for his statement:
h
And you turn away from the path of God whoever believes in Him

, he says: And you turn away from the path of God, which is turning away from belief in God and working in obedience to Him, whoever believes in Him, he says: You turn away from the path of God whoever believes in God and His Oneness, and you seek to make it crooked, he says: And you seek for whoever follows the path of God and believes in Him and works in obedience to Him, a crookedness, from the straight path and the truth, to deviation and misguidance, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And you turn people away from the way of God, he said: its people, and you seek to make it crooked, you seek to make it Surat al-A’raf 7:86
h
And do not sit on every path

, threatening and averting from the way of God those who believe in Him and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He increased you, and see how was the end of the corrupters. deviate.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And you seek to make it crooked, he said: You seek to make the path crooked away from the truth.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And you turn people away from the path of God, from Islam, seeking the path, crooked, destruction. And His statement:
h
And remember when you were few and He multiplied you

, Shu’aib reminds them of the blessing of God upon them by increasing their group after they were few in number, and that He raised them from humiliation and baseness. He says to them: So thank God who has bestowed that blessing upon you, and worship Him sincerely, and fear His punishment by obeying Him, and beware of His wrath by abandoning disobedience. And see how was the end of the corrupters, He says: And see what happened to those nations before you when they rebelled against their Lord and disobeyed His messengers, of punishments and vengeance, and how they found the consequences of their disobedience to Him! Were not some of them destroyed by drowning in the flood, and some by stoning, and some by the blast? Corruption, in this context, means disobeying God.

x: What is meant by the words of God Almighty: And if there is a party among you, even if there is a group of you and a faction, who believe, he says: they believe in what I was sent with of sincere worship of God, abandoning His disobedience, oppressing people, and cheating them in measures and weights, then follow me in that, and a party do not believe, he says: and another group did not believe in that and did not follow me in it, then be patient until God judges between us, he says: then hold back on God’s judgment that decides between us and you, and He is the best of judges, he says: the father of the best of those who decide and the most just of those who judge, because there is no inclination towards anyone in his judgment, nor favoritism for anyone.

God Almighty says: The chiefs who were arrogant said, meaning by chiefs, the group of men, and by those who were arrogant, he means those who were too arrogant to believe in God, and to obey His command, and to follow His Messenger Shu'ayb, when Shu'ayb warned them of the punishment of God, for their disobedience to the command of their Lord, and their disbelief in Him, We will surely expel you, Shu'ayb, and those who followed you, believed in you, and believed in you and what you brought with you, from our city, or you must return to our religion, meaning: You and they must return to our religion and what we are upon. Shu'ayb said in response to them: Or even if we were reluctant. The meaning of the words: Shuʿayb said to his al-Nas 114:Will you expel us from your village and prevent us from the path of God, even if we are reluctant to do so? Then the interrogative alif was inserted into the waw of law.

God, the Most High, says: Shuʿayb said to his people when they called him to return to their religion and enter it, and threatened to expel him and those who followed him from their city if he and they did not do that: We have fabricated a lie against God, meaning: We have fabricated a lie against God and fabricated false statements about Him if we return to your religion, and we return to it after God has saved us from it, by seeing its error and the correctness of the guidance that we are upon. It is not for us to return to it and adhere to it and abandon the truth that we are upon, unless God, our Lord, wills, unless it was previously known to us that we would return to it, then God’s decree would be carried out for us, and He would execute His will upon us. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge, meaning: If our Lord’s knowledge encompasses all things and encompasses them, then nothing that was, and nothing that will be, is hidden from Him.

If He has previously known that we will return to your religion, and nothing that was or will be is hidden from Him, then what He previously knew must have happened. Otherwise, we will not return to your religion. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. He who said that: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: “We have fabricated a lie against God if we return to your religion after God has saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it unless God, our Lord, wills. Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. Upon God we have put our trust. Our Lord,
h
judge between us

and our people in truth.” He says: It is not appropriate for us to return to your polytheism after God has saved us from it, unless God, our Lord, wills. So God does not will polytheism, but we say: unless God has known something, for He has encompassed all things in knowledge.
And his saying:
h
In God we trust

, means: We rely on God in our affairs, and we rely on Him in what you threaten us with of your evil, O people, for He is sufficient for those who rely on Him. Then he, may God’s prayers be upon him, turned to his Lord to pray against his people, as he despaired of their success, and his hope of their submission to God in obedience and acknowledgment of His message was cut off, and he feared for himself and for those believers who followed him from his people from their wickedness and destruction, by the hastening of the punishment, so he said: Our Lord,
h
judge between us
and our people in truth, meaning:
h
Judge between us

and them with Your true judgment in which there is no injustice, unfairness, or oppression, but rather it is justice and truth, and You are the best of judges, meaning: the best of judges. Al-Farra’ mentioned that the people of Oman call the judge Al-Fatih and Al-Fattah.

Others who are knowledgeable about the Arabic language mentioned that it is from the language of Murad, and he recited a verse from one of them, which is: Shall I not send a messenger to Banu Asam that I am independent of your conquest? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: I did not know what his saying, Our Lord,
h
judge between us
and our people in truth, meant, until I heard the daughter of Dhi Yazan say: Come, let me open up to you, meaning: let me sue you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord,
h
judge between us
and our people in truth, meaning:
h
Judge between us
and our people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Dukayn told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, he said,
m: I heard Qatada say, Ibn Abbas said: I did not know what his saying meant: Our Lord,
h
judge between us
and our people in truth, until I heard the daughter of Dhi Yazan say: Come, let me open up to you.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Judge between us and our people with justice
, meaning:
h
Judge between us and our people with justice

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Judge between us and our people with justice
h
judge between us and our people with justice

. Surat al-A’raf 7:89 We would have fabricated a lie against God if we returned to your religion after God has delivered us from it. And it is not for us to return to it unless God, our Lord, wills. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Upon God we have relied. Our Lord,
h
judge between us
and our people in truth, for You are the best of judges.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for his saying:
h
Judge between us
, he says:
h
Judge between us

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said:
m: Deal between us and our people, and Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory (al-Fath 48:1), We have given you a clear judgment.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: Open, decide.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: I did not know what open the door between us and our people in truth meant, until I heard the daughter of Dhi Yazan say to her husband: Go, I will open the door with you.

x: God Almighty says: And the group of the unbelieving men of Shuʿayb’s people - and they are the elite - who denied the signs of God, belied His Messenger, and persisted in their error, said to others among them: If you follow Shuʿayb in what he says, and respond to what he calls you to of the oneness of God, and abiding by his commands and prohibitions, and acknowledge his prophethood, then you will be losers, meaning: you will be deceived by your actions, and by your abandoning your religion that you are established upon, for his religion that he calls you to, and you will perish because of that by your actions.

He says: So the earthquake seized those who disbelieved from the people of Shuaib. I have explained the meaning of the tremor before, and that it is the earthquake that triggers God’s punishment. So they became in their homes, kneeling, on their knees, dead and destroyed.
The description of the punishment with which God destroyed them was as follows:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shuʿayb, he said: God sent Shuʿayb to Madyan and to the people of the thicket, and the thicket is a thicket of trees, and they were cheating in measure and weight with their disbelief, so he called them but they denied him, so he told them what God mentioned in the Qur’an, and they did not respond to him. So when they rebelled and denied him, they asked him for punishment, so God opened for them a door from the gates of Hell, and its heat destroyed them, so neither shade nor water benefited them. Then He sent a cloud with a pleasant wind, and they found the coolness and pleasantness of the wind, so they called out to one another: The shade! Take it! So when they gathered under the cloud, their men, women and children, it closed in on them and destroyed them, so this is His saying: So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them (al-Shuʿara’: 189). Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: The story of Shuʿayb and his people was mentioned by God in the Qur’an. They were people who cheated people in their measures and scales, despite their disbelief in God and their denial of their Prophet. He used to call them to God and His worship, and to stop oppressing people and cheating them in their measures and scales. He advised them, and he was truthful: “I do not intend to go against you in that from which I forbid you. I only desire reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through God. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back.”
r

Ibn Ishaq said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned Shuʿayb, he would say: That is the orator of the prophets! This was because of his good argument with his people about what was intended for them. But when they denied him and threatened him with stoning and exile from their land, and rebelled against God, the punishment of the Day of the Shadow seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.

c: It was reported to me that
m: when a man from Madyan, called Amr ibn Jalha’, saw her, he said: O my people, Shuʿayb is a messenger, so leave behind Sameer and Imran bin Shaddad. I see a foolish woman, O people, who has come out, calling out in a loud voice from the valley's silence. And you will not see in it tomorrow morning anything but the old man walking among the hills. And Sameer and Imran, their priests, and Al-Raqeem, their dog.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us:
m: It reached me, and God knows best, that God sent heat upon them until it cooked them, then He created for them a shade like a black cloud. When they saw it, they rushed towards it, seeking relief from its coolness from the heat they were in. When they entered beneath it, it closed in on them, and they all perished. God saved Shuaib and those who believed with him by His mercy.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Abu Abdullah al-Bajali told me:
m: Abu Jad, Hawz, Kalmun, Sa’fas, and Qurasht were the names of the kings of Madyan. Their king on the Day of the Shadow in the time of Shu’ayb was Kalmun. Kalmun’s sister said, weeping for him: Talk to this corner man and kill him in the middle of the neighborhood The master of the people was met with death by fire in the middle of his own shadow. I made a fire upon them, their home is like a wasteland

x: God Almighty says: So He destroyed those who denied Shuʿayb and did not believe in him, so He annihilated them, and their city became empty and desolate of them, as if they had never dwelt therein, meaning: as if they had never settled there and had never lived there when they were destroyed. It is said: So-and-so is rich in such-and-such a place, so he is rich in it, if he resides there and is there, as the poet said: And your neighbors who are bound by your covenant and union will sing about it. Ru'bah said: And the covenant of the singer of Damna with Dulfa It is a verb from the root word ghana. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: As if they had not sufficed therein, as if they had not lived, as if they had not enjoyed themselves.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: As if they had not sufficed in it, he said: As if they had not lived in it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
As if they had never sung therein
, as if they had never been there. And His statement:
h
Those who denied Shuʿayb were the losers

, the Most High says: Those who followed Shuʿayb were not the losers, rather those who denied him were the losers who would perish. Because He, the Most High, informed us about them: Those who denied Shuʿayb said to those who wanted to follow him: If you follow Shuʿayb, then indeed you will be losers, so God denied them by bringing upon them the immediate punishment. Then He said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: It was not the followers of Shuʿayb who lost, rather it was those who denied Shuʿayb when God’s punishment came, who were the losers, not those who believed and had faith in him.

x: God Almighty says: So Shuʿayb turned away from them, standing out from among them when God’s punishment came to them, and he said when he was certain that God’s vengeance would descend upon his people who had denied him, grieving for them: O my people, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord, and I have delivered to you what He sent me with, of warning you of His wrath for your persistence in disbelief in Him, and the oppression of people of their things, and I have advised you, by commanding you to obey God, and forbidding you from disobeying Him - so how can I grieve, meaning: So how can I grieve for a people who denied the oneness of God and denied His Messenger, and feel pain for their destruction. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
How can I be sad
? means:
h
How can I be sad

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So
h
how can I be sad
? He said: So
h
how can I be sad

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Shuʿayb was overcome with grief over his people, because of what he saw of God’s vengeance upon them, then he said, consoling himself, in what God mentioned about him: O my people, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how can I grieve over a disbelieving people?

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, informing him of His way with the nations that had passed before his nation, and reminding those of the Quraysh who disbelieved in him, so that they would be deterred from what they were doing, which was associating partners with God and denying His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We did not send to any city a prophet before you, except that We seized its people with poverty and hardship, which is misery, hardship, and narrowness of life, and hardship, which is distress and bad conditions in their worldly affairs, that they might humble themselves, meaning: We did that so that they might humble themselves to their Lord and submit to Him, and turn back, by ceasing their disbelief, and repenting from denying their prophets. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: We seized its people with poverty and hardship, meaning: with poverty and hunger. We have previously mentioned the evidence for the correctness of what we said about the meaning of distress and adversity, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. It was said: They supplicate, and the meaning is: they supplicate, but the ta was assimilated into the dhad, because their points of articulation are close together.

x: God Almighty says: Then We replaced the people of the town whose people We seized with poverty and hardship, with bad in place of bad” which is poverty and hardship. And He made that bad because it is something that upsets people, and good which is ease, comfort, and abundance in living does not upset them, until they became abundant meaning until they became numerous.

i: Likewise, everything that is abundant is said about it: It has become obsolete, as the poet said:
x: But we bite the sword from it with the markets of the fat pile And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: In place of the bad, there is good, he said: In place of the hardship, there is ease, until they are forgiven.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: In place of the bad, there is the good, he said: The bad is evil, and the good is prosperity, money, and children.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Instead of the bad, there is the good. He said: The bad is evil, and the good is good.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We replaced the bad with the good
, meaning: the place of hardship is ease.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Then We replaced the bad with good until they repented
, he said: We replaced what they disliked with what they loved in this world, until they repented, of that torment,
h
and they said
, ‘Our fathers were touched by hardship and prosperity.’ They differed in the interpretation of his saying: until they pardoned.

x: Some of them said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: until they became numerous, meaning: until they multiplied and their wealth multiplied.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: Until they became free, he said: they became free.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: until they became wealthy, he said: their wealth and children increased.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Until they became numerous, until they became numerous.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheera, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Until they became numerous, he said: Until they became numerous and numerous. ... He said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Until they became free, he said: Until they became free. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: Until they became abundant, meaning: they gathered and multiplied. ... He said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Until they became plentiful, he said: Until their wealth and children increased.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: until they became abundant, they multiplied as plants and feathers multiplied, then He seized them suddenly while they were not aware.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: until they were happy.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said,
m: Surat al-A’raf 7:95 Then We replaced the evil with good until they pardoned and said, "Our fathers were touched by hardship and prosperity." But We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive.

c: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until they forgave, he said: until they were pleased with that.

x: What Qatada said about the meaning of pardon is an interpretation that has no basis in the speech of the Arabs. Because pardon is not known to mean joy in any of their speech, unless he meant: until they were pleased with their great number and the great amount of their wealth, in which case that would be a basis, even if it is far-fetched. As for his statement:
h
And they said

, ‘Our fathers were touched by hardship and prosperity,’ it is report from God about these people whom He replaced the good with the bad that they were in, as a lure and a test. They said when He did that to them: These are conditions that afflicted our fathers before us, and befell our ancestors, and we are nothing more than like them, afflicted by what afflicted them of hardship in life and prosperity in it, and it is prosperity, because it pleases its people. The poor people were ignorant of thanking God for His blessings, and out of their ignorance they neglected the continuity of His grace by turning to His obedience and hastening to give up what He hates by repenting, until His command came to them while they were not aware.

His Majesty says: So We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive. He says: So We seized them with destruction and torment suddenly. It came to them by surprise with its coming, and they did not know or realize that it would come to them. Rather, they were denying that it would come to them until they witnessed it and saw it.

"And if only the people of the towns had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they were earning."
Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come to them at night while they are asleep?
Or do the people of the towns feel secure against Our punishment coming upon them at noon while they are playing?

God Almighty says: “O Muhammad, do these people who disbelieve in God and His Messenger and reject His signs feel secure that God will lure them in with the blessings He bestowed upon them in this world of healthy bodies and comfortable living, just as He lured those nations before them whose stories He told them? For God’s plan does not make anyone feel secure - he says: no one feels secure from that being a lure, while they remain in their disbelief and persist in their disobedience - “except the people who are losers,” and they are the ones who will perish.

He says: Has it not been made clear to those who are appointed successors on the earth after the destruction of others before them who were its people, and who followed their ways, did their deeds, and were insolent towards the command of their Lord, that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins, meaning: that if We willed, We could do to them as We did to those before them, so We seized them for their sins, and hastened Our punishment upon them as We hastened to those who were before them from whom they inherited the earth, so We destroyed them for their sins, and set a seal upon their hearts, meaning: We seal their hearts, so they do not hear, admonition or reminder, hearing that benefits from both. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Has he not been guided? He said: It is clear.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. ... He said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Or was he not guided, or he did not clarify.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Has it not been made clear to those who inherit the earth after its people
? He said: Or has it not become clear to them?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Have they not been guided to those who inherit the earth after its people? He says: Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its people, they are the polytheists.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
Have there not been guidance for those who inherit the earth after its people

, or have We not made clear to them, that if We willed, We could have afflicted them for their sins, he said: And guidance is the explanation that was sent as a guide for them, explaining to them so that they would know. If it were not for the explanation, they would not have known.

x: God Almighty says: These towns that I have mentioned to you, O Muhammad, their situation and the situation of their people, meaning the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot and Shu'aib, We relate to you some of their report, so we inform you about them and the report of their people, and what happened to them and the situation of the Messengers of God who were sent to them, so that you may know that We support Our Messengers and those who believe in this worldly life against Our enemies and those who disbelieve in us, and so that those who deny you from your people may know what the consequences of denying the Messengers of God are, so that they may be deterred from denying you and turn to the Oneness of God and His obedience. And their Messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs, meaning: And the people of the towns whose situation I have related to you, their Messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs, meaning with clear arguments, but they would not believe in what they had denied before.
Then the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: These polytheists whom We destroyed from the people of the towns would not have believed when We sent to them what they hated before that, and that was on the day He took their covenant when He brought them out from the back of Adam, peace be upon him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They would not believe in what they denied before, he said: That was the day when the covenant was taken from them and they believed unwillingly.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They would not have believed when the messengers came, because God knew that they would deny it on the day He brought them out from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, on the authority of Abu Ibn Kaʿb:
m: So they would not believe in what they denied before, he said: It was in his knowledge on the day they acknowledged the covenant to him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, he said:
m: It is right for the servants to take from the knowledge that their Lord and the prophets have shown them, and to leave the knowledge of what God has hidden from them, for His knowledge is effective in what was and what will be, and in that He said: “And indeed, their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before.
h
Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers

,” he said: His knowledge was effective in them, which of them is obedient and which is disobedient, when He created them in the time of Adam. And the confirmation of that is when He said to Nuh 71:“Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon the peoples who are with you. And [there are] peoples whom We will grant enjoyment, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us”
r
. And He said in that:
h
And if they were returned

, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars (al-An’am 6:28). And in that He said: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger (al-Isra’ 17:15). And in that He said: So that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers
r
(An-Nisa’: 165)
. And no one has an argument against God.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They would not have believed in what they denied before, if We had brought them back to life after their destruction and their seeing what they saw of God’s punishment, as God Almighty said:
h
And if they were returned
, they would have returned to what they were forbidden (al-An’am 6:28).
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Because they denied it before, like His statement:
h
And if they were returned
, they would return to what they were forbidden (al-An’am 6:28).

x: The most similar of these sayings to the interpretation of the verse and the most correct is the saying that we mentioned from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and al-Rabiʿ. That is because whoever God, the Blessed and Exalted, knew that he would not believe in Him will never believe. And God, the Blessed and Exalted, knew that those nations that perished, whose story is told in this Surah, would never believe. So He, the Most High, informed us about them that they would not Surat al-A’raf 7:101 These towns - We relate to you some of their news. And their messengers had already come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before.
h
Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers

. believe in what they denied in His foreknowledge before the coming of the messengers when they came to them. And if it was said: Its interpretation is: So it was not those who inherited the earth, O Muhammad, from the polytheists of your people after its inhabitants, who were in it from Aad and Thamud, to believe in what those who inherited it from them denied of the oneness of God and His promise and His threat, it would be a view and a doctrine, but I do not know of anyone who said it from among those whose knowledge of the interpretation of the Qur’an is relied upon.

As for what Mujahid said, that its meaning is: If they were returned, they would not have believed, this is an interpretation for which there is no evidence from the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor from any authentic report from the Messenger. Since that is the case, then what is more correct than it is what there is evidence for from the apparent meaning of the revelation. As for His statement:
h
Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers

, the Most High says: Just as God set a seal upon the hearts of those who disbelieved in their Lord and disobeyed His messengers from among these nations whose story We have related to you, O Muhammad, in this surah, until the punishment of God came to them and they were destroyed by it,
h
Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers
, those upon whom it was decreed that they would never believe, from among your people.

God Almighty says: And we did not find for most of the people of these towns which we destroyed and which we related to you, O Muhammad, their report, any covenant, meaning: any fulfillment of what we commanded them to do, of the monotheism of God, following His messengers, working in obedience to Him, avoiding His disobedience, and abandoning the worship of idols and statues. The covenant is the will, and we have explained this previously in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And if We found most of them, he says: And We found most of them to be nothing but wicked, disobedient to their Lord, abandoning His covenant and His commandment. We have explained the meaning of wickedness before. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: And indeed, We found most of them to be wicked, he said: the past generations.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We did not find for most of them any covenant
, the verse, he said: the past generations. And His covenant, which He took from the children of Adam in the back of Adam and they did not fulfill it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, on the authority of Abu bin Kaʿb:
m: h
And We did not find for most of them any covenant
, he said: in the covenant that He took in the back of Adam, peace be upon him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And We did not find most of them to be true to their covenant, and indeed, We found most of them to be wicked. That is because God only destroyed the towns because they did not keep what He commanded them.

x: God Almighty says: Then We sent after Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, Moses, son of Imran. The ha and mim in His statement: after them are a metaphor for mentioning the prophets, peace be upon them, which were mentioned from the beginning of this surah to this place. With Our signs means: with Our arguments and proofs, to Pharaoh and his chiefs, meaning: to Pharaoh’s group of men, but they wronged them, meaning: they disbelieved in them. The ha and alif in his saying: with it refer to the verses. This means: They were unjust to Our signs that We sent to Moses. It is permissible to say: They were unjust to them in the sense of: they disbelieved in them, because injustice is putting something in the wrong place. I have previously demonstrated that this is its meaning, so there is no need to repeat it. And disbelief in the verses of God is placing them in the wrong place and diverting them to a purpose other than that for which they were intended. Then see how was the end of the corrupters. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So see, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, how was the end of those who corrupted the earth, meaning Pharaoh and his people, when they wronged the verses of God that Moses, peace be upon him, brought to them, and their end was that they were all drowned in the sea.
God Almighty says: And Moses said to Pharaoh: O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.
There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
It is true that I do not say about God except the truth

A group of the Meccan, Medinan, Basran and Kufan reciters read it as: It is true that I should not say about God except the truth, by sending the ya from ala, and leaving out the emphasis on it, meaning: I am true that I should not say about God except the truth. They directed the meaning of ala to the meaning of the ba, just as one says: I threw with the bow and on the bow, and I came in a good state and in a good state.
Some scholars of Arabic speech used to say: If it is read in this way, it means: I am keen not to say, or: It is right that I not say.

A group of the people of Medina read it as: It is obligatory upon me not to say, meaning: It is obligatory upon me not to say, and it is obligatory upon me not to say. Alo Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about that is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, and each one of them has been read by the imams of the recitation, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct in his recitation. And his saying:
h
I have come to you with a clear proof from your Lord

, meaning: Moses said to Pharaoh and his al-Nas 114:I have come to you with a proof from your Lord, which bears witness, O people, to the truth of what I say, and the truth of what I mention to you about God sending me to you as a messenger, so send, O Pharaoh, the Children of Israel with me.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: It is true that I do not say about God except the truth.

A group of the Meccan, Medinan, Basran and Kufan reciters read it as: It is true that I should not say about God except the truth, by sending the ya from ala, and leaving out the emphasis on it, meaning: I am true that I should not say about God except the truth.
Some scholars of Arabic speech used to say: If it is read in this way, it means: I am keen not to say, or: It is right that I not say.
A group of the people of Medina read it as: It is obligatory upon me not to say, meaning: It is obligatory upon me not to say, and it is obligatory upon me not to say.

Alo Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about that is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, and each one of them has been read by the imams of the recitation, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct in his recitation.

x: Then Pharaoh said to him: If you have come with a sign, meaning: an argument and a sign that testifies to the truth of what you say, then bring it if you are of the truthful.

God Almighty says: Then Moses threw down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent evident, meaning a snake. Evident, he says: it is evident to whoever sees it that it is a snake. And what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then it became a clear serpent, he said: It turned into a huge snake.

x: Another said: Like the city.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then it was a clear serpent
, meaning: Then it was a snake that almost climbed over him, meaning: it almost jumped on him.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And behold, it was a serpent manifest, and the serpent is the male of the serpents, opening its mouth, placing its lower jaw on the ground, and its upper jaw on the wall of the palace, then it headed towards Pharaoh to take it. When he saw it, he was terrified of it, and he jumped up and started talking, and he had never done so before, and he shouted: O Moses, take it, and I believe in you, and I will send the Children of Israel with you! So Moses took it, and it turned into a staff.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, he said, Abu Saada told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And behold, it was a serpent manifest, he said: He threw the staff and it became a snake, and it placed a seal for itself under the dome, and a seal for itself on top of the dome - Abdul Karim said, Ibrahim said: Sufyan pointed with his thumb and index finger like this: he likened the arch - and when it wanted to take it, Pharaoh said: O Moses, take it! So Moses took it in his hand, and it became a staff as it was the first time.

c: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Al-Asbagh bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub, who said, Saeed bin Jubair told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: He threw down his staff and it turned into a huge serpent, opening its mouth and rushing towards Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw that it was heading towards him, he rushed off his bed and called upon Moses to stop it from approaching him, and he did so.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A manifest serpent
, he said: The male snake.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me:
m: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When Moses entered upon Pharaoh, Pharaoh said to him: Do I know you? He said: Yes! He said: Did We not raise you among us as a child?
r
(Ash-Shu’ara’: 18)
. He said: So Moses returned to him what he had returned, and Pharaoh said: Take him! So Moses rushed to him and threw down his staff, and behold, it was
h
a manifest serpent
, and it charged at the people and they fled, and twenty-five thousand of them died, killing one another, and Pharaoh stood up in defeat until he entered the house.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say regarding His statement:
h
So he threw it down
, and behold, it was a serpent, darting about
r
(Ta-Ha: 20)
, he said: The distance between its jaws was forty cubits.

c: Wakiʿ told us, he said, ʿAbdah bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
Then it was a clear serpent
, he said: the male snake.

x: As for his saying:
h
And he took out his hand
, and behold, it was white to the beholders, he is saying:
h
And he took out his hand

, and behold, it was white, appearing to whoever among the people looked at it. Moses, as we have been told, was Adam, so God made his hand turn white without leprosy, as a sign for him, and an argument for the truth of his saying: I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Abbas told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Al-Asbagh bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub, he said, Saeed bin Jubair told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He took his hand out of his pocket and saw it white without any defect - meaning: without leprosy - then he put it back in his sleeve, and it returned to its original color.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: white to the observers, meaning: without leprosy.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And he took out his hand
, and behold, it was white to the beholders, he said: He took out his hand from his pocket, white, without leprosy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And he took out his hand
, he took it out of his pocket, and behold, it was white to the onlookers.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say regarding His statement,
h
And he took out his hand

, he said: He took his hand out of his pocket, and behold, it was white to the beholders, and Moses was a dark-skinned man, so he took out his hand and behold, it was white, whiter than milk, without disease, he said: without leprosy, as a sign for Pharaoh.

x: God Almighty says: The group of men from the people of Pharaoh and the nobles among them said, This, meaning Moses, peace be upon him, is a learned magician, meaning that he takes people’s eyes by deceiving them, until he makes them think that the staff is a snake, the man is white, and the thing is different from what it is. Hence it was said: The rain bewitches the earth, if it is generous to it, cutting off its plants from their roots, and turning the earth upside down, so it bewitches it with bewitchment, and the earth is bewitched, if that befalls it. So he likened the magician’s magic to that, because he makes the one he bewitches imagine that he sees something other than what it is. Hence the saying of Dhu al-Rummah in describing the mirage: And the enchantress of the eyes of the Mawami dances in her fragrant breezes And his saying: Knowledgeable, means: a magician who is knowledgeable in magic.

He wants to expel you from your land, the land of Egypt, the Coptic magicians. And Pharaoh said to the assembly: Then what do you command? He said: What do you command us to do about him? What do you advise us to do about him? It was said: So what do you command? The report of that is about Pharaoh, and Pharaoh was not mentioned, and something like that rarely comes in speech, and that is similar to his saying:
“The wife of Al-Aziz said: Now the truth has become clear. I did seek to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful. That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret.”
So it was said: That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret.
r
(Yusuf 12:52)
, from the words of Yusuf, but Yusuf is mentioned, and from that is his saying: (I said to Zaid, stand up, for I am standing), and he means: (So Zaid said, I am standing).
God Almighty says: The leaders of Pharaoh's people said to Pharaoh: Postpone it, meaning: delay it.

Some of them said: its meaning is: detain it. In Arabic, Irja’at means delay. It is said, I postponed this matter, or I postponed it, if you delay it. From this is the saying of God Almighty: You may postpone whichever of them you wish (al-Ahzab 33:51), you postpone. The hamza is from the speech of some of the Qais tribes, they say, I postponed this matter, and leaving the hamza is from the language of Tamim and Asad, they say, I postponed it. There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Medina and some of the Iraqis read it as arja without the hamza and with the ha in the accusative case.

i: Some of the Kufian reciters read it as arja without leaving the hamza and making the ha silent, according to the language of those who stop on the ha in the word makun in the connection, if what precedes it is moved, as the rajaz poet said:
x: Time has brought upon me a man and a hand that swears, and nothing can be repaired except corruption.

i: It fixes today and spoils tomorrow They may do the same with the feminine ending, saying: This is a talha tree that has come, as the rajaz poet said:
x: When he saw that he was neither satisfied nor satisfied, he went to a palm grove and lay down.
Some Basrans read it as: Arji’u with a hamza and a damma on the ha’, according to the language of the Qais tribe I mentioned.

The most correct of the readings in this regard is the most famous and most eloquent in the speech of the Arabs, which is leaving out the hamza and dragging the ha’, even though the other two are permissible. However, what we have chosen is the most eloquent of the languages and the most common on the tongues of the eloquent Arabs.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying: Postpone it.
Some of them said: It means: delay it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ata’ Al-Khurasani told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Postpone him and his brother
, he said: Delay him.

x: Others said: It means: Detain him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Postpone him and his brother
, meaning: Detain him and his brother. As for his saying:
h
And send gatherers into the cities
, he says: Who will gather the magicians and gather them to you? It was said: They are the condition.

x: Who said that?

c: Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Dhahir told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And he sent gatherers into the cities, he said: the police.

c: Ibn Wakhi’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And he sent gatherers into the cities, he said: the police. He said: Hamid told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And he sent gatherers into the cities, he said: the police.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Ismail bin Ibrahim bin Muhajir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of his son Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: In the cities, gathered together, he said: the condition.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And he sent gatherers into the cities, he said: the police.

evidence.text: The majority of the people of Medina and some of the Iraqis read it as arja without the hamza and with the ha in the accusative case.

Some of the Kufian reciters read it as arja without leaving the hamza and making the ha silent, according to the language of those who stop on the ha in the word makun in the connection, if what precedes it is moved, as the rajaz poet said: Time has brought upon me a man and a hand that swears, and nothing can be repaired except corruption.
Some Basrans read it as: Arji’u with a hamza and a damma on the ha’, according to the language of the Qais tribe I mentioned.

Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the readings in this regard is the most famous and most eloquent in the speech of the Arabs, which is leaving out the hamza and dragging the ha’, even though the other two are permissible.

x: This is report from God, may He be glorified, about the advice of the leaders of Pharaoh’s people to Pharaoh, to send gatherers into the cities to gather every learned magician. There is an omission in the speech. I will suffice with the apparent meaning of its manifestation, which is: So he sent gatherers into the cities, to gather the magicians.

And the magicians came to Pharaoh and said, 'Indeed, we have a reward from you,' meaning, We have a reward from you for defeating Moses, if we are, O Pharaoh, the victors." And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Abbas told us, Yazid told us, Al-Asbagh bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub, who said, Saeed bin Jubair told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: And he sent gatherers among the cities, and he gathered for him every sorcerer who pretended to be a magician. When they came to Pharaoh, they said: What does this magician do? They said: He works with snakes. They said: By God, there are no people on earth who work with magic, snakes, ropes, and sticks more knowledgeable than us. So what is our reward if we are defeated? He said to them: You are my relatives and my protectors, and I will do for you whatever you like.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Pharaoh said:
