m: We will not defeat him - meaning Moses - except with someone who is from him. So he appointed scholars from the Children of Israel and sent them to a village in Egypt called Al-Farma, to teach them magic as children are taught the Book in the Book. He said: So they taught them a lot of magic. He said: Moses made an appointment with Pharaoh, and when that appointment was made, Pharaoh sent and brought them and their teacher with them, and said to him: What have you done? He said: I have taught them magic that the magicians of the people of the earth cannot bear, unless it is a command from heaven, for they have no power over it. As for the magic of the people of the earth, it will not defeat them. So when the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh: Will there be a reward for us if we are the victors? He said: Yes, and then you will be among those brought near.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So Pharaoh sent summoners to the cities, and they summoned the magicians against him, And the magicians came to Pharaoh and said, ‘Indeed, for us is a reward if we are the victors.’ He said, A gift will be given to us, if we are the victors. He said, Yes, and indeed, you are among those brought near. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Put him and his brother on hold, and send to the cities gatherers * to bring you every learned magician. That is, multiply the magicians among them, so that you may find among the magicians someone who can do the same as he did. Moses and Aaron had left him when he showed them the power of God. Pharaoh sent magicians throughout his kingdom, and he did not leave a magician in his kingdom without bringing him to him. It was mentioned to me, and God knows best, that he had gathered fifteen thousand magicians. When they gathered around him, he gave them his orders and said to them: A magician has come to us, the likes of whom we have never seen before. If you defeat him, I will honor you, favor you, and bring you closer to the people of my kingdom! They said: And will we have that if we defeat him? He said: Yes!

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: The magicians were seventy.

x: I think he said: One thousand.
He said: Yahya bin Wadh told us, he said:

c: Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Mundhir, he said:
m: The magicians were eighty thousand.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of Abu Sawda, on the authority of Ka’b, who said:
m: Pharaoh’s magicians were twelve thousand.

x: God Almighty says: Pharaoh said to the magicians, when they said to him: Do we have a reward from you if we defeat Moses? He said: Yes, you have that, and you are among those closest and nearest to me.

They said, 'O Moses,' he says: The magicians said to Moses: O Moses, choose whether you throw down your staff, or we throw down our staffs. Therefore, (an) was included with (imma) in the speech, because it is in the position of a command to choose. So (an) is in the position of the accusative for what I described of the meaning, because the meaning of the speech is: Choose, you throw, or we throw, and the speech with (imma) if it is in the form of a command, then it is necessary that (an) be in it, like when you say to the man: (Either you go, or you sit), meaning the command: go or sit. So if it is in the form of a report, then there is no (an) in it, like his saying: And others are awaiting the command of God, either He will punish them or He will forgive them (al-Tawbah 9:106). This is what is called (choice), and so is everything that is in the form of a report, and (imma) in all of that is broken.

God Almighty says: Moses said to the magicians: Throw down what you are going to throw! So the magicians threw down what they had, and when they threw that, they bewitched the eyes of the people, they made the people's eyes imagine with what they created of illusion and deception that it was moving, and they terrified them, he says: and they terrified the people with what they bewitched in their eyes, until they feared the sticks and ropes, thinking that they were snakes, and they came, as God said, with a great magic, with a great and mighty illusion of imagination and deception.
And that is like that which:

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Moses said to them: Throw down what you are going to throw down! So they threw down their ropes and their staffs! They were thirty-odd thousand men, and there was not a man among them who did not have a rope and a staff. So when they threw down, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, meaning: they frightened them, so Moses felt fear within himself.

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: They threw thick, long ropes and long pieces of wood. He said: So she approached, and it seemed to him, because of their magic, that she was moving. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: Fifteen thousand magicians lined up, each with his own ropes and staffs. Moses went out with his brother, leaning on his staff, until they reached the assembly, and Pharaoh was in his council with the nobles of his kingdom. Then the magicians said: O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw. He said: Rather, throw. And suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him, because of their magic, to be crawling.”
r

The first thing they stole with their magic was Moses’ sight and Pharaoh’s sight, then the sight of the people after that. Then each man threw down the staffs and ropes that were in his hand, and suddenly they were serpents like mountains, filling the valley, one riding on the other. So Moses felt fear within himself.
r
and he said: By God, they were only staffs in their hands, but they have turned into serpents! And this staff of mine is not moving! Or something like that.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai, he said, al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza told us:
m: Pharaoh gathered seventy thousand magicians, and they threw down seventy thousand ropes, and seventy thousand sticks, until it seemed to him from their magic that they were moving.

x: God Almighty says: And We inspired Moses, Throw down your staff, so he threw it down, and behold, it swallowed up what they were bewitching, falsely and in vain. It is said: I caught the thing, so I catch it, and I catch it. Such as: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And We inspired Moses, ‘Throw down your staff.’ So Moses threw down his staff, and it turned into a snake, and it consumed all their magic.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told us, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, Sufyan told us, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So he threw down his staff and behold, it was a snake devouring what they were fabricating. It did not pass by anything of their ropes or wood that they had thrown down without devouring it. So the magicians knew that this was a command from heaven, and that this was not magic, so they fell down in prostration and said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: God revealed to Moses: Do not be afraid, and throw down what is in your right hand and it will swallow up what they are fabricating. So he threw down his staff, and every snake ate them. When they saw that, they prostrated themselves and said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that God revealed to him: Throw down what is in your right hand! So he threw down his staff from his hand, and it looked back at what they had thrown down of their ropes and staffs, and they were snakes in the eyes of Pharaoh while the eyes of the people were crawling, so it began to scoop them up and swallow them, snake by snake, until little or much of what they had thrown down could be seen in the valley. Then Moses took it, and behold, it was his staff in his hand as it had been, and the magicians fell down in prostration, saying: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron. If this had been magic, it would not have overcome us!

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai, he said, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza told us:
m: God revealed to him: Throw down your staff! So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent with its mouth open, and it swallowed their ropes and staffs. Then the magicians fell down in prostration, and they did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell and the reward of their people.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: They slander, he said: They lie.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then it swallows up what they are fabricating, he said: They are lying.

c: Ibrahim bin Al-Mustamir told us, he said, Othman bin Omar told us, he said, Qara bin Khalid Al-Sadosi told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He swallows up what they fabricate, he said: Their ropes and sticks, he stretches them out.

x: God Almighty says: So the truth appeared and became clear to those who witnessed it and were present in the matter of Moses, and that he was God’s Messenger calling to the truth, and what they were doing was nullified, of the slander of magic, its lies, and its illusions. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then the truth occurred, he said: it appeared.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ismail bin Ibrahim bin Muhajir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So the truth came into effect
, and what they were doing was nullified, he said: The truth appeared, and the slander that they were doing was gone.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then the truth came to pass
, he said: The truth appeared.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Then the truth came to pass
, Moses appeared.

x: God Almighty says: So Moses defeated Pharaoh and his army, there at that time, and they turned back in humiliation, meaning: and they left their place in humiliation and defeat. It is said: The man’s youth becomes smaller, smaller, smaller, smaller.
God Almighty says: And the magicians were thrown down, when they saw the great power of God, falling on their faces, prostrating to their Lord.

They say: We believe in the Lord of the Worlds, they say: We believe in what Moses brought us, and that the One we must worship is the One who owns the jinn and mankind and all things, and other than that, and He manages all of that.
The Lord of Moses and Aaron, not Pharaoh, as the one who:

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said,
m: when the magicians saw what they saw, they knew that it was a command from heaven and not magic, so they fell down in prostration and said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.

x: God Almighty says: Pharaoh said to the magicians when they believed in God, meaning they believed in His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, when they witnessed the great power and authority of God: You believed in him, meaning: you believed in Moses and acknowledged his prophethood, before I gave you permission, to believe in him, This, meaning: your belief in him and your acknowledgment of his prophethood, is a plot you plotted in the city, meaning: a trick you deceived them with from our city, to expel them from it, and you will soon know, what I will do to you, and what punishment you will receive from Me for this action of yours. Their plot was that: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, in a hadith he mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik, and Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Moses and the leader of the magicians met, and Moses said to him: Tell me, if I defeat you, will you believe in me and testify that what you have brought is the truth?

The magician said: I will come tomorrow with magic that no magic can defeat, and by God, if you defeat me, I will believe in you and testify that you are the truth! And Pharaoh was looking at them, and this is what Pharaoh said: This is indeed a plot you have plotted in the city, when you met to show support so that its people could leave it.

God Almighty says, informing about what was said about the magicians when they believed in God and believed in His Messenger Moses: I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, meaning that He cuts off one of them’s right hand and left foot, or He cuts off his left hand and right foot, so that the two limbs are cut off differently, and His difference in that between them is (cutting off on opposite sides). It is said that the first person to institute this cutting was Pharaoh, Then I will crucify you all. Pharaoh only said this when he saw God abandoning him and Moses, peace be upon him, prevailing over him and subduing him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Dawud Al-Hafri and Habawayh Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Ya’qub Al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja’far Ibn Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: I will surely cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then I will crucify you all, he said: Or on crucified ones, and the first to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides was Pharaoh.

x: God Almighty says: The magicians said in response to Pharaoh, when he threatened them with the cutting off of their hands and feet on opposite sides, and with crucifixion: Indeed, to our Lord we will return, meaning by returning to God, returning to Him and destined for Him.
And His statement:
h
And you do not blame us for anything except that we have believed in the signs of our Lord
, meaning that you do not blame us, O Pharaoh,
h
and you do not blame us for anything except that we have believed in the signs of our Lord

, meaning that you have confirmed them, in the signs of our Lord, meaning that you have proofs, signs, and evidence that neither you nor anyone else can match, except God, to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. Then they turned to God, asking Him to grant them patience in the face of Pharaoh's torment and the taking of their souls while they were in Islam, and they said: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience, meaning by their statement, pour out, send down upon us a detainment that will prevent us from disbelieving in You when Pharaoh tortured us, and let us die as Muslims, meaning that we should take you to Yourself in Islam, the religion of Your friend Abraham, peace be upon him, not in associating partners with You.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, so he killed them and crucified them, as Abdullah bin Abbas said, when they said: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and let us die as Muslims. He said: They were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of the day.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, who said:
m: The sorcerers were sorcerers at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of the day.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And the magicians fell down prostrating, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and let us die as Muslims. He said: They were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of it.

x: God Almighty says: And a group of men from among Pharaoh’s people said to Pharaoh: Will you leave Moses and his people from among the Children of Israel, to cause corruption in the land, meaning: so that they may corrupt your servants and slaves against you in your land of Egypt, and abandon you
h
and your gods
, meaning: and abandon you, and abandon your service to Moses and your worship and the worship of your gods. In his saying:
h
And leaves you and your gods

, there are two aspects of interpretation. One of them: Do you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption on earth, while he has abandoned you and abandoned your worship and the worship of your gods? If the speech is directed to this aspect of interpretation, the accusative in his saying: and leaves you is in the form of a declension, not in conjunction with his saying: to cause corruption. The second: Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land, and to leave you
h
and your gods
? is like their rebuke to Pharaoh for leaving Moses to do these two actions.
If the speech is directed in this way, and leave you would be in the accusative case in apposition to to spread corruption.
The first aspect is the more correct of the two aspects, which is that the accusative of and He leaves you is in the genitive case, because the interpretation came from the people of interpretation.
And then, in the reading of Abi bin Kaab who:

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said:
m: In the letter of Abi bin Kaab: (And they have abandoned you to worship you
h
and your gods
). A clear indication that this is an accusative.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri
m: that he used to recite this: And He will leave you
h
and your gods
, linking his saying: And He will leave you to his saying: Will you leave Moses? It is as if he directed its interpretation to: Will you leave Moses and his people, and he will leave you
h
and your gods
, to spread corruption on earth? This reading of Al-Hasan may mean: Do you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption on earth, while he leaves you
h
and your gods
? Thus, leaves you is raised by the beginning of the speech and safety from accidents. As for his saying:
h
And your gods
, the reading of the regions is with the opening of the alif in it and its extension, meaning: Moses has abandoned your worship and the worship of your gods that you worship.

c: It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said:
m: He had a cow that he worshipped.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid
m: that they used to recite it: And He leaves you
h
and your gods
with a kasra on the alif, meaning: And He leaves you and your worship.

x: The reading that we do not see as a reading other than it is the reading that the regions read, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers on it. It was mentioned that Pharaoh used to worship gods, according to the reading of the one who read: And he will leave you
h
and your gods

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And He leaves you
h
and your gods

, and his gods, according to what Ibn Abbas claimed, were cows. When they saw a beautiful cow, he ordered them to worship it, so for that reason he brought out for them a calf, a cow. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Abu Sufyan narrated: Amr narrated: Al-Hasan narrated: Pharaoh had a jewel hanging from his throat, which he worshipped and prostrated to. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated: Abaan ibn Khalid narrated: I heard Al-Hasan say: It has reached me that Pharaoh used to worship a god in secret, and he recited: And he will abandon you
h
and your gods

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Pharaoh had a god whom he worshipped in secret. He mentioned those who said: The meaning of that is: And he leaves you and your worship, according to the reading of those who read: (
h
and your gods

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And he leaves you
h
and your gods
, he said: Surat al-A’raf 7:127 And the leaders of Pharaoh's people said, "Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and abandon you
h
and your gods

?" He said, "We will kill their sons and spare their women, and indeed, we are over them dominant." Pharaoh was only worshipped and not worshipped. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Nafiʿ bin ʿUmar, on the authority of ʿAmr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: that he recited,
h
And leaves you and your gods
, he said: And your worship, and he said: He was worshipped and was not worshipped.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said: Muʿawiyah told me, on the authority of ʿAli bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And leaves you and your gods
, he said: He abandons your worship.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he used to recite: And your deity, meaning: And your worship.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And leaves you and your gods
), he said: your worship.

c: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Hassan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he used to recite: And leave you
h
and your gods
, and he said: Pharaoh was only worshipped and not worshipped.

x: Some of them claimed that whoever reads:
h
and your gods
intends something similar to the meaning of the reading of whoever reads:
h
and your gods
, except that he made it feminine while he meant one god, as if he meant: and he leaves you and your god, then you are the god, so he said:
h
and your gods

. Some Basrans mentioned that an Arab was asked about the goddess, and he said: It is a sign, meaning: a sign. So he feminized the sign, as if it were something set up for worship. Bint Utaybah bin Al-Harith bin Shihab Al-Yarboui said: We left the palace and hastened the goddess to return In this context, goddess means the sun.

i: It is as if this person who interpreted this interpretation, addressed the goddess, since he inserted the feminine ha into it, and he meant one goddess, similar to their insertion of the ha into my birth, my planet, and my hundred, which is that crescent, and as the rajaz poet said:
x: Oh, Mudar Al Hamra, you are my family, you are my refuge, and you are my support.

He wants: my back. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid explained what they intended by the meaning in their reading of it as they read it, so there is no reason for this speaker to say what he said, with their explanation of what they intended by the meaning of that. And his saying: He said, ‘We will kill their sons,’ means: Pharaoh said: We will kill their male children from the children of the Children of Israel, and spare their women, meaning: And we will spare their females, and indeed, We are over them, dominant, meaning: And We are superior to them by force, meaning by force of kingship and authority. We have shown that everything is high by force and dominance over something, as the Arabs say: He is above it.

evidence.text: And then, in the reading of Abi bin Kaab who:
It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to recite this: And He will leave you and your gods, linking his saying: And He will leave you to his saying: Will you leave Moses?
This reading of Al-Hasan may mean: Do you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption on earth, while he leaves you and your gods?

As for his saying: And your gods, the reading of the regions is with the opening of the alif in it and its extension, meaning: Moses has abandoned your worship and the worship of your gods that you worship.
It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid that they used to recite it: And He leaves you and your gods with a kasra on the alif, meaning: And He leaves you and your worship.
Abu Jaafar said: The reading that we do not see as a reading other than it is the reading that the regions read, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers on it.
It was mentioned that Pharaoh used to worship gods, according to the reading of the one who read: And he will leave you and your gods.
He mentioned those who said: The meaning of that is: And he leaves you and your worship, according to the reading of those who read: (and your gods).

Some of them claimed that whoever reads: and your gods intends something similar to the meaning of the reading of whoever reads: and your gods, except that he made it feminine while he meant one god, as if he meant: and he leaves you and your god, then you are the god, so he said: and your gods.

Ibn Abbas and Mujahid explained what they intended by the meaning in their reading of it as they read it, so there is no reason for this speaker to say what he said, with their explanation of what they intended by the meaning of that.

x: God Almighty says: Moses said to his people, from the Children of Israel, when Pharaoh said to the leaders of his al-Nas 114:(We will kill the sons of the Children of Israel and keep their women alive), Seek help from God, against Pharaoh and his people in what befalls you in your affair, and be patient, in the face of the hardships that befell you in yourselves and your children from Pharaoh.
And Moses had been followed by the Children of Israel in what:

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the magicians believed, six hundred thousand of the Children of Israel followed Moses. And His statement: “Indeed, the earth belongs to God. He gives it as an inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants,” meaning: The earth belongs to God. Perhaps God will give you as an inheritance, if you are patient with the harm that befell you and your children from Pharaoh, and you seek reward for that, and you remain steadfast in the right path, the land of Pharaoh and his people, by destroying them and making you successors in it. Indeed, God gives His land as an inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous, meaning: The praiseworthy outcome is for the one who fears God and is mindful of Him, so he fears Him by avoiding His disobedience and performing His obligations.

x: God Almighty says: The people of Moses said to Moses, when he said to them: Seek help from God and be patient, “We have been harmed,” by the killing of our sons, before you came to us, meaning: before you came to us with God’s message to us, because Pharaoh was killing their male children when the time of Moses came upon him, as I have explained previously in this book of ours. And his saying:
h
And after you came to us
, he says:
h
And after you came to us

with God’s message, because when Pharaoh’s magicians were defeated, and he said to the leaders of his people what he said, he wanted to renew the punishment upon them by killing their sons and taking their women captive. It was said: The people of Moses said that to Moses when they feared that Pharaoh would catch up with them while they were fleeing from him. The two armies saw each other and said to him: O Moses, We were harmed before you came to us, they used to slaughter our sons and keep our women captive,
h
and after you came to us
, today Pharaoh will catch up with us and kill us.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: before you come to us, before God sent you and after it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: So when the two armies saw each other and the Children of Israel saw Pharaoh behind them, they said, Indeed, we are to be overtaken. And they said, We were harmed before you came to us, they used to slaughter our sons and keep our women alive, and after you have come to us, today Pharaoh will overtake us and kill us, we are to be overtaken.

c: Abdul Karim told me, Ibrahim told us, Sufyan told us, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Moses walked with the Children of Israel until they attacked the sea, so they turned and saw the beasts of Pharaoh roaring, and they said: O Moses, we were harmed before you came to us
h
and after you came to us

, this sea is in front of us, and this is Pharaoh and those with him! He said: It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land and see how you act. And His statement: He said: It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy, God Almighty says: Moses said to his al-Nas 114:Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy Pharaoh and his people, and make you successors, meaning: He will make you succeed them in their land after their destruction, not fearing them or anyone else, and see how you act, meaning: Your Lord will see what you do after them, from your haste in obeying Him, and your reluctance to do so.

x: God Almighty says: And We tested the people of Pharaoh and his followers for their misguidance, with years, meaning: with drought year after year, and famine. It is said: The people became barren, if they became barren. And a decrease in the fruits, meaning: We tested them with drought by causing their fruits and crops to disappear, except for a little, so that they might remember, meaning: A lesson for them and a reminder to them, so that they would be deterred from their misguidance and turn to their Lord with repentance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years
of famine, he said: years of famine.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: by the years, the catastrophe, and a decrease in the fruits, less than that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim bin Dinar told me, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Raja bin Haywah,
m: regarding his statement: And a reduction in the fruits, he said: When the palm tree does not bear more than one fruit.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of Ka’b, who said:
m: A time will come upon the people when the palm tree will bear nothing but fruit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Raja’ bin Haywah:
m: And a decrease in the fruits, he said: A time will come upon the people when the palm tree will bear nothing but fruit.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years

, God seized them with years, with famine, year after year, and a decrease in the fruits, as for years, that was in their desert and with their livestock, and as for a decrease in the fruits, that was in their cities and villages.

x: God Almighty says: So when the people of Pharaoh were visited by health, fertility, prosperity, and an abundance of fruits, and they saw what they loved in their worldly life, they said, ‘This is for us,’ meaning we are more deserving of it, but if a bad thing befalls them, meaning drought, famine, and calamity, they take ill omen from Moses and those with him, meaning they take them as bad omens, and say: Our fortunes and our portions of prosperity, fertility, and health have gone since Moses, peace be upon him, came to us. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when good comes to them
, well-being and prosperity, they say, ‘This is for us,’ we are more deserving of it, but if evil befalls them, a calamity or a punishment, they take an omen, they have bad omens about Moses.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
But when good comes to them, they say, This is for us, but if evil befalls them, they ascribe an evil omen to Moses and those with him.
They said: This has not befallen us except because of you, O Moses, and those with you. We have not seen evil nor has it befallen us until we saw you! And His statement:
h
But when good comes to them, they say, This is for us.

He said: Good is what they love. And when it is what they dislike, they say, This has not befallen us except because of the evil of those who did wrong! The people of Salih said: We ascribe an evil omen to you and those with you. So God said:
h
Your evil omen is with God. Rather, you are a people being tested.
(al-Naml 27:47) The statement in the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, their omen is with God, but most of them do not know.

x: God Almighty says: Behold, what is the bird of the people of Pharaoh and others? That is their share of prosperity and fertility and other shares of good and evil, with God, but most of them do not know, that this is so, so because of their ignorance of that they were flying with Moses and those with him. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Behold, their ill omen is with God, meaning: Their misfortunes are with God. God said: But most of them do not know.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: Behold, their omen is only with God, he said: The matter is from God.

x: God Almighty says: And the people of Pharaoh said to Moses: O Moses, whatever sign or indication you bring us, to bewitch us, meaning: to distract us from the religion of Pharaoh, we will not believe you, meaning: we will not believe you in that, that you are right in what you are calling us to. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of magic, so there is no need to repeat it.
Ibn Zayd used to say about the meaning of
h
whatever sign you bring us
, what:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whatever sign you bring us
, he said:
h
Whatever sign you bring us
, and this has an additional what in it.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the flood.
Some of them said: It is water.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, Habawayh Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Ya’qub al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When Moses came with the signs, the first of the signs was the flood, so God sent the sky upon them.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Malik, he said:
m: The flood means water.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: The flood means water. ... He said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The flood means drowning.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The flood is water, and the plague is death in any case.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told me, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The flood is death in every case.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The flood means water.

x: Others said: Rather, it is death.
Who said that?

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, Al-Munhal bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Mina’, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The flood is death.

c: Abbas bin Muhammad told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I asked Ata’: What is the flood? He said: Death.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The flood means death.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer:
m: h
So We sent upon them the flood
, he said death. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked Ata’ about the flood, he said: death. Ibn Jurayj said: And Mujahid said: death in every case.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Khalifa, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The flood is death.

x: Others said: Rather, it was an order from God that came to them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
So We sent upon them the flood
, he said: God commanded the flood, then he recited: And a company from your Lord swept over them while they were asleep (al-Qalam 68:19).

x: Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable about the Arabic language claimed that the flood comes from the word toor which means torrential rain and torrential rain which means severe. And from death, it means extremely rapid and severe.

Some of them said: It is a lot of rain and wind. Some Kufi grammarians used to say: The flood is a verbal noun like al-rajhan and al-naqsan and is not pluralized. Some Basra grammarians used to say: It is a plural, and its singular form in analogy is al-tufanah.

The correct statement regarding this, in my opinion, is what Ibn Abbas said, according to what Abu Dhibyan narrated from him: that it was a command from God that swept over them, and that it is a source of the saying of the speaker: (The command of God swept over them, swept over them, a flood), just as it is said: (This thing decreased, decreases). If that is the case, then it is possible that what befell them was heavy rain, and it is possible that it was a terrible death. And among the indications that heavy rain may be called a flood is the saying of Hasil bin Arfatah: Surat al-A’raf 7:133
h
So We sent upon them the flood

and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a people of criminals. Other than its signs, the wind is piercing and the rain is torrential. It is narrated: The wind blew with the rain And the shepherd said: If the camels catch up with us, they will sacrifice their misfortunes, accustomed to floods and provisions.
And Abu Al-Najm said: The flood has spread, and it has spread a month of rain and a month of cold. As for lice, the interpreters differed about its meaning.
Some of them said: It is the weevil that comes out of the wheat.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ya’qub al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Lice is the weevil that comes out of wheat.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: It is the locust, which is a small locust that has no wings.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said,
m: Lice means the locust.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The lice are the lice.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Lice is the lice.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Lice means the locust.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Lice is the locust, which is the offspring of locusts.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jaber bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Lice means lice. ... He said: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of someone who mentioned it, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Lice are the daughters of locusts.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: (Lice) means the locust.

x: Others said: Rather, lice means fleas.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
So We sent upon them the flood
, the locusts, and the lice, he said: Some people claimed that the lice were fleas.

x: Some of them said: They are small black animals.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said,
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Hasan say: Lice are small black insects.

x: Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from Basra claimed that al-Qaml among the Arabs means al-Hamnan, and al-Hamnan is a type of monkey, the singular of which is Hamnanah, above al-Qamqamah. Lice is a plural, and its singular is louse. It is a creature that resembles lice and is eaten by camels, as far as I have heard. It is what Al-A’sha meant in his saying:
h
A people whose children are treated with lice

, their grandfathers with chains, and their doors are locked. Al-Farra’ used to say: I did not hear anything about it. If it is a plural, then its singular is qamil, like sajid and raki’. If it is a noun with the meaning of qamlah, then its singular is qamlah. Mentioning the meanings that occurred to the people of Pharaoh as a result of these signs occurring, and the reason for which God caused them to occur to them. Ibn Hamid narrated that Yaqub al-Qummi narrated on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn al-Mughira on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr who said: When Moses came to Pharaoh, he said to him: Send the Children of Israel with me!

But Pharaoh refused, so God sent the flood upon them - which is rain - and poured some of it on them. They feared that it was a punishment, so they said to Moses: Ask your Lord to remove the rain from us, so that we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon his Lord, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. So He caused to grow for them that year something that had not grown before of crops, fruits, and pasture. They said: This is what we wished for. So God sent locusts upon them and let them destroy the pasture. When they saw their traces in the pasture, they knew that they would not leave the crops. So they said: O Moses, ask your Lord to remove the locusts from us, so that we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the locusts from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him!

They trampled and seized the lice in the houses, and said: We have seized them! Then God sent lice upon them - which are mites that come out of them - and a man would take ten sacks to the mill, but he would not return even three of them. They said: O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove the lice from us, so that we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon his Lord and He removed them, but they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. While he was sitting with Pharaoh, he heard the croaking of a frog. Pharaoh said: What will happen to you and your people from this? He said: What could this plot be? By nightfall, a man was sitting up to his chin among the frogs, and he was about to speak when the frogs jumped into his mouth. They said to Moses: Call upon your Lord to remove these frogs from us, so that we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you!

So he removed it from them, but they did not believe. So God sent blood upon them, and whatever they drew from rivers and wells, or whatever was in their vessels, they found it to be spoiled blood. So they complained to Pharaoh and said: We have been afflicted with blood, and we have no drink! He said: He has bewitched you! They said: Where did he bewitch us, when we do not find any water in our vessels except that we find it spoiled blood? So they came to him and said: O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove this blood from us, so that we will believe in you, and send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Habawayh Abu Yazid told us, on the authority of Ya’qub al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When they feared drowning, Pharaoh said: O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove this rain from us, so that we may believe in you. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Ya’qub.

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: Then God sent upon them - meaning upon the people of Pharaoh - the flood, which is rain, and everything they had was drowned. They said: O Moses, ask your Lord to remove it from us and we will believe in you, and we will send the Children of Israel with you! So God removed it from them, and their crops grew with it. They said: It would not please us if we did not receive rain! So God sent locusts upon them, and they ate their crops. They asked Moses to ask his Lord to remove it, and they would believe in him. So he called, and He removed it, and a remnant of their crops remained. They said: Why do you believe, and a remnant of our crops remains that would suffice us? So God sent upon them the locust - which is the louse - and it licked the entire ground, and it would enter between the clothing of one of them and his skin and bite it. And one of them had food, and it would fill up with locusts, to the point that one of them would build a column with plaster, and he would slip it so that nothing could rise above it. He would raise the food above it, and when he went up to eat it, he would find it full of flies. They were not afflicted with a calamity that was more severe for them than the flies - which is the (devilship) that God mentioned in the Qur’an that befell them - so they asked Moses to call upon his Lord to remove it from them and they would believe in Him. But when He removed it from them, they refused to believe. So God sent blood upon them, and the Israelite and the Copt would come to draw water from one water, and the Copt’s water would come out as blood, and the Israelite’s water would come out as water. When that became too much for them, they asked Moses to remove it and they would believe in him, so he removed it, but they refused to believe, and that is when God says: But when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their promise (al-Zukhruf 43:50).

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then We sent upon them the flood, he said: God sent water upon them until they stood in it, then it was removed from them and they did not believe, and their land became fertile in a way that had never been fertile before, then God sent locusts upon them and they ate it except for a little, so they did not believe either. Then God sent lice - which are the offspring of locusts - and they ate what remained of their crops, so they did not believe. Then God sent frogs upon them, and they entered their homes and fell into their vessels and bedding, so they did not believe. Then God sent blood upon them, so when one of them wanted to drink, that water would turn into blood. God said: Detailed Signs. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari' narrated, Sa'id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
Then We sent upon them the flood until he reached criminals

, he said: God sent water upon them until they stood in it, so they called upon Moses, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned to the evil that was coming upon them. Then their land grew, then God sent upon them locusts, and they ate most of their crops and fruits. Then they called upon Moses, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned to the evil that was coming upon them. Then God sent upon them lice, this was the scorpion that you saw, and it ate what the locusts left of their crops, and licked it. So they called upon Moses, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned to the evil that was coming upon them. Then God sent upon them frogs until they filled their houses and courtyards. So they called upon Moses, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. Then they returned with evil that had not come to them, so God sent blood upon them, and they would not scoop from their water except red blood, so much so that it was mentioned that the enemy of God, Pharaoh, would gather two men in one vessel, the Copt and the Israelite, so that what was near the Israelite would be water, and what was near the Copt would be blood. So they called upon Moses, and he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, in nine signs: years and a decrease in fruits, and He showed them the hand of Moses, peace be upon him, and his staff.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
So We sent upon them the flood
, which is rain, until they feared destruction, so they came to Moses and said: O Moses, pray to your Lord to remove the rain from us, we will believe in Surat al-A’raf 7:133
h
So We sent upon them the flood

and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a people of criminals. you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he prayed to his Lord, and He removed the rain from them. So God caused their crops to grow and made their land fertile with it, but they said: We do not like that we did not receive rain for abandoning our religion, so we will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you! So God sent locusts upon them, and they hastened the corruption of their fruits and crops, so they said: O Moses, pray to your Lord to remove the locusts from us, so we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you! So he prayed to his Lord, and He removed the locusts from them. There were remnants of their crops and livelihood, but they said: We have enough left for us, so we will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you. Then God sent lice upon them - which are termites - and they followed what the locusts had left behind. They were alarmed and felt doomed, so they said: O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove the locusts from us, for we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the locusts from them. They said: We will not believe in you, nor will we send the Children of Israel with you! So God sent frogs upon them, and they filled their homes with them, and they suffered severe harm from them, the like of which they had never suffered before. They would jump into their pots, spoil their food, and extinguish their fires. They said: O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove the frogs from us, for we have suffered from them afflictions and harm, for we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon his Lord, and He removed the frogs from them. They said: We will not believe in you, nor will we send the Children of Israel with you! Then God sent blood upon them, and they would eat nothing but blood and drink nothing but blood. They said: O Moses, ask your Lord to remove the blood from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon his Lord, and the blood was removed from them. They said: O Moses, we will not believe you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you! So there were detailed signs, one after the other, so that God would have an argument against them. Then God seized them for their sins and drowned them in the sea.

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The signs were sent upon the people of Pharaoh: locusts, lice, frogs, and blood, detailed signs. He said: So a man from the Children of Israel would ride with a man from Pharaoh’s people in the ship, and the Israelite would scoop up water, and the Pharaoh would scoop up blood. He said: And a man from Pharaoh’s people would sleep on one side, and the lice and frogs would multiply around him until he was unable to turn over to the other side. And they did not stop until God revealed to Moses: Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When Moses came with the message to Pharaoh, he refused to believe and to send the Children of Israel with him, so they were arrogant. He said: I will not send the Children of Israel with you! So God sent upon them the flood - which is water - and it rained upon them until they were almost destroyed, and everything was withheld from them, so they said: O Moses, call upon your Lord for us according to what He promised you, if you remove this from us, we will believe in you and we will send the Children of Israel with you! So he called upon God and He removed the rain from them, so God caused their crops to grow for them, and with that rain He revived everything in their land, so they said: By God, we would not like it if we had not received this rain, it would have been better for us, so we will not send the Children of Israel with you, and we will not believe in you, O Moses! Then God sent locusts upon them, and they ate most of their crops, and the locusts quickly destroyed them. They said, O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove the locusts from us, for we will believe in you, and we will send the Children of Israel with you! So God removed the locusts from them. The locusts had left them a remnant of their crops, so they said, We have enough of our crops left, so we will not abandon our religion, and we will not believe in you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you! So God sent lice upon them - and lice is the locust that does not have wings - and it hunted down what was left of their crops, their trees, and every plant that they had. The lice were more severe on them than the locusts, so they could not do anything to deal with the lice, and they were alarmed by that. They came to Moses and said, “O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove the lice from us, for they have left us nothing; they have eaten what is left of our crops! If you remove the lice from us, we will believe in you, and we will send the Children of Israel with you!” Then God removed the lice from them, but they broke their oath and said: We will not believe you, and we will not send the Children of Israel with you! Then God sent frogs upon them, and the houses were filled with them, and there was no food or drink for them except that it contained frogs. They encountered something from it that they had never encountered before, and they said: O Moses, call upon your Lord for us, that if You remove this punishment from us, we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you! So God removed this punishment from them, but they did not do so. Then God revealed: But when We removed the punishment from them for a term they were to reach, at once they broke their oath to and were heedless of it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Abu Tamila told us, Al-Hasan bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The frogs were wild, and when God sent them to the people of Pharaoh, they heard and obeyed, so they began to drown themselves in the pots while they were boiling, and in the ovens while they were bubbling, so God rewarded them for their good obedience by cooling the water.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: So the enemy of God - meaning Pharaoh, when the magicians believed - returned defeated and shackled, then he refused to remain in disbelief and persist in evil, so God continued to punish him with signs, and took him with years, so He sent upon him the flood, then locusts, then lice, then frogs, then blood, detailed signs. Then He sent the flood - which is water - and it overflowed the face of the earth and then stagnated, and they were unable to plough or do anything, until they were exhausted from hunger. When that reached them, they said: O Moses, call upon your Lord for us, that if You remove this punishment from us, we will believe in you and we will send the Children of Israel with you! Then Moses called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfill any of what they said. So God sent locusts upon them, and they ate the trees, as I have heard, until they ate the iron nails of doors, until their houses and dwellings fell down. They said as they said, so he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfill any of what they said. Then God sent lice upon them, and it was mentioned to me that Moses was ordered to walk to a sand dune and strike it with his staff. So he went to a huge sand dune and struck it with it, and lice swarmed upon them until they covered the houses and food, and prevented them from sleeping and resting. When they were exhausted from doing so, they said to him as they had said, so he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfill any of what they had said. So God sent frogs upon them, and they filled the houses, food, and vessels, so that no one uncovered a garment, food, or vessel except that he found frogs in it that had overwhelmed it. When they were exhausted from doing so, they said to him as they had said, so he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfill any of what they had said. So God sent blood upon them, and the water of Pharaoh's people turned into blood. They did not draw water from a well or a river, nor did they scoop from a vessel, except that it turned into fresh blood.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi: That he said:
m: A woman from the family of Pharaoh would come to a woman from the Children of Israel when they were overcome by thirst, and she would say: Give me some of your water to drink! So she would scoop it for her from her jar or pour it for her from her waterskin, but the water would return to the vessel as blood, until she would say to her: Put it in your mouth, then pour it into my mouth, and she would take water in her mouth, and when she poured it into her mouth it would turn into blood, and they remained in that state for seven days.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The locusts will eat their crops and plants, and the frogs will fall on their bedding and food, and blood will be in their homes, their clothes, their water, and their food. He said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: When the Nile flowed with blood, the Israelite would draw pure water, and the Pharaoh would draw blood, and they would share one vessel, so what was near the Israelite would be pure water, and what was near the Pharaoh would be blood.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said, Saeed bin Jubair narrated to me:
m: When Moses dealt with Pharaoh with the four signs: the staff, the hand, the decrease in fruits, and the years, he said: O Lord, this servant of yours has become arrogant and transgressed on the earth, and he has transgressed against me and transgressed against you, and transgressed against his people. O Lord, take your servant with a punishment that will be a punishment for him and his people, and a lesson for my people, and a sign for those who come after me among the remaining nations! So God sent upon them the flood - which was water - and the houses of the Children of Israel and the houses of the Copts were intertwined and mixed with each other, and the houses of the Copts were filled with water until they stood in the water up to their collarbones. Whoever of them sat was drowned, and not a drop entered the houses of the Children of Israel. So the Copts began to call out to Moses: Call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you: If you remove this punishment from us, we will believe in you and we will send the Children of Israel with you! He said: So they made a covenant with Moses, and he took their covenants from them. The water had taken them on the Sabbath, and remained for seven days until the next Sabbath. Then Moses called upon his Lord, and He removed the water from them, and their land became green from that water. They remained in good health for a month, then they denied it and said: This water was nothing but a blessing to us, and fertility for our land. We would not like it not to have been. He said: Someone said to Ibn Abbas: I asked Ibn Omar about the flood and he said: I do not know, was it death or water! Ibn Abbas said: Doesn’t Ibn Omar read Surat Al-Ankabut when God mentioned the people of Noah and said: So the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers (al-Ankabut 29:14). Have you seen, if they had died, to whom did Moses, peace be upon him, come with the four signs after the flood? Moses said: O Lord, Your servants have broken Your covenant and failed to fulfill My promise. O Lord, take them with a punishment that will be a punishment for them, a lesson for my people, and a sign for those who promise them among the remaining nations! So God sent locusts upon them, and they did not leave a leaf, tree, flower, or fruit without eating it, until there was no fruit left. When they had destroyed all the greenery, they ate the wood, and even ate the doors and roofs of the houses. The locusts were afflicted with hunger, and they were never satisfied, except that they did not enter the houses of the Children of Israel. So they swarmed and cried out to Moses, and they said: O Moses, this time call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you: If you remove this punishment from us, we will believe in you and we will send the Children of Israel with you! So they gave him the covenant and pledge of God, so he called upon his Lord for them, and God removed the locusts from them after they had remained upon them for seven days Surat al-A’raf 7:133
h
So We sent upon them the flood

and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a people of criminals. from Saturday to Saturday. Then they stayed for a month in good health, then they returned to their denial and rejection and their evil deeds. He said: Moses said: O Lord, Your servants have broken My covenant and failed to keep My promise, so punish them with a punishment that will be a punishment for them, a lesson for my people, and a sign for those who come after me among the remaining nations! So God sent lice upon them. Abu Bakr said: I heard Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Hasan say: There was a dusty dune next to them in a village in Egypt called Ain Shams, so Moses walked to that dune and struck it with his staff so that lice began to crawl towards them, and they are small black creatures. The lice crawled towards them and took their hair, skin, eyelashes, and eyebrows, and stuck to their skin as if they were running on them, so they cried out and cried out to Moses: We will repent and not return, so call upon your Lord for us! So he called upon his Lord and He removed the lice from them after they had stayed on them for seven days from Saturday to Saturday. They stayed for a month in peace, then they returned and said: We were never more certain that he was a magician than we are today. He turned the sand into beasts, and Pharaoh's glory made him so strong that we will never believe him or follow him! So they returned to their denial and rejection, so Moses invoked against them and said: O Lord, Your servants have broken My covenant and failed to keep My promise, so take them with a punishment that will be a punishment for them, a lesson for my people, and a sign for those who come after me among the remaining nations! So God sent frogs upon them, and one of them would lie down and the frogs would ride him, and they would pile up on him until he could go to the other side and open his mouth to eat, but the frog would beat his food to his mouth, and he would not knead dough except that it would lie down in it, and he would not cook a pot except that it would fill with frogs, so they were tortured with the most severe torture, so they complained to Moses, peace be upon him, and they said: This time we will repent and not return! So he took their covenant and pledge. Then he called upon his Lord, and God removed the frogs from them after He had established seven days over them from Sabbath to Sabbath. They remained in good health for a month, then they returned to their denial and rejection, and said: His magic has become clear to you; he turns the dust into beasts, and brings forth frogs in the absence of water! So they harmed Moses, peace be upon him, and Moses said: O Lord, Your servants have broken My covenant and failed to fulfill My promise, so take them with a punishment that will be a punishment for them and a lesson for my people, and a sign for those who come after me among the remaining nations! So God afflicted them with blood, and corrupted their livelihoods. The Israelite and the Copt would come to the Nile to draw water, and water would come out for the Israelite, and blood would come out for the Copt. They would go to the grain in which there was water, and water would come out for the Israelite in his vessel, and blood would come out for the Copt.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid regarding his statement:
h
So We sent upon them the flood

, he said: death, and locusts, he said: locusts eat their belongings, their clothes, and the nails of their doors, and lice, he is the scorpion, God sent it upon them after the locusts, he said: and frogs, they fall into their food in their homes and into their drinks.

x: Some of them said: The blood that God sent upon them was a nosebleed.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, Yahya ibn Abi Bakr told us, Zuhair told us, Zaid ibn Aslam said:
m: As for lice, they are lice, and as for blood, God sent nosebleeds upon them. As for His statement: detailed signs, its meaning is: signs and indications of the truth of Moses’ prophethood and the truth of what he called them to. Detailed, He separated between them, making some of them follow others, and some of them follow others. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: So there were detailed verses, one after the other, so that God would have an argument against them, so God seized them for their sins, and drowned them in the sea.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: detailed verses, he said: They follow one another, so that God may have an argument against them, and then He will take revenge on them. And the verse would remain with them from Saturday to Saturday, and would be lifted from them for a month. God Almighty said: So We took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea, the verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq said:
m: Detailed verses, meaning: verse after verse, one following the other. Mujahid used to say, in what was mentioned about him regarding the meaning of the joints, what:

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say about detailed verses, he said: information.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
So they were arrogant and were a criminal people

God Almighty says: “These people, upon whom God sent what was mentioned in these verses and arguments, were too arrogant to believe in God and to believe in His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, and to follow him in what he called them to. They acted arrogantly towards God and were insolent towards Him. ‘And they were a criminal people.’” He says: They were a people who did what God hates of sins and immorality, insolently and rebelliously.
God Almighty says:
h
And when the punishment fell upon them
, and when God’s punishment descended upon them and His wrath descended upon them. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding that disaster that God said had befallen these people.
Some of them said: It was a plague.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: Moses commanded his people from the Children of Israel, and that was after he had brought to the people of Pharaoh the five signs: the flood and what God mentioned in this sign, but they did not believe and did not send the Children of Israel with him, so he said: Let each man among you slaughter a ram, then let him dip his hand in its blood, then let him strike it on his door! The Copts said to the Children of Israel: Why do you treat this blood on your doors? They said: God will send a punishment upon you, so we will submit and you will perish. The Copts said: How does God know you except by these signs? They said: This is what our Prophet commanded us to do! So they woke up and seventy thousand of Pharaoh’s people had been stabbed, and they spent the night not burying each other. Then Pharaoh said at that: Call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you, if you remove the plague from us, meaning the plague, we will believe in you and we will send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them. The most faithful of them all was Pharaoh. He said to Moses: Go with the Children of Israel wherever you wish.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Habawayh Al-Razi and Abu Dawud Al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair - Habawayh
m: said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - If You remove the calamity from us, he said: the plague.

x: Others said: It is torment.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Al-Rajz means torment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: So when We removed the punishment from them, meaning the torment.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And when the punishment fell upon them
, meaning: the torment.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when the punishment fell upon them

, he said: The punishment is the torment that God inflicted upon them from locusts and lice and other things, and they would make a covenant with Him and then break it. We have explained the meaning of rajaz in the previous part of this book, with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

x: The more correct of the two sayings in this context is to say: God, the Most High, mentioned that when the punishment befell Pharaoh and his people, which is the torment and wrath of God upon them, they turned to Moses and asked his Lord to remove that from them. It is possible that that punishment was the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, because all of that was a torment upon them. It is possible that that punishment was a plague, and God did not tell us which of those things it was, nor was there any authentic report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which of those things it was, so we submit to it. So it is correct to say about it as God, the Most High, said: And when the punishment befell them, and we do not go beyond that except with the explanation that there is no objection to among the people of interpretation, which is: when the punishment and wrath of God befell them.

They said, O Moses, call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you. He says: according to what He has commanded and ordered you to do. We have explained the meaning of covenant previously. If you remove the punishment from us, meaning: if you lift the torment we are in, we will believe in you, meaning: we will believe in what you have brought and called to, and we will acknowledge it for you, and we will send with you the Children of Israel, meaning: we will leave the Children of Israel with you, and we will not prevent them from going wherever they wish.

God Almighty says: Then Moses called upon his Lord, and He answered him. Then when God lifted from them the punishment that He had sent down upon them, for a term they would reach, to complete the punishment of the days that God had set for them in life, until the time of their destruction, at once they broke their covenants, meaning: when they broke their covenants that they had made with their Lord and Moses, and persisted in their disbelief and misguidance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Until a term they will reach, he said: A number specified for them from their days.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So when We removed the punishment from them for a term they were to reach, at once they broke it. He said: What they had given of covenants, which is when God says: And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years, which is famine, and a loss of fruits that perhaps they would remember.
