x: God Almighty says: So when they broke their covenants, (We took revenge on them), meaning: We took revenge on them by inflicting Our vengeance on them, and that is His punishment, So We drowned them in the sea, which is the ocean, as Dhu al-Rummah said: The darkness of the night is like a sea on whose edges the Romans are chattering.

i: As the rajaz poet said:
x: The sea gave him a drink Because they denied Our signs, meaning: We did that to them because they denied Our proofs and signs that We showed them, and they were heedless of them, meaning: They were heedless of the punishment that We brought upon them, before it came upon them, that it was a condition upon them.

The letter ha and the letter alif in his saying: from it are a metaphor for mentioning vengeance. If someone said: It is a metaphor for mentioning the verses, and the interpretation of the statement was directed to: And they were turning away from them, so he made their turning away from them a neglect of them since they did not accept them, that would be a doctrine. It is said from (negligence), (The man was negligent about something, he was negligent, negligently, and negligently).

God Almighty says: And We gave as an inheritance to the people whom Pharaoh and his people oppressed, slaughtering their sons, keeping their women alive, and using them as slaves and enslavement from the Children of Israel, the eastern regions of the earth, meaning the Levant, which is what is east of it, and its western regions which We have blessed, in which We made goodness a permanent fixture for its people. God Almighty said: And We gave him an inheritance, because He gave that to the Children of Israel by destroying the Amalekites who were there. And similar to what we said about His statement: the easts of the earth and its wests, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We caused the people who were oppressed to inherit the eastern regions of the earth and the western regions which We had blessed
, he said: the Levant.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, he said,
m: I heard al-Hasan say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: The land which We have blessed, he said: Ash-Sham. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And We gave as an inheritance to the people who were oppressed the eastern regions of the earth and the western regions which We had blessed
, referring to the land of Ash-Sham. Muhammad bin Abd al-A’la narrated, on the authority of Muhammad bin Thawr, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
The eastern regions of the earth and the western regions which We had blessed

, referring to the land of Ash-Sham. Some Arabists claimed that the easts and wests of the earth is in the accusative case, meaning: And We gave the people who were oppressed the easts and wests of the earth inheritance, and that his saying, And We gave them inheritance, was in reference to his saying, which We blessed. This is a meaningless statement, because the Children of Israel were not oppressed during the days of Pharaoh except by Pharaoh and his people, and he had no authority except in Egypt. So it is not permissible, and the matter is thus, to say: those who are oppressed are in the east and west of the earth.

x: If someone says: Its meaning is: in the east and west of the land of Egypt, then that is far from the concept in the speech, while it is outside the sayings of the people of interpretation and scholars of exegesis. As for his saying:
h
And the good word of your Lord has been fulfilled

, he says: And in the promise of God that He promised the Children of Israel, He fulfilled it as He promised them, of establishing them in the land, and His victory for them over their enemy Pharaoh, and His good word, His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: “And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them heirs * And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared.” (Al-Qasas, 28:5-6). And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel, he said: The people of Moses prevailed over Pharaoh, and God established him in the land, that is, what he inherited from it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told me, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. As for his statement:
h
And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making
, he says:
h
And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making

of buildings and farms, and what they were building, he says: and what they were building of buildings and palaces, and We expelled them from all of that, and We destroyed all of that. We have explained the meaning of arbouring previously, with its evidence. Surat al-A’raf 7:137 And We caused the people who were oppressed to inherit the eastern and western regions of the land which We had blessed, and the good word of your Lord was fulfilled upon the Children of Israel because of their patience.
h
And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making
and what they were building. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And they did not build, meaning: they did not build.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They build trellises, they build houses and dwellings as much as they can, and their grapes were not trellised.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. There are different readings of this. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as ya’rashūn with a kasra on the ra’, except for Asim ibn Abi al-Najūd, who read it with a damma on the ra’.

x: They are two well-known languages among the Arabs. It is said: Arsh ya’rash and ya’rash. If this is the case, then whichever reading the reader recites, he is correct, because the meanings of both are the same, and they are both well-known in the speech of the Arabs. The Arabs do the same with the verb faʿala when they refer it to the future tense, sometimes adding a damma to the ‘ayn and sometimes adding a kasra to it. However, the reading I prefer is the kasra to the ra’, because of its popularity among the public, the frequency with which it is recited, and because it is the more correct of the two languages.

evidence.text: The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as ya’rashūn with a kasra on the ra’, except for Asim ibn Abi al-Najūd, who read it with a damma on the ra’.
However, the reading I prefer is the kasra to the ra’, because of its popularity among the public, the frequency with which it is recited, and because it is the more correct of the two languages.

x: God Almighty says: And We crossed the sea with the Children of Israel after the signs that We showed them, and the lessons that they witnessed at the hands of the Prophet of God, Moses. But those signs did not deter them, nor did those lessons and clear proofs admonish them! Until they said, despite witnessing the arguments that are worthy of mentioning animals with, when they passed by a people who were devoted to their idols - he says: they were standing on an example of theirs that they worshipped instead of God - Make for us O Moses (a god), he says: an example that we worship and an idol that we take as a god, just as these people have idols that they worship. And worship is not appropriate for anything other than God, the One, the Subduer. And Moses, peace be upon him, said: You, O people, are a people who are ignorant of the greatness of God and the obligation of His right upon you, and you do not know that it is not permissible to worship anything other than God, to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth.
It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Jurayj regarding this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me:
m: And We crossed the sea with the Children of Israel and they came upon a people who were devoted to their idols. Ibn Jurayj said: On their idols. He said: Statues of cows. So when it came to the Samaritan’s calf, it appeared to them that it was from those cows, and that was the beginning of the matter of the calf: They said, ‘O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods.’ He said, ‘Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly.’ It was said: The people who were devoted to their idols, whom God mentioned in this verse, were people from Lakhm.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Bishr bin Omar told us, he said, Al-Abbas bin Al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Awam, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then they came upon a people who were devoted to their idols, he said: On Lakhm. It was said that they were Canaanites whom Moses, peace be upon him, was ordered to fight. And: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, “that Abu Waqid al-Laythi said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before Hunayn, and we passed by a lote tree. I said: O Prophet of God, make this Dhat Anwat for us as the infidels have a Dhat Anwat - and the infidels used to hang their weapons on a lote tree and worship around it - so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is Great! This is like what the Children of Israel said to Moses: ‘Make for us a god as they have gods’. You will follow the ways of those who came before you.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sinan bin Abi Sinan,
m: “on the authority of Abu Waqid al-Laythi, he said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before Hunayn, and we passed by a lote tree, so we said: O Prophet of God, make this Dhat Anwat for us, and he mentioned something similar.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sinan bin Abi Sinan, on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Sinan bin Abi Sinan Al-Dailami told me,
m: “On the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laythi: That they went out from Mecca with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Hunayn. He said: And the infidels had a lote tree near which they would worship, and they would hang their weapons on it, and it was called Dhat Anwat. He said: So we passed by a great green lote tree, he said: So we said: O Messenger of God, make for us a Dhat Anwat. He said: You said, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, what did the people of Moses say: “Make for us a god as they have gods?” He said: Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. These are the ways, you will follow the ways of those who were before you.”

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about what Moses said to his people from the Children of Israel. God, the Most High, says: Moses said to them: Indeed, those who are devoted to these idols, God owns what they are doing of work, and He corrupts it and makes them lose it, by rewarding them for it with a humiliating punishment, and what they were doing is in vain, of their worship of it, so it is in vain because it will not benefit them when God’s command comes and descends upon their court, nor will it defend them from God’s punishment if it descends upon them, nor will it save them from His punishment if He punishes them on the Day of Resurrection, so it is in the meaning of what was not. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Musa ibn Harun told us, he said, Amr ibn Hammad told us,
m: they both said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: Indeed, what they are in is ruined, meaning: what they are in is ruinous.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, what they are in is ruined, meaning: loss.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, these people will perish in what they are doing, and in vain is what they used to do, he said: This is all one, like the form of: (Forgiving, Most Merciful), (Pardoning, Most Forgiving). He said: The Arabs say: (Indeed, the wretched one will perish), and (Indeed, the wretched one will be at a loss).

x: God Almighty says: Moses said to his al-Nas 114:Shall I make you equal to God, and make for you a god whom you worship, while God, who is your Creator, has favored you over the people of your time and age? He says: Shall I make for you a god who neither benefits you nor harms you, whom you worship and leave the worship of the One Who has favored you over creation? This is indeed ignorance on your part!

God Almighty says to the Jews of the Children of Israel who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God: And remember, along with what you said to Moses after you saw the signs and lessons, and after the blessings that preceded from Me to you, and the favors that preceded, and what you did, when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, and they were those who followed his path and method in disbelief in God from his people, who subjected you to the worst of torment, meaning: when they burdened you with the worst and worst of torment. We have previously explained in this book what kind of punishment they were subjected to. They kill your sons, meaning their male children, and spare your women, meaning they keep their females alive. And in that is a great trial from your Lord, meaning that in their inflicting upon you a terrible punishment, it is a test from God for you and a great blessing.

God Almighty says: And We appointed for Moses to converse with Us for thirty nights. And it was said that they were thirty nights of Dhul-Qi'dah. And we completed it with ten, meaning: We completed the thirty nights with ten nights, completing forty nights. It was said: The ten days that he completed with it were forty, the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We appointed for Moses thirty nights
and completed them with ten, he said: Dhul-Qa’dah and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. ... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And We appointed for Moses thirty nights
and completed them with ten, he said: Dhul-Qi’dah and ten of Dhul-Hijjah. They differed about that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We appointed for Moses thirty nights
, that is, Dhul-Qi’dah and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. So that is what He said:
h
So the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said,
m: a Hadrami claimed that the thirty that Moses had promised his Lord were Dhul-Qi'dah and the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah with which God completed the forty.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And We appointed with Moses thirty nights, he said: Dhul-Qi'dah, And completed them with ten, he said: the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said something similar.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abd al-Aziz told us, he said, Abu Sa'd told us,
m: he heard Mujahid say about His statement:
h
And We appointed with Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten

, he said: Dhul-Qi'dah and the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. ... He said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Masruq: And We completed it with ten, he said: The ten days of sacrifice. As for his saying:
h
So the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights
, it means: So the time that God promised Moses was completed as forty nights, and he reached it, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: So the appointed time of his Lord was fulfilled, he said: So the appointed time of his Lord was forty nights. Say in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And Moses said to his brother Aaron
, ‘Take my place among my people and do right and do not follow the way of the corrupters.’

x: God Almighty says: When he went to meet his Lord, he said to his brother Aaron: Take my place among my people, meaning: Be my successor among them until I return. It is said: (He succeeded him, he succeeded him in succession).
And reform, he says: And reform them by making them obey God and worship Him, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: h
And Moses said to his brother Aaron
, ‘Take my place among my people and do good.’ Part of his good deeds was not to allow the calf to be worshipped. And His statement:
h
And do not follow the path of the corrupters

, meaning do not follow the path of those who corrupt the earth by disobeying their Lord and helping the people of disobedience in their disobedience to their Lord, but follow the path of those who obey their Lord. And God promised Moses, peace be upon him, after he had destroyed Pharaoh and saved the Children of Israel from him, according to what the scholars said, as follows:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Al-Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We appointed for Moses thirty nights

, the verse, he said: He says: That was after He had finished with Pharaoh and before the Mount, when God saved Moses, peace be upon him, from the sea and the people of Pharaoh had drowned, and he reached the good land, God sent down upon them manna and quails, and his Lord commanded him to meet Him. So when he wanted to meet his Lord, he appointed Aaron as his successor over his people, and he promised them that he would come to them in thirty nights, an appointment from him, without the command or appointment of his Lord. So he set out to meet his Lord, and when thirty nights were completed, the enemy of God, the Samaritan, said: Moses will not come to you, and nothing will reform you except a god whom you worship! So Aaron implored them and said: Do not do that, look to this night and this day of yours, and if he comes, otherwise you will do whatever you want! They said: Yes! So when they woke up the next morning and did not see Moses, the Samaritan returned to what he had said the day before. He said: And God created ten more days after the day that their prophet had set, so the appointed time of his Lord was forty nights. Then Aaron returned and implored them not to wait that day as well, and if it comes, then do as you please! Then the Samaritan returned a third time with the same words he had said to them, and Aaron returned and implored them to wait, but when they did not see... Al-Qasim said, Al-Husayn said, Hajjaj told me, Abu Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Hudhali told me: When Moses set out, the Samaritan went to Aaron and said: O Prophet of God, when we left, we borrowed from the Copts a lot of jewelry from their adornments, and the soldiers who were with you have hastened to sell and spend the jewelry, but it was a loan from the people of Pharaoh, so they are not alive so that we can return it to them. We do not know, perhaps when your brother, the Prophet of God, Moses, comes, he will have an opinion about it, either to offer it as a sacrifice so that the fire will consume it, or to give it to the poor and not the rich! Aaron said to him: What you saw and what you said is good! So he ordered a crier to call out: Whoever has any of the jewelry of the people of Pharaoh, let him bring it to us! So they brought it to him, and Aaron said: O Samaritan, you are the one who is most deserving of having this treasury! Then the Samaritan took it, and the evil enemy of God was a goldsmith, so he made a calf out of it with a body, then he threw into its stomach soil from the handful that he had taken from the trace of Gabriel’s horse when he saw it in the sea, so it began to bellow, and it only bellowed once, and he said to the Children of Israel: Moses stayed behind after thirty nights seeking this! This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot
r
. He said: Moses, peace be upon him, forgot his Lord.

x: God Almighty says: And when Moses came to the time that He promised us that he would meet us, and his Lord spoke to him, and spoke to him privately, Moses said to his Lord, Show me, that I may look at you, God said to him in response: You will not see Me, but look at the mountain.
And the reason for Moses asking his Lord to look at him was:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When his Lord spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, he wanted to look at Him. He said: My Lord, show me, that I may look at You. He said: You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me. So the mountain was surrounded by angels, and the angels were surrounded by fire, and the fire was surrounded by angels, and the angels were surrounded by fire. Then his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement: And We brought him near for a private conversation
r
(Maryam 19:52)

, he said: Someone who met the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me that the Lord brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen, and then he said out of longing for Him: My Lord, show me so that I may look at You. He said: You will not see Me, but look at the mountain. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, who said: When Moses, peace be upon him, remained behind after thirty days until he heard the speech of God, he longed to look at Him, so he said: O Lord, show me, so I may look at You! He said: You will not see Me, and no human being can bear to look at Me in this world. Whoever looks at Me will die! He said: O God, I heard Your speech, and I long to look at You, and for me to look at You and then die is more beloved to me than to live and not see You! He said: Then look at the mountain, if it remains in its place, then you will see Me.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Show me, so I may look at you, he said: Give it to me. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that Moses appointed Aaron as his successor over the Children of Israel and said: I am in a hurry to meet my Lord, so take my place among my people and do not follow the path of the corrupters. So Moses went out to his Lord in a hurry to meet Him, yearning for Him. Aaron remained among the Children of Israel, and with him was the Samaritan, walking with them in the footsteps of Moses to catch up with him. When God spoke to Moses, he desired to see Him, so he asked his Lord to look at Him. God said to Moses: You will not see Me, “But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me.” Ibn Ishaq said: This is what has reached us in the Book of God about the story of Moses when he asked to see his Lord. The People of the Book and the People of the Torah claim that there was an explanation, a story, many matters, and a review for that that did not come to us in the Book of God. And God knows best. Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the people of the first knowledge of the hadiths of the People of the Book, that they find in the interpretation of what they have of the story of Moses when he asked that of his Lord, that it was from his speech to him when he desired to see him, and asked that of him, and his Lord responded to him from him what he responded: that Moses had purified himself and purified his clothes, and fasted for the meeting with his Lord. Then when he came to Mount Sinai, and God approached him in the clouds and spoke to him, he glorified and praised Him and magnified and sanctified Him, with supplication and sad weeping, then he began to praise Him and said: My Lord, how great are You and how great is all Your affair, from Your greatness that there was nothing before You, for You are the One, the Subduer, as if Your throne beneath Your greatness is a fire lit for You, and You made a canopy of light and beneath it a canopy of light, so how great are You, my Lord, and Surat al-A’raf 7:143 And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] so that I may look at You." He said, "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level,
h
and Moses fell unconscious
. But when he regained consciousness, he said, "
h
Glory be to You
! I repent to You,
h
and I am the first of the believers

." how great is Your kingdom! You made between You and Your angels a journey of five hundred years, so how great are You, my Lord, and how great is Your kingdom in Your authority! And if You will something, You will carry it out in Your soldiers who are in the heavens or those on the earth, and Your soldiers who are in the sea, You send the spirit from You, and none of Your creation can see it except You, if You will, so it enters the belly of whomever You will of Your prophets, and they convey to whomever You will of Your servants. And none of Your angels can do anything of Your greatness or of Your throne, nor hear Your voice, for You have bestowed Your favors upon me and have magnified me in Your favor, and have done me all good! You have made me great among the nations of the earth, and You have made me great before Your angels, and You have made me hear Your voice, and You have given me Your speech, and You have given me Your wisdom. If I were to count Your favors, I would not be able to count them, and if I were to thank You, I would not be able to do so. I called upon You, my Lord, against Pharaoh with great signs and severe punishment, so I struck the sea with my staff, and it split for me and for those with me! And I called upon You when I crossed the sea, and You drowned Your enemy and my enemy. And I asked You for water for me and my nation, so I struck the rock with my staff that was in my hand, and from it I quenched my thirst and my nation. I asked You for my nation food that no one before them had eaten. You commanded me to call upon You from the east and from the west. So I called upon You from the east of my nation, and You gave them manna from the east of My soul, and You brought them quails from the west of their sea. I complained of the heat, so I called upon You, and You shaded them with clouds. I cannot count Your blessings or enumerate them, and if I wanted to thank You, I could not. So I have come to You today, desiring, seeking, asking, and beseeching You, so that You may give me what You have denied to others. I ask You and implore You, O Possessor of Majesty, Glory, and Power, to let me see You, for I have loved to see Your face which none of Your creation has seen! The Lord of Majesty said to him: Do you not see, O son of Imran, what you are saying? You have spoken words that are greater than all of creation! [No one sees me and lives. There is no one in the heavens who can support me, for they are too weak to bear my greatness. And there is no one on the earth who can support me, for it is too weak to contain my army.] I am not in one place, so I appear to an eye that looks at me. Moses said: O Lord, that I see you and die is more beloved to me than that I not see you and live. The Lord of Glory said to him: O son of Imran, You have spoken words that are greater than all creation. No one sees me and lives! He said: O Lord, complete Your blessings upon me, complete Your favor upon me, and complete Your kindness upon me, with this that I have asked of You. It is not for me to see you and then die, but I love to see you so that my heart may be at peace. He said to him: O son of Imran, no one will see me and live! Moses said: O Lord, complete Your blessings upon me, complete Your favor upon me, and complete Your kindness upon me with this that I have asked of You, so that I die as a result of that, which is more beloved to me than life! Then the Most Merciful, the Compassionate, said: O Moses, you have asked [and been inspired], I will grant you your request if you are able to look at Me. Go and take two tablets, then look at the largest stone at the top of the mountain, for what is behind it and below it is a narrow place that will not accommodate anything but your seat, O son of Imran. Then look, for I will descend to you with My soldiers, few and many. So Moses did as his Lord commanded him. He carved two tablets, then ascended with them to the mountain, and sat on the stone. When he was firmly on it, God commanded His soldiers who were in the lowest heaven, saying: Place your shoulders around the mountain. So I heard what the Lord said, so I did what He commanded. Then God sent thunderbolts, darkness and fog over the mountain that was next to Moses, four leagues on each side. Then God ordered the angels of the world to pass by Moses, and they intercepted him. They passed by him like the flight of kites, their mouths glorifying and praising God in great voices like the sound of loud thunder. Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him, said: “O Lord, I was independent of this. My eyes see nothing. Their sight has gone from the ray of light that descended upon the angels of my Lord!” Then God ordered the angels of the second heaven to descend upon Moses, and they intercepted him. They descended like lions, glorifying and sanctifying God. The weak servant, son of Imran, was terrified by what he saw and heard, and every hair on his head and skin shuddered. Then he said: “I regret asking you. Can anything save me from the place I am in?” The chief of the angels and their head said to him: O Moses, be patient for what you asked, for it is little of the great deal that you have seen! Then God commanded the angels of the third heaven: Descend upon Moses, and intercept him! So they came like eagles, with a violent clatter, trembling, and roaring, and their mouths were glorifying and sanctifying, like the roar of a great army, like the flames of fire. Moses was terrified and his soul was distressed, and his thoughts were bad, and he despaired of life. So the chief of the angels and their head said to him: Stay where you are, O son of Imran, until you see what you cannot bear! Then God commanded the angels of the fourth heaven: Descend and intercept Moses, son of Imran! So they came and descended upon him, and nothing of those who passed by him before them resembled them. Their colors were like the flames of fire, and the rest of their creation was like white snow. Their voices were loud with glorification and sanctification, and nothing of the voices of those who passed by him before them could come close to them. His knees knocked, his heart trembled, and his crying became intense. So the chief of the angels and their head said: O son of Imran, be patient for what you asked, for it is little of the much that you saw! Then God commanded the angels of the fifth heaven: Descend and intercept Moses! So they descended upon him in seven colors, but Moses could not follow them with his eyes, and he did not see anyone like them, nor hear anyone like their voices, and his heart was filled with fear, and his sadness intensified and his crying increased, so the chief of the angels and their head said to him: O son of Imran, stay where you are until you see what you cannot bear! Then God commanded the angels of the sixth heaven: Descend upon My servant who asked to see Me, Moses son of Imran, and intercept him! So they descended upon him, in the hand of each angel like a tall palm tree was a fire brighter than the sun, and their clothing was like the flames of fire. When they glorified and sanctified, the angels of the heavens who were before them responded to them, all of them saying in loud voices: Glory be to God, the Holy, the Lord of Majesty, who never dies. On the head of each angel of them were four faces. When Moses saw them, he raised his voice glorifying God with them when they glorified God, and he was crying and saying: “My Lord, remember me and do not forget Your servant. I do not know whether I will escape from what I am in or not. If I go out, I will be burned, and if I stay, I will die.” The chief of the angels and their leader said to him: O son of Imran, your insides are about to be filled, your heart will be torn out, and your crying will intensify, so be patient for what you are sitting looking at, O son of Imran! Moses’ mountain was a great mountain, so God commanded him to carry His throne, then He said: Pass me by My servant so that he may see Me, for this is little of the much that he saw! The mountain split open from the majesty of the Lord, and the light of the Throne of the Most Merciful covered the mountain of Moses, and the angels of the heavens raised their voices together, so the mountain shook and was destroyed, along with every tree that was in it, and the weak servant Moses, son of Imran, fell unconscious on his face, his soul not with him, so God sent life with His mercy, so the spirit covered him with His mercy, and turned the stone that he was on and made it like a stomach in the shape of a dome, so that Moses would not be burned. Then the spirit raised him, like a mother raising her fetus when it is struck down. He said: So Moses stood up, glorifying God and saying: I believe that You are my Lord, and I believe that no one sees You and comes to life, and whoever looks at Your angels, his heart is torn out, so how great You are, Lord, and how great are Your angels, You are the Lord of lords and the God of gods and the King of kings, You command the soldiers who are with You and they obey You, and You command the heaven and what is in it and it obeys You, You do not disdain that, and nothing is equal to You, and nothing can stand up to You, my Lord, I repent to You, praise be to God who has no partner, how great and majestic You are, Lord of the worlds!

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain
, He rendered it level,
h
and Moses fell unconscious
God Almighty says: When the Lord looked up at the mountain, God made the mountain level, meaning: level with the ground,
h
and Moses fell unconscious
, meaning: unconscious. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Amr Al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told me, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain
, He rendered it level, he said: Nothing was revealed of it except the size of a little finger. He rendered it level, he said: dust.
h
And Moses fell unconscious
, he said: unconscious.

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said:
m: Al-Suddi claimed, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: He revealed from Him something like the little finger, and He made the mountain crumble,
h
and Moses fell unconscious
, and he remained unconscious as long as God willed.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And Moses fell unconscious
, he said: He was unconscious.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain
, He made it crumble, he said: Some of it collapsed on top of others,
h
and Moses fell unconscious
, meaning: dead.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And Moses fell unconscious
, meaning dead.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: pounded, he said: He pounded some of it against others.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us:
m: I heard Sufyan say regarding His statement:
h
So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain
, He rendered it level, he said: The mountain sank into the earth until it fell into the sea, and it went with it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali:
m: h
So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain
, He made it level, it sank and went under the ground, and will not appear until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ahmad bin Suhayl al-Wasiti told us, he said, Qara bin Isa told us, he said, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He pointed with His finger and made it crumble. And Abu Ismail showed us his index finger.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble,’ he said like this with his finger - and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him Surat al-A’raf 7:143 And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] so that I may look at You." He said, "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level,
h
and Moses fell unconscious
. But when he regained consciousness, he said, "
h
Glory be to You
! I repent to You,
h
and I am the first of the believers
." peace, placed his thumb on the upper joint of the little finger - and the mountain crumbled.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hudbah bin Khalid told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level,’ he said: He placed his thumb close to the tip of his little finger, he said: And the mountain crumbled.” So Humayd said to Thabit: Do you say this? Thabit raised his hand and struck Humayd on the chest, and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, says it, and Anas says it, and I am concealing it!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
So when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain
, He rendered it level,
h
and Moses fell unconscious
. That is because when the mountain’s cover was removed and he saw the light, it became like a leveling of the levels.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, ‘My Lord, show me [yourself] that I may look at You.’ He said, ‘You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in its place,’ for it is larger than you and more solid in creation. ‘So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain,’ it looked at the mountain and could not control itself, and the mountain began to overtake it on its head. So when Moses saw what the mountain was doing, it fell unconscious. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: “Daka.” The people of Medina and Basra generally read it as dakka, shortened with tanween, meaning: God crushed the mountain with a crushing blow, meaning: He shattered it, and taking into consideration the words of God: No! When the earth is crushed, crushed with a crushing blow (al-Fajr 89:21). And His words: And the earth and the mountains will be borne and crushed with a single crushing blow (al-Haqqah 69:14).

x: Some of them cited as evidence for that the words of Humayd: Your hand has defeated the pillars of the mountains. You threaten the delicate whites with your concern. The majority of the Kufians read it as: (Jaʿalu dakaʿ), with a long vowel and leaving out the jar and tanween, like (hamraʿ) and (sawdaʿ).
Among those who read it like this was ʿIkrimah, and he said about it what:

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Ibad bin Ibad told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Hazim, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: (A dust from the dust). And he said: When God Almighty looked at the mountain, it became a desert of dust. The Arabs differed about its meaning if it is read in this way.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The Arabs say: (a she-camel of dakaa), which does not have a hump. He said: (the mountain) is masculine, so it does not seem likely that it is from it, unless he made it: (like dakaa), deleted (like), and made it follow the example of: And ask the town
r
(Yusuf 12:82)

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: The meaning of this is: He made the mountain into a flat land, then the land was deleted and the flat land was used in its place, since it led to its being replaced.

The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: (Jaʿalahu Dakkaʿ) with the extension and without the jar, because the report that we narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, indicates its authenticity. That is because it was narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The mountain collapsed, and he did not say (Fatafatta) or (Turn into dust). There is no doubt that when it collapses and disappears, the surface of the earth will appear, and it will be like a camel whose hump has been lost, and it will become flat without a hump. As for when some of it is crushed, then some of it will break some of it and crumble, but it will not collapse. As for dakaa, it is derived from earth, and therefore it is feminine, as I have explained. The meaning of the words is: When his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, it melted and became flat ground in its place.
We have explained the meaning of stun with its evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it here.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
So when he regained consciousness
, he said:
h
Glory be to You
I repent to You,
h
and I am the first of the believers
God Almighty says: When he returned to Moses, peace be upon him, he understood him from his fainting spell, and that is the recovery from the shock that Moses, peace be upon him, fell to, He said,
h
Glory be to You

, glorifying You, O Lord, and absolving anyone from seeing You in this world and then living, I repent to You, from my asking You for what I asked You to see, and I am the first of my people to believe, in You, that no one should see You in this world except that he perishes.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi’ Anas, on the authority of Abu al-A’aliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
I repent to You and I am the first of the believers
, he said: There were believers before him, but he says: I am the first to believe that none of Your creation will see You until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: When Moses saw that and regained consciousness, he knew that he had asked for something that was not appropriate for him, so he said:
h
Glory be to You
h
I repent to You and I am the first of the believers
. Abu Al-ʿAliyah said: He meant: I am the first to believe in You and that no one will see You before the Day of Resurrection.

c: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said,
m: Sufyan said, Abu Saad said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And Moses fell unconscious
, so the angels passed by him while he was unconscious, and they said: O son of menstruating women, you have asked your Lord for a great matter!
h
So when he regained consciousness
, he said:
h
Glory be to You
, there is no god but You, I repent to You,
h
and I am the first of the believers
! He said: I am the first to believe that none of Your creation can see You, meaning: in this world.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: He said, ‘
h
Glory be to You
! I repent to You,
h
and I am the first of the believers
.’ He said: I am the first to believe that none of Your creation sees You.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Glory be to You
, I repent to You, he said: from my question about seeing Him.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He said,
h
Glory be to You
, I repent to You, that I ask You to see me.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Na’eem told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Glory be to You
, I repent to You, that I ask You to see me.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Glory be to You
, I repent to You, he said: I repent to You from asking You to see me.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: His saying: And I am the first of the children of Israel to believe in you.
Who said that?

c: Al-Husayn bin Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And I am the first of the believers
, he said: The first to believe in you, from the Children of Israel.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And I am the first of the believers
, meaning: the first of the believers from the Children of Israel.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And I am the first of the believers
, I am the first of my people to believe.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Abu Na’eem told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And I am the first of the believers
, meaning: the first of my people to believe.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And I am the first of the believers
, he said: I am the first of my people to believe.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say regarding His statement:
h
And I am the first of the believers
, he said: The first of my people to believe.

x: We chose the statement that we chose regarding his statement:
h
And I am the first of the believers

, over the statement of those who said: Its meaning is: I am the first of the believers from the Children of Israel, because before him there were believers and prophets among the Children of Israel, among whom were the children of Israel from his loins, and they were believers and prophets. Therefore we chose the statement that we said before.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble,’ he said like this with his finger - and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him Surat al-A’raf 7:143 And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] so that I may look at You."
There is a difference in the reading of his saying: “Daka.”

The people of Medina and Basra generally read it as dakka, shortened with tanween, meaning: God crushed the mountain with a crushing blow, meaning: He shattered it, and taking into consideration the words of God: No!
The majority of the Kufians read it as: (Jaʿalu dakaʿ), with a long vowel and leaving out the jar and tanween, like (hamraʿ) and (sawdaʿ).
Among those who read it like this was ʿIkrimah, and he said about it what:
The Arabs differed about its meaning if it is read in this way.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: (Jaʿalahu Dakkaʿ) with the extension and without the jar, because the report that we narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, indicates its authenticity.

x: God Almighty says, God said to Moses: O Moses, I have chosen you over mankind, meaning: I have chosen you over mankind, with My messages, to My creation, I sent you with them to them, and with My speech, I spoke to you and spoke privately to you, not to any other of My creation, so take what I have given you, meaning: take what I have given you of My commands and prohibitions and hold fast to them, and act according to […], and be among the grateful, to God for what He has given you of His message, and what He has singled you out for of private conversation, by obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, and hastening to please Him.
God Almighty says: And We wrote for Moses on His tablets.

i: The definite article was added to al-Alawh instead of the addition, as the poet said:
x: Dreams are not single And as God Almighty said: Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge (al-Nazi’at 79:41), meaning: it is his refuge.

And his saying: of everything, he says: of reminding and drawing attention to the greatness of God and the might of His power, admonition, for his people and for those who were commanded to act according to what was written in the tablets,
h
and a detailed explanation of everything
, he says: and a clarification of everything of God’s command and prohibition. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid - or:
m: Saeed bin Jubair, and it is in the original of my book: on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair - regarding the statement of God:
h
And a detailed explanation of everything
, he said: What they were commanded to do and what they were forbidden from doing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things
, of what is permissible and what is forbidden.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say regarding His statement:
h
And a detailed explanation of everything
, he said: What they were commanded to do and what they were forbidden from doing.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things

, Atiyah said: Ibn Abbas told me: When death distressed Moses, peace be upon him, he said: This is because of Adam! God had made us in a house of settlement where we would not die, but Adam made a mistake and sent us down here! So God said to Moses: Shall I send Adam to you so that you may argue with him? He said: Yes! So when God sent Adam, Moses asked Him, and our father Adam, peace be upon them both, said: O Moses, did you ask God to send me to you? Moses said: If it were not for you, we would not be here! Adam said to him: Has God not given you of all things an admonition and a detailed explanation? Do you not know that no disaster befalls upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before He brings it into being? Moses said: Yes! So Adam, peace be upon them both, argued with him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abd al-Samad bin Maqal:
m: that he heard Wahb say regarding His statement:
h
And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things

, he said: He wrote to him: Do not associate with Me anything of the people of the heavens or the people of the earth, for all of that is My creation. Do not swear falsely by My name, for whoever swears by My name, I do not praise him, and respect your parents.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
Take it with force

God Almighty says: And We said to Moses, when We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailed account of all things: Take the tablets with strength. He brought out the report about the tablets, and what is meant is what is in them.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of power in this context.
Some of them said: It means: Seriously.
Who said that?

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, he said,
m: Abu Saad said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Take it with force
, he said: seriously.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Take it with strength
, he said: with seriousness and diligence.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is, take it in obedience to God.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Take it with strength

, he said: with obedience. We have explained the meaning of this with its evidence, and the differences of the people of interpretation regarding it, in Surat Al-Baqarah when He says: Take what We have given you with strength (al-Baqarah 2:63), so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And command your people to take the best of it
God Almighty says: We said to Moses: And command your people, the Children of Israel, to take the best of it, meaning to do the best they find in it, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And command your people to take the best of it
, the best of what they find in it.

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And command your people to take the best of it
, he said: Moses was commanded to take it more severely than what he had commanded his people.

x: What is the meaning of his saying:
h
And command your people to take the best of it
, was it one of their characteristics to leave some of the good in it?

No, but it contained a command and a prohibition, so God commanded them to do what He commanded them to do and to leave what He forbade them from doing, so doing what is commanded is better than doing what is forbidden.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
I will show you the abode of the wicked

God Almighty said to Moses, when He wrote on the tablets of everything: Take it with diligence in working according to what is in it and striving, and command your people to take the best of what is in it, and forbid them from wasting it and wasting work according to what is in it and associating partners with Me, for whoever associates partners with Me from them and others, then I will show him in the Hereafter when he returns to Me, the home of the wicked, which is the fire of God that He has prepared for His enemies. Rather, he said:
h
I will show you the abode of the wicked

, just as someone says to someone he is addressing: I will show you tomorrow what will happen to those who disobey my command! as a threat and warning to those who disobey him and disobey his command.
The interpreters differed on the meaning of this.
Some of them said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
I will show you the home of the wicked
, he said: Their destiny in the Hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
I will show you the home of the wicked
, he said: Hell.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: I will bring you into the land of Ash-Sham, and I will show you the dwellings of the infidels who are its inhabitants, the giants and titans.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
I will show you the home of the wicked
, their homes.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The abode of the wicked, he said: their homes.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: I will show you the home of Pharaoh’s people, which is Egypt.
Who said that? ... .
We chose the statement that we chose in interpreting that because what preceded His Most High’s statement:
h
I will show you the abode of the wicked

, was a command from God to Moses and his people to act according to what is in the Torah. So it is more appropriate, according to God’s wisdom, to conclude that with a threat to whoever neglects it, neglects to act for God, and deviates from His path, without reporting what has been cut off, or what has not been mentioned.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that.
Some of them said: It means: I will take away from them the understanding of the Book.
Mention who said that:

c: Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Marwazi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Bakr told me, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Uyaynah say about the statement of God: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right, he said, he says: I will take away from them the understanding of the Qur’an, and turn them away from My signs.

x: Ibn ʿUyaynah’s interpretation of this indicates that this statement was, in his view, a threat from God to the people of disbelief in God to whom our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, not to the people of Moses, because the Qur’an was only revealed to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, not to Moses, peace be upon him.
Others said about this: It means: I will distract them from considering the arguments.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: I will turn away from My signs, from the creation of the heavens and the earth and the signs in them. I will turn them away from contemplating them and taking heed.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God has informed that He will turn away from His signs, which are His evidence and signs of the truth of what He has commanded His servants to do and imposed upon them of obedience to Him in His Oneness and Justice, and other than that of His obligations. The heavens and the earth and every existing thing of His creation are among His signs, and the Qur’an is also among His signs. The report has been generalized that He will turn away from His signs the arrogant ones on earth without right, and they are those upon whom the word of God has come into effect that they will not believe, so they are turned away from understanding all of His signs and from considering and remembering them, because if they were guided to understand some of that and were guided to consider it, they would be admonished and turn to the truth, and that will not happen from them, because He, the Most High, said:
h
And if they see every sign
, they will not believe in it, so there is no changing the words of God.
The statement in the interpretation of His statement: “
h
And if they see every sign
, they will not believe in it.

And if they see the path of right guidance, they will not take it as a path. And if they see the path of error, they will take it as a path. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.”

God Almighty says: “And if these people who are arrogant in the land without right - and (their arrogance therein without right), their tyranny therein, and their arrogance in refusing to believe in God and His Messenger, and submitting to His commands and prohibitions, and they are servants of God whom He nourishes with His blessings, and provides them with His provision morning and evening - see “every sign,” meaning: every proof of God’s oneness and Lordship, and every indication that worship should only be done to Him alone, without anyone else, they will not believe in it, meaning: they will not believe in that sign that it indicates what it is a proof for, but they will say: (It is magic and a lie), And if they see the path of right guidance, they will not take it as a path, meaning: And if these people whose description He has described see the path of guidance and rectitude which, if they follow it, they will be saved from destruction and ruin, and will reach eternal bliss, they will not follow it nor take it as a path for themselves, out of their ignorance and confusion, And if they see the path of error, meaning: And if they see The path of destruction, which if they follow, they will go astray and perish. We have explained the meaning of al-Ghay previously, so there is no need to repeat it.

They take it as a way, meaning: they follow it and make it a path for themselves, because God has diverted them from His signs and has sealed their hearts, so they will neither succeed nor prosper. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them, meaning: God Almighty says: We diverted them from Our signs so that they would understand them and consider them and remember and turn back, as a punishment from Us for their denial of Our signs. And they were heedless of them, meaning: They were heedless of Our signs and evidence that testify to the truth of what We have commanded them to do and Surat al-A’raf 7:146 I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right.
h
And if they see every sign
, they will not believe in it. And if they see the path of right guidance, they will not take it as a path. And if they see the path of error, they will take it as a path.

That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them. forbidden them from, “not thinking about them, distracted from them, not considering them, so the word of our Lord came true upon them at that time, so they were ruined. There is a difference in the reading of his saying “guidance.” The majority of the people of Medina, some of the people of Mecca, and some of the people of Basra read it as al-Rashd, with a damma on the ra and a sukoon on the shin. The majority of the people of Kufa and some of the people of Mecca read it as al-Rashd, with the ra and shin open. Then the people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed about the meaning of that if its ra’ is closed and its shin is silent, and about it if they are both open. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ that he used to say: Its meaning, if its ra’ is pronounced with a damma and its shin is silent, is righteousness, as God said:
If you perceive in them sound judgment
meaning: righteousness.

And that is how he used to recite it. And its meaning, if its ra’ and shin are pronounced with a fatha, is: righteousness in religion, as God, the Most High, said: Learn from what I have been taught sound judgment (al-Kahf 18:66), meaning uprightness and correctness in religion. Al-Kisa’i used to say: They are two words with one meaning, such as saqam and saqam, “hazn” and hazn, and also rashd and rashd.

The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that are widely recited in the readings of the regions, and they agree in meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct in it.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying “guidance.”
The majority of the people of Medina, some of the people of Mecca, and some of the people of Basra read it as al-Rashd, with a damma on the ra and a sukoon on the shin.
The majority of the people of Kufa and some of the people of Mecca read it as al-Rashd, with the ra and shin open.
And that is how he used to recite it.

Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that are widely recited in the readings of the regions, and they agree in meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct in it.

x: God Almighty says: And these arrogant ones on earth without right, and everyone who denies the proofs of God and His messengers and His signs, and denies that he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection after his death, and denies meeting God in the Hereafter, their deeds have gone and become null and void, and they have received their burdens and they have been confirmed, because they worked for other than God, and they exhausted themselves in what does not please God, so their deeds have become a burden upon them. God Almighty says: Are they recompensed except for what they used to do? He says: Are they rewarded except for what they used to do? So the reward for their deeds has become eternity in a fire whose walls surround them, because their deeds were in obedience to Satan, not in obedience to the Most Merciful. We seek refuge in God from His wrath. We have explained the meaning of disaster, “reward,” and the afterlife in the past, so there is no need to repeat it.

God Almighty says: And the Children of Israel, the people of Moses, took after Moses had departed from them, going to his Lord to commune with Him, and to fulfill the promise that his Lord had made him, from their ornaments a calf, which is the young of a cow, and they worshipped it. Then God Almighty explained what that calf was, saying: A body that had a lowing sound - and (mooing) is the sound of a cow - God Almighty informs about them that they went astray in a way that people of reason do not go astray. That is because the Lord, glory be to Him, who owns the heavens and the earth, and is the manager of that, cannot have a body that has a lowing sound, does not speak to anyone, and does not guide to good. And those, whose stories God related for that reason, said: (This is our god and the god of Moses), so they devoted themselves to it and worshipped it, out of ignorance on their part, and out of departure from God and misguidance.

We have explained the reason for their worship of it, and how those of them who took the calf had taken it in the past, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. In al-Hilli there are two pronunciations: with a damma on the ha’, which is the original, and with a kasra on it, and the same is true for everything similar to it, such as salli, jathi, and ‘ati. Whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct, because they are widely recited in the recitation, and because their meanings are the same. And His statement:
h
Have they not seen that it does not speak to them nor guide them to a way

? He says: Have those who devoted themselves to the calf which they took as an ornament to worship, not seen that the calf does not speak to them nor guide them to a way? He says: Nor does it guide them to a path. And this is not from the description of their Lord who is truly to be worshipped, rather His description is that He speaks to His prophets and messengers, and guides His creation to the path of good, and forbids them from the path of destruction and ruin.

God Almighty says: They took it, meaning: They took the calf as a god, and by taking it as a god to be worshipped, they were wronging themselves, because they worshipped someone other than the One to whom worship is due, and they attributed divinity to someone other than the One to whom divinity is due. We have explained the meaning of injustice previously, so there is no need to repeat it.

evidence.text: Whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct, because they are widely recited in the recitation, and because their meanings are the same.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement: And when it fell into their hands, and when those who worshipped the calf whose description God Almighty described regretted it when Moses returned to them, and they submitted to Moses and his judgment over them. Likewise, the Arabs say to anyone who regrets something he has missed or has done in the past, and is unable to do something: He has fallen into his hands and he has fallen. These are two eloquent expressions, and their origin is from the word istisa’ir, which means that a man strikes another or wrestles him down, then throws him from his hands to the ground to capture him and tie him up. So the one who is thrown has fallen into the hands of the one who has fallen with him. So it is said to anyone who is unable to do something, humbled by his inability, and regretting what he said: He has fallen into his hands and he has fallen.
What he meant by his saying:
h
And they saw that they had gone astray

, is that they saw that they had deviated from the right path, departed from the religion of God, and disbelieved in their Lord. They said, repenting to God and turning to Him from their disbelief in Him:
h
If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us
, we will surely be among the losers. Then the reading differed in reading that.

Some of the reciters of the people of Medina, Mecca, Kufa and Basra read it as: If our Lord does not have mercy on us, in the nominative case, as a statement. The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: If you do not have mercy on us, our Lord, in the accusative case, with the interpretation: If you do not have mercy on us, O our Lord, as a way of addressing their Lord. The readers of this also argued that in one of the two readings it is said: ((They said: Our Lord, if You do not have mercy on us and forgive us)), and this is evidence of the address.

What is more correct than the reading in this is the reading in the form of a statement with the letter ya in have mercy on us, and with the nominative in his saying: Our Lord, because there was nothing before that that would require it to be directed to the address. The reading that was narrated based on what we mentioned of its reading: (They said, Our Lord, if You do not have mercy on us), we do not know its correctness from the aspect that must be accepted. The meaning of his saying:
h
If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us
, is that if our Lord does not show us compassion by allowing us to repent with His mercy and cover our sins with it, we will be among those who perish, whose deeds have been in vain.

evidence.text: Then the reading differed in reading that.
Some of the reciters of the people of Medina, Mecca, Kufa and Basra read it as: If our Lord does not have mercy on us, in the nominative case, as a statement.

The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: If you do not have mercy on us, our Lord, in the accusative case, with the interpretation: If you do not have mercy on us, O our Lord, as a way of addressing their Lord.
The readers of this also argued that in one of the two readings it is said: ((They said: Our Lord, if You do not have mercy on us and forgive us)), and this is evidence of the address.

Abu Jaʿfar said: What is more correct than the reading in this is the reading in the form of a statement with the letter ya in have mercy on us, and with the nominative in his saying: Our Lord, because there was nothing before that that would require it to be directed to the address.
The reading that was narrated based on what we mentioned of its reading: (They said, Our Lord, if You do not have mercy on us), we do not know its correctness from the aspect that must be accepted.

x: God Almighty says: When Moses returned to his people from the Children of Israel, he returned angry and sad, because God had informed him that he had tempted his people, and that the Samaritan had led them astray, so he returned angry and sad about that.
And regret is intense anger and vexation towards the one who angered him, such as:

c: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me, he said: Abd Al-Salam bin Muhammad Al-Hadrami told us, he said: Shureih bin Yazid told me, he said:
m: I heard Nasr bin Alqamah say: Abu Al-Darda’ said: God’s statement: angry and grieved, he said: Grief is a position beyond anger, more severe than that, and the explanation of that is in the Book of God: He went to his people angry, and he went grieved.

x: Others said about this:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Asfa he said:
m: sad.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when Moses returned to his people
, angry and grieved, he says: grieved, sad. And he said in al-Zukhruf 43:So when they angered Us (al-Zukhruf 43:55), he says: they angered Us. And grief has two meanings: anger and sadness.

c: Nasr bin Ali told us, Sulayman bin Sulayman told us, Malik bin Dinar told us, Al-Hasan said
m: in his statement:
h
And when Moses returned to his people

, angry and grieved, he said: angry and sad. And his saying: He said, ‘How evil is that which you have left behind me after me.’ He says: How evil is the deed that you have done after my departure from you, and you have appointed me among those whom I left behind from my people among you, and my religion which your Lord has commanded you to follow. It is said: He left him with good or He left him with evil, if he treated his family or people and whoever was related to him after his departure from them, good or evil. And his saying:
h
Did you hasten the command of your Lord

? He says: Did you precede the command of your Lord in your souls and turn away from it? It is said: So-and-so hastened this matter, if he preceded it, and so-and-so hastened so-and-so, if he preceded him, and do not hurry me, so-and-so, do not go away from me and leave me, and I hastened him, I urged him on.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head
, dragging him towards him.
Ibn Umm said: Indeed, the people have weakened me and almost killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice over me
h
and do not place me with the wrongdoing people
God Almighty says: And Moses threw down the tablets. Then the scholars differed about the reason for his throwing them down.
Some of them said: He threw it out of anger at his people who worshipped the calf.
Who said that?

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Al-Asbagh bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub, he said, Saeed bin Jubair told me, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: When Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he took hold of his brother’s head, dragging him towards him, and he threw down the tablets in anger.

c: And Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, he said,
m: Abu Saad said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When Moses returned to his people, and he was close to them, he heard their voices, so he said: I hear the voices of a people who are distracted. So when he saw them devoted to the calf, he threw down the tablets and broke them, and took hold of his brother’s head and dragged him towards him.

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: Moses took the tablets, then Moses returned to his people angry Surat al-A’raf 7:150
h
And when Moses returned to his people
, angry and grieved, he said, "Evil is that which you have done to me after I left!
h
Did you hasten the command of your Lord
h
