And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head
, dragging him toward him. He said, "
h
O son of my mother

, indeed the people have oppressed me and almost killed me. So do not let my enemies rejoice over me and do not make me a disgrace." With the wrongdoing people and grieved, and said: O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise? until His saying:
h
Thus did the Samaritan throw it down (Ta-Ha
: 86-87). So Moses threw down the tablets and took hold of his brother’s head, dragging him towards him. He said,
h
O son of my mother
, do not seize me by my beard or by my head
r
(Ta-Ha: 94)

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When Moses reached his people and saw what they were doing of worshipping the calf, he threw the tablets from his hand, then he took hold of his brother’s head and beard, and said: What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Did you disobey my command?
r

x: Others said: Moses threw the tablets because of the virtues he had achieved in them for people other than his own, and that was difficult for him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He took the tablets (al-A’raf 7

:154), he said: O Lord, I find in the tablets a nation, the best nation produced for mankind, they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, so make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Muhammad! He said: O Lord, I find in the tablets a nation who are the last - meaning the last in creation - the first to enter Paradise, O Lord, make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad! He said: O Lord, I find in the tablets a nation whose Gospels are in their chests, they read them - and those before them used to read their books by looking, until when they raised them they did not memorize anything, nor did they recognize it. Qatada said: And God has given you, O nation, of memorization something that He has not given to any other nation - he said: O Lord, make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad! He said: O Lord, I find in the Tablets a nation who believe in the First Book and the Last Book, and fight against the excess of misguidance, until they fight the one-eyed liar, so make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad! He said: O Lord, I find in the Tablets a nation whose charity they eat in their bellies, then they are rewarded for it - and there were nations before them, if they gave charity and it was accepted from them, God would send a fire upon it and it would consume it, and if it was returned to them, it would be left to be eaten by birds and wild beasts. He said: And God has taken your charity from your rich for your poor - He said: O Lord, make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad! He said: O Lord, I find in the Tablets a nation, if one of them intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him, and if he does it, ten good deeds are recorded for him up to seven hundred. O Lord, make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad! He said: O Lord, I find in the Tablets a nation, if one of them intends to do a bad deed, it is not recorded against him until he does it, but if he does it, a single bad deed is recorded against him, so make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad! He said: O Lord, I find in the Tablets a nation who are the responders and those for whom prayer is answered, so make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad. He said: O Lord, I find in the Tablets a nation who are the intercessors and those for whom prayer is interceded, so make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad. He said: And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, threw away the Tablets and said: O God, make me from the nation of Ahmad! He said: So the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, was given two things that were not given to any other prophet. God said: O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and with My speech (al-A’raf 7:143). He said: So the Prophet of God was pleased, then he was given the second: And among the people of Moses is a nation who guide with the truth and thereby do justice (al-A’raf 7:159). He said: So the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was completely pleased.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When Moses took the tablets, he said: O Lord, I find in the tablets a nation who are the best of nations, they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, so make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad! He said: O Lord, I find in the tablets a nation who are the last but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection, so make them my nation! He said: That is the nation of Ahmad. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Bishr ibn Muadh, except that he said in his hadith: Then Moses, peace be upon him, threw down the tablets and said: O God, make me from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless them both.

x: What is more correct than what is said about that, is that the reason for Moses throwing down the tablets was because of his anger at his people for worshipping the calf, because God, may He be glorified and praised, informed us of that in His Book, saying: “
h
And when Moses returned to his people
, angry and grieved, he said, ‘How evil is that which you have replaced me with after me!
h
Did you hasten the command of your Lord
h
And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head
, dragging him toward him.” He mentioned that when God wrote the Torah for Moses, peace be upon him, on the tablets, He brought it close to him until he heard the scratching of the pen.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Amara, on the authority of Ali,
m: peace be upon him, he said: God wrote the tablets for Moses, peace be upon him, and he heard the scratching of the pens on the tablets. ... He said: Israel told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: He brought him close until he heard the scratching of the pens. It was said: The Torah was seven-sevenths, and when Moses threw the tablets, they were broken, so he took up six-sevenths of them, and among what was taken up was (the details of everything), about which God said: And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy remained in the remaining seven, which is about which God said: He took up the tablets, and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord (al-A’raf 7:154). The Torah was mentioned as seventy camel loads, and a part of it was read in a year, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad bin Khalid Al-Makfoof told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, he said:
m: The Torah was revealed and it was seventy camel loads long, and a part of it was read in a year. Only four people read it: Moses bin Imran, Jesus, Ezra, and Joshua bin Nun, may God’s prayers be upon them. They differed about the tablets.

x: Some of them said: It was made of green emerald.
Some of them said: It was made of ruby.
Some of them said: It was from cold. Mention the narration with what we mentioned of that.

c: Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ya’la bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Moses threw the tablets and they broke, then they were lifted up except for a sixth of them. Ibn Jurayj said: And he told me that the tablets were of chrysolite and emerald from Paradise. Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli, Ali bin Dawud, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Shabwayh, and Ahmad bin al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi told me:

c: Adam al-Asqalani told us: Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah, who said:
m: The tablets of Moses, peace be upon him, were made of hail.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu al-Junayd, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, he said:
m: I asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr about the tablets, what were they made of? He said: They were made of ruby, written in gold, the Most Gracious wrote them with His hand, and the people of the heavens heard the scratching of the pen as He wrote them.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Al-Qasim told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi al-Waddah, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid or Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: The tablets were emerald, but when Moses threw down the tablets, guidance and mercy remained, and the details were gone. He said, Al-Qasim told us, Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The tablets were made of green emerald.

x: Some of them claimed that the tablets were two tablets. If what he said was as he said, then it was said: And We wrote for him on the tablets, and they are two tablets, just as it was said: If he had brothers
r
(An-Nisa’: 11)
, and they are two brothers. As for his saying:
h
And he seized his brother’s head

, dragging him towards him, this was an action of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of his resentment towards his brother Aaron for leaving his followers and staying with the Children of Israel in the place where he had left them, as God, the Most High, said, informing about what Moses, peace be upon him, said to him:
What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Did you disobey my command?
when Aaron informed him of his excuse and he accepted his excuse, and that was what he said to Moses: “Do not seize me by my beard or by my head.
Indeed, I feared that you would say, ‘You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word.’”
r
, and he said: Son of my mother, indeed the people have weakened me and almost killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice over me, the verse. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
O son of my mother

. This was read by most of the people of Medina and some of the people of Basra: O son of mother, with the opening of the mim of umm. The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: Ibn Umm, with a kasra on the mim of umm. The Arab scholars differed on the opening and closing of this word, with all of them agreeing that they are two languages used by the Arabs.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It was said with the fat-ha, on the basis that they are two nouns that were made into one noun, as was said: (O son of uncle), and he said: This is anomalous and cannot be used as a basis for analogy. He said: Whoever reads it as (O son of mother), it is in the language of those who say: (This is a young man who has come), making it one noun with a kasra at the end, like his saying: (Khaz Baz). Some grammarians of Kufa said: It was said (O son of mother) and (O son of cousin), so it was placed in the accusative case as the Arabic word is placed in the accusative case in some cases, so it is said (O regret), (O woe to us). He said: It is as if they said (O mother) and (O uncle), and they did not say that in (brother), and if that was said it would have been correct. He said: And those who lowered it, it is common in their Surat al-A’raf 7:150
h
And when Moses returned to his people
, angry and grieved, he said, "Evil is that which you have done to me after I left!
h
Did you hasten the command of your Lord
h
And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head
, dragging him toward him. He said, "
h
O son of my mother

, indeed the people have oppressed me and almost killed me. So do not let my enemies rejoice over me and do not make me a disgrace." With the wrongdoing people speech to the point that they deleted the (ya) He said: The Arabs hardly delete the (ya) except from the vocative noun that the vocative adds to himself, except for their saying (O son of mother) and (O son of cousin), and that is because they are used a lot in their speech, so if something comes that is not used they keep the (ya), so they say (O son of my father) and (O son of my sister and brother) and (O son of my maternal aunt), and (O son of my maternal uncle).
The correct thing to say about this is to say: If the (mim) of Ibn Umm is opened, then what is meant by it is lamentation:
h
O son of my mother

, and likewise of (Ibn Am). If it is broken, then what is meant by it is addition, then the (ya) is deleted, which is a metaphor for the name of the informant about himself. It seems that some of those who denied the likeness of the kasra of this if it is broken is like the kasra of the zay of (Khazbaz), because the second of (Khazbaz) is not known except by the first, and the first is not known except by the second, so it became like sounds.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yunus al-Jarmi
m: that (Umm) is feminine and (Am) is feminine, and he said: It is not made into one name except with (Ibn) the masculine. They said: As for the good language and correct analogy, it is the language of the one who said: (
h
O son of my mother
) by proving the (ya), as Abu Zubayd said:
h
O son of my mother
, O brother of my soul, you left me for a difficult time As the other said:
h
O son of my mother

! If I had witnessed you calling on Tamim, but your call was not answered These people have included the letter ya in al-umm because it is not a vocative, but rather it is al-ibn without it. The Arabs only drop the letter ya from the vocative if they add it to themselves, not if they add it to someone other than themselves, as we have explained. It was said: Aaron only said to Moses, peace be upon him:
h
O son of my mother
, and he did not say: O son of my father, and they had one father and one mother, to appeal to him for his own sake through the womb of the mother. And His statement:
h
The people considered me weak and almost killed me

, means by the people those who devoted themselves to worshipping the calf and said: This is our god and the god of Moses, and they disobeyed Aaron. Their weakening of him was their abandonment of obeying him and following his command. And almost killed me, meaning: they came close but did not do so. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
Do not gloat

. The reciter of the regions read it as: Do not let the enemies rejoice over me, with a damma on the ta from tashamt and a kasra on the mim from it, from their saying: So-and-so rejoiced over so-and-so, if he pleased him with something that the one being rejoiced over dislikes.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid
m: that he recited: So do not let the enemies gloat over me.

c: Abdul Karim told me that Ibrahim bin Bashar told us that Sufyan told us that Hamid bin Qais said:
m: Mujahid recited: So do not let the enemies rejoice over me.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Hamid, he said:
m: Mujahid recited: (So do not let the enemies rejoice over me).

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Ziyad Al-Farra’,
m: who said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said:
h
Do not gloat

. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Kisa’i said: I don’t know, perhaps they meant: Do not have the enemies gloat over me. If it is correct, then it has similar verbs. The Arabs say: (I emptied and I emptied), so whoever says (I emptied) says: (I emptied), and whoever says (I emptied) says: (I emptied), and likewise (rakunt) and (warkan), and (shamlhum amr) and (shamlhum), in many speeches. He said: (the enemies) are in the nominative case, because the action belongs to them, for whoever says (gloat) or (gloat).

x: The reading that I do not permit reading except with it is the reading of those who read:
h
Do not gloat

with a damma on the first ta’ and a kasra on the mim from ashmat bihi ‘aduhu ashmattu bihi and the accusative of al-‘ada’ the enemies, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings of the regions on it, and the anomaly of the readings that differ from it, and that is sufficient as evidence for what differs from it. This is in addition to the general denial of the knowledge of the scholars of the speech of the Arabs: Shamat so-and-so so-and-so with so-and-so and Shamat so-and-so with so-and-so yashmud bihi he gloats with so-and-so. Rather, what is known from their speech when they report about a man gloating over his enemy is: Shamat bihi with a kasra on the mim: Yashmud bihi he gloats with him, with a fatha in the future tense. As for his saying:
h
And do not place me with the wrongdoing people
, it is the saying of Aaron to his brother Moses.

He says: Do not place me in your anger at me and your punishment of me, and I did not disobey your command, in the place of someone who disobeyed you and disobeyed your command, and worshipped the calf after you, and wronged himself, and worshipped someone other than the one to whom worship is due, and I did not agree with them on any of that, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And do not place me with the wrongdoing people
, he said: The people of the calf.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

evidence.text: He said: O Lord, I find in the tablets a nation whose Gospels are in their chests, they read them - and those before them used to read their books by looking, until when they raised them they did not memorize anything, nor did they recognize it.
The Torah was mentioned as seventy camel loads, and a part of it was read in a year, as:

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad bin Khalid Al-Makfoof told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, he said: The Torah was revealed and it was seventy camel loads long, and a part of it was read in a year.
Only four people read it: Moses bin Imran, Jesus, Ezra, and Joshua bin Nun, may God’s prayers be upon them.
There is a difference in the reading of his saying: O son of my mother.
This was read by most of the people of Medina and some of the people of Basra: O son of mother, with the opening of the mim of umm.
The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: Ibn Umm, with a kasra on the mim of umm.
He said: Whoever reads it as (O son of mother), it is in the language of those who say: (This is a young man who has come), making it one noun with a kasra at the end, like his saying: (Khaz Baz).
There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Do not gloat.

The reciter of the regions read it as: Do not let the enemies rejoice over me, with a damma on the ta from tashamt and a kasra on the mim from it, from their saying: So-and-so rejoiced over so-and-so, if he pleased him with something that the one being rejoiced over dislikes.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that I do not permit reading except with it is the reading of those who read: Do not gloat with a damma on the first ta’ and a kasra on the mim from ashmat bihi ‘aduhu ashmattu bihi and the accusative of al-‘ada’ the enemies, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings of the regions on it, and the anomaly of the readings that differ from it, and that is sufficient as evidence for what differs from it.

x: God Almighty says: Moses said, when his brother’s excuse became clear to him, and he knew that he had not neglected the duty that was upon him from God’s command, in committing what the ignorant worshippers of the calf had done: My Lord, forgive me, seeking forgiveness for what he had done to his brother, and for his brother for a past that had occurred between him and God: Envelop our sins with a veil from You with which You conceal them, and admit us into Your mercy, meaning: Have mercy on us with Your vast mercy, Your believing servants, for You are more merciful to Your servants than anyone who has had mercy on anything.

God Almighty says: Indeed, those who took the calf as a god, will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord by God hastening that for them, and humiliation which is disgrace, by God’s punishment of them for their disbelief in their Lord, in the life of this world in the immediate life of this world before the Hereafter.
Ibn Jurayj used to say about this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: “Indeed, those who took the calf will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world.
h
And thus do We recompense the slanderers
.” He said: This is for those who died from among those who took the calf before Moses, peace be upon him, returned, and those who fled from them when Moses ordered them to kill one another.

x: What Ibn Jurayj said, even if it is a statement that has merit, the apparent meaning of the Book of God, with the interpretation of most of the people of interpretation, is contrary to it. That is because God, the Exalted, made the report about those who took the calf general, that they would be afflicted with the wrath of their Lord and humiliation in this worldly life. The report from the people of interpretation from the Companions and the Followers is consistent that when God returned to the Children of Israel, Moses, peace be upon him, repented to the worshippers of the calf for their actions as He had informed about what Moses, peace be upon him, had said in His Book, and that is His saying: And when Moses said to his people, ‘O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves’ (al-Baqarah 2:54), so they did what their Prophet, peace be upon him, had commanded them to do.

So God’s command to them was what He had commanded them to do, killing one another, out of His wrath upon them for worshipping the calf. So killing one another was a humiliation and disgrace for them, by which God humiliated them in this worldly life, and a repentance from them to God before that. No one can make a report that the Book came with its generality, in a specific matter that the apparent meaning is general, without proof from the argument of the report or reason. We do not know of a report that came with the obligation to transfer the apparent meaning of His statement: Indeed, those who took the calf - wrath from their Lord will overtake them, to a specific hidden meaning, nor is there any evidence for it from reason, so it is necessary to refer its apparent meaning to its hidden meaning. What is meant by his saying:
h
And thus do We recompense the slanderers

, is that just as We recompensed those who took the calf as a god, by bringing wrath upon them and humiliating them in this worldly life for their disbelief in their Lord and their apostasy from their religion after their belief in God, thus do We recompense everyone who slanders God, lies about Him, acknowledges the divinity of someone other than Him, and worships something other than Him from idols, after acknowledging the oneness of God and after his belief in Him and in His prophets and messengers.
And it was said that if he does not repent from his disbelief before he is killed.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, he said:
m: Abu Qilabah recited: There will overtake them wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, the verse, he said: It is the reward of every slanderer until the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:that God Almighty will humiliate him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Al-Nu’man A’rim told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said:
m: Abu Qilabah recited this verse one day: “Indeed, those who took the calf will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world.
h
And thus do We recompense the slanderers

.” He said: By God, it is for every slanderer until the Day of Resurrection. ... He said: Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit and Hamid: Qais bin Abbad and Jariyah bin Qudamah entered upon Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him and said: Do you think this matter that you are in and that you are calling to, did the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) entrust it to you, or is it an opinion that you saw? He said: What is this to you? Turn away from this! They said: By God, we will not turn away from it until you tell us! He said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) entrusted me with nothing but a letter in the scabbard of my sword! So he drew it, and took out the letter from the scabbard of his sword, and in it was: ((There was no prophet who did not have a sanctuary, and I have made Madinah sacred just as Abraham (peace be upon him) made Makkah sacred. No weapons may be carried in it for fighting. Whoever innovates something new or shelters an innovator, upon him is the curse of God, the angels, and all of mankind. No ransom or compensation will be accepted from him.)) So when they left, one of them said to the other: Do you not see this letter? So they returned and left him and said: We heard God say: Indeed, those who took the calf will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord (al-Baqarah 2:17). And the people have fabricated a lie, and I do not know anything except that humiliation will befall them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And thus do We recompense the slanderers
, he said: Every innovator is humiliated.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Al-Nu’man A’rim told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said: Abu Qilabah recited this verse one day: “Indeed, those who took the calf will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world.

x: This is report from God Almighty that He accepts the repentance of every person who repents to Him for a sin he has committed, whether his disobedience is minor or major, whether it is disbelief or not, just as He accepted the repentance of the worshippers of the calf after their disbelief in Him by worshipping the calf and their apostasy from their religion. God Almighty says: And those who have done evil deeds, then returned to seeking God’s pleasure by turning to what He loves from what He hates, and to what He is pleased with from what He is angry with, after their evil deeds, and believed that God accepts the repentance of sinners and accepts the repentance of those who turn back, through the sincerity of their hearts and their certainty of that, He is Forgiving of them, meaning He conceals their evil deeds for them, and does not disgrace them with them, Merciful of them and of everyone who is like them among the repentant.
God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And when the anger subsided from Moses

, when he was restrained from it and calmed down. Likewise, every one who is restrained from something is: (silent about it), and the one who is silent about speech is called (silent) because he refrained from it.

c: It was reported from Yunus al-Jarmi that he said:
m: It is said: (grief subsided from him), and everything, as he claimed, and from this is the saying of Abu al-Najm: The snake wanted to run away and the meowing stopped. He took the tablets, meaning he took them after he had thrown them down, and some of them had gone. And in its inscription is guidance and mercy, meaning what was written in it, guidance, a clarification of the truth. And mercy for those who fear their Lord, meaning for those who fear God and dread His punishment for their sins. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of the letter lam in the phrase they fear their Lord, with the Arabs finding it undesirable to say in speech I feared you, meaning: I feared you, and I honored you, meaning: I honored you.

x: Some of them said: This is as God Almighty said:
If you interpret dreams
he connected the verb with the letter lam.
Some of them said: For the sake of their Lord they fear.

Some of them said: It was only introduced after the addition: those who are fearful of their Lord, and fearful of their Lord, then the lam was introduced for this meaning, because it was introduced after the addition, not for the obligation.
Some of them said: He did that because the noun preceded the verb, so it was good to insert the lam.
Others said: Something similar has come in delaying the noun in His statement: He has given you some of what you are hastening (al-Naml 27:72).

c: It was reported on the authority of Isa bin Omar that he said:
m: I heard Al-Farazdaq say: I gave him one hundred dirhams, meaning: I gave him one hundred dirhams. He said: The speech is broad.

x: God Almighty says: And Moses chose from his people seventy men, for the time and term that God promised him that he would meet them in, to repent for what their fools had done in the matter of the calf, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: God commanded Moses, peace be upon him, to come to Him with some of the Children of Israel, to apologize to Him for worshipping the calf, and He promised them an appointment. So Moses chose seventy men from his people in his sight, then he went with them to apologize. When they came to that place, they said: We will not believe you, O Moses, until we see God clearly, for you have spoken to Him, so show Him! So the thunderbolt struck them and they died. Then Moses stood up crying and supplicating to God, saying: My Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel when I come to them and You have destroyed their best? If You had wished, You could have destroyed them and me before! Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that Moses chose seventy men from among the Children of Israel, the best of whom were the best, and said: Go to God and repent to Him for what you have done, and ask Him to forgive those of your people whom you have left behind you. Fast and purify yourselves, and purify your clothes! So he went out with them to Mount Sinai, for the appointed time that his Lord had set for him. He would not come to it except with His permission and knowledge. So the seventy said - as I was told - when they had done what he had commanded them to do, and went out with him to meet his Lord, to Moses: Ask us to hear the words of our Lord! He said: I will. So when Moses approached the mountain, a pillar of cloud fell upon him until it covered the whole mountain. Moses approached and entered it, and said to the al-Nas 114:Come near. And when God spoke to Moses, a bright light fell upon his forehead that none of the children of Adam could look at! So a veil was drawn between him and them. The people drew near, and when they entered the cloud, they fell down in prostration. They heard Him speaking to Moses, commanding him and forbidding him: Do and do not do! When God finished His command, the cloud cleared from Moses. He came towards them, and they said to Moses: We will not believe you until we see God clearly! Then the earthquake - which is the thunderbolt - seized them and their souls were torn away, and they all died. Moses, peace be upon him, stood up, imploring his Lord, calling upon Him and beseeching Him, and saying: My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me! They acted foolishly. Will You destroy those of the Children of Israel who come after me?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time

, he said: God had commanded him to choose from his people seventy men, so he chose seventy men, and he went out with them to call upon their Lord. And among what they called upon God was that they said: O God, give us that which You have not given to anyone after us! But God disliked that from their call, so the earthquake seized them. Moses said: O Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before!

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Khalid bin Hayyan told us, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Maimun:
m: h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time
, he said: for the appointed time that He had promised them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Seventy men for our appointment, he said: He chose them to fulfill the promise.

x: Others said: The tremor only took them because of their claim that Moses killed Aaron.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, Sufyan told us, Abu Ishaq told me, on the authority of Ammarah bin Abdul Salouli, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: Moses, Aaron, Shiber, and Shabir set out, and they went to the foot of a mountain. Aaron slept on a bed, and God took him. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel, they said to him: Where is Aaron? He said: God took him! They said: You killed him, you envied us for his character and his gentleness - or a word to that effect - He said: Then choose whomever you wish! He said: So they chose seventy men. He said: That is why His statement:
h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time

, He said: So when they came to him, they said: O Aaron, who killed you? He said: No one killed me, but God took me! They said: O Moses, you will never disobey again from today on! He said: Then the earthquake seized them. He said: So Moses kept going back and forth, and said: “O Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before.
h
Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done
? This is nothing but Your trial by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will.” He said: So God revived them and made them all prophets.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Banu Salul:
m: that he heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say about this verse:
h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time

, he said: Aaron was of good character and beloved by the Children of Israel. He said: When he died, Moses buried him. He said: When he came to the Children of Israel, they said to him: Where is Aaron? He said: He died! They said: You killed him! He said: So he chose seventy men from among them. He said: When they came to the grave, Moses said: Were you killed or did you die? He said: I died! They were stunned, and Moses said: My Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel? When I return, they will say: You killed them! He said: So they were brought back to life and made prophets.

c: Abdullah bin Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Al-Rabi bin Habib told us, he said:
m: I heard Abu Saeed - meaning Al-Raqashi - and he recited this verse: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment, and he said: They were sons, except for twenty, and they did not exceed forty, and that is because the ignorance and youth of a twenty-year-old have gone, and that the one who has not exceeded forty has not lost anything of his mind.

x: Others said: The people were shaken by the earthquake because they refused to leave the worshippers of the calf, not because they were among its worshippers.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time

, and he recited until he reached: the fools among us, it was mentioned to us that Ibn Abbas used to say: The earthquake only overtook them because they did not leave the people when they set up the calf, and they hated to have intercourse with them over it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time

, from among those who had not said that statement, although they had not agreed with them on it, so the earthquake seized them because they had not separated from their people when they made the calf. He said: So when they went out and made supplication, God caused them to die and then brought them back to life. So when the earthquake seized them, he said: “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me.
h
Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said, Mujahid said:
m: h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time

, and the appointment is the appointment. So when the earthquake took them after Moses went out with the seventy from his people, calling upon God and asking Him to remove the affliction from them, but He did not answer them, Moses knew that they had committed the same sin that their people had committed. Abu Saad said: Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi told me, he said: They were not answered, because they did not forbid them from evil and command them to do good. He said: So the earthquake took them, and they died, then God revived them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Awn, on the authority of Saeed bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The seventy whom Moses chose from his people were only struck by the earthquake because they were not satisfied and did not forbid the calf.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Awn told us, he said, Saʿid ibn Hayyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the accusative case of his statement:
h
His people are seventy men at our appointed time
. Some Basra grammarians said: Its meaning is: Moses chose seventy men from his people. When he removed from he made the verb work, as Al-Farazdaq said: Surat al-A’raf 7:155
h
And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time
. But when the earthquake seized them, he said, "My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before.
h
Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done
? It is only Your trial by which You mislead whom You will and guide whom You will.
h
You are our protector

, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the All-Hearing, the All-Wise." The best of forgivers And among us are those men who were chosen for their generosity and kindness, when the stormy winds blow As the other said: I have commanded you to do good, so do what I have commanded you to do, for I have left you with wealth and lineage. The shepherd said: People chose you when their nature became weak and those who had hope in you became ill.

x: Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The verb was permitted to occur to them if you omitted min because it is taken from your saying: These are the best of the people and the best of the people. So when the addition was permitted in place of min and the meaning did not change, they permitted to say: I chose you a man and I chose a man from you.

i: The poet said:
x: I said to him: Choose a fat camel.

i: The rajaz poet said:
x: Under which God chose the tree Meaning God chose it for him from the trees.

This second statement is more correct in my opinion, because the word choice indicates the request for from which means partiality. It is the custom of the Arabs to delete something from the context of a sentence if its location is known, and what I have shown indicates what was deleted. So this is one of those things, God willing. We have previously explained the meaning of the earthquake with its evidence, and that it is: what shakes the people, shakes them, and moves them, destroys them and causes them to die, or stuns them and takes away their understanding. We have mentioned the narration in other places and the statement of those who said: It was a thunderbolt that killed them.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So when the earthquake seized them, they died, then He brought them back to life.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nahih, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Seventy men for Our appointed time, Moses chose them to complete the appointment, and when the earthquake seized them, they died and then God revived them.

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said,
m: Abu Saʿd said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So when the earthquake seized them, he said: It shook them.

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “
h
Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done
It is only Your trial by which You mislead whom You will and guide whom You will.
h
You are our protector
, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, for You are the best of forgivers.”
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Will you destroy those whom you destroyed for what the fools among us did, that is, for the worship of those who worshipped the calf? They said: And God only destroyed them because they were among those who worshipped the calf. And Moses said what he said, and he had no knowledge of what they had done.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done
? So God revealed to Moses: These seventy are among those who took the calf! That is when Moses said:
h
It is only your trial
by which You mislead whom You will and guide whom You will.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Your destruction of those whom you destroyed is the destruction of those who came after them from the Children of Israel if you turn to them and they are not with me. And the fools, according to this statement, were the destroyed ones who asked that their Lord show them.
Who said that?

i: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said:
x: When the earthquake struck the seventy and they all died, Moses stood up and implored his Lord, calling upon Him and beseeching Him, saying: My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before. They acted foolishly. Will You then destroy those of the Children of Israel who come after me for what the fools among us have done?

That is, this is their destruction. I have chosen from among them seventy men, the best of the best. I will return to them, and not one man is with me! So what will they believe me about, or trust me with, after this!
Others said about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done
? Will You hold us accountable while there is not a single man among us who has abandoned Your worship, nor replaced You with someone else?

x: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the one that says: Moses was only saddened by the destruction of the seventy by saying:
h
Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done

? and that he meant by the fools the worshippers of the calf. This is because it is impossible that Moses, peace be upon him, would have chosen from among his people to ask his Lord what he saw that he should ask for them except the best of them, and it is impossible that the best in his view was the one who associated partners in worshipping the calf and took it as a god besides God.

i: He said:
x: If someone says: It is possible that Moses, peace be upon him, believed that God Almighty punishes a people for the sins of others, and he says: Will you destroy us for the sins of those who worshipped the calf, and we are innocent of that? It was said: It is possible that the meaning of destruction is the taking of souls without punishment, as God Almighty said: If a man perishes,
r
(An-Nisa’: 176)
- meaning: he dies - then He says: Did you kill us because of what the fools among us did? As for His statement:
h
It is nothing but your trial
, He, the Most High, says: This action that my people did, of worshipping what they worshipped instead of you, is nothing but a trial from you that befell them.

He means by trial the trial and examination. He says: I tested them with it, so that it would become clear who is led astray from the truth by worshipping it, and who is guided by abandoning its worship. He attributed their misguidance and guidance to God, since what they did was due to a cause from Him, the Most High. And similar to what we said about the trial, a group of people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah:
m: h
It is nothing but your trial

, he said, your affliction. ... He said, Habawayh al-Razi told us, on the authority of Yaʿqub, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr: Except your trial, except your affliction.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas:
m: h
It is nothing but your trial

, he said, your affliction. ... He said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is nothing but Your trial by which You mislead whomever You will, it is nothing but Your punishment by which You inflict upon whomever You will, and turn it away from whomever You will.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is only your trial
, you are their trial. And His saying:
h
You are our protector

, meaning: You are our supporter. So forgive us, meaning: So cover our sins by not punishing us for them. And have mercy on us, meaning: Have compassion on us with Your mercy. And You are the best of forgivers, meaning: The best of those who pardon a crime and cover up a sin.

evidence.text: Abdullah bin Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Al-Rabi bin Habib told us, he said: I heard Abu Saeed - meaning Al-Raqashi - and he recited this verse: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment, and he said: They were sons, except for twenty, and they did not exceed forty, and that is because the ignorance and youth of a twenty-year-old have gone, and that the one who has not exceeded forty has not lost anything of his mind.

x: God Almighty says, informing about the supplication of His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, that he said in it: And write for us, meaning: make us among those for whom You have written, in this world good, which are the righteous deeds, and in the Hereafter, among those for whom You have written forgiveness for their sins, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And decree for us in this world [that which is] good
, he said: forgiveness. And his saying: Indeed, we have turned to You, means: We have repented to You. And the people of interpretation said something similar.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said,
m: Jarir, Ibn Fadil, and Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr - and Imran said: on the authority of Ibn Abbas - Indeed,
h
we have been guided to You

, he said: We have repented to You. ... He said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: We repent to You. ... He said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: We repent to You. ... He said, Abdullah bin Bakr told us, on the authority of Hatim bin Abi Saghira, on the authority of Samak: that Ibn Abbas said about this verse: Indeed, we have turned to You, he said: We have repented to You.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair - he
m: said: I think it was on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed,
h
we have been guided to You
, he said: We have repented to You.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Indeed, we have turned to You, meaning: We have repented to You.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, Abd al-Rahman bin al-Asbahani told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, we have turned to You, he said: We have repented to You. ... He said, Abd al-Rahman and Wakiʿ ibn al-Jarrah told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Al-Asbahani, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: the same. ... He said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: We repent to You. ... He said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, who said: We repent to You.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi,
m: the same.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, we have turned to You, meaning: We have repented to You.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We have been guided to You
, he said: We have repented.

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Indeed,
h
we have been guided to You
, he says: We have repented to You.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Indeed, we have turned to You, he says: We have repented to You.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, he said:
m: h
We have been guided to You

, we have repented to You. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hujair, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: We repent to You. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: We repent to You. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say:

c: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak say, and he mentioned something similar. ... He said, my father and Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: We repent to You. ... He said, Habawayh, may God be pleased with him, told us, on the authority of Yaʿqub, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, the same. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yahya, on the authority of Ali, peace be upon him, who said: They were called the Jews because they said: We have been guided to you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Indeed,
h
we have been guided to You
, meaning: we have repented to You.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr told us, he said,
m: I heard a man asking Saeed:
h
We have been guided to You
, he said: We have repented to You. We have explained the meaning of this with evidence previously, so there is no need to repeat it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “He said, ‘
h
My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will
, but My mercy encompasses all things.
So I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakat and those who believe in Our verses.’”

God Almighty says: God said to Moses: This earthquake that I have inflicted upon your people is My punishment, which I inflict upon whomever I wish of My creation, just as I inflicted upon those whom I inflicted upon your people.
h
And My mercy encompasses all things
, meaning: My mercy encompasses all of My creation.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.

Some of them said: Its source is general, but its meaning is specific, and what is meant by it is: My mercy has encompassed the believers in Me from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he cited as evidence the statement that follows it, which is His statement: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear Me, the verse.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salamah Al-Manqari told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, he said, Ata bin Al-Saib told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he read:
h
And My mercy encompasses all things
, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me, he said: God made it for this nation.

c: Abdul Karim told me, he said, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, he said,
m: Sufyan said, Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali said: When the verse:
h
And My mercy encompasses all things

was revealed, Satan said: I am from the thing! So God took it away from Satan, He said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakat and those who believe in Our verses. The Jews said: We fear God and give zakat and believe in the verses of our Lord! So God took it away from the Jews and said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, all the verses. He said: So God took it away from Satan and the Jews, and made it for this nation.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: When the verse:
h
And My mercy encompasses all things

was revealed, Satan said: I am from all things! God said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakat and those who believe in Our verses, the verse. The Jews said: And we fear God and give zakat! So God revealed: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, he said: God took it away from Satan and the Jews, and made it for the nation of Muhammad: I will prescribe it for those who fear God among your people.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will
h
and My mercy encompasses all things

, so Iblis said: I am from that (thing)! So God revealed: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God, the disobedience of God, and those who believe in Our verses, so the Jews and Christians wished for it, so God revealed a firm and clear condition, and said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, so he is your Prophet, he was unlettered and did not write, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ya’qub narrated to me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, he said, Khalid al-Hadha’ informed us, on the authority of Anis bin Abi al-‘Aryan, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good
. Indeed, we have turned back to You,” he said: So he was not given it, so he said: My punishment - I will afflict with it whom I will,
h
and My mercy encompasses all things
, so I will prescribe it for those who fear God, until His statement: The Messenger, the unlettered Prophet.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah and Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Anis Abi al-Aryan - Abd al-A’la
m: said, on the authority of Anis Abi al-Aryan - and he said: Ibn Abbas said: “
h
And decree for us in this world [that which is] good
and in the Hereafter. Indeed, we have turned back to You.” He said: So Moses did not give it to him, he said:
h
My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will
h
and My mercy encompasses all things
, so I will write it Surat al-A’raf 7:156
h
And decree for us in this world [that which is] good
and in the Hereafter. Indeed, we have turned back to You. He said, "
h
My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will
, but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will decree it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses." down, to the end of the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God had written on the tablets the mention of Muhammad and the mention of his nation, and what He had stored for them with Him, and what He had made easy for them in their religion, and what He had made easy for them in what He had made permissible for them, and He said:
h
My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will
h
and My mercy encompasses all things
, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me - meaning: polytheism - the verse.

x: Others said: Rather, this is general in this world, and specific in the hereafter.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And My mercy encompasses all things
, they said: It encompasses in this world the righteous and the wicked, and on the Day of Resurrection it is specifically for those who feared God.

x: Others said: It is general, and it is repentance.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “You are our protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, for You are the best of forgivers.
h
And decree for us in this world [that which is] good
and in the Hereafter. Indeed, we have turned back to You.” He said: Moses asked this, and God said:
h
My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will

, the punishment that was mentioned, and My mercy, repentance, has encompassed all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me. He said: So His mercy was the repentance that Moses, peace be upon him, asked for, God wrote it for us. As for his saying: Then I will write it for those who fear God, he is saying: Then I will write My mercy that encompasses all things. The meaning of I will write in this place: I will write on the tablet on which the Torah was written, for those who fear God, meaning: for the people who fear God and dread His punishment for disbelieving in Him and disobeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, so they perform His obligations and avoid His disobedience.

x: The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of what God described of these people as fearing Him.
Some of them said: It is polytheism.
Mention of those who said that: Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Then I will write it down for those who fear God, meaning polytheism.

x: Others said: Rather, it is all sins.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Then I will write it down for those who fear God, the sins of God. As for zakat and its payment, we have explained its description previously, so there is no need to repeat it. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas in this place that he said about that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they give zakat, he said: They obey God and His Messenger. It is as if Ibn Abbas interpreted this to mean that it means doing what purifies the soul and cleanses it of good deeds. As for his saying:
h
And those who believe in Our signs
, he says: And for the people who believe and acknowledge our signs and proofs.

x: This statement is a clarification from God, the Most High, that those whom He promised His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, that He would write for them the mercy that He, the Most High, described by saying: And My mercy encompasses all things, are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because there is no known messenger of God described with this description - I mean unlettered - other than our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is what the narrations from the people of interpretation came with.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Then I will write it down for those who fear God

, he said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. ... He said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then I will write it down for those who fear God
, he said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Moses, peace be upon him, said: I wish I had been created in the nation of Muhammad!

c: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Then I will write it down for those who fear God

, he said: for those who follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Jarir narrated, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Nawf al-Himyari, who said: When Moses chose seventy men from his people for the meeting with his Lord, God said to Moses: I will make the earth a place of prostration and purification for you, and I will place tranquility with you in your homes, and I will make you recite the Torah from memory, and it will be read by the man among you and the woman, the free and the slave, the young and the old. Moses said to his al-Nas 114:God has indeed made the earth a place of prostration and purification for you. They said: We do not want to pray except in churches! He said: And He will place tranquility with you in your homes. They said: We do not want anything except for it to be as it was, in the Ark! He said: And He will make you recite the Torah from memory, and it will be read by the man among you and the woman, the free and the slave, the young and the old. They said: We do not want to read it except by looking! God said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakah until His saying:
h
Those are the successful

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Nawf al-Bakali, he said:
m: When Moses set out with the delegation of the Children of Israel, God spoke to him and said: I have spread out the earth for them as a place of purification and places of worship in which they may pray wherever the prayer overtakes them, except near a toilet, grave, or bathhouse. I have placed tranquility in their hearts and made them read the Torah with their tongues. He said: Moses mentioned that to the Children of Israel, and they said: We cannot carry tranquility in our hearts, so make it for us in a chest, and we will not read the Torah except by looking, and we will not pray except in the church. God said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakat, until he reached
h
Those are the successful

ones. He said: Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, make me their prophet! He said: Their prophet is from them! He said: O Lord, make me from them! He said: You will never reach them! He said: O Lord, I came to you with the delegation of the Children of Israel, and you made our delegation for others! Then God revealed: And among the people of Moses was a community who guided with the truth and did justice thereby (al-A’raf 7:159). Nawf Al-Bakali said: So thank God who preserved your absence, took your share for you, and made the delegation of the Children of Israel yours.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Nawf al-Bakali,
m: something similar, except that he said: Surat al-A’raf 7:157
h
Those who follow the Messenger

, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel. He enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the bad and relieves them of their burden
h
and the shackles which were upon them
. So those who have believed And they honored him and supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him.
h
Those are the successful

ones. I am sending down to you the Torah, and you will read it from your tongues, your men, your women, and your children. They said: We will not pray except in a church. Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith in a similar manner.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Then I will write it down for those who fear God
, he said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Then I will write it down for those who fear God
, he said: These are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When it was said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses, the Jews and Christians desired it, so God revealed a clear and firm condition and said:
h
Those who follow the Messenger

, the unlettered Prophet, and he is your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was unlettered and did not write. We have explained the meaning of illiterate previously, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his saying:
h
Which they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel
, the ha in his saying: they find it refers back to the Messenger, who is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, like the one who:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who follow the Messenger
, the unlettered Prophet, this is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Uthman bin Omar told us, he said, Falih told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, he said:
m: I met Abdullah bin Amr and said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah as he is described in the Qur’an: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner and a protection for the unlettered. You are My servant and Messenger. I have named you Al-Mutawakkil. He is not rude nor harsh nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil for evil, but pardons and overlooks. And We will not take him until We establish through him the crooked religion, by them saying: (There is no god but God), so We open through him covered hearts, deaf ears, and blind eyes. Ata said: Then I met Kaab and asked him about that, and they did not differ a word, except that Kaab said in his language: Covered hearts, deaf ears, and blind eyes.

c: Abu Kuraib told me, he said, Musa bin Dawud told us, he said, Falih bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, he said, Ata’ told me, he said:
m: I met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said in Ka’b’s words: General eyes, deaf ears, and closed hearts. ...

c: Abu Kuraib told me, he said, Musa bin Dawud told us, he said, Falih bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, he said, Ata’ told me, he said:
m: I met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said in Ka’b’s words: General eyes, deaf ears, and closed hearts. ... He said, Musa told us, Abdul Aziz bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah, in a similar manner, and there is no word from Ka’b in it.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God said: Which they find written with them, meaning: they find his description, his command, and his prophethood written with them.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “He enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the bad things and removes from them their burden
h
and the shackles which were upon them

God Almighty says: This unlettered Prophet commands his followers to do what is right, which is belief in God and to adhere to His obedience in what He commands and forbids. This is the right that he commands them to do, and he forbids them from what is wrong, which is associating partners with God and refraining from what God forbade them from.
And His saying:
h
And He has made lawful for them the good things

, which is what the Jahiliyyah prohibited of the Bahā’ir, the Sā’ib, the Wasā’il, and the Hāwāmi, And He has forbidden for them the bad things, which is the meat of pigs, usury, and what they considered lawful of the foods and drinks that God has prohibited, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And He forbids them the impure things, which are pork and usury, and what they considered permissible of the forbidden foods that God forbade. As for his saying:
h
And He removes from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: He means by the covenant the covenant and pledge that he took from the Children of Israel to act according to what was in the Torah.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jaber bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And He will remove from them their burden, he said: their covenant. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: Their covenant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And He will remove from them their burden, he said: the covenants that they gave of themselves. ... He said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Musa bin Qais, on the authority of Mujahid: And He will remove from them their burden, he said: their covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And He will remove from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them
, he said: He will remove from them their covenants and agreements which were taken from them in the Torah and the Gospel.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And He will remove from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them
, what God had taken from them of the covenant regarding what He had forbidden them. He says: He will remove that from them.

x: Some of them said: He meant by that that he removes from those who followed the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the severity that was imposed on the Children of Israel in their religion.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He will remove from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them
, so Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with a release from him and overlooked him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: And He will remove from them their burden, he said: urine and the like, which were difficult for the Children of Israel. ... He said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Yaqoub told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed, he said: The intensity of the work.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: Mujahid said, regarding his statement:
h
And He will remove from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them
, he said: Whoever follows Muhammad and his religion from the People of the Book, He will remove from them what was upon them of the severity in their religion.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: Abu Hurairah said to Ibn Abbas: Is there no blame upon us in religion for committing adultery and stealing? He said: Yes! But the burden that was on the Children of Israel has been lifted from you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And He removes from them their burden
, he said, their burden that He placed upon them.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say that the covenant is the covenant - and we have explained that with its evidence in a place other than this sufficiently - and that the meaning of the statement is: And the unlettered prophet will abolish the covenant that God took from the Children of Israel, of establishing the Torah and doing what is in it of severe deeds, such as cutting off the skin from urine, and prohibiting spoils of war, and similar deeds that were imposed upon them, but the ruling of the Qur’an abrogated them.
As for the shackles that were upon them, Ibn Zayd used to say:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And the shackles which were upon them
, he said: The shackles. He read: Their hands were shackled (al-Ma’idah 5:64). He said: Those shackles. He said: And he called them to believe in the Prophet so that he would remove that from them.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: So those who believed in him, honored him, supported him, and followed the light which was sent down with him -
h
those are the successful
ones.
God Almighty says: Those who believed in the unlettered Prophet and acknowledged his prophethood, “and honored him, meaning: they respected him, glorified him, and protected him from the people, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they punished him, meaning: they protected him and honored him.

c: Al-Harithqal told me, Abd al-Aziz told us, Musa ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they supported him
and aided him. “They supported him” means they made his matter right and helped his Messenger, and aided him. And His statement:
h
And they supported him

, meaning: and they aided him against the enemies of God and his enemies, by striving against them and waging war against them, and they followed the light which was sent down with him, meaning the Qur’an and Islam, Surat al-A’raf 7:157
h
Those who follow the Messenger

, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel. He enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the bad and relieves them of their burden
h
and the shackles which were upon them
. So those who have believed And they honored him and supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him.
h
Those are the successful
ones. and
h
those are the successful

ones, meaning: those who do these actions with which the Most High described the followers of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are the successful ones who attain what they sought and hoped for by doing that.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: They - meaning the Jews - did not resent him except because they envied the Prophet of God, so God said: Those who believed in him, honored him, and supported him. As for supporting and honoring him, you have preceded them in that, but the best of you are those who believe in God and follow the light that was sent down with him. Qatada means by his statement: (They only resented him because they envied the Prophet of God) that the Jews considered Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, a mercy to them with what he brought from God if they had followed him, because he came to remove the burden and shackles from them, but envy led them to disbelieve in him and to refuse to accept the relief, because God’s abandonment of them was overwhelming.
