evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Jarir narrated, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Nawf al-Himyari, who said: When Moses chose seventy men from his people for the meeting with his Lord, God said to Moses: I will make the earth a place of prostration and purification for you, and I will place tranquility with you in your homes, and I will make you recite the Torah from memory, and it will be read by the man among you and the woman, the free and the slave, the young and the old.
He said: And He will make you recite the Torah from memory, and it will be read by the man among you and the woman, the free and the slave, the young and the old.
They said: We do not want to read it except by looking!
I am sending down to you the Torah, and you will read it from your tongues, your men, your women, and your children.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to all people, I am the Messenger of God to you all, not to some of you and not others, as the messengers before me were sent to some people and not others. So whoever among them was sent in this way, then my message is not to some of you and not others, but to all of you. His saying: Who is an attribute of the name God. The meaning of the speech is: Say: O people, I am the Messenger of God, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, to you. And what He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth

, is the One who has the authority over the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and the management and administration of that, There is no god but Him, that divinity and worship should not be for anyone but Him, the Most High, without all other things besides Him of rivals and idols, except for the One who has the authority over everything, and is able to create whatever He wills and bring it to life, and to destroy it if He wills to cause it to die, So believe in God and His Messenger, the Most High says: Say to them: So believe in the signs of God, whose description is this, and acknowledge His Oneness, and that He is the One to whom divinity and worship belong, and believe in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was sent to His creation, calling to His Oneness and obedience.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
The unlettered prophet who believes in God and His words
And follow him that you may be guided.”
As for his saying:
h
The unlettered prophet

, it is a description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have explained the meaning of prophet in the past, so there is no need to repeat it, and the meaning of his saying: the illiterate. He who believes in God means:
h
he who believes in God and His words
. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: and His words.
Some of them said: It means: and its verses.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He who believes in God and His words
, he said: His verses.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Mujahid said, regarding his statement: who believes in God and His words, he said, Jesus, son of Mary.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
He who believes in God and His words
, he is Jesus, son of Mary.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God Almighty commanded His servants to believe in the prophethood of the unlettered Prophet who believed in God and His words. He did not specify the report of his belief in God’s words to some and not others, but rather He informed them of all of the words. So the truth in this is to make the statement general, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed in all of God’s words, according to what is stated in the apparent meaning of God’s Book. As for the Almighty’s saying: And follow him that you may be guided, so be guided by him, O people, and do what he has commanded you to do in obeying God, that you may be guided, he says: so that you may be guided, so that you may be guided and attain the truth in following him.

God Almighty says: And among the people of Moses, meaning the Children of Israel, is a nation, meaning a group, guiding by the truth, meaning they are guided by the truth, meaning they are upright in it and act upon it, and by it they are just, meaning: and by the truth they give and take, and they are fair to themselves and do not act unjustly. And a group of people said about the description of this nation that God mentioned in the verse, and we will mention what we have witnessed of it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Sadaqah Abu Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And among the people of Moses is a community who guide with the truth and do justice thereby, he said: A people between you and them is a river of honey.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among the people of Moses was a community guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby

, he said: I was informed that when the Children of Israel killed their prophets, they disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes. One tribe disavowed what they had done, apologized, and asked God to separate them from them, so God opened a tunnel in the earth for them, so they traveled through it until they came out from behind China, and they are there, monotheists, Muslims, facing our Qiblah. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: That is what God said: “And We said after him to the Children of Israel, ‘Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in droves. ’” (al-Isra’ 17:104). And the promise of the Hereafter means Jesus, son of Mary, with whom they will come out. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: They traveled in the flock for a year and a half.

x: God Almighty says: We divided them, meaning the people of Moses from the Children of Israel. God divided them and made them into different tribes, twelve tribes. We have previously explained the meaning of the tribes and who they are. The Arab scholars differed on the reason for the feminization of the twelve and the tribes as a masculine plural.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He meant twelve groups, then he said that the groups are tribes, and he did not make the number tribes.

Some of them used this interpretation and said: The number does not come out to anything other than what follows, but (the groups) comes before (the twelve), so that (the twelve) would be feminine according to what preceded it, and the speech would be: And we divided them into groups of twelve tribes, so the feminine is correct for what came before.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: He said: (the twelve) in the feminine form, and (the grandson) in the masculine form, because the speech referred to (the nations), so the feminine form prevailed, even though (the grandson) is masculine, and it is like the poet’s saying: These dogs have ten clans, and you are innocent of their ten tribes. He went with al-batn to the tribe and the faction, so he pluralized al-batn with the feminine ending. Other grammarians of Kufa said: The twelve are feminine and the grandson is masculine, because of the mention of the nations.

The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that (the twelve) was made feminine because (the piece) was made feminine, and the meaning of the statement is: And we cut them into twelve pieces, then (the pieces) was translated as (the tribes), and it is not permissible for (the tribes) to be an explanation of (the twelve) which is a plural, because the explanation of what is above (the ten) to (the twenty) is singular, not plural, and (the tribes) is plural, not singular, and this is like their saying: (I have twelve women), and it is not said: (I have twelve women), so it is clear from that that (the tribes) is not an explanation of the twelve, and the statement in that is as we said. As for nations, they are groups, and tribe in the Children of Israel is like century. It was said: They were divided into tribes because of their differences in their religion.
The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “
h
And We inspired Moses when his people asked him for water
, saying, ‘Strike the rock with your staff.’

Then twelve springs gushed forth from it. Each people knew its drinking place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, ‘Eat from the good things We have provided for you.’ And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.”

God Almighty says: And We inspired Moses, when We divided his people, the Children of Israel, into twelve groups, and We caused them to wander in the wilderness, and they asked Moses for water from thirst and the water had subsided, Strike the stone with your staff. We have explained the reason why his people asked him for water, and we have explained the meaning of revelation with its evidence. Then twelve springs of water gushed forth, meaning each of the twelve tribes, knowing their drinking place, meaning each tribe of the twelve tribes, and We shaded them with clouds, protecting them from the heat and harm of the sun. We have explained the meaning of clouds previously, as well as manna and quails. “And We sent down upon them manna and quails,” as food for them, Eat from the good things We have provided for you, meaning: And We said to them: Eat from the lawful things We have provided for you, O people, and We have made it good for you, and they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves, and there is something omitted in the speech, which was left out because what appeared about that was: (So they were silent about that, and said, We will not be patient with one kind of food, so they substituted that which is better for that which is worse), and they Surat al-A’raf 7:160 And We divided them into twelve tribes, nations.
h
And We inspired Moses when his people asked him for water

, "Strike the rock with your staff." Then twelve springs gushed forth from it. Each people knew their drinking place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, "Eat of the good things that We have given you." We provided for you, and they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves. did not wrong Us, meaning: and they did not bring about a decrease in our kingdom and authority by asking us what they asked, and doing what they did, but they were wronging themselves, meaning: they were reducing their portions by substituting the better for the worse, and the better for the worse.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember also, O Muhammad, the error of the actions of these people, their opposition to their Lord, their disobedience to their Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, and their changing the statement they were commanded to say when God said to them: Dwell in this city, which is the city of Jerusalem, and eat from it, meaning from its fruits, grains, and plants, wherever you wish, from it, meaning: wherever you wish from it, and say, ‘Forgiveness,’ meaning: and say: this action (Forgiveness), it will erase our sins, We will forgive you, meaning your Lord will cover you, your sins, which you have committed in the past, so He will pardon you for them, and will not hold you accountable for them, We will increase the doers of good, from among you, and they are the obedient ones to God, in accordance with what I promised you of forgiveness of sins. We have mentioned the narrations on all of this, with the differences between the different scholars, and the correct statement we have on it in the past, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

God Almighty says: So those who disbelieved in God among them changed what God commanded them to say, so they said - and it was said to them: Say: This is forgiveness -: (Wheat in barley). And their saying that is like that, it is not the saying that they were told to say. God Almighty says: So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky, We sent upon them a punishment, We destroyed them because they changed what they were commanded to do, so they did something other than what God commanded them to do, and they said something other than what God commanded them to do. We have explained the meaning of rajaz previously.
God Almighty says: And ask, O Muhammad, these Jews, who are your neighbors, about the matter of the village that was by the sea, meaning: it was by the sea, meaning: near the sea and on its shore.
The interpreters differed on it.
Some of them said: It is Ayla.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Dawud ibn Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And ask them about the town that was by the sea
, he said: It is a town called Ayla, between Madyan and al-Tur.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And ask them about the town that was by the sea
, he said: We heard that it was Ayla.

c: Salam bin Salem Al-Khuza’i told me, he said, Yahya bin Saleem Al-Ta’ifi told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: I entered upon Ibn Abbas and the Qur’an was in his lap and he was crying, so I said: What makes you cry, may God make me your ransom? He said: Woe to you, do you know the village that was by the sea? I said: That is Ayla!

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And ask them about the town that was by the sea
, he said: It is Ayla.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It is a village on the seashore, between Egypt and Medina, and it is called (Ayla).

c: Musa bin Harun told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They are the people of Ayla, the village that was near the sea.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And ask them about the town that was by the sea
, he said: Ayla.

x: Others said: It means: the coast of Madyan.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And ask them about the town that was by the sea
, the verse. He told us that it was a town on the seashore, called Ayla.

x: Others said: It is a niche.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And ask them about the town that was by the sea
, he said: It is a town called Maqna, between Madyan and Aynun.

x: Others said: It is Madyan.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It is a village between Ayla and al-Tur, and it is called (Madyan).

x: The correct thing to say about that is: It is a village by the sea. It is possible that it is Ayla, or Madyan, or Maqna, because all of that is by the sea, and there is no report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that would excuse any of that, and the difference of opinion about it is as I have described. And one cannot reach knowledge of what has been and passed that we have not witnessed, except through a report that requires knowledge. And there is no report like that about that. His saying:
h
When they transgressed on the Sabbath
, he means his people,
h
when they transgressed on the Sabbath

the command of God, and exceeded it to what God forbade them. It is said: So-and-so transgressed my affair or transgressed, if he exceeded it. Their aggression on the Sabbath was that God had forbidden them the Sabbath, so they used to fish on it. When their fish come to them on their Sabbath day, openly, he says: When their fish come to them on their Sabbath day, on which they were forbidden to work, openly, he says: openly, visible on the water from Surat al-A’raf 7:163
h
And ask them about the town that was by the sea
, when they transgressed the Sabbath, when their fish came to them on their Sabbath day in full view, but on the day when they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them.
Thus do We test them for what they used to do. every path and direction, like the streets of roads, like that which:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman bin Saad told us, on the authority of Bishr bin Ammarah, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: When their fish come to them on their Sabbath day, in plain view, meaning: visible on the water.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Sharia, he says: from every place. And His statement:
h
And a day on which they do not observe the Sabbath

means: And a day on which they do not honor it as they honor the Sabbath, and that is all days except the Sabbath, the whales will not come to them, “Thus do We test them because they were defiantly disobedient,” meaning: Just as We described to you the test and trial that We mentioned, by showing them the fish on the surface of the water on the day when it was forbidden for them to hunt it, and hiding it from them on the day when it was permissible to hunt it, Thus do We test them, and examine them, because they were defiantly disobedient, meaning: by their defiant disobedience to God and their departure from it. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And a day when they will not be able to recite. It was read with the opening of the ya of yasbatun. From the saying: So-and-so celebrated Saturday, he celebrates Saturday and Saturdays, if he glorifies Saturday. It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to recite it: And on the Day when they will not repent with a damma on the ya. From (asbat al-qawm yasbatun), if they entered (Saturday), as it is said: (ajmaʿna), a Friday passed us, and (ashharna) a month passed us, and (asbatna), a Saturday passed us. The subject of the word day in his statement:
h
And a day when they do not have a rest is do not come to them
, because the meaning of the statement is: do not come to them on a day when they do not have a rest.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And a day when they will not be able to recite.
It was read with the opening of the ya of yasbatun.
It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to recite it: And on the Day when they will not repent with a damma on the ya.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember also, O Muhammad, When a community among them said, a group of them to a group who were admonishing the transgressors on the Sabbath and forbidding them from disobeying God on it, Why do you admonish a people whom God is about to destroy, in this world for their disobedience to Him, their opposition to His command, and their making lawful what He has forbidden them, or punishing them with a severe punishment, in the Hereafter. The one whom they were forbidding from disobeying God said, answering their statement: We admonished them as an excuse to your Lord, so that we may fulfill His obligation upon us in enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and perhaps they will become righteous, meaning: Perhaps they will become righteous and fear God, so that they will turn to His obedience and repent from their disobedience to Him and their transgression of what He has forbidden them, such as their transgression on the Sabbath, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: They said, ‘An apology to your Lord,’ because we were angry with their actions. And perhaps they will become righteous, meaning: they will abandon what they are doing.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And perhaps they will fear God

, he said: They will abandon this action that they are doing. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: They said, ‘Excuse me.’ The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Kufa and Basra read it as excuse me in the nominative case, as I described of its meaning.

x: Some of the people of Kufa read it as: excuse me, in the accusative case, meaning: we admonished them and did that. Scholars differed about this group that said: Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy? Was it among the saved or the doomed?
Some of them said: It was among the saved because it was the one that forbade the doomed group from transgressing on the Sabbath.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And when a group of them said

, ‘Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?’ It is a village on the seashore between Mecca and Medina, called Ayla. So God forbade them from taking whales on their Sabbath. The whales would come to them on their Sabbath in the open sea. When the Sabbath passed, they were unable to get hold of them. So they remained like that as long as God willed. Then a group of them took the whales on their Sabbath, so a group forbade them, saying, You will take them, while God has forbidden them to you on your Sabbath! But they only increased in transgression and rebellion.

x: Another group kept forbidding them. When that went on for a long time, a group of the forbidding ones said, “You know that these are a people upon whom the punishment has come due. Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy?” They were more angry with God than the other group, so they said: An excuse before your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God

. And they had all forbidden, so when God’s wrath fell upon them, the two groups that said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? and those who said: An excuse before your Lord? were saved, and God destroyed the people of His disobedience who took the whales, and He made them into apes and pigs.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And ask them about the town that was by the sea, until His saying: And on the day they do not observe the Sabbath, it does not come to them, that is, the people of a town that was by the sea, their fish used to come to them on their Sabbath. He says: When it was the day they observed the Sabbath, they would come to them freely - meaning: from every place - and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they would not come to them, and that they said: If we took from these fish on the day they came what would suffice us on other days! So a group of believers preached to them and forbade them. And a group of believers said: These people have intended to do something they will not desist from, and God will disgrace them and punish them with a severe punishment. The believers said to one another: An apology before your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God

, if it is destruction, then perhaps we will be saved, or if they desist, then we will have a reward. God had appointed a day for the Children of Israel to worship Him and devote themselves to Him, which was Monday. But the wicked ones transgressed from Monday to Saturday, and said: It is the Sabbath! So Moses forbade them, and they disagreed about it, so he made the Sabbath obligatory for them, and forbade them from working on it or transgressing on it. One of them went to collect firewood, so Moses, peace be upon him, took him and asked him: Did anyone order you to do this? But he did not find anyone who ordered him, so his companions stoned him.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Some of those whom they forbade said to one another: Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy or punish with a severe punishment? He said: Why do you preach to them, when you preached to them and they did not obey you?

x: Some of them said: An excuse before your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muadh ibn Hani’ told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when a group of them said

, ‘Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?’ He said: I do not know whether those who said, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? were saved or not! He said: So I kept on at him until I knew that they had been saved, so he gave me a robe.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Ban Abbas recited this verse, and he mentioned something similar to it, except that he said in his hadith: I kept looking at him until he knew that they had been saved.

c: Salam bin Salem Al-Khuza'i narrated to me, he said: Yahya bin Sulayma Al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: I entered upon Ibn Abbas and the Qur'an was in his lap, and he was crying, so I said: What makes you cry, may God make me your ransom? He said: He recited: And ask them about the city which was by the sea until His saying: Because they were wicked. Ibn Abbas said: I do not hear the third group mentioned, we fear that we will be like them! So I said: Do you not hear God say: But when they transgressed against what they were forbidden? So he cheered him up and clothed me with a robe. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Ibn Jurayj narrated, a man narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: I came to Ibn Abbas one day while he was crying, and there was a copy of the Qur’an in his lap. I felt too anxious to come closer, but I kept on doing so until I came forward and sat down. I said: What makes you cry, O Ibn Abbas, may God make me your ransom? He said: These are the pages! He said: It is in Surat Al-A’raf! He said: Do you know Aylah? I said: Yes! He said: There was a tribe of Jews there, and the whales were driven to them on the Sabbath, then they sank and they could not catch them until they had sunk, after great toil and hardship. They would come to them on the Sabbath, white and fat, like a churning mother, their backs prostrated to their bellies in their courtyards and buildings. They remained like that for a while, then Satan inspired them and said: You were only forbidden from eating it on the Sabbath, so take it on the Sabbath and eat it on any other day!

x: A group of them said that, and a group of them said: Rather, you were forbidden to eat it, take it, and hunt it on the Sabbath. And they continued like that until the following Friday came, and a group returned with themselves, their children, and their women, and a group withdrew to the right and stepped aside, and a group withdrew to the left and remained silent. And those on the right said: Woe to you! God, God, we forbid you from exposing yourselves to God’s punishment!

i: And those on the left said:
x: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? The ones on the right said: An excuse before your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God

That is, they will desist, for it is more preferable for us that they not be afflicted or destroyed, and if they do not desist, then an excuse before your Lord. So they continued in their sin, and those on the right said: You have done it, O enemies of God! By God, we will not let you spend the night in your city, and by God, we will not see you wake up until God afflicts you with a sinking or a stoning or some of the punishments He has! When morning came, they knocked on the door and called out, but no one answered. So they put up a ladder and climbed the city wall. A man turned to them and said: O servants of God, monkeys, by God, howl with tails! He said: So they opened it and they entered upon them. The monkeys recognized their lineage from humans, but humans do not recognize their lineage from monkeys. So the monkeys would come to their human relatives and smell their clothes and cry, and say to them: Didn’t we forbid you from such and such?
And they would nod: Yes!

i: Then Ibn Abbas recited:
x: But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who had forbidden evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment for what they used to commit.

He said: So I see that the Jews who were forbidden were saved, but I do not see that the others were reminded. We see things that we disapprove of, but we do not speak about them! I said: Yes, may God make me your ransom, do you not see that they hate what they are doing, and they oppose them and say: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish? He said: So he ordered me to wear two thick cloaks.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And ask them about the town that was by the sea, he mentioned to us that if it was the Sabbath, the whales would come and lie flat on their shores and their yards, because of what they heard from God’s command in the water. But if it was not the Sabbath, they would go far in the water until their pursuer sought them out. Then Satan came to them and said: You were only forbidden to eat them on the Sabbath, so hunt them on the Sabbath and eat them later! ... His statement: “
h
And when a group of them said
, ‘Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a Surat al-A’raf 7:164
h
And when a group of them said
, "Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said, "An excuse before your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God
." severe punishment?’ They said, ‘An excuse before your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God

.’” The people became three types. As for one type, they refrained from the sanctity of God and were forbidden from disobeying God. As for another type, they refrained from the sanctity of God out of awe of God. As for another type, they violated the sanctity and fell into sin.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God: present in the sea, he said: The whales were forbidden to them on the Sabbath, and they used to come to them on the Sabbath as a law, as a trial that they were afflicted with, and they would not come to them on any other day unless they sought them, as a trial also, because they were committing evil. So they took them on the Sabbath as a lawful and sinful act, so God said to them: (Be apes, despised) (al-Baqarah 2:65 - al-A’raf 7:166), except for a group of them who did not transgress and He forbade them, so some of them said to one another: Why do you preach to a people?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And when a group of them said
, ‘Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy?’ until he reached
h
and perhaps they will fear God

, perhaps they will abandon what they were doing. He said: They had been afflicted by the whales holding back from them, and they would rest on the Sabbath and not do anything on it. When it was the Sabbath, the whales would come to them lawfully, and when it was not the Sabbath, not a single whale would come. He said: They were a people who had become addicted to the love of whales and had suffered afflictions from them. One of them took a whale, tied a string to its tail, then tied it to a piece of wood, then left it in the water until the sun set on Sunday. He dragged it with the string and then roasted it. Then his neighbor smelled the smell of a whale, so he said: O so-and-so, I smell the smell of a whale in your house! He said: No! He looked into his oven and found it in it, so he told him the report, and he said: I think that God will punish you. He said: When he did not see it, he hastened the punishment. When the next Saturday came, he took two of them and tied them up. Then his neighbor looked at him. When he saw it, he did not hasten the punishment. They began to hunt it down. The people of the village looked at them. Those who forbid evil forbade them from doing so. They were divided into two groups: one group forbade them and refrained, and another group forbade them but did not refrain. Those who forbade them and refrained said to those who forbade them but did not refrain: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? The others said: An apology to your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God

. So God said: But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who had forbidden evil until His saying because they were defiantly disobedient. God said: But when they transgressed against what they were forbidden,
h
We said to them

, ‘Be apes, despised.’ (al-A’raf 7:166), and the people of that city said to them: You have committed evil deeds. Whoever wants to isolate himself and purify himself, let him isolate himself from these people! He said: So these people and those people isolated themselves in their city, and they built a wall between them, and they made doors in that wall so that some of them could go out to others. He said: When night came, God struck them with a punishment, and those believers saw no one in the morning. They entered upon them and found that they were apes, the man and his wives and his children. They entered upon the man and recognized him and said: O so-and-so, did we not warn you of the wrath of God? Did we not warn you of the punishments of God? And we warn you and we warn you? He said: Then it was nothing but weeping! He said: God only punished those who did wrong and persisted in that. He said: As for those who forbade, all of them forbade, but some of them were better than others. So he recited: We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment because they were defiantly disobedient.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas recited this verse: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? He said: I do not know whether the people were saved or were destroyed? I kept looking at him until he knew that they were saved, and he gave me a robe.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab ibn Abd al-Aziz told me, on the authority of Malik, he said:
m: Ibn Ruman claimed that his statement, Their fish come to them on their Sabbath day as a law, but on the day they do not observe the Sabbath, they do not come to them, he said: It used to come to them on the Sabbath, and when evening came, it went away, and nothing of it was seen until the Sabbath. So a man from among them took a string and a peg, and tied one of them to the water on the Sabbath. When they spent the night, he took it and hung it up. The people smelled its smell, so they came to him and asked him about it, but he denied it. They kept on at him until he said to them, It is the skin of a whale that we found! So when the next Sabbath came, he did the same thing - and I do not know, perhaps he said, He tied two whales. So when evening came on the night of Sunday, he took it and hung it up. They smelled its smell, so they came and asked him, and he said to them, If you wished, you could do as I do! So they said to him, What did you do?

c: So he told them,
m: and they did as he did, until that became common. They had a city with a suburb, but they closed it, and they were afflicted with the same transformation that afflicted them. Then their neighbors who used to live around them came to them, asking them what people ask, and they found the city closed to them. They called out, but they did not answer them, so they climbed over the wall and found that they were monkeys. The monkey began to approach and rub against the one it had known before, and to approach him and rub against him.

x: Others said: Rather, the group that said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? was from the doomed group.

Who said that? Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said: Ibn Idris narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Dawud ibn Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And ask them about the town that was by the sea until His saying: by law. He said: Ibn Abbas said: They innovated the Sabbath and were tested on it, so whales were forbidden to them on it. So when the Sabbath came, the whales would be set out for them so that they could look at them in the sea. Then when the Sabbath passed, they would go away and not be seen until the next Sabbath. Then when the Sabbath came, they would come back by law. So they stayed as long as God willed them to stay like that, then one of them took a whale and pierced its nose with his, then he struck a stake for it on the shore, tied it up and left it in the water. Then the next day, he took it, roasted it and ate it.

He did that while they were watching and did not disapprove, and none of them forbade him, except a group of them who forbade him, until it became apparent in the markets and he did it openly. He said: A group said to those who forbade: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment? They said: An excuse before your Lord, in Our anger at their actions,
h
and perhaps they will fear God
. But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, until His saying:
h
We said to them

, ‘Be apes, despised,’ (al-A’raf 7:166). Ibn Abbas said: They were three: a third forbade it, a third said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy, and a third were the people of sin. Only those who forbade it were saved, and the rest of them perished. Then those who forbade evil were in their gatherings one day checking on the people but could not see them, so they did it in their homes, and they began to say: The people have a matter, so look at what their matter is!

They looked into their homes, and behold, the people had been transformed into monkeys in their homes. They recognized the man by name, even though he was an ape, and they recognized the woman, even though she was an ape. God said: So We made it a deterrent to those before it and those after it, and an admonition to the righteous. (al-Baqarah 2:66) Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: We saved those who forbade evil the verse. Ibn Abbas said: Those who forbade were saved, and those who did it perished. I do not know what was done to those who remained silent!

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? He said: They are three groups: the group that preached, the group that was preached to, and God knows best what the third group did, and they are the ones who said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? Al-Kalbi said: They are two groups: the group that preached, and the group that said: Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy? He said: It is the preaching.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: For me to have known of those who said, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment, would be more beloved to me than what he did to him!

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And when a group of them said

, ‘Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy?’ He said: I hear God say: We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment. I wonder what happened to those who said, Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy?

c: Ibn Hamid narrated that Yaqub narrated to us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Haman al-Hanafi Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement: Their fish come to them on their Sabbath day openly, but on the day they do not observe the Sabbath, they do not come to them. He said: They were in the city on the seashore, and the days were six, Sunday to Friday. Then the Jews instituted the Sabbath and declared it a Sabbath for themselves, so God declared it an Sabbath for them, and there was no Sabbath before that, so God made it a burden on them and tested them with whales, so they began to come out on the Sabbath, and they were afraid of being afflicted by them, until one of them said: By God, the Sabbath is not a day, and God made it a burden on us, and we made it a burden on ourselves, so if you had some of this fish! So he ate a whale from the whales, and his neighbor heard about that, and he feared punishment, so he fled from his house. When he stayed as long as God willed and he was not afflicted with punishment, he ate something else on the Sabbath as well. When they were not afflicted with punishment, many ate on the Sabbath, and they took the Sabbath and the night of the Sabbath as a holiday in which they would drink alcohol and play musical instruments. Their best and most righteous people said to them: Woe to you! Stop what you are doing! God will either destroy you or punish you with a severe punishment. Will you not use your reason? And do not transgress on the Sabbath! They refused. Their best people said: Let us build a wall between us and them. They did so, and when it was Saturday night, they were bothered by what they heard of their voices and the sounds of the musical instruments. When it was the night in which they were transformed, their voices stopped at the beginning of the night. Their best people said: What is the matter with your people that their voices stopped last night?

x: Some of them said: Perhaps the wine overcame them and they slept. When morning came, they did not hear a sound from them.

Some of them said to one another: Why do we not hear a sound from your people? They said to a man: Climb the wall and see what is the matter with them. He climbed the wall and saw them surging Surat al-A’raf 7:164
h
And when a group of them said
, "Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?" They said, "An excuse before your Lord,
h
and perhaps they will fear God

." against one another, having been transformed into monkeys. He said to his al-Nas 114:Come and see what your people have encountered! So they climbed and began to look at the man and make out his features, saying: O so-and-so, are you so-and-so? He pointed to his chest with his hand, saying, Yes, for what my hands have earned.

c: Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said,
m: Al-Hasan recited one day: “And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed on the Sabbath. When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day as a law, but on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus do We test them for what they used to do.” He said: A fish that God had forbidden them on one day, and had made lawful for them on other days, so it came to them on the day that God had forbidden them as if it were labor pains, and no one could resist it. I have rarely seen anyone who was so concerned about sin that he did not commit it, so they would be concerned and hold back until they seized it and ate the most disgusting meal that a people have ever eaten, which left them with shame in this world and a severe punishment in the Hereafter! By God, no fish that a people seized and ate was more serious in the sight of God than killing a believing man! And the believer has greater sanctity in the sight of God than a fish, but God has made the appointed time for a people at the Hour, And the Hour is more grievous and more bitter. (al-Qamar 54:46) Yunus told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The whales came to them, rushing into their ponds as if they were laboring, so they ate, by God, the worst meal that any people have ever eaten, the worst punishment in this world, and the most severe torment in the Hereafter! Al-Hasan said: By God, killing a believer is worse than eating whales! Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: I was sitting in the mosque when an old man came and the people sat around him. They said: This is one of the companions of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud! He said: Ibn Mas’ud said: And ask them about the town that was by the sea (al-Baqarah 2:14). He said: When the Sabbath was forbidden to them, the whales would come on the Sabbath and feel safe, so they would come, and they could not touch them. And when the Sabbath was over, they would go away, and they would hunt as people hunt. When they wanted to transgress on the Sabbath, they hunted, but some of their righteous people forbade them, but they refused, and the wicked were many among them. The wicked wanted to fight them, but among them were those whom they did not wish to fight, such as the father of one of them, or his brother, or his relative. When they forbade them and they refused, the righteous people said: Then we will accuse you! We will put a wall between us and you! So they did, and when they lost their voices they said: If you had looked at your brothers, what they did! They looked and saw that they had been transformed into monkeys, recognizing the old by his old age and the young by his young age, so they began to cry to them. This happened after Moses, peace be upon him.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: They said, ‘Excuse me.’
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Kufa and Basra read it as excuse me in the nominative case, as I described of its meaning.
Some of the people of Kufa read it as: excuse me, in the accusative case, meaning: we admonished them and did that.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Ban Abbas recited this verse, and he mentioned something similar to it, except that he said in his hadith: I kept looking at him until he knew that they had been saved.

Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Ibn Abbas recited this verse: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?

x: God Almighty says: So when the group that transgressed on the Sabbath abandoned what God had commanded them to do, which was to abandon transgression on it, and neglected what the admonishing group had admonished them and reminded them of, which was to warn them of God’s punishment for their disobedience, and they proceeded to consider permissible what God had forbidden them, God saved those of them who were forbidden from (evil), meaning from disobeying God and considering permissible what He had forbidden, And We seized those who did wrong, meaning: God seized those who transgressed on the Sabbath, and they considered permissible what God had forbidden, such as catching fish and eating it, so He brought down His wrath upon them, and destroyed them with a severe and wretched punishment because they disobeyed God’s command, and they went out from His obedience to His disobedience, and that is (transgression). And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us
m: regarding His statement:
h
So when they forgot what they had been reminded of
, We saved those who forbade evil, he said: So when they forgot the admonition of the believers to them, who said: Why do you admonish a people?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Harami told me: Shu’bah told me: ‘Amara told me, on the authority of ‘Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas:
m: We saved those who forbade evil. He said: I wonder what evil they forbade? As for his saying: with a terrible punishment, the readings differed in its reading. So I read it as the people of Medina generally read: (with the torment of bays), with a kasra on the ba’ and a light ya’, changing the hamza, like (fa’ala).

x: Some of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it as: with a miserable torment on the model of fa’il from al-ba’us with the accusative of the ba and the kasra and extension of the hamza. Some Meccans read it in the same way, except that they broke the Ba’ of ba’is like fa’il. Some Kufians read it as: (بديس) with a fatha on the ba’ and a sukoon on the ya’, and a hamza after it with a kasra, like (فيعَعل).

i: This is anomalous according to the Arabs, because if (فيعَعل) is not one of those with ya’ and waw, then the fatha on its ‘ayn is the eloquent word in the speech of the Arabs, and this is like their saying for its equivalent in the sound: (وّادرب،ِديقال), and the ‘ayn is only broken in that in those with ya’ and waw like their saying (ْوماي،سيد), and some of them recited the saying of Imru’ al-Qais ibn ‘Abis al-Kindi:
x: Both were miserable presidents who hit the day of the riots.

By breaking the ‘ayn of (fa’il), which is the hamza of (ba’is), like the reading that we mentioned before this, and that is by opening the ba’ and sukunating the ya’ and opening the hamza after the ya’, on the example of (fa’il) like (sa’iqal).

c: It was narrated on the authority of some Basrans
m: that he read it: Ba’isa with the opening of the ba and the breaking of the hamza, on the example of fa’ala, as Ibn Qais al-Ruqayyat said: I wish I could cast a spell in private without any harm It was narrated on the authority of another of them that he read: Ba’isa with a kasra on the ba’ and a fatha on the seen, meaning: Ba’isa the torment.

x: The most correct of these readings, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: Baʿis with the opening of the ba’, the kasra of the hamza and its extension, on the example of Faʿil, as Dhu al-Isbaʿ al-ʿAdwani said: Out of anger at me, and you don't see any trace of me in them Because this interpretation was agreed upon by all to mean: severe, so this indicates the correctness of what we chose.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: A man told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment, painful and grievous.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: With a terrible punishment, he said: severe.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: With a terrible torment, meaning painful and severe.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: With a terrible torment, he said: painful.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: With a terrible punishment, he said: With a severe punishment.

evidence.text: As for his saying: with a terrible punishment, the readings differed in its reading.
So I read it as the people of Medina generally read: (with the torment of bays), with a kasra on the ba’ and a light ya’, changing the hamza, like (fa’ala).
Some of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it as: with a miserable torment on the model of fa’il from al-ba’us with the accusative of the ba and the kasra and extension of the hamza.
Some Meccans read it in the same way, except that they broke the Ba’ of ba’is like fa’il.
Some Kufians read it as: (بديس) with a fatha on the ba’ and a sukoon on the ya’, and a hamza after it with a kasra, like (فيعَعل).

By breaking the ‘ayn of (fa’il), which is the hamza of (ba’is), like the reading that we mentioned before this, and that is by opening the ba’ and sukunating the ya’ and opening the hamza after the ya’, on the example of (fa’il) like (sa’iqal).

It was narrated on the authority of some Basrans that he read it: Ba’isa with the opening of the ba and the breaking of the hamza, on the example of fa’ala, as Ibn Qais al-Ruqayyat said: I wish I could cast a spell in private without any harm It was narrated on the authority of another of them that he read: Ba’isa with a kasra on the ba’ and a fatha on the seen, meaning: Ba’isa the torment.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these readings, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: Baʿis with the opening of the ba’, the kasra of the hamza and its extension, on the example of Faʿil, as Dhu al-Isbaʿ al-ʿAdwani said: Out of anger at me, and you don't see any trace of me in them Because this interpretation was agreed upon by all to mean: severe, so this indicates the correctness of what we chose.

x: God Almighty says: When they rebelled, in what they were forbidden from doing, such as transgressing on the Sabbath, and making lawful what God had forbidden them, such as hunting and eating fish, and they persisted in doing so, We said to them, ‘Be apes, despised,’ meaning: hostile to good. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So when they transgressed what they were forbidden, he said: when the people persisted in disobedience, We said to them, ‘Be apes, despised,’ so they became apes with tails, howling, after they had been men and women.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: But when they transgressed what they were forbidden, We said to them, ‘Be apes, despised.’ So God made them into apes and pigs, so he claimed that the youth of the people became apes, and that the elders became pigs.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik or Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: Moses, peace be upon him, saw a man carrying a reed on the Sabbath, so he struck his neck.
b.via: Abu Malik or Saeed bin Jubair

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: And when you gave permission, is remember, O Muhammad, when your Lord gave permission and informed. It is tafaʿal from i-idhan, as Al-Aʿsha, Maymun bin Qays, said: So today Gertie lightly cut the rope of a thousand familiar He means by his saying: (permission), I know. We have explained that with its evidence in other places. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And when your Lord gave the command, he said: I command your Lord.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And when your Lord gave the command, he said: Your Lord commanded. And His saying:
h
He will surely send against them

, means: Your Lord knows that He will surely send against the Jews those who will subject them to the worst of torment. It was said: That is, the Arabs, whom God sent against the Jews, to fight those among them who did not convert to Islam and did not pay the jizya, and whoever among them paid the jizya, that was humiliation and disgrace for him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim and Ali bin Dawud told me, they said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst of punishment, he said: It is the jizya, and those who afflict them are Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst of punishment, meaning poverty and taking the jizya from them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst of punishment, he said: The Jews, and the humiliation and poverty that were imposed upon them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So God sent this tribe of Arabs against them, and they are in torment from them until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He will send against them until the Day of Resurrection someone who will torment them, he said: He sent against them this tribe of Arabs, and they are in torment from them until the Day of Resurrection. Abdul Karim Al-Jazari said: It is recommended to send the Nabataeans to pay the jizya.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection

those who would afflict them with a terrible punishment, he said: the Arabs, the tax, he said: the tribute. And the first one to impose the tax was Moses, peace be upon him, so he collected the tax for seven years.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid:
m: h
And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection
those who would afflict them with a terrible punishment. He said: The Arabs. The tax. He said: The first to impose the tax was Moses, so he collected the tax for seven years.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid:
m: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst of punishment, he said: They are the People of the Book. God sent the Arabs against them to collect taxes from them until the Day of Resurrection, so it is the worst of punishment. And no prophet ever collected taxes except Moses, peace be upon him, for thirteen years, then he stopped, and except for the Prophet, peace be upon him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst of punishment, he said: He would send against them this tribe of Arabs, and they would be in torment from them until the Day of Resurrection. ... He said: Muammar told us, he said:

c: Abdul Karim told me, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, he said:
m: It is recommended that you send the Nabataeans to pay the jizya.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst of punishment, meaning: Your Lord would send the Arabs against the Children of Israel, and they would afflict them with the worst of punishment, taking tribute from them and killing them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection
, that He would send against the Jews.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.

God Almighty says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is swift in punishing whoever deserves punishment from Him for his disbelief in Him and his disobedience. And He is Forgiving and Merciful. He says: And He is Forgiving of the sins of whoever repents from his sins, returns to Him and returns to His obedience. He covers them with His forgiveness of them. Merciful means that He does not punish him for his crime after he repents from it, because He accepts repentance and forgives mistakes.
God Almighty says: And We dispersed the Children of Israel throughout the land, nations, meaning: different, scattered groups, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ishaq bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And We divided them into nations throughout the land, he said: In every land that a group of Jews enter.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And We divided them into nations throughout the land, he said: Jews. And his saying:
h
Among them are the righteous

, he says: Among these people whom God described from the Children of Israel, the righteous, meaning: those who believe in God and His Messenger, and among them are less than that, meaning: less than the righteous. God Almighty described them as being like this before they apostatized from their religion and disbelieved in their Lord, and that was before Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, was sent among them. And His statement:
h
And We tested them with good and bad that perhaps they would return

, meaning: And We tested them with ease in life, and ease in this world and comfort, and abundance in provision, and these are the good things that the Most High mentioned, and by bad He means hardship in life, and hardship in it, and calamities and misfortunes in wealth, that perhaps they would return, meaning: So that they would return to the obedience of their Lord and turn to it, and repent from His disobedience.

x: God Almighty says: Then after these people came those whose characteristics He described, a successor, meaning: a bad successor. He says: There occurred after them and their successor, and there was a change from them, a bad replacement. It is said of it: (He is a true successor), and (a bad successor), and most of what came in praise is with the opening of the (lam), and in blame with its sukun, and it may be moved in blame, and sukun in praise, and from that in sukun it in praise is the saying of Hassan: We are the first to come to you, and we are the successors to our first in obeying God. Follow I think that if it is directed towards corruption, it is taken from their saying: (Khalaf al-Laban), if it sours from being left in the water skin for a long time until it spoils, so it is as if the corrupt man is likened to him. It may also be from their saying: (Khalaf al-Sa’im’s mouth), if his smell changes.

As for the quiescence of (lām) in blame, it is the saying of Labid: Those who lived in their care are gone, and I am left behind like the skin of a mangy dog. It was said: The successors whom God mentioned in this verse are the Christians.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Then there came after them a generation
, he said the Christians.

x: The correct thing to say about that, in my opinion, is that God Almighty mentioned that He only described that He left behind the people whose stories He related in the previous verses, a bad and wretched successor, but He did not mention to us that they were Christians in His book, and their story is more similar to the stories of the Jews than to the stories of the Christians. Moreover, what preceded that was report about the Children of Israel, and what followed it was likewise, so what was between them was more likely to be report about them, since there was no evidence in the verse to divert the report from them to others, nor did there come any evidence that would necessitate the correctness of saying it. So the interpretation of the statement is: Then after them, a bad substitute was substituted.
h
They inherited the Book
of God and learned it, but neglected to act upon it, so they disobeyed its ruling.

They bribe in the ruling of God, so they take bribes in it from the offer of this immediate nearest thing, meaning by nearest that which is closer than the distant future. And they say when they do that: God will forgive us our sins, wishing falsehoods upon God, as God the Most High said: “So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, ‘This is from God,’ in order to exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.” (al-Baqarah 2:79), And if an offer like it comes to them, they take it. He says: And if a sin as forbidden as it is prescribed for them, such as bribery, is made permissible for them after that, they take it and consider it permissible and do not refrain from it. God the Most High informs us about them that they are people who persist in their sins, and are not people of repentance or repentance.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, even though their expressions differed.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Al-Muqaddam told us, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They take the goods of this lower world and say
, ‘We will be forgiven.’ But if a similar goods come to them, they take them. He said: They commit a sin, then they seek forgiveness from God, and if that sin comes to them, they take it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And if something similar comes to them, they will take it, he said: from the sins.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: They take the offering of this lower world and say, ‘We will be forgiven.’ He said: They commit sins. And if an offering like it comes to them, they take it. He said: Another sin, which they commit.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: They take the goods of this lower class, he said: sins, and if a goods like it come to them, they take it, he said: sins.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They take the goods of this world, he said: Whatever is most honorable to them in this world today, whether lawful or unlawful, they desire it and take it and seek forgiveness, and if they find something similar tomorrow, they take it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar, except that he said: They wish for forgiveness.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saeed told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They take the goods of this world, he said: Nothing of this world is honored for them except that they take it, whether it is lawful or unlawful, and they wish for forgiveness, and they say: He will forgive us, and if they find a goods like it, they take it.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then there came after them a generation
, yes, by God, a bad generation who inherited the Book after their prophets and messengers. God inherited them and made a covenant with them. And God said in another verse:
h
Then there came after them a generation
who neglected prayer and pursued desires.
r
(Maryam 19:59)

He said: They take the goods of this world and say, ‘He will forgive us.’ They wished for hopes from God, and they were deceived by them. And if an offer like it comes to them, nothing distracts them from anything else, nor does it prevent them from that. Whenever something of this world is presented to them, they eat it, not caring whether it is lawful or unlawful.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They take the goods of this lower class, he said: They take them if it is lawful and if it is unlawful, And if an goods like it comes to them, he said: If something lawful or unlawful comes to them, they take it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then a generation succeeded them to his statement
h
and they studied what was in it

, he said: The Children of Israel would not appoint a judge unless he took a bribe in the ruling. Their best people gathered and some of them took covenants from others that they would not do so or take bribes. So when a man from among them was appointed as a judge, he would take a bribe. It would be said to him: What is the matter with you taking a bribe in the ruling? He would say: I will be forgiven! Then the rest of the Children of Israel would criticize him for what he did. Then when he died or was removed, and a man from among those who used to criticize him was put in his place, he would take a bribe. He said: And if the others were given the worldly goods, they would take them. As for the lowest goods, it is the worldly goods of money.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then there came after them a generation who inherited the Scripture

, taking the goods of this world and saying, ‘It will be forgiven for us.’ He said: They take what they acquired and leave whatever they wished of what was lawful or unlawful, and they say, It will be forgiven for us.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
They take the goods of this lower world

, he said: the book that they wrote, and they say, ‘He will forgive us,’ we do not associate anything with God, and if a goods like it comes to them, they take it, the one who is right would come to them with a bribe, so they would bring out for him the book of God, then they would rule in his favor with the bribe. And when the oppressor came to them with a bribe, they would bring out for him al-Muthanna, which is the book that they wrote, and they would rule in his favor with what was in al-Muthanna, with the bribe, so he is right in it, but in the Torah he is oppressive, so God said:
h
Was not a covenant taken from them of the Book that they would not say about God except the truth
h
And they studied what was in it

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: his saying:
h
Then there came after them a generation who inherited the Scripture
, taking the goods of this world, he said: they commit sins, and they say, ‘We will be forgiven,’ but if something like it comes to them, they take it, he said: sins.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
Was not a covenant taken from them of the Book that they would not say about God except the truth
h
And they studied what was in it
. And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God. So will you not reason?”
God Almighty says: “Was not the covenant of the Book taken from these bribers in their rulings, who say: (God will forgive us for doing this), if Surat al-A’raf 7:169
h
Then there came after them a generation who inherited the Scripture

, taking the goods of this world and saying, "We will be forgiven." But if a similar goods came to them, they would take it. Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them that they would not say about God except the truth?
h
And they studied what was in it

. And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God. Do you not understand? they are rebuked for that, “the covenant of the Book taken,” which is the covenant God took from the Children of Israel, to establish the Torah and act according to what is in it. So He, the Most High, said to those whose story He related in this verse, rebuking them for disobeying His command and breaking His covenant and pledge: Did not God take from them the covenant of His Book, that they would not say about God except the truth, and would not add to Him except what He revealed to His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, in the Torah, and that they would not lie about Him?

Like: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: Was not a covenant taken from them in the Book that they would not say about God except the truth? He said: In what they require of God of forgiveness for their sins that they continue to return to and do not repent from. As for his saying:
h
And they studied what was in it
, it is connected to his saying:
h
They inherited the Book
, and its meaning is:
h
Then there came after them a generation
who inherited the Book, “and studied what was in it,” and what he means by his saying: and studied what was in it, is that they read what was in it.
He says:
h
They inherited the Book
, so they learned what was in it and studied it, so they neglected it and abandoned acting upon it, and they disobeyed God’s covenant with them in that, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they studied what was in it
, he said: They learned it, they learned what was in the book that God mentioned, and he recited: Because you used to teach the Book and because you used to study it
r
(Al Imran 3:79)

x: And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God, meaning God, the Most High, says: “And what is in the home of the Hereafter, which is what is in the afterlife with God, of what He has prepared for His friends, and those who act according to what He has revealed in His Book, and who preserve His limits, is better for those who fear God, and fear His punishment, and observe His commands and prohibitions, and obey Him in all of that in their worldly life. Do they not understand?” He says: Do these people who take the offer of this worldly life for their rulings, and say: He will forgive us, not understand that what is with God in the home of the Hereafter for the righteous who are just among people in their rulings, is better than this small offer that they hasten in this world in opposition to God’s command, and the judgment between people with injustice?
The readings differed in the reading of that.
Some of them read: yamsok with a lightened or sukoon on the mim, from amaska yamsok.
Others read it as yamsok, with the mim open and the seen stressed, from masak yamsok.

What is meant by that is: And those who act according to what is in the Book of God, and establish prayer, within its limits, and do not waste its times, Indeed, We do not waste the reward of the righteous, the Most High says: So whoever among My creation does that, then I do not waste the reward of his righteous work, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And those who hold fast to the Book
, he said: The Book of God that Moses, peace be upon him, brought.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: Mujahid said, regarding his statement:
h
And those who hold fast to the Book
, whether Jews or Christians, We will not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.
Others read it as yamsok, with the mim open and the seen stressed, from masak yamsok.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, when We uprooted the mountain and raised it above the Children of Israel, as if it were a canopy of clouds from the shadows, and We said to them: Take what We have given you with strength, of Our obligations, and the rulings We have imposed on you from Our Book, so accept it, work diligently to fulfill it, without falling short or lagging, and remember what is in it, meaning: what is in Our Book of the covenants and agreements that We took from you to work according to what is in it, that you may become righteous, meaning: so that you may fear your Lord, and fear His punishment for not working according to it if you remember what He took from you in it of covenants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy
