, then Moses said to them: Take what We have given you with strength, meaning: to act according to the Book, or else the mountain will fall on you and destroy you! They said: Rather, we will take what God has given us with strength, then they broke their promise after that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy
, is his saying:
h
And We raised the mountain above them with their covenant (An-Nisa’
: 54), so he said: Take what We have given you with strength, or else I will send it upon you.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told me, he said, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: I know the reason why God created the Jews to prostrate on their faces: When the mountain was raised above them, they prostrated, and they kept looking at the mountain for fear that it would fall on them. He said: So it was a prostration that God was pleased with, so they took it as a tradition.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “
h
And when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy

, and they thought it was going to fall on them. Take what We have given you with strength,” meaning with seriousness, and remember what is in it that you may become righteous, a mountain that God removed from its base, then placed it above their heads, and said: You must take My command, or I will throw it at you!

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: And when We picked the mountain, he said: As butter is picked. Ibn Jurayj said: They refused to accept the Torah or believe in it. Take what We have given you with strength, he said: He says that you must believe in the Torah and accept it, or it will fall upon you. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah, who said: This is the Book of God, do you accept it for what is in it? For in it is an explanation of what is permissible for you and what is forbidden to you, what is commanded you and what is forbidden to you! They said: Spread to us what is in it, for if its obligations are easy and its limits are light, we will accept it! He said: Accept it for what is in it! They said: No, until we know what is in it, how its limits and obligations are! So they went back to Moses repeatedly, and God inspired the mountain, so it moved up and rose into the sky, until it was between their heads and the sky. Moses said to them: Do you not see what my Lord says? If you do not accept the Torah for what is in it, I will throw you with this mountain. He said: Al-Hasan Al-Basri narrated to me, he said: When they looked at the mountain, each one of them fell down in prostration on his left eyebrow, and looked with his right eye at the mountain, fearing that it would fall on him. For this reason, there is no Jew on earth who prostrates except on his left eyebrow. They say: This is the prostration by which the punishment was lifted from us. Abu Bakr said: When he spread out the tablets on which was the Book of God, which he had written with his own hand, there remained on the face of the earth no mountain, tree, or stone that did not shake. Today, there is no Jew on the face of the earth, young or old, to whom the Torah is read, but he shakes and shakes his head at it.

x: The scholars of Arabic speech differed regarding the meaning of his saying: We mastered it. Surat al-A’raf 7:171
h
And when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy

, and they thought that it would fall upon them, [saying], “Take what We have given you with strength and remember what is in it that you may become righteous.” Some Basrans said: The meaning of natqana is we raised, and he cited the words of Al-Ajjaj as evidence: Picking the stump He said: He meant by his saying: (picks), he lifts it from his back, and by the saying of the other: And we avoid our heavy dreams Another saying has been reported from the author of this article: that the root of nataq and natuq is everything you pluck from its place and throw it away. It is said from it: nataq nataqan. He said: This is why a woman with many children is called nataq, because she throws her children away.

He cited as evidence the verse of Al-Nabigha: They were not deprived of good food, and their mother crushed you with the most beautiful memories. Another of them said: Its meaning in this place is: And we raised it. He said: They said: (We made the journey easy), move me. He said: They said: (What is not made easy with his leg does not run), and (natq), the animal makes its owner run with it and tires him out until he grows, so (natq) and (nataq), and (nataqtani the animal), and (nataq the woman, nataq, nataqan), her children increased.

Some of the Kufians said: We picked up the mountain, meaning we hung the mountain above them and raised it. We pick it up, picking it up, and a woman who is picky means she has many children. And I heard: He took the bag and picked up what was in it, meaning he scattered what was in it.

evidence.text: Today, there is no Jew on the face of the earth, young or old, to whom the Torah is read, but he shakes and shakes his head at it.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, your Lord when He extracted the children of Adam from the loins of their fathers, and confirmed to them His Oneness, and made some of them bear witness to others with their testimony to that and their acknowledgment of it, as:

c: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi told me, he said, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, on the authority of Kalthum ibn Jabr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God took the covenant from the back of Adam at Naʿman - meaning Arafat - and brought forth from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before Him like ants, then completed them in the first place, and said: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we bear witness.’ - lest you say, ‘The verse,’ to ‘What did the falsifiers do?’”

c: Imran bin Musa told us, Abdul Warith told us, Kalthoum bin Jabr told us:
m: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about His statement:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: I asked Ibn Abbas about it and he said: Your Lord wiped the back of Adam, every soul He will create until the Day of Resurrection, with this Na’man - and he pointed with his hand - then he took their covenants and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ya’qub narrated to us, they said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Kalthoum ibn Jabr narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves

, [saying], ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we testify.’ He said: Your Lord wiped the back of Adam and every soul that He created came out until the Day of Resurrection with this Nu’man who is behind Arafat, and He took their covenant: Am I not your Lord? They said, ‘Yes, we testify.’” The wording is from the hadith of Ya’qub.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us,
m: Rabi’ah ibn Kulthum said, on the authority of his father, in this hadith: They said, ‘Yes, we have testified, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this.’

c: Amr told us, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, Ata bin Al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The first thing that God sent down to Adam was a land in India. Then God wiped his back and brought forth from him every soul that He created until the Hour comes. Then He took a covenant from them: And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we testify.’ (7:17) Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Imran bin Uyaynah narrated, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When Adam was sent down, God wiped his back and brought forth from him every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection. Then He said: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. Then he recited:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam
, from their loins, their descendants, and the pen dried from that day on what would happen until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: When God created Adam, He took his descendants from his loins, like an atom, and took two handfuls, and said to the companions of the right: “Enter Paradise in peace,” and He said to the others: Enter the Fire, and I do not care.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God wiped Adam’s back and brought out all that was good in his right hand, and brought out all that was bad in the other.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God wiped the back of Adam and extracted from it every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, he said, Amr ibn Abi Qais told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: When God created Adam, He wiped his back with a brush, and brought forth from his back every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection, and He said: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, he said: On that day they will see the pen dry with what will be until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Masoudi, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When God created Adam, peace be upon him, He took his covenant, then He wiped his back, then He took his offspring in the form of ants, then He wrote down their terms, their provisions, and their misfortunes, And He made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ ... He said: Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: When God created Adam, He took his covenant that He was his Lord, and wrote down his lifespan and his misfortunes, and extracted from his descendants like ants, and took their covenant, and wrote down their lifespans, their provisions, and their misfortunes.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Rabia bin Kalthoum bin Jabr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, he said: God wiped the back of Adam, peace be upon him, while he was in Batn Nu’man - a valley next to Arafat - and brought out his descendants from his back in the form of ants, then made them testify of themselves, Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we testify. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Abu Jamrah al-Dab’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, God brought forth the offspring of Adam, peace be upon him, from his back in the form of ants while he was in a pool of water.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, Abu Mas’ud told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, who said:
m: A son of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim died at the age of six days. He said: O Jabir, when you place my son in his grave, expose his face and untie his knots, for my son will be gathered and questioned! So I did what he commanded me to do, and when I finished I said: May God have mercy on you, what is your son asking about? Who is asking him about it? He said: He is asking about the covenant that he acknowledged in the loins of Adam, peace be upon him. I said: O Abu Al-Qasim, and what is this covenant that he acknowledged in the loins of Adam? He said: Ibn Abbas told me: God wiped the back of Adam and extracted from him every soul that He would create until the Day of Resurrection, and He took a covenant from them: that they would worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and He guaranteed them sustenance. The Hour will not come until the one who was given the covenant is born on that day. Whoever among them reaches the second covenant and fulfills it, the first covenant will benefit him, and whoever reaches the second covenant and does not fulfill it, the first covenant will not benefit him, and whoever dies young before reaching the second covenant, dies upon the first covenant, according to the fitrah.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A'la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Al-Sari bin Yahya told me: Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan told them,
m: "On the authority of Al-Aswad bin Sari' from Bani Sa'd, he said: I participated in four battles with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: The people sought after their offspring after they had killed the fighters, and that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was upset with him, then he said: (What is the matter with people seeking after their offspring)? A man said: O Messenger of God, are they not the children of the polytheists? He said: (The best of you are the children of the polytheists)! However, no soul is born except that it is born in a state of fitrah, and it remains in that state until its language becomes clear to it, then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian. Al-Hasan said: And God said that in His Book, He said: (
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam
- from their loins - their descendants).

c: Abdul Rahman bin Al-Waleed told us, he said, Ahmad bin Abi Tayyiba told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Mansur, and on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: They took from his loins, as a comb is taken from the head, and he said to them: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ The angels said: ‘We bear witness, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this.’”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr,
m: regarding his statement: (
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam
, from their loins, their descendants), he said: He took them as a comb is taken from the head.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr:
m: h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam
, from their loins, their descendants, he said: He took them as a comb is taken from the head. Ibn Hameed said: As one is taken with a comb.

c: Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying:
m: Ruh bin Ubadah and Saad bin Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar Surat al-A’raf 7:172 And [remember] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], Am I not your Lord? They said, Yes, we testify, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this unaware. narrated to us, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Anisa, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Al-Khattab, on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar Al-Juhani: “Umar bin Al-Khattab was asked about this verse: ‘
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

from their loins,’ Umar said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God created Adam, then He wiped his back with His right hand and extracted from him his offspring and said: ‘I created these for the Fire, and they will do the deeds of the people of the Fire.’ Then He wiped his back and extracted from him his offspring and said: ‘I created these for Paradise, and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise.’ A man said: O Messenger of God, then what is the purpose of the deeds? He said: ‘When God creates a servant for Paradise, He uses him to do the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and He enters him into Paradise. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He uses him to do the deeds of the people of the Fire until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and He enters him into the Fire.’”

c: Ibrahim told us, he said, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, on the authority of Baqiyah, on the authority of Umar ibn Ja'tham al-Qurashi, he said, Zaid ibn Abi Anisa told me, on the authority of Abdul Hamid ibn Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Muslim ibn Yasar, on the authority of Na'im ibn Rabi'ah, on the authority of Umar, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasah, on the authority of Amara,
m: “On the authority of Abu Muhammad, a man from the people of Medina, he said: I asked Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, about the statement of God Almighty:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants

, he said: I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it as you asked me, and he said: God created Adam with His hand, and breathed into him of His spirit, then He seated him, and wiped his back with His right hand, and brought out a seed and said: The seed of their seed for Paradise, then He wiped his back with His other hand, and both of His hands are right, and He said: The seed of their seed for the Fire, they do whatever deeds You will, then I will conclude for them with the worst of their deeds and cast them into the Fire.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: God created Adam, peace be upon him, then brought forth his descendants from his loins like ants, and said to them: Who is your Lord? They said: God, our Lord! Then He returned them to his loins, until everyone from whom He took a covenant is born, and nothing is added to them nor is anything subtracted from them until the Hour comes.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: (
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam
, from their loins, their descendants) until His statement:
h
They said, "Yes, we bear witness."

Ibn Abbas said: When God created Adam, He wiped his back and brought forth all of his descendants in the form of ants, and He made them speak, and He made them bear witness against themselves, and He made light with some of them, and He said to Adam: These are your descendants, I take a covenant from them: I am their Lord, that they may not associate anything with Me, and upon Me is their provision. Adam said: Who is this who has the light? He said: He is David. He said: O Lord, how much lifespan have You written for him? He said: Sixty years! He said: How much have You written for me? He said: A thousand years, and You have written for each person how long he will live and how long he will remain? He said: O Lord, increase it. He said: This book is placed, so give it if you wish from your lifespan! He said: Yes. The pen had dried up on the life span of all the children of Adam, so it was written for him that Adam would have forty years, so his life span became one hundred years. When he had lived nine hundred and sixty years, the Angel of Death came to him. When Adam saw him, he said: What is the matter with you? He said to him: Your life span has been completed! Adam said to him: You have only lived nine hundred and sixty years, and forty years remain! He said: When he said that to the angel, the angel said:

c: My Lord has informed me
m: of it! He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him. So the angel returned to his Lord and said: What is the matter with you? He said: O Lord, I have returned to You as I knew from Your honor to me. God said: Go back and tell him that He has given his son David forty years. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Az-Zubayr ibn Musa, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his statement: God, the Blessed and Exalted, struck His right shoulder, and every soul created for Paradise came out white and pure. He said: These are the people of Paradise. Then He struck His left shoulder, and every soul created for Hell came out black. He said: These are the people of Hell. Then He took their pledges of faith and knowledge of Him and His command, and belief in Him and His command, all of the children of Adam. He made them bear witness against themselves, so they believed and were truthful and recognized and acknowledged. It has reached me that He brought them out on His palm like mustard seeds. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: When God brought them out, He said: O servants of God, respond to God - and response means obedience - and they said: We obey, O God, we obey, O God, here we are! He said: So Abraham, peace be upon him, gave it in the rituals: (Here we are, O God, here we are). He said: He struck the back of Adam when He created him. He said: Ibn Abbas said: He created Adam, then brought forth his offspring from his back like ants, and spoke to them, then returned them to his loins, and there is no one who did not speak, and he said: (My Lord is God). He said: And every creation that was created will exist until the Day of Resurrection, and it is the nature upon which people were created. Ibn Jurayj said: Saeed bin Jubair said: He took the covenant from them at Nu’man, and (Nu’man), from behind Arafat. That you may say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, we were unaware of this,’ of the covenant that was taken from them.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said:
m: He gathered them all together on that day, about what would happen until the Day of Resurrection, then He made them speak and took a covenant from them, and made them bear witness against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we bear witness. This is lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this unaware. Or say, “Our fathers associated others with God before, and we were descendants after them. Will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers have done?” He said: I call upon you the seven heavens and the seven earths, and I call upon you your father Adam, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, We did not know of this! Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, and do not associate anything with Me, and that I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you My books! They said: We bear witness that You are our Lord and our God, we have no lord but You, and we have no god but You. So they acknowledged their obedience to Him on that day, and He raised their father Adam over them and looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, and the handsome and the lesser, so he said: O Lord, why did You not make them equal? He said: Then I would like to be grateful. He said: And among them were the prophets, peace be upon them, on that day like lamps, and He singled out the prophets with another covenant, as God said: And when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary, and We took from them a solemn covenant (al-Ahzab 33:7), and it is what God the Most High says: “So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the nature of God upon which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God”
r
(Al-Rum: 30)

, and in that He said: This is a warner from the first warners (al-Najm 53:56). He says: We took his covenant with the first vow, and from that is His saying: And We found not for most of them any covenant, and indeed, We found most of them to be wicked (al-A’raf 7:102), and it is the saying of God Almighty: Then after him We sent messengers to their people, and they brought them clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before
r
(Yunus 10:74)
. He said: It was in His knowledge on the day they acknowledged Him, who would believe and who would deny.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], Am I not your Lord? He said: He brought them out from the loins of Adam, and gave Adam a lifespan of one thousand years. He said: So they were shown to Adam, and he saw a man from his descendants who had light, and he was pleased, so he asked about him, and he said: He is David, and he made his lifespan sixty years! So he made forty years of his lifespan. When Adam was dying, he began to argue with them about the forty years, and it was said to him: You gave them to David! He said: So he began to argue with them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: He brought forth his descendants from his loins in the form of an atom, and presented them to Adam with their names and the names of their fathers and their terms! He said: Then the spirit of David was presented to him in a shining light, and he said: Who is this? He said: This is from your descendants, a prophet and caliph. He said: How old is he? He said: Sixty years. He said: Add to him forty years from my life. He said, while the pens were wet and flowing, so he recorded forty for David, and Adam’s life was one thousand years. When he had completed them except for forty years, the Angel of Death was sent to him, and he said: O Adam, I have been commanded to take you. He said: Do not I have forty years left? He said: Then the Angel of Death returned to his Lord and said: Adam will be called from his age of forty years! He said: He informed Adam that He had made them for his son David, and the pens were wet, so he recorded them for David.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Dawood told us, on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed,
m: something similar. ... He said: Ibn Fadil and Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam
, from their loins, their descendants, he said: He brought them out from the loins of Adam until He took a covenant from them, then He returned them to his loins.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Nadr ibn Arabi:
m: h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants, he said: He brought them out from the loins of Adam until He took a covenant from them, then He returned them to his loins. ... He said: Muhammad bin Ubaid narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bistam, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: When God created Adam, peace be upon him, He said: He created them and made them testify of themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes.

c: I was told on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their Surat al-A’raf 7:172 And [remember] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], Am I not your Lord? They said, Yes, we testify, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, Indeed, we were of this unaware. loins, their descendants, he said: Ibn Abbas said: God created Adam, then brought forth his descendants from his loins, and God spoke to them and made them speak, and said: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes! Then He returned them to his loins, and there is no one among creation who has not spoken and said: (My Lord is God), and the Resurrection will not come until one is born who on that day testified of himself. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Amr ibn Talhah narrated, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And when your Lord took from the children of Adam

, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ That is when the Most High says: And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion.
r
(Al Imran 3:83)

That is when He says: “Then to God belongs the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He could have guided you all.” (al-An’am 6:149) That is, on the day He took the covenant from them, then presented them to Adam, peace be upon him.

x: God Almighty says: We bear witness against you, O you who acknowledge that God is your Lord, so that you will not say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Indeed, we were unaware of this, that is, we did not know that, and we were inattentive to it, or say, ‘Our fathers associated others with God before, and we were descendants after them,’ that is, we followed their path. Will You destroy us? for associating others with God among our fathers, and following their path out of ignorance of the truth? What he means by his saying:
h
Because of what the falsifiers did
, is what those who falsified did, in their claim to a god other than God. There are different readings of this.

Some of the Meccans and Basrans read: that they say with a ya meaning: We testified so that they do not say, as a way of reporting the unseen. The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: that you say, with the letter ta’, as a way of addressing the witnesses to those who are being witnessed to.

The correct statement regarding this matter is that they are two readings with correct meanings and the same interpretation, even if their wording differs. This is because the Arabs do this in narration, as God said:
You will surely make it clear to the people and He will surely make it clear
We have explained similar examples of this previously, so there is no need to repeat them.

evidence.text: The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: that you say, with the letter ta’, as a way of addressing the witnesses to those who are being witnessed to.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement regarding this matter is that they are two readings with correct meanings and the same interpretation, even if their wording differs.

x: God Almighty says: Just as We have detailed, O Muhammad, the verses of this Surah for your people, and explained in it what We did to the previous nations before your people, and what We brought upon them of the examples of their disbelief and their associating others with Me in worshipping Me, thus We detail the other verses and explain them to your people, so that they may be deterred and deterred, so that they may turn to My obedience, and repent from their polytheism and disbelief, and return to faith and acknowledgment of My Oneness, and singling out obedience to Me alone, and abandoning the worship of anyone other than Me.

God Almighty says to the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And recite, O Muhammad, to your people, the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, meaning his report and story. The signs of God were for the one to whom God gave them, as it is said: the greatest name of God, and it was said: prophecy.
The interpreters differed about it.
Some of them said: He is a man from the Children of Israel.
Who said that?

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is Balaam.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: He is Balaam bin Aber.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, he said: A man from the Children of Israel called Balaam ibn Abr.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said,
m: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar, Ibn Mahdi, and Ibn Abi ʿUday told us, they said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of ʿAbdullah: that he said regarding this verse, and he mentioned something similar, and he did not say: Ibn Aber.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ibn Masoud:
m: h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, but he slipped out of them. He said: A man from the Children of Israel called Balaam ibn Abr.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Imran bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He is Balaam bin Ba’er.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ibn Masoud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs to and he was among the deviators
, he is Balaam bin Abr.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ibn Masoud,
m: the same, except that he said: Ibn Aber, with a dammah on the ra’.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is a man from the city of the tyrants called Balaam.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then he slipped out of it, he said: Balaam bin Ba’er, from the Children of Israel.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abdullah bin Katheer told me:
m: that he heard Mujahid say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman and Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said
m: regarding: He to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is Balaam.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: He is Balaam. ((( He said: Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: He is Balaam.

c: Humayd bin Masʿadah told us, Bishr told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Hisayn, who said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: He is Balaam.

c: Al-Harith told us, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: He is Balaam.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He is Balaam. Thaqif said: He is Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt.

x: Others said: This Balaam was from Yemen.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is a man called Balaam, from the people of Yemen.

x: Others said: He was from the Canaanites.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is a man from the city of the tyrants, called Balaam.

x: Others said: He is Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Saeed Ibn Al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Ghatif Ibn Abi Sufyan, on the authority of Ya’qub and Nafi’ Ibn Asim, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, he said
m: regarding this verse: He to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is Umayyah Ibn Abi Al-Salt.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ya’la Ibn Ata’, on the authority of Nafi’ Ibn Asim, he said: Abdullah Ibn Amr said:
m: He is your companion Umayya Ibn Abi Al-Salt.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Rahman and Wahb Ibn Jarir told us, they said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ya’la Ibn Ata’, on the authority of Nafi’ Ibn Asim, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr:
m: But he clung to the earth and followed his desires. He said: He is Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Andar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Ata’, he said:
m: I heard Nafi’ ibn Asim ibn Urwah ibn Mas’ud say: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say about this verse: He to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is your companion, meaning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: He is Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt. ... He said: Yazid told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Fadala - or Ibn Fadala - on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, who said: He is Umayya.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, he said:
m: They discussed this verse in the Great Mosque of Damascus: Then he slipped out of it.

x: Some of them said: It was revealed about Balaam bin Ba’oura.

Some of them said: It was revealed about the monk. Then Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas came out to them and they said: About whom was this revealed? It was revealed about Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt Al-Thaqafi.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Kalbi,
m: He to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, he said: He is Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt. And Qatada said: He is in doubt, some of them say: Balaam, and some of them say: Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the signs that he was given, about which God Almighty said: We gave him Our signs.
Some of them said: It was the greatest name of God.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When the forty years had passed, meaning the ones in which God said: It is forbidden to them for forty years (al-Ma’idah 5:26), God sent Joshua bin Nun as a prophet.

c: He called the Children of Israel and informed them that
m: he was a prophet and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants, so they pledged allegiance to him and believed him. A man from the Children of Israel called Balaam, who was a scholar who knew the Greatest Hidden Name, went out, but he disbelieved and went to the tyrants and said: Do not terrorize the Children of Israel, for if you go out to fight them, I will call down a curse upon them and they will perish! He was with them as much as he wanted of this world, except that he was unable to approach women because of their great size, so he used to marry a female donkey of his, and he is the one about whom God says:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs

, but he slipped out of them, meaning: see, and he slipped out of them until His saying: but he clung to the Surat al-A’raf 7:175 And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them. So Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators. earth.
b.via: He called the Children of Israel and

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, he said: He is a man called ((Balaam)), and he knew the greatest name of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, but he slipped out of them, he said: He would not ask God for anything without Him giving it to him.

x: Others said: Rather, the verses that were given to him are a book from the books of God.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There was Balaam bin Ba’er among the Children of Israel, and he was given a book.

x: Others said: Rather, he was given prophecy.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of someone else - Al-Harith
m: said: Abdul Aziz said: meaning: on the authority of someone other than himself - on the authority of Mujahid, he said: He is a prophet among the Children of Israel, meaning Balaam, he was given prophethood, he asked his people to keep quiet, so he did and left them as they were.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father:
m: that he was asked about the verse:
h
And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs
, but he slipped out of them, so he narrated on the authority of Sayyar: that there was a man called (Balaam), and he had been given prophethood, and his prayers were answered.

x: The correct thing to say about this is that God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to recite to his people the report of a man who had given him his arguments and proofs, which are the verses. We have demonstrated that the meaning of verses is evidence and signs, in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. It is possible that the one to whom God gave this was Balaam, and it is possible that it was Umayya. Likewise, if the verses are in the sense of the argument that is some of the books of God that He sent down to some of His prophets, and the one who learned them was the one whom God mentioned in this verse, and meant by it, then it is possible that the one who was given them was Balaam, and it is possible that it was Umayyah, because Umayyah, as it is said, had read from the books of the People of the Book. If it means a book that God sent down to the one whom the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, ordered to recite to his people his report, or it means the greatest name of God, or it means prophethood, then it is not permissible for it to mean Umayyah, because the nation does not differ in that Umayyah was not given anything of that, and there is no report of which of that is meant, and which of the two men is meant, that requires proof, nor is there in reason an indication of which of that is meant by which.

The correct thing to say about it is what God said, and we accept the apparent meaning of the revelation as what God brought in the revelation. As for his saying: So he stripped himself of it, it means: he left the signs that God had given him, so he disavowed them. And the people of interpretation said something similar.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When Moses, peace be upon him, descended... - meaning the tyrants - and those with him, his cousins and people came to him - meaning Balaam - and said: Moses is a man of iron, and he has many soldiers, and if he prevails over us, he will destroy us, so pray to God to turn Moses and those with him away from us. He said: If I pray to God to turn Moses and those with him away, my world and the hereafter will be lost! So they kept on at him until he prayed against them, and God stripped him of what he was upon, and this is why He said: So he slipped out of it, and Satan pursued him, and he became of the deviators.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God had given him His signs, but he abandoned them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: Then he was stripped of it, he said: knowledge was taken from him. And his saying: Then Satan followed him, means: He made him a follower of himself, who would follow his command in disobeying God, and would disobey his Lord’s command in disobeying Satan and obeying the Most Merciful. His saying: So he was among the astray, means: So he was among those who perished, due to his misguidance, disobedience to the command of his Lord, and obedience to Satan.

x: God Almighty says:
h
And if We had willed
, We could have elevated this one to whom We gave Our signs with the signs that We gave him,
h
but he clung to the earth

, meaning: he settled in the worldly life on earth and what is in it, and preferred its pleasures and desires over the Hereafter, and followed his own desire, and rejected the obedience of God and disobeyed His command.
The story of this man whose story God described in this verse, despite the differences among scholars regarding his story and his affair, was:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of his father,
m: that he was asked about the verse: And recite to them the report of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped away. So he narrated on the authority of Sayyar that there was a man called Balaam, and he had been given prophethood, and his prayers were answered. He said: And Moses came with the Children of Israel, intending the land in which Balaam was - or he said: Ash-Sham - he said: The people were terrified of him with intense fear. He said: So they went to Balaam and said: Invoke God against this man and his army! He said: Even according to the commands of my Lord - or until I am commanded - he said: So he was commanded to invoke God against them, and it was said to him: Do not invoke God against them, for they are My servants, and among them is their prophet! He said: So he said to his al-Nas 114:I have commanded my Lord to invoke God against them, and I have forbidden it. He said: So they brought him a gift and he accepted it, then they returned to him and said: Invoke God against him! He said: Even according to the commands! He was commanded, but nothing came to him. He said: So he said: I was commanded, but nothing came to me! They said: If your Lord had disliked that you should supplicate against them, He would have forbidden you as He had forbidden you the first time! He said: So he began to supplicate against them, and when he supplicated against them, his tongue would supplicate against his people, and when he wanted to supplicate for victory for his people, he would supplicate for victory for Moses and his army, or something like that, God willing. He said: They said: We do not see you supplicating except against us! He said: It only comes out of my mouth like this, and if I supplicate against him, my prayer would not be answered. But I will show you something that may lead to their destruction: God hates adultery, and if they commit adultery, they will perish. I hope that God will destroy them, so bring out the women and let them meet them, for they are a people traveling, so perhaps they will commit adultery and perish. He said: So they did, and brought out the women to meet them. He said: The king had a daughter, and he mentioned about her greatness what God knows best! He said: Her father, or Balaam, said: Do not let yourself be with anyone except Moses! He said: And they committed adultery. He said: And the head of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her and wanted to have intercourse with her. He said: She said: I will not allow myself to be with anyone except Moses! He said: So he said: My position is such and such, and my condition is such and such! He said: So she sent to her father to ask him, and he said to her: So let him be with her. He said: And a man from the sons of Aaron came to them with a spear and stabbed them. He said: And God supported him with strength, so he strung them both together and raised them on his spear. He said: So the people saw them, or something like that. He said: And God sent the plague upon them. He said: And seventy thousand of them died. He said: Abu Al-Mu'tamir said:

c: Sayyar told me:
m: Balaam rode his donkey, and when he came to the remnants - or he said: a path between the remnants - he began to beat it and it would not move forward. He said: And it stood up to him and said: Why are you beating me? Do you not see this who is in front of you? He said: And behold, Satan is in front of him. He said: So he got down and prostrated to him, and God said: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, so Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators until His saying:
h
Perhaps they will give thought

c: Sayyar told me
m: this, and I do not know, perhaps something from someone else’s hadith was included in it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I was informed of the hadith of a man from the People of the Book who said: Moses asked God to stamp him and make him one of the people of Hell. He said: So God did. He said, I was informed that Moses killed him later. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq on the authority of Salim Abu al-Nadr that he narrated: When Moses descended to the land of the Canaanites in the land of Ash-Sham, Balaam was in Bal’ah, a village in Balqa. When Moses descended to that place with the Israelites, Balaam’s people came to Balaam and said to him: O Balaam, this is Moses, son of Imran, among the Israelites. He has come to expel us from our land and kill us and settle the Israelites in it and inhabit it. We are your people and we have no home, and you are a man whose supplications are answered, so go out and supplicate to God against them! He said: Woe to you! The Prophet of God has with him the angels and the believers. How can I go and supplicate against them, while I know from God what I know!! They said: We have no home! They kept on beseeching him and supplicating him until they tempted him and he was tempted. He rode his donkey towards the mountain that overlooked the camp of the Children of Israel, which was Mount Hisban. After he had walked on it for a short time, it lay down with him, so he got off and hit it. When he made it slippery, it stood up and he mounted it. It did not walk with him for long until it lay down with him, so he hit it. When he made it slippery, God gave it permission and it spoke to Him as an argument against Him. It said: Woe to you, Balaam, where are you going? Don’t you see the angels in front of me, preventing me from this path? Are you going to the Prophet of God and the believers to invoke curses upon them? But he did not stop hitting it, so God let it go when He had done that to it. He said: So she set off until she overlooked the top of Mount Hisban, over the camp of Moses and the Children of Israel. He kept invoking curses upon them, and he did not invoke anything against them except that he turned his tongue to his people, and he did not invoke anything good for his people except that he turned his tongue to the Children of Israel. His people said to him: Do you know, Balaam, what you are doing? You only pray for them and against us! He said: This is something I do not own, this is something that God has overcome! He said: His tongue stuck out and cracked on his chest, and he said to them: Now the world and the hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but deceit and trickery, so I will deceive and scheme for you. Beautify the women and give them the goods, then send them to the camp to sell them there, and order them that no woman should refuse herself to a man who wants her, for if one of them commits adultery, you will be spared them! So they did. When the women entered the camp, a Canaanite woman named (Kasba the daughter of Sur), the head of his nation, passed by a man from the nobles of the Children of Israel, and he was Zimri son of Shallum, the head of the tribe of Simeon son of Jacob son of Isaac son of Abraham. He stood up to her, took her by the hand when he admired her beauty, then he brought her until he stood with her in front of Moses, peace be upon him, and he said: I think you will say this is forbidden to you? He said: Yes, it is forbidden to you, do not go near her! He said: By God, we will not obey you in this! So he entered his tent with her and fell upon her. And God sent the plague upon the children of Israel. And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron, the one who was in charge of Moses, was a man who had been given the breadth of character and the power to strike. He was absent when Zimri the son of Shallum did what he did. Then he came while the plague was raging among the children of Israel. He reported the report, and took his spear, which was all iron, and entered the tent upon them while they were lying down. He strung them together with his spear, and then he went out with them, raising them to heaven, and he held the spear in his arm, and leaned his elbow on his waist, and leaned the spear on his jaw - and he was the firstborn of Eleazar - and he began to say: O God, this is how we deal with those who disobey you! And the plague was lifted. So he calculated how many of the children of Israel had perished in the plague between the time Zimri afflicted the woman and Phinehas killed him, and they found that seventy thousand of them had perished - and the lesser says: twenty thousand - in one hour of the day. From there the children of Israel gave to the son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, from every sacrifice they slaughtered: the cloak, the forearm, and the jawbone, because he leaned the grain on his waist, took it with his forearm, and supported it on his jawbone, and the firstborn of all their wealth and their lives, because he was the firstborn of Eleazar. So concerning Balaam, son of Ba’ur, God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, meaning Balaam, and Satan pursued him, and he was among the deviators, until His saying: that they might reflect.

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: A man from the Children of Israel called Balaam set out and went to the tyrants and said: Do not be afraid of the Children of Israel, for if you go out to fight them, I will invoke a curse upon them and they will perish. So Joshua went out to fight the tyrants among the people, and Balaam went out with the tyrants on his donkey, and he wanted to curse the Children of Israel. So whenever he wanted to invoke a curse upon the Children of Israel, he invoked a curse upon the tyrants. The tyrants said: You are only invoking a curse upon us! But he said: I only meant the Children of Israel! When he reached the gate of the city, an angel took hold of the donkey by the tail and held her back. He tried to move her but she would not move. When he beat her more, she spoke and said: You have intercourse with me at night and ride me during the day! Woe to me from you! If I had the power to go out, I would have, but this king is holding me back! And about Balaam, God says: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, the verse.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, a man told me that
m: he heard Ikrimah say: A woman among them said: Show me Moses, so I may tempt Surat al-A’raf 7:176 And if We willed, We could have raised him thereby,
h
but he clung to the earth
and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him alone, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs.
h
So relate the stories
that
h
perhaps they will give thought

. him! He said: So she perfumed herself and passed by a man who looked like Moses, and he had intercourse with her. Then Ibn Harun was brought and informed, so he took a sword and stabbed him in his urethra until he pulled it out and pulled it out from before her, then he raised them so that the people could see them, and they knew that he was not Moses. So the family of Harun was given preference in sacrifice over the family of Moses in terms of the shoulder, the upper arm, and the thigh. He said: He is the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, meaning Balaam.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His statement:
h
And if We had willed
, We could have raised him thereby.
Some of them said: It means: We raised him with his knowledge of it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And if We had willed
, We could have raised him thereby, meaning God Almighty raised him by His knowledge.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: We removed from him the state he had reached of disbelief in God, through Our verses.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And if We had willed
, We could have raised him thereby, meaning We could have pushed him away from it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And if We had willed
, We could have raised him thereby, meaning We could have pushed him away from it.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is that God made the report general with His statement,
h
And if We had willed

, We could have elevated him thereby, meaning that if He had willed, He could have elevated him by His signs that He gave him. And elevation includes many meanings: including elevation in status with Him, elevation in the honor and bounties of this world, and elevation in beautiful mention and high praise. It is possible that God meant all of that: that if He had willed, He could have elevated him and given him all of that, by enabling him to act upon His signs that He had given him. Since that is possible, the correct statement about it is that nothing is specific to it, since there is no evidence of its specificity from the report or the mind. As for his saying: with it, Ibn Zayd said about that the same as we said.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And if We had willed
, We could have raised him thereby, with those verses. As for his saying:
h
But he clung to the earth
, the people of interpretation said about it something similar to what we said about it.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: But he leaned on the ground, meaning: he leaned on the ground. ... He said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: But he inclined to the ground, he said: He was drawn to the ground.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: akhlaad means to remain still.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There was among the Children of Israel Balaam bin Ba’er, who was given a book, but he was inclined to the desires of the earth, its pleasures and its wealth. He did not benefit from what the book brought.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But he clung to the earth
and followed his desires. As for clung to the earth, he followed the world and relied on it.

x: The root of ikhlaad in Arabic speech is to slow down and stay. It is said: So-and-so stayed in a place, if he stayed there, and he stayed himself in a place, if he came to it from another place. From this is the saying of Zuhair: Whose home is it that you have covered with the rain like a revelation in the slope of the eternal stream? It means the resident, and from it is the saying of Malik bin Nuwairah: With the sons of a neighborhood from the tribes of Malik and Amr bin Yarbu’ they settled and became immortal Some Basrans used to say: The meaning of his saying, Ikhlad, is to adhere to, be lazy, and be slow. Al-Mukhlad also means the man whose gray hair is slow to appear, and he is one of the animals whose front teeth remain until his two front teeth emerge.
As for his saying: And he followed his desires, Ibn Zayd said in its interpretation, what:

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: about his statement:
h
And he followed his desire
, he said: His desire was with the people.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
His example is like that of a dog
: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.”

God Almighty says: The example of this one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped away from them, is like that of a panting dog, whether you chase him away or leave him alone. Then the people of interpretation differed about the reason why God made his example like that of a dog.

Some of them said: His example is like that of the panting, because he neglected to act according to the Book of God and His verses that He gave him, and his turning away from the admonitions of God, which are the turning away of one to whom God has not given anything of that. So God, the Most High, said about him, since it was the same as his command, whether he was admonished by the verses of God that He gave him or not, in that he would not be admonished by them, nor would he abandon disbelief in them: So his example is like that of the dog, whose command is the same as his panting, whether he was chased away or not, since he would never stop panting.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Like a dog, if you chase it, it pants, he said: You chase it away, it is like the one who reads the book but does not act upon it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: “
h
His example is like that of a dog

: if you chase him, he pants,” he said: You chase him with your mount and your foot, He pants, he said: Like the one who reads a book but does not act upon what is in it. Ibn Jurayj said: The dog is one whose heart is cut off, he has no heart. If you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. He said: Like the one who abandons guidance, he has no heart, his heart is cut off.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of some of them:
m: h
His example is like that of a dog
: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.” Therefore, he is the disbeliever. He is astray whether you admonish him or not.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
His example is like that of a dog
, if wisdom is imposed on him, he will not carry it, and if he is left alone, he will not be guided to good, like a dog that, if it is lying down, it pants, and if it is chased, it pants.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God gave him His signs, but he abandoned them, so God made his example like that of a dog: If you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him alone, he pants.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them, so Satan pursued him, the verse. This is a parable that God gave for the one to whom guidance was offered but he refused to accept it and abandoned it. He said: Al-Hasan used to say: He is the hypocrite. “
h
And if We had willed
, We could have elevated him thereby,
h
but he clung to the earth
and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants,” he said: This is the example of the disbeliever, dead of heart.

x: Others said: He, may His praise be glorified, is like a dog, because he was panting like a dog.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
His example is like that of a dog
: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him alone, he pants.” Balaam used to pant like a dog. As for attack him, it means you force him.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations of this is the interpretation of the one who said: It is only an example of his abandoning the work of the verses of God that He gave him, and that its meaning is: whether he was admonished or not, in that he does not abandon what he is doing of disobeying the command of his Lord, just as whether he attacked a dog and chased it away or left it and did not chase it away, in that it does not stop panting in either of its states. We said: This is the more correct of the two statements, because of the evidence of the Almighty’s saying:
h
That is the example of the people who denied Our signs

, so He made that an example of those who deny His signs. And we know that panting is not in the nature of every denier who is destined to abandon repentance from his denial of the signs of God, and that this is only an example that God has given them.
So it was known from this that it is for the one whose description God described in this verse, as it is for all those who deny the signs of God, an example.
The saying in the interpretation of his saying:
h
That is the example of the people who denied Our signs
h
so relate the stories
that
h
perhaps they will give thought

God Almighty says: This example that I have given for this one to whom We gave Our signs and then he detached himself from them is like the example of the people who denied Our proofs, signs and evidence, and followed in that the path of this one who detached himself from Our signs that We gave him, in his abandonment of acting upon what We gave him of that. As for His saying:
h
So relate the stories

, He is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So relate, O Muhammad, this story that I have related to you, from the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs and the report of the nations whose report I have told you in this Surah, and I have related to you their report and the report of their likes, and what befell them of Our punishment, and what descended upon them when they denied Our Surat al-A’raf 7:176 And if We willed, We could have raised him thereby,
h
but he clung to the earth
and followed his own desire.
So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him alone, he pants. That is the example of the people who deny Our signs.
h
So relate the stories
that
h
perhaps they will give thought

. messengers of Our vengeance upon your people from Quraysh, and those before you from the Jews of the Children of Israel, so that they may reflect on that, and take heed and turn to Our obedience, lest the same vengeance and punishment that befell those before them befall them, and the Jews of the Children of Israel may ponder it, and know the truth of your matter and the truth of your prophethood, since the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs was from the hidden knowledge of theirs, and the hidden report of them, and none knows it except their rabbis, and those of them who read and studied the books. And in your knowledge of this, while you are illiterate and do not write, nor read, nor study books, and you have not sat with people of knowledge, is the clear proof for you against them, that you are a Messenger of God, and that you did not know what you know of this and your condition as you are, except by revelation from heaven.
Abu Al-Nadr used to say something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Salim Abu al-Nadr:
m: h
So relate the stories
that
h
perhaps they will give thought
, meaning the Children of Israel, when you came to them with report of what had happened to them that they had hidden from you, that
h
perhaps they will give thought
, and know that no one brought this report of what had happened to them except a prophet to whom report from heaven came.

x: Ayu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: Evil is the example of the people who denied God's proofs and evidence, and rejected them, while they themselves were reducing their portions and depriving themselves of their benefits, by denying them, and nothing else. It was said: Bad example, from saw, meaning: bad example - like the people - and the people was used in place of the example and the example was deleted, since the meaning of the speech was understood, as God Almighty said: But righteousness is of him who believes in God (al-Baqarah 2:177), for its meaning is: but righteousness is of him who believes in God. We have explained similar examples in other places, so there is no need to repeat it.

God Almighty says: Guidance and misguidance are in the hand of God, and the guided - who is the one who follows the path of truth, riding the straight path - in his religion, is the one whom God guides to that and makes him successful in achieving it, and the misguided is the one whom God lets down and does not make him successful in obeying Him. And the one to whom God does that is the loser, meaning the one who is doomed. We have explained the meaning of loss, “guidance,” and misguidance in more than one place in this book, so there is no need to repeat it here.
God Almighty says:
h
And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind
. It is said: God scattered His creation, scattered them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Azdi told me, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind
, he said: From what We created.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We have certainly created for Hell

, he said: We created. ... He said: Zakariya told us, on the authority of Atab bin Bashir, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The children of fornication are among what God has created for Hell. ... He said: Zakariya bin Adi and Uthman Al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Marwan bin Muawiyah, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Amr, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Ishaq, on the authority of a companion of his in Taif, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When God created for Hell what He created, the child of fornication was among those created for Hell.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And We have certainly created for Hell
, meaning: We created.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say regarding His statement:
h
And We have certainly created for Hell
, he said: We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And We have certainly created for Hell
, we created.

x: And God Almighty said:
h
And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind
, because His knowledge penetrated them that they would go there because of their disbelief in their Lord. As for His statement:
h
They have hearts with which they do not understand

, its meaning is: For those of His creation whom God has created for Hell, there are hearts with which they do not reflect on the verses of God, nor do they ponder His proofs for His Oneness, nor do they consider His arguments for His Messengers, so that they may know the Oneness of their Lord and recognize the truth of the prophethood of their Prophets. So our Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, described them as: with which they do not understand, because of their turning away from the truth, and their failure to ponder the truth of the prophethood of the Messengers, and because of their long periods of disbelief.
Likewise, His statement:
h
And they have eyes with which they do not see

, means: And they have eyes with which they do not look at the signs and evidence of God, so they do not contemplate them and reflect on them, so they know with them the truth of what their messengers call them to, and the corruption of what they are abiding upon, of associating partners with God and denying His messengers. So God described them by their abandonment of their actions in the truth, that they do not see with them. Likewise, His statement:
h
And they have ears with which they do not hear
, the verses of the Book of God, so they consider them and reflect on them, but they turn away from them and say: Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it that you may overcome
r
(Fussilat 41:26)
. This is similar to God’s description of them in another place, when He says: Deaf, dumb and blind, so they do not understand (al-Baqarah 2:171).

The Arabs say this to someone who has abandoned the use of some of his limbs in a way that is good for him. An example of this is the saying of Miskeen Al-Darimi: Blind if my neighbor goes out until my neighbor is covered by the curtain And my hearing is deaf to what is between them, and there is no dignity in my hearing He described himself as blind and deaf because he had abandoned sight and hearing.

Another said: The one-eyed, mean ones are deaf to it, and if I wish, I am All-Hearing of it. And the initiative distributed the soul about it and the ribs were filled with anger This is common in Arabic speech and poetry. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say about His statement,
h
They have hearts with which they do not understand
, he said: They do not understand with them anything about the matter of the Hereafter,
h
And they have eyes with which they do not see
, the guidance,
h
And they have ears with which they do not hear
, the truth. Then He made them like livestock, equal, then He made them worse than livestock, and said: Rather, they are more astray, then He informed that they are the heedless.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
Those are like livestock
, rather, they are more astray.
It is those who are the heedless.”
What God, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
Those are like livestock
