, is that these are the ones He has created for Hell. They are like livestock, which are beasts that do not understand what is said to them, nor do they comprehend what they see, what is good and what is not good, nor do they reason in our hearts between good and evil, so that they can distinguish between them. So God likened them to them, since they do not remember what they see with their eyes of His proofs, nor do they ponder what they hear from the verses of His Book. Then He said, Rather, they are more astray, meaning: These unbelievers whom He has created for Hell are more astray from the truth, and more committed to the path of falsehood, than the beasts, because beasts have no choice or discernment, so they can choose and distinguish, but they are subjugated, and despite that they flee from harm, and seek for themselves the best food.

Those whom God described in this verse, with what they were given of understanding and minds that distinguish between benefits and harms, abandon what is good for their worldly life and the hereafter, and seek what is harmful to them. Among the beasts, there are lions, and there are more astray than them, as our Lord, may His praise be glorified, described them. And His statement: Those are the heedless ones. God Almighty says: These are the ones whose description I have described, the people who were heedless - meaning: inadvertently - of My signs and proofs, and left contemplating them and considering them and deducing what they indicate of the oneness of their Lord, not the animals whose Lord has made them aware of what He has subjected them to.
God Almighty says: And to God belong the best names, and they are as Ibn Abbas said:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them, and among His names is: (The Almighty, the Compeller), and all of His names are good.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever counts them all will enter Paradise.” As for his saying:
h
And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names

, he means the polytheists. Their blasphemy regarding the names of God was that they changed them from what they were, so they named their gods and idols with them, and they added to them and subtracted from them. They named some of them Al-Lat, deriving them from the name of God, which is God, and they named some of them Al-Uzza, deriving them from the name of God, which is Al-Aziz. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names
, he said: The blasphemy of the blasphemers is that they invoke al-Lat among the names of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names
, he said: They derived Al-Uzza from Al-Aziz, and they derived Al-Lat from God.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement: They commit heresy.
Some of them said: They are lying.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names
, he said: Blindness means denial.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: they associate others with God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They commit blasphemy, he said: they associate others with God. The root of ilhad in Arabic is to deviate from the intended goal, to go against it, and to turn away. It is then used for everything that is crooked and not straight. That is why the grave's boundary is called lahd because it is on one side of it, not in the middle. It is said from it: So-and-so ilhad ilhadan, Walhad yalhadan lahad wa lahudan The boundary is a grave, not a tomb. It was mentioned about Al-Kisa’i that he differentiated between ilhad and lahd, saying that ilhad means deviating from the intended purpose, and lahd means leaning towards something. He used to read everything in the Qur’an as yalhadun with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ha’, except for the one in An-Nahl [verse 103], as he used to read it as yalhadun with a fatha on the ya’ and the ha’, and he claimed that it means leaning towards something. As for the rest of the people who know the Arabic language, they see that their meaning is one, and that they are two languages that came in one letter with one meaning. There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Medina, some of the Basrans, and the Kufians read it as yalhadun, with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ha’, from alhad yalhad, in the entire Qur’an. The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: Yalhadun with the opening of the ya and the ha, from lahd yalhad.

x: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two languages with one meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct in that, except that I choose the reading with a damma on the ya’, according to the language of the one who said: (alhad), because it is the most famous of the two languages and the most eloquent of them. Ibn Zayd used to say about his statement:
h
And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names
, that it was abrogated.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names
, he said: These are the people of disbelief, and it has been abrogated, abrogated by fighting. Ibn Zayd’s statement that it is abrogated does not make sense, because his statement,
h
And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names

, is not a command from God to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to leave the polytheists to say that until He gives him permission to fight them. Rather, it is a threat from God to those who blaspheme concerning His names, and a warning from Him to them, as He said in another place, Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope delude them (al-Hijr 15:3), and as He said, That they may disbelieve in what We have given them and enjoy themselves, for they are going to know (al-Ankabut 29:66). These are statements that were issued in the form of a command in the sense of a warning and a warning, and its meaning is: O Muhammad, those who blaspheme concerning the names of God will be given a respite until a term they reach, so they will be recompensed, when the term that God has given them comes to them, for the deeds that they used to do before that, of disbelief in God, blaspheming concerning His names, and denying His Messenger.

evidence.text: He used to read everything in the Qur’an as yalhadun with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ha’, except for the one in An-Nahl [verse 103], as he used to read it as yalhadun with a fatha on the ya’ and the ha’, and he claimed that it means leaning towards something.
The majority of the people of Medina, some of the Basrans, and the Kufians read it as yalhadun, with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ha’, from alhad yalhad, in the entire Qur’an.
The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: Yalhadun with the opening of the ya and the ha, from lahd yalhad.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct thing to say about this is that they are two languages with one meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct in that, except that I choose the reading with a damma on the ya’, according to the language of the one who said: (alhad), because it is the most famous of the two languages and the most eloquent of them.

x: God Almighty says: And among the creation whom We created is a nation, meaning a group, who guide, meaning: they are guided by the truth, and by it they do justice, meaning: and by the truth they judge and treat people fairly, as Ibn Jurayj said.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A nation who guides with the truth and does justice thereby
. Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is my nation! He said: With the truth they take, give, and judge.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And among those We created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: His statement:
h
And among those We created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby

, “It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when he recited it: This is for you, and the people before you have been given something similar: ‘And among the people of Moses is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby’ (al-A’raf 7:159).”

evidence.text: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His statement: And among those We created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby, “It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when he recited it: This is for you, and the people before you have been given something similar: ‘And among the people of Moses is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby’ (al-A’raf 7:159).”

x: God Almighty says: And those who denied Our proofs and signs, and rejected them, and did not remember by them, We will give them respite by deceiving them, and make their evil deeds seem good to them, until they think that they are doing good to themselves in their denial of God’s signs, and until they reach the limit of the respite that was written for them. Then He will seize them with their evil deeds, and will reward them with the punishment that He has prepared for them. And that is God’s luring them. The origin of luring is the person being deceived by the kindness of the person who lured him, as the person being lured sees that the person being lured is a good person, until he gets him involved in something unpleasant. We have previously explained the reason for God’s action against the people who disbelieved in Him, so there is no need to repeat it here.

God Almighty says: And those who denied Our signs were delayed. The origin of imla’ is from their saying: A long time has passed for him, and a long time has passed, with kasra, damma, and fatha, of time, which means the time, and from it it is said: I waited for you for a long time. So that they may attain, through their disobedience to their Lord, the amount of punishment and torment that He has written for them, and then He will take them to Himself. My kid. (And the plot) is deceit. His saying: strong, means: strong and powerful. From this comes the poet’s saying: The most just of people are the most ugly, and the most painful of all is the one who is afflicted with various kinds of evil. Meaning: a strong, continuous, and uninterrupted journey.

God Almighty says: Did not these people who denied Our signs reflect, ponder with their minds, and know that Our Messenger whom We sent to them is neither mad nor insane, and that what he called them to is the correct opinion, the upright religion, and the clear truth?
This verse was revealed, as it was said, as follows:

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us,
m: “On the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on Al-Safa, and he called the Quraysh and began to strike them thigh by thigh: O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so! So he warned them of the wrath of God and the events of God, and one of them said: This companion of yours is mad! He kept shouting until morning - or: until morning! So God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: “Have they not considered? There is no madness in their companion.
h
He is only a clear warner
.” What he means by his saying:
h
He is only a clear warner

, is that he is only a warner warning you of God’s punishment for your disbelief in Him, if you do not repent to believing in Him. By his saying: clear, he means that he has made clear to you, O people, his warning of what he warned you of of God’s punishment for your disbelief in Him.

x: God Almighty says: Have these deniers of God’s signs not looked at God’s kingdom and His authority in the heavens and the earth, and at what He, the Most High, has created in them, so that they may reflect on that, take heed of it, and know that this is for One who has no equal or likeness, and from the actions of One to whom worship and pure religion should not be except, so that they may believe in Him, believe in His Messenger, turn to His obedience, renounce rivals and idols, and beware that their appointed times may be approaching, so that they may perish in their disbelief and be subject to God’s punishment and painful chastisement. And his saying:
h
So in what statement after this will they believe

? He says: So in what frightening and warning and terror after the warning and terror of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, which he brought to them from God in the verses of his book, will they believe, if they do not believe in this book that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them from God Almighty?

God Almighty says: The aversion of those who denied Our signs, who abandoned contemplating and thinking about God’s proofs, is because God has led them astray. If God had guided them, they would have considered and pondered and seen their right path. But God has led them astray, so they do not see right path nor are they guided to a path. And whoever He leads astray from right path, there is no guide for him to it. But God leaves them in their persistence in their disbelief and their rebellion in their polytheism, wavering, so that they may deserve the goal that God has written for them of His punishment and painful chastisement.
The people of interpretation differed about those meant by his saying:
h
They ask you about the Hour

Some of them said: This refers to the people of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Quraysh, and they had asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Quraysh said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is a kinship between us and you, so tell us secretly when the Hour will be! God said: They ask you as if you were anxious about it.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant a group of Jews.

Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad Musa Zaid bin Thabit narrated, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Jabal bin Abi Qushair and Shamul bin Zaid said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, tell us when the Hour will be, if you are a prophet as you say, for we know when it will be! Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: “
h
They ask you about the Hour
: when is its appointed time? Say, ‘The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord,’” until His saying:
h
But most of the people do not know

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept mentioning the matter of the Hour until this verse was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the Hour
: when is its arrival?”

x: The correct thing to say about that is that some people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Hour, so God revealed this verse. It is possible that they were from Quraysh, and it is possible that they were from the Jews, but we do not have any information about that, so it is permissible to say with certainty which one it was.
The interpretation of the verse is: The people who ask you about the Hour ask you: When is its arrival? He says: When will it occur?

i: The meaning of Ayan is: when, in Arabic speech, and from it the rajaz poet said:
x: When will my need be met?

Don't you see that her success is ours? The meaning of his saying: its anchorage is its standing, from the saying of the speaker: God anchored it, so it is an anchor, and the people anchored it, if they detained it, and it anchored, they anchored, an anchor. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
They ask you about the Hour
: when is its arrival?” He said: When will it come?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
They ask you about the Hour
: when is its arrival?” When will it come?

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: its end, and that is close in meaning to the meaning of the one who said: Its meaning is: (its establishment), because its end is its reaching its time. We have shown that the origin of this is: imprisonment and standing.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “
h
They ask you about the Hour

: when is its arrival?” meaning: its end. As for his saying: “Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None can reveal its time except Him,” then it is a command from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer those who ask him about the Hour by saying that none knows the time of its occurrence except God, who knows the unseen, and that He does not reveal its time and none knows it except Him, may He be glorified and exalted, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None can reveal it at its time except Him.” He says: Its knowledge is with God, He will reveal it at its time, none knows that except God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He does not reveal it, he brings it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Mujahid said:
m: He does not reveal it, he said: No one brings it except Him.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: None can reveal it at its time except Him, meaning: None can send it at its time except Him.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: “
h
It is heavy in the heavens and the earth
It will not come upon you except suddenly.”
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: The Hour is too difficult for the people of the heavens and the earth to know its time and coming, because it is hidden from them, and God has kept its knowledge to Himself.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is heavy in the heavens and the earth
, meaning: It is hidden in the heavens and the earth, so no close angel or sent prophet knows when it will rise.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of some of the people of interpretation:
h
It is heavy in the heavens and the earth
, he said: Its knowledge is heavy for the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, they do not know.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that it became great when it came upon the people of the heavens and the earth.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Muammar, he said, al-Hasan said regarding His statement:
h
It is heavy in the heavens and the earth
, meaning: When it comes, it is heavy on the people of the heavens and the people of the earth. He says: It is too great for them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
It is heavy in the heavens and the earth
, he said: When it comes, the sky will split, the stars will scatter, the sun will be rolled up, the mountains will move, and what God said will happen. That is its weight.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Some people said
m: about thaqalat: it became great.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying: in the heavens and the earth is the heavens and the earth.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It is heavy in the heavens and the earth
, meaning: on the heavens and the earth.

x: The most correct of these, in my opinion, is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is: The Hour in the heavens and the earth will be too heavy for its inhabitants to know its time and its occurrence, because God has hidden that from His creation, and has not informed any of them of it. This is because God informed of this after His statement: “Say, ‘Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None can reveal its time except He.’” And He informed after that that it will not come except suddenly. So what is more correct is that what is between that also be report of the concealment of its knowledge from creation, since what came before it and what came after it was like that.
As for his saying:
h
It will not come to you except suddenly
, he is saying: The Hour will not come except suddenly, you will not feel its coming, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
It will not come to you except suddenly
, meaning: Its occurrence will take them by surprise, it will come to them unawares.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It will not come to you except suddenly
, God has decreed that
h
it will not come to you except suddenly

. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “The Hour will come upon the people while a man is repairing his cistern, while a Surat al-A’raf 7:187
h
They ask you about the Hour
: when is its appointed time? Say, "The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord. None can reveal its time except Him.
h
It is heavy in the heavens and the earth
. It will not come upon you except suddenly." They ask you as if you were anxious about it. Say, "The knowledge thereof is only with God,
h
but most of the people do not know
." man is watering his livestock, while a man is displaying his merchandise in the market, while a man is lowering his scales and raising them.”

x: The statement in the interpretation of His saying: “
h
They ask you as if you are knowledgeable about it
Say, ‘The knowledge thereof is only with God, but most people do not know.’”
God Almighty says: These people ask you about the Hour, as if you are aware of it.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying:
h
He was protected from it
Some of them said: They ask you about it as if you are aware of them. They said: The meaning of his saying: about it is to bring it forward, even if it is delayed.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They ask you as if you were aware of it

, meaning: as if there was love between you and them, as if you were their friend. Ibn ʿAbbas said: “When the people asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Hour, they asked him the question of people who thought that Muhammad was aware of them, so God revealed to him: Its knowledge is with Him alone. He has kept its knowledge to Himself, and has not informed any angel or messenger of it.”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Qatada said:
m: The Quraysh said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: There is a kinship between us and you, so tell us in secret when the Hour will be! God said:
h
They ask you as if you were aware of it

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They ask you as if you were aware of it
, meaning: aware of them. He said: The Quraysh said: O Muhammad, tell us in secret the knowledge of the Hour, because of the kinship between us and you, because of our kinship to you.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar and Hani’ bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah:
m: h
They ask you as if you were aware of it
, he said: Be aware of them when they ask you.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: They ask you as if you were aware of them, he said: Close to them, and you are aware of them. He said: Abu Malik said: As if you were aware of them. He said: Close to them, and you are aware of them. He said: Abu Malik said: As if you were aware of them, so you talk to them.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
They ask you as if you are aware of it
, as if you are a friend of theirs.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It is as if you had been too shy to ask about it, so you learned it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: As if you were careful about it, you were careful about asking about it until you knew it.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: As if you were afraid of it, he said: I was afraid of asking about it until I knew its time.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
They ask you as if you are knowledgeable about it

, he said: As if you are knowledgeable about it. ... He said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: They ask you as if you are well-versed in it, he said: As if you know it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
They ask you as if you are aware of it
, meaning:
h
They ask you about the Hour
, as if you have knowledge of it. Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of some of them:
m: As if you are aware of it, as if you are knowledgeable about it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, As if you were well-versed in it, he said: As if you were knowledgeable about it. And he said: He concealed its knowledge from His creation. And he recited: Indeed, with God is knowledge of the Hour
r
(Luqman 31:34)
, until he finished the surah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They ask you as if you are aware of it

, meaning: as if you are pleased with their questioning of you, Say, ‘Its knowledge is only with God.’ And his saying: As if you were gentle with her, means: gentle with her. These people interpreted his statement: As if you were a thief about it, as meaning he was a thief about it. They said: The Arabs say: I was a thief to him in the matter and I was a thief about him. They said: That is why it was said: We came to so-and-so to ask him, meaning: we asked about him.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: As if you are keen on asking about it and learning it.
How was it said:
h
He was protected from it
, and not: He was protected by it, if that is the interpretation of the statement?

That was said in this way, because (al-hafwah) is only in the question, and it is the cheerfulness to the one being asked when asked, and asking a lot about him, and (al-salah) is connected with (an) once, and with (ba) once.
So it is said: (I asked about him), and (I asked about him).

i: So when he put his saying (hafy) in place of (al-salah), he connected with most of the two letters that (al-salah) is connected with, which is (an), as the poet said:
x: A sincere question about his brother, as if he mentioned him and Sinan or they are equal As for his saying: “Say: Its knowledge is only with God,” its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to those who ask you about the time of the Hour and the time of its coming: I have no knowledge of that, and no knowledge of it is with God who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, but most people do not know, meaning: But most people do not know that only God knows that, rather they think that knowledge of that is with some of His creation.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who ask you about the Hour: When will it come? “I do not possess for myself benefit or harm,” meaning: I am not able to bring benefit to myself, nor to ward off harm that befalls it, except what God wills that I possess of that, by strengthening me and helping me. And if I knew the unseen, meaning: if I knew what would happen of what has not yet happened, I would have multiplied good, meaning: I would have prepared much good. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of good that God meant by His saying:
h
I would have increased in good
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: I would have done many good deeds.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qamis told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, his statement: Say, ‘I do not control for myself any benefit or harm,’ he said: guidance and misguidance, And if I knew the unseen,
h
I would have increased in good
, he said: (I know the unseen), when I will die, I would have increased in righteous deeds.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: And if I had known the unseen,
h
I would have increased in good
, and no evil would have touched me, he said: I would have avoided what is evil and guarded against it.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: If I knew the unseen, I would have prepared for the barren year from the fertile one, and I would have known the high prices from the low prices, and I would have prepared for it in the low prices. And His statement:
h
And no harm has touched me
, meaning:
h
And no harm has touched me

. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings, meaning: I am only a messenger of God who sent me to you, warning of His punishment to those of you who disobey Him and go against His command, and giving good tidings of His reward and honor to those of you who believe in Him and obey Him. And His saying:
h
For a people who believe
, means: They believe that I am a Messenger of God, and they acknowledge the truth of what I have brought to them from Him.
God Almighty says: It is He who created you from one soul, meaning by one soul, Adam, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He created you from one soul, he said: Adam, peace be upon him.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He is the One who created you from a single soul from Adam
. What he means by his saying:
h
And made from her her mate
, is that he made from the single soul, which is Adam, her mate, Eve, as:

c: Bishr told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And made from her her mate

, Eve, so she was made from one of his ribs, so that he might find peace with her. What he means by his saying: “to find peace in it” is to take refuge in it, to satisfy his need and enjoy it. What he means by his saying:
h
So when he covered her

, is that when he covered her to satisfy his need from her, and he satisfied his need from her, she bore a light burden. There is something omitted in the speech, and he left mentioning it in order to suffice with what is apparent from what was omitted, and that is his saying:
h
So when he covered her
, she bore, but the speech is:
h
So when he covered her
- and satisfied his need from her - she bore. His saying:
h
She carried a light load

, he means by light load, the water that Eve carried in her womb from Adam, that it was a light load, and likewise the woman’s carrying of the man’s water, it is light for her. As for his saying: She passed by it, it means: She continued in the water, stood and sat in it, and completed the pregnancy, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Umair, on the authority of Ayoub, he said,
m: I asked Al-Hasan about his saying:
h
She carried a light load and passed by with it
. He said: If I were an Arab, I would know what it means. It is: She continued with it.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So when he covered her
, she carried a light burden and passed around with it, her pregnancy became apparent.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
So she passed by him
, he said: Her pregnancy continued.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
She carried a light load
, he said: It is the sperm, and his statement: So it passed by him, he said: It continued with him.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is, she doubted it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So she passed by him
, he said: So she doubted whether she was pregnant or not? What he means by his saying:
h
When she became heavy

, is when what was in her womb of the pregnancy that was light became heavy, and her birth was near. It is said: So-and-so became heavy with her load, if she became heavy with her load, just as it is said: So-and-so became heavy, if he became heavy with her load, just as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
When she became heavy
, meaning the child grew in her womb.

x: They called upon God, their Lord, meaning: Adam and Eve called upon their Lord and said: O our Lord,
h
If You give us something good
h
we will surely be among the grateful

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of righteousness, which Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, swore that if He gave them a righteous pregnancy, then we would be among the grateful.
Some of them said: That means the pregnancy will be a boy.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Al-Hasan said
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you give us a righteous person
, he said: A boy.

x: Others said: Rather, it is that the newborn is a normal human being like them, and not an animal.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Zaid bin Jubayr al-Jashmi, on the authority of Abu al-Bukhtari,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If You give us something good
h
we will surely be among the grateful

, he said: They feared that it would be something less than a human being. ... He said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Zaid bin Jubair, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, who said: They feared that he would not be human. ... He said, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: When Adam’s wife became pregnant and became heavy, they were afraid that he would be an animal, so they called upon their Lord: If You give us a good child, the verse. ... He said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They feared that it would be an animal.

c: Al-Qasim told me, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Saeed bin Jubair said:
m: When Adam and Eve descended, lust was cast into his soul, so he had intercourse with her. As soon as he had intercourse with her, she became pregnant. As soon as she became pregnant, her child began to stir in her womb. She said: What is this? Then Satan came to her and said to her: You have become pregnant, so will you give birth? She said: What do I give birth to? He said: Do you see on earth anything but a she-camel, a cow, a sheep, a goat, or some of that? And it comes out of your nose, or your ear, or your eye. She said: By God, there is nothing in me that is not too narrow for that! He said: Then obey me and name him Abdul-Harith - and his name among the angels was Al-Harith - and she will give birth to someone similar to you, like you. He said: So I mentioned that to Adam, peace be upon him, and he said: He is our companion whom you did! Then he died, and she became pregnant with another. He came and said: Obey me and name him Abd al-Harith - and his name among the angels was al-Harith - or else I will give birth to a camel, a cow, a sheep, or a goat, or I will kill him, for I am the one who killed the first! He said: So I mentioned that to Adam, and it was as if he did not hate it, so she named him Abd al-Harith. That is what His saying:
h
If you give us a righteous child
, means: We will be like us. So when He gave them both a righteous child, means: He will make them like us.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And when she became heavily pregnant, meaning the child grew in her womb, Satan came to her and frightened her and said to her: How do you know what is in your womb? Perhaps it is a dog, or a pig, or a donkey! And how do you know from where it will come out? From your back to kill you, or from your front, or your belly to split open and kill you? So that was when they called upon God, their Lord, ‘If You should give us a good thing,’ he said: like us,
h
we will surely be among the grateful

c: The correct thing to say about this is that God informed us
m: about Adam and Eve that they called upon God, their Lord, to conceive Eve, and they swore that if He gave them what was in Eve’s womb, good, they would be among those who are grateful to God. And righteousness may include many meanings: including righteousness in the perfection of creation, righteousness in religion, and righteousness in reason and management. Since this is the case, and there is no report from the Messenger that requires proof that this is for some meanings of righteousness and not others, and there is no evidence for it from reason, it must be general as God made it general, so it is said: They said: If you bring us something good, with all meanings of righteousness. As for the meaning of his saying:
h
We will surely be among the grateful
, it is: We will surely be among those who thank You for the righteous child You have given them.
b.via: correct thing to say about this is that God

x: God Almighty says: When God blessed them with a righteous child as they asked, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them, and He provided for them. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the partners that they made in what they were given of the newborn.
Some of them said: They made partners with Him in the name.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abd al-Samad told us, Umar bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Eve did not have a child who lived, so she vowed that if she had a child who lived, she would name him ‘Abd al-Harith.’ So she had a child who lived, so she named him ‘Abd al-Harith.’ But that was due to the inspiration of Satan.”

c: Muhammad bin Abdul Ala told me, he said, Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, he said, Abu Ala’ told us, on the authority of Samra bin Jundub, that he said:
m: Adam, peace be upon him, named his son Abdul Harith. ... He said, Al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of his father, who said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Al-Ala’ Ibn Al-Shakheer, on the authority of Samra Ibn Jundub, who said: Adam named his son Abdul-Harith.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Eve would give birth to children for Adam and they would worship God, and she would name them Ubaidullah and Abdullah and the like, and then death would befall them. Then Satan came to her and Adam and said: If you named him something other than what you named him, he would live! So she gave birth to a man for him and he named him Abdul-Harith. And about him God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: It is He who created you from one soul, to His saying: They attributed to Him partners in what He has given them, to the end of the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement about Adam: It is He who created you from one soul, to His statement: So she passed by him, and she doubted whether she had conceived or not, But when she became heavy, they called upon God, their Lord, ‘If You give us a righteous child,’ the verse. Then Satan came to them and said: Do you know what will be born to you? Or do you know what will be? Will it be an animal or not? And he made falsehood seem good to them, for it is clearly a deviant. And before that she had given birth to two boys who died, so Satan said to them: If you do not name him by my name, he will not come out sound, and he will die as the first two died! So they named their son Abd al-Harith, and that is what He said: But when He gave them both a righteous child, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them, the verse.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: When his first son was born, Satan came to him and said: I will advise you regarding this son of yours, name him Abdul-Harith. Adam said: I seek refuge in God from obeying you! - Ibn Abbas said: His name in heaven was Al-Harith. Adam said: I seek refuge in God from obeying you, I obeyed you in eating from the tree and you expelled me from Paradise, so I will not obey you! So his son died! Then another son was born to him after that, and he said: Obey me or he will die as the first one died! So he disobeyed him. So he died, and he said: I will continue killing them until you name him Abdul-Harith! So he kept on at him until he named him Abdul-Harith. So that is what His statement: They have attributed to Him partners in what He has given them, made him share in His obedience in something other than worship, and he did not associate partners with God, but he obeyed Him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said,
m: he told us..., on the authority of Harun, he said, Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Kharit told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Adam and Eve did not associate partners, and they did not have any children who lived. Then Satan came to them and said: If you want a child to live, then name him Abd Al-Harith! So this is what He said:
h
They attributed to Him partners in what He gave them

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And when he covered her, she conceived a light burden. He said: Adam, peace be upon him, never had a son born to him except that he died. Then Satan came and said: If you want this son of yours to live, then name him Abdul-Harith! So he did. He said: So they associated partners in the name, but they did not associate partners in the worship.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatalidah:
m: But when He gave them both a son who was righteous, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. He told us that they had no surviving children, so Satan came to them and said to them: Name him Abd al-Harith! This was from Satan’s inspiration and command, and it was a form of polytheism in obedience, but it was not a form of polytheism in worship.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “But when He gave them both a righteous child, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them.
h
So exalted is God above what they associate with Him

.” He said: Adam and his wife would not have a child living. So Satan said to them: If a child is born to you, name him Abd al-Harith! So they did and obeyed him, and that is what God said: But when He gave them both a righteous child, they ascribed to Him partners. Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Ibn Fadil narrated on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Hafsah on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement: They became heavy, so call upon God, their Lord until His statement:
h
So exalted is God above what they associate with Him

, he said: When Eve became pregnant with the first child she gave birth to when she became heavy, Satan came to her before she gave birth and said: O Eve, what is this that is in your belly? She said: I do not know! He said: Where does it come out from? From your nose, or from your eye, or from your ear? She said: I do not know! He said: Tell me if it comes out healthy, will you obey me in what I command you? She said: Yes! He said: Name him Abdul-Harith - and Satan was called Al-Harith - She said: Yes! Then she said after that to Adam: Someone came to me in my sleep and said to me such and such! He said: That is Satan, so beware of him, for he is our enemy who expelled us from Paradise! Then Satan came to her and repeated it to her, and she said: Yes! When she gave birth to him, God brought him out safe and sound, and she named him Abd al-Harith. This is what He said: “They attributed to Him partners in what He had given them.
h
So exalted is God above what they associate with Him

c: Ibn Wakee' told me, he said, Jarir and Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: It was said to him: Adam committed shirk. He said: I seek refuge in God from claiming that Adam committed shirk. But when Eve became ill, Satan came to her and said: Where did this come from? From your nose, or from your eye, or from your mouth? So he made her despair, then he said: Tell me, if it comes out healthy - Ibn Fadil added: it will not harm you or kill you - will you obey me? She said: Yes! He said: Then name him Abdul Harith, so she did. Jarir added: His shirk was only in the name.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: So she gave birth to a boy - meaning Eve - and Satan came to them and said: Name him My slave or I will kill him! Adam, peace be upon him, said to him: I obeyed you and you expelled me from Paradise! But he refused to obey him, so he named him Abd al-Rahman. So God empowered Satan over him and he killed him. So she became pregnant with another, and when she gave birth to him, he said to her: Name him My slave or I will kill him! Adam said to him: I obeyed you and you expelled me from Paradise! But he refused, so he named him Salih, so he killed him. When the third came, he said to them: So since you have overcome me, name him Abd al-Harith. This was Satan’s name, and he was only named Iblis when he became a loser, so they meant it, and that is when God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: They attributed to Him partners in what He had given them, meaning in naming.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by this is a man and a woman from the people of disbelief from the children of Adam, who made partners for God from the gods and idols when He provided them with what He provided them of children. They said: The meaning of the statement: “It is He who created you from one soul and created from it its mate that he might dwell in tranquility with her. But when he covered her,” meaning: this disbelieving man, she carried a light burden and passed through it, but when it became heavy, you called upon God, your Lord. They said: This is one of the things with which the statement begins in the form of address, then returns to reporting on the absent, as was said: It is He who guides you on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them with a good wind
r
(Yunus 10:22)
. We have already explained similar examples of this with their evidence in what came before.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: They made partners for Him in what He gave them. He said: This was with some of the people of religions, and it was not with Adam.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said, al-Hasan said:
m: What is meant by this are the descendants of Adam, those of them who associated partners with God after him, meaning by His statement:
h
So when He gave them [someone] good
, they ascribed to Him partners in what He had given them.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Surat al-A’raf 7:190 But when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them.
h
So exalted is God above what they associate with Him
. Al-Hasan used to say: They are the Jews and Christians, God gave them children who became Jews and Christians.

x: The more correct of the two opinions is the opinion of the one who said: What is meant by his statement:
h
So when He gave them both a good child
, they ascribed to Him partners is in name, not in worship, and that what is meant by that is Adam and Eve, because of the consensus of the people of interpretation on that.
What would you say - since the matter is as you described in the interpretation of this verse, and that what is meant by it is Adam and Eve - in His statement:
h
So exalted is God above what they associate with Him

? Is it a disdain from God to have a partner in names, or in worship? If you say: In names, its corruption is indicated by His statement: Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing and they themselves are created?? If you say: In worship, it would be said to you: Did Adam associate with God someone other than Him in worship?
The interpretation of His statement:
h
So exalted is God above what they associate with Him

, is not what you thought. Rather, the statement is: So exalted is God above what the polytheists of the Arabs, the idol worshippers, associate with Him. As for the report about Adam and Eve, it ended with His statement:
h
They attributed to Him partners in what He gave them
, then His statement:
h
So exalted is God above what they associate with Him
, was resumed, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So God is exalted above what they associate with Him

, he said: This is a virtue from the signs of Adam, especially in the gods of the Arabs. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: partners. This was read by most of the people of Medina, some of the Meccans and the Kufians: They made partners for him, with a kasra on the shin, meaning partnership. Some Meccans, most Kufians, and some Basrans read: They made partners for him, with a damma on the shin, meaning the plural of partner.

x: This reading is the more correct of the two readings, because if the reading were correct with the kasra on the shin, the statement would have to be: So when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to others in it a share, because Adam and Eve did not believe that their son was a gift from Satan, then they attributed to God a share in naming him Abdullah, but they believed, without a doubt, that their son was a provision and gift from God, then they named him Abd al-Harith, so they attributed to Satan a share in the name. If the reading of the one who read: (association) was correct, then what we said would be necessary, that the statement should be: they made for someone else a partner in it. And in the revelation of God’s saying: they made for him, what clarifies that the correct reading is: partners, with a damma on the shin, as I explained before.

Adam and Eve named their son Abd al-Harith, and al-Harith is one, and His saying: partners is a group, so how did He, the Most High, describe them as making partners for Him, when they only associated one person with Him?!

We have previously demonstrated that the Arabs report the report of one person in the same way as they report the report of a group, if they do not intend a specific person or name him, like His statement: Those to whom the people said, ‘The people have gathered against you’
r
(Al Imran 3:173)

. The speaker was only one person, so he reported the report of the same way as he reported the report of a group, since he did not intend his intention. This is widespread in the speech and poetry of the Arabs. As for his saying:
h
So God is exalted above what they associate with Him
, it is a purification from God, the Blessed and Exalted, of Himself, and a glorification of Himself above what the falsifiers say about Him, and what they call upon with Him of gods and idols, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
So God is exalted above what they associate with Him
, he said: It is turning away. He turned away from Himself, may He be glorified and exalted - he says: He magnified Himself - and the angels turned away from Him, and they did not glorify Him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, he said,
m: I heard Sadaqah narrating, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: This is from the relative and the separated, his statement:
h
They attributed to Him partners in what He gave them
, in the matter of Adam and Eve, then God Almighty said: So exalted is God above what they associate, he said: above what the polytheists associate, and He did not mean them.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: partners.
This was read by most of the people of Medina, some of the Meccans and the Kufians: They made partners for him, with a kasra on the shin, meaning partnership.

Abu Jaʿfar said: This reading is the more correct of the two readings, because if the reading were correct with the kasra on the shin, the statement would have to be: So when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to others in it a share, because Adam and Eve did not believe that their son was a gift from Satan, then they attributed to God a share in naming him Abdullah, but they believed, without a doubt, that their son was a provision and gift from God, then they named him Abd al-Harith, so they attributed to Satan a share in the name.
If the reading of the one who read: (association) was correct, then what we said would be necessary, that the statement should be: they made for someone else a partner in it.
And in the revelation of God’s saying: they made for him, what clarifies that the correct reading is: partners, with a damma on the shin, as I explained before.

x: God Almighty says: Do they associate partners in the worship of God, so that they worship with Him that which does not create anything, while God creates and brings it into being? And pure worship is for the Creator, not for the created.
Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: A son was born to Adam and Eve, and they named him Abdullah. Then Satan came to them and said: What did you name your son, O Adam and Eve? He said: They had a son before that, and they named him Abdullah, but he died. They said: We named him Abdullah. Satan said: Do you think that God will leave His servant with you? No, by God, He will take him away as He took the other! But I will show you a name that will remain for you as long as you live. So they named him Abd Shams. He said: That is the statement of God, the Most High: Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing and is created? Does the sun create anything so that it could have a servant? It is created! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He deceived them twice, he deceived them in Paradise, and he deceived them on Earth. It was said: And they create, so He brought out their metaphor in the same way as the metaphor of the sons of Adam. He said: Do they associate with what? So He brought out their mention with what and not with whom as a report about other than the sons of Adam because what they worshipped was only stone or wood or copper or some of the things that are reported about with what and not with whom. So it was said for that reason: what, then it was said and they, so He brought out their metaphor in the same way as the metaphor of the sons of Adam, because the report about it is about the polytheists’ glorification of it, similar to the report about people’s glorification of one another.

x: God Almighty says: Do these polytheists thank in the worship of God that which does not create any of God's creation, and is not able to help them if God wills evil for them or inflicts punishment on them, nor is it able if God wills evil for it to help itself or ward off harm from itself? Rather, the worshipper worships what he worships to bring benefit from it or to ward off harm from it from himself, and their gods that they worship and doubt in the worship of God, neither benefit them nor harm them, rather they do not bring benefit to themselves nor ward off harm from themselves, so they are further from benefiting other than themselves or warding off harm from themselves? God Almighty amazes His creation at the enormity of the error of these people who associate others with God in their worship.

God Almighty says in describing and denouncing what these polytheists associate with Him in their worship of their Lord: And among His descriptions is that you, O people, if you call them to the straight path and the correct and sound matter, they will not follow you, because they do not understand anything, so they abandon the paths that were unfair and unjust, and they adopt what was straight and sound. God, the Most High, intended by describing their gods with these attributes to alert them to the enormity of their error and the ugliness of their choice. He, the Most High, says: How can He guide you to the right path when He, if He is called to the right path and recognizes it, does not recognize it, and does not distinguish between right and wrong? It is the same whether the one calling him to the right path calls to the right path or whether he remains silent, because he does not understand his call, hear his voice, or comprehend what is said to him.

He says: How can one be worshipped who has these attributes? Or how can the great ignorance of one who takes something with these attributes as a god be problematic? The Lord who is worshipped is the One who benefits those who worship Him, harms those who disobey Him, supports His friend, abandons His enemy, guides those who obey Him to the right path, and hears the supplication of those who call upon Him. It was said: It is the same to you whether you call them or remain silent, so he connected his saying: Silent, which is a noun, to his saying: Did you call them, which is a past tense verb, and he did not say: Or were you silent, as the poet said: It is the same for you to leave or spend the night with the people of the domes of Namir bin Aamer He may chant: Or are you staying?

God Almighty says to these polytheists who worship idols, rebuking them for their worship of idols that neither harm nor benefit them: Indeed, those whom you call upon, O polytheists, as gods besides God, and you worship them, as polytheism on your part and disbelief in God, are servants like you, meaning: They are the property of your Lord, just as you are His slaves. So if you are truthful that they harm and benefit, and that they require your worship because of their benefit to you, then let them respond to your call when you call upon them. If they do not respond to you, because they do not hear your call, then be certain that they neither benefit nor harm, because harm and benefit only come from someone who, when asked, hears the question of the one asking him and gives and is generous, and from someone who, when complained to about something, hears, so he harms the one who deserves punishment, and benefits the one who does not deserve harm.

God Almighty says to those who worshipped idols besides Him, their knowledge being their ignorance of what they are established upon: Are these idols of yours, O people, legs with which they walk, so that they strive with you and for you in your needs, and use them to benefit you, or do they have hands with which they strike, so that they repel you and support you when someone intends to harm you with evil and harm, or do they have eyes with which they see, so that they make you aware of what they have witnessed and seen of what you are absent from and do not see, or do they have ears with which they hear, so that they inform you of what they have heard but you have not heard. God the Almighty says: If your gods that you worship do not have any of these tools that I mentioned, and most things are only glorified for the benefits that are hoped for from them that some of these meanings lead to with you, then what is the reason for your worshipping your idols that you worship, while they are devoid of all these things that lead to bringing benefit and warding off harm?

And His statement: “Say: Call upon your partners, then plot,” say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who worship idols: Call upon your partners whom you have made partners with God in worship, then plot, you and they, and do not wait, meaning: do not delay with plotting and deceit, but hasten to do so. God the Almighty informs him with this that they will not harm him, and that He has protected him from them, and the disbelievers know with it the inability of their idols to support those who wrong their allies with evil.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists who worship idols, My Guardian, my Helper, my Supporter, and my Supporter against you, is God, who sent down the Book upon me with the truth, and He is the One who takes care of those of His creation whose deeds are righteous through obedience to Him.

This is also a command from God, the Most High, to His Prophet to say to the polytheists. He, the Most High, says to him: Say to them: God is my Helper and my Supporter, and those gods that you, O polytheists, call upon besides God, cannot help you, nor are they able to help themselves, despite their inability to help you. So which of these two is more deserving of worship and more worthy of divinity? He who helps his friend and protects himself from whoever wants him, or he who is unable to help his friend and is unable to protect himself from whoever wants him and desires harm?

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to the polytheists: And if you, O polytheists, call upon your gods to guidance - which is the straight path to the right path - they will not hear, meaning they will not hear your call, and you will see them looking at you, but they do not see. This is a speech from God to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: And you see, O Muhammad, their gods looking at you, but they do not see. And for this reason he is singular. If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been commanded to address the polytheists, he would have said: (
h
And you see them looking at you
Al-Suddi narrated in this regard:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And if you call them to guidance
, they will not hear, and you will see them looking at you while they do not see, he said:
h
These are the polytheists
. Al-Suddi’s statement may mean that he meant by his statement:
h
These are the polytheists
, God’s statement:
h
And if you call them to guidance
, they will not listen. Mujahid used to say about this:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And you see them looking at you

, but they do not see, what you are calling them to is guidance. It is as if Mujahid directed the meaning of the statement to mean: And you see the polytheists looking at you, but they do not see, so this is an interpretation, but the statement is in the context of reporting about the gods, so it is more like describing them.

x: If someone were to say: What is the meaning of his saying:
h
And you see them looking at you

, but they do not see? Is it permissible for something to look at something and not see it? It was said: The Arabs say about something when it faces something or is parallel to it: (It is looking at such and such), and it is said: (So-and-so’s house is looking at my house), if it is opposite it. And it was narrated from her: (If you come to such and such a place and the mountain looks at you, take a right or a left), and it was narrated from Abu Ubaid who said: Al-Kisa’i said: (The wall is looking at you), if it is close to you where you can see it, and from this is the saying of the poet: If you look at the land of Bani Tamim with one eye or the land of Bani Sabah He wants: to meet its plants and grass and be in line with it.

The meaning of the statement is: And you see, O Muhammad, the gods of these polytheists who worship idols, facing you and facing you, but they do not see you, because they have no sight. It was said: And you see them, and he did not say: And you see them, because they are images depicted in the images of the sons of Adam, peace be upon him.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that: Some of them said: Its interpretation is:
h
Take what is easy
from the morals of people, which is excellence and what does not exhaust them.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Take what is easy
, he said: From the morals and actions of people, without being sensitive.

c: Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Take what is easy
, he said: Forgiveness of people’s morals and forgiveness of their affairs.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Take what is easy
, the verse, Urwah said: God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to
h
take what is easy
from people’s morals.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, who said:
m: God did not reveal this verse except regarding people’s morals: Adopt forgiveness and enjoin what is right, the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: It reached me on the authority of Mujahid: Take pardon from people’s morals and actions without being sensitive. ... He said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of Wahb bin Kaysan, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr:
h
Take what is easy

, he said: It is from the morals of the people, and by God I will take it from them as long as I keep company with them. ... He said, Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, who said: God revealed:
h
Take what is easy
, because of people’s morals.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Take what is easy
, he said: of people’s morals and actions, without looking into - or: spying, Abu Asim was not sure.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
h
Take what is forgiven
from people’s money, which is the surplus. They said: This was ordered before the revelation of zakat, but when zakat was revealed, it was abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
Take what is easy

, means take what they have forgiven you of their money, and whatever they bring you, take it. This was before the revelation of Bara’ah with the obligatory charity and its details, and what the charity ends with.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Take what is easy
. As for what is easy, it is the surplus of money, and it was abrogated by zakat.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Take what is forgiven
, meaning:
h
Take what is forgiven
from their wealth. This was before the obligatory charity was revealed.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a command from God to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to forgive the polytheists and not be harsh with them, before it was imposed on him.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
Take what is easy

, he said: He ordered him to turn away from them for ten years in Mecca. He said: Then he ordered him to be harsh with them, to sit in ambush for them, and to besiege them. Then he said: But if they repent and establish prayer (al-Tawbah 9:5, 11) the whole verse. And he recited: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them (al-Tawbah 9:73 - al-Tahrim 66:9). He said: And he ordered the believers to be harsh with them, so he said: O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you and let them find in you harshness (al-Tawbah 9:123), after he had ordered them to forgive. And he recited the statement of God, Tell those who have believed to forgive those who do not expect the days of God (al-Jathiyah 45:14), then nothing was accepted from them after that except Islam or death, so this verse abrogated forgiveness.

x: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: Be lenient with people’s morals, and leave being harsh with them. He said that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded this with regard to the polytheists. We said that this is more correct, because God Almighty followed that by teaching His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, how to argue with the polytheists in speech, and that is His saying: “Say, ‘Call upon your partners, then plot against us, and do not give us respite. ’” And He followed it with His saying: “And their brothers extend them in error, then do not stop. And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, ‘Why did you not choose it? ’” (al-A’raf 7:202-203). So what is between that, that it is from His disciplining His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their treatment of him, is more similar and more appropriate than the objection to taking charity from the Muslims.
Has this been abrogated?

We do not have any evidence that it was abrogated, since it was abrogated, since it was permissible that - even though God revealed it to His Prophet, peace be upon him, in defining ten of the polytheists who were not commanded to fight him - it was intended to discipline the Prophet of God and all Muslims in their treatment of people, and to command them to accept the leniency of their morals. So, even though it was revealed for their sake, it was a teaching from God to His creation of the characteristic of treating one another, if it was not necessary to use error and severity towards some of them. So if it was necessary to use that towards them, then the obligatory was used. So His saying: (Take the leniency) is a command to take it unless something other than the leniency was necessary. So if something other than the obligatory was necessary, then the obligatory and the non-obligatory were taken if that was possible.
So the verse should not be ruled to be abrogated, because we have explained that in its counterparts in more than one place in our books. As for his saying:
h
And he commanded what is right
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

Some of them said: Al-Hasan bin Al-Zubayr Al-Nakha’i told me, he said, Hussain Al-Ja’fi told me, on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of a man whom he named, who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘Show forgiveness, enjoin what is right,
h
and turn away from the ignorant

,’ the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Gabriel, what is this? He said: I do not know, until I ask the scholar! Then Gabriel said: O Muhammad, God hopes that you will connect with those who have severed you, give to those who have deprived you, and forgive those who have wronged you.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of my mother, he said:
m: “When God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Show forgiveness, enjoin what is right,
h
and turn away from the ignorant

,’ the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: God commands you to forgive those who wrong you, give to those who deprive you, and connect with those who cut you off.”

x: Others said: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father:
h
And he commanded what is right
, meaning: what is right.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And he commanded custom, he said: As for custom, it means what is known.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And he commanded what is right
, meaning: what is right.

x: The correct thing to say about this is that God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to command people to do good, which is known in the speech of the Arabs, a source in the meaning of known. It is said: I gave him a certain knowledge, a certain man, and a certain woman. All of this means: the known. If the meaning of custom is that, then good includes maintaining family ties with someone who has severed them, giving to someone who has been kind to someone, and forgiving someone who has wronged someone. And everything that God has commanded or encouraged of deeds is from custom. God did not specify one meaning over another, so the truth is to say: God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to command His servants to do all of good, not just some of its meanings and not others. As for his saying:
h
And turn away from the ignorant
, it is a command from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn away from those who are ignorant.

And even though it is a command from God to His Prophet, it is a discipline from Him, may He be glorified, to His creation to tolerate those who wrong them or transgress against them, not by turning away from those who are ignorant of what is required of them from the right of God, nor by forgiving those who disbelieve in God and are ignorant of His Oneness, which is war against the Muslims. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Adopt forgiveness, enjoin what is right,
h
and turn away from the ignorant
, he said, morals that God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to have and guided him to them. Surat al-A’raf 7:199 Show forgiveness, enjoin what is right,
h
and turn away from the ignorant
