x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, or if Satan angers you with an anger that prevents you from turning away from the ignorant and makes you punish them, then seek refuge in God, meaning: seek refuge in God from his suggestion, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, meaning: God, in whom you seek refuge from the suggestion of Satan, Hears, of the ignorance of the ignorant towards you, and of your seeking refuge in Him from his suggestion, and of other speech of His creation, nothing is hidden from Him, All-Knowing, of what removes the suggestion of Satan from you, and other matters of His creation, such as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Show forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, the Messenger of God said: How about anger, O Lord? He said: “
h
But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan
, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.”

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan

, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing,” he said: God knows that this enemy is powerful and willful. The root of nazgh is corruption. It is said: The devil has caused corruption among the people, if he has caused trouble between them and incited some of them against others. It is also said: Nazagh yanzagh and Naghaz yanghaz.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who fear God from among His creation, and fear His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins, when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember, meaning: when a touch from Satan befalls them, from anger or something else that prevents them from fulfilling the duty of God’s right over them, they remember God’s punishment and reward, His promise and His threat, and they see the truth and act upon it, and they adhere to obeying God in what He has imposed upon them, and they abandon obeying Satan in it. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: (a specter). The people of Medina and Kufa generally read it as Ta’if, on the pattern of fa’il. Some Meccans, Basrans, and Kufians read it as: A specter of Satan. Scholars of Arabic speech differed on the difference between al-Ta’if and al-Tayf. Some Basrans said: Al-Ta’if and Al-Tayf are the same, and it is something like a phantom or a thing that touches you.

He said: It is possible that Al-Tayf is an abbreviation of “Tayf, like Mayyit and Mayyit. Some Kufians said: Al-Ta’if is what surrounds you from the whisperings of Satan. As for Al-Tayf, it is from lamm and touch. Another of them said: The ghost, “the touch,” and the wandering, are everything that surrounds a person. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Amr bin Al-Alaa that he used to say: The ghost is the whisper.

The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of the one who reads: A spectre of Satan, because the people of interpretation interpreted it to mean anger, and the slip is from the one who spectres. If that is its meaning, then it is known, since the spectre is only a source from the saying of the speaker: It spectres, that this is report from God about what touches those who fear Him from Satan, and what touches them is what spectres them from its causes, such as anger and whisperings. Satan only spectres around the son of Adam to make him slip away from obeying his Lord, or to whisper to him. And whispering and stumbling is the spectre of Satan. As for (the ghost), it is the imagination, and it is the source of (from tafa yatif), and he says: I did not hear in that (tafa yatif), and he interprets it as meaning (the dead), and it is from waw. The Basrans and some of the Kufians narrated hearing from the Arabs: taaf yatif and tafat atif, and they recited about that: Wherever I come across you, my imagination wanders and my memory and feelings for you travel.
As for the interpretation, they differed in its interpretation.
Some of them said: That is the sect, which is anger.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed:
m: When a spectre touches them, he said: And ‘the spectre’ means anger.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: (When a phantom from Satan touches them), he said: It is anger.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Anger.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: (When a phantom of Satan touches them, they remember), he said: It is anger.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: A spectre of Satan, he said: Anger.

x: Others said: It is a slip and a mistake from Satan.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember, and the impulse is the gathering from Satan, and at once they have insight.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan, he says: an insinuation from Satan, they remember. Surat al-A’raf 7:201 Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [God] and at once they have insight.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember, meaning: if they slip, they repent.

x: These two interpretations are close in meaning, because anger is from the devil’s temptation, and the gathering is also from sin, and all of that is from the devil’s group. Since that is the case, there is no reason to make one meaning specific without another, but rather the correct thing is to make it general as He, the Most High, made it general, and to say: Those who fear God, when an obstacle from the causes of Satan arises to them, whatever that obstacle may be, they remember the command of God and abide by His command.
As for his saying:
h
Then they will see
, he means:
h
Then they will see
God’s guidance, His explanation, and His obedience in it, so they will refrain from what the devil’s sect called them to, as:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Then they will see
, meaning: if they are desisting from disobedience, taking God’s command, and disobeying Satan.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: (a specter).
The people of Medina and Kufa generally read it as Ta’if, on the pattern of fa’il.
Some Meccans, Basrans, and Kufians read it as: A specter of Satan.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of the one who reads: A spectre of Satan, because the people of interpretation interpreted it to mean anger, and the slip is from the one who spectres.

x: God Almighty says: And the brothers of the devils - the devils extend them in error. What He means by His statement: extend them is that they increase them, then they do not decrease from what those who feared God decreased from when an impulse from Satan touches them. This is report from God about the two groups of faith and disbelief, that the group of faith and the people of God’s fear, when Satan makes them slip, remember God’s greatness and His punishment, so their fear of Him prevents them from committing sins, and returns them to repentance and turning to God for what they have erred in, and that the group of disbelievers, Satan increases their error upon their error if they commit a sin of God’s sins, and neither the fear of God nor the fear of the return to Him prevents them from continuing in it and increasing it, so they are always increasing in committing sin, and Satan is always increasing it, and the human being does not stop from committing any of the obscenities, nor does Satan increase it from him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And their brothers extend them in error and then they do not stop, he said: Neither do mankind stop what they do of evil deeds, nor do the devils stop them.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their brothers extend them in error and then do not stop
, he says: They are the jinn, inspiring their human allies, and then do not stop, he says: They do not get tired.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And their brothers extend them in error, the brothers of the devils from the polytheists, the devil extends them in error, and then they do not stop.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Abdullah ibn Kathir said: And their brothers from the jinn extend their brothers from mankind, Then they do not stop, meaning: Then mankind does not stop. He said: And the extension is the increase, meaning the people of polytheism. He says: The people of polytheism do not stop as those who fear God do, they do not heed, faith does not restrain them. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: And their brothers, from the devils, Extend them in error, then they do not stop, out of ignorance, they extend the people of polytheism. Ibn Jurayj said: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind (al-A’raf 7:179). He said: So these are mankind. God says: And their brothers extend them in error.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told me, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And their brothers extend them in error and then do not stop
. He said: The brothers of the devils, the devils extend them in error, and then do not stop.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: and their brothers, from the devils, prolong them in error, out of ignorance.

x: Some of them interpreted his statement: Then they will not fall short, to mean: Nor will the devils fall short in helping their brothers from error.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their brothers extend them in error and then do not stop
, about them and do not have mercy on them.

x: We have explained the first of the two interpretations as being correct in our view. We have chosen what we have chosen from the statement on that, based on what we have explained, because God described in the verse before it the people of faith in Him, and their deterrence from disobeying Him and what He hates to loving Him when they remember His greatness, then He followed that with the report about the brothers of the devils and their committing His sins, so it was more appropriate to describe them as persisting in them, since it was following the report about the shortcomings of the believers in them. As for his saying: They extend them, the readings differed in its reading.
Some of the Medinans read it as: (Yamdunhum), with a damma on the ya’, from (Amdadt). The majority of the Kufians and Basrans read it as: Yamdunhum with the opening of the ya of maddat.

The correct reading of this according to us is: Muddudunhum, with the fat-ha on the ya’, because the one who provides the devils with their brothers from the polytheists is an addition of the same type as the extended. If the one who extends is of the same type as the extended, then the Arabs would say Muddaddat, not Amdaddat. As for his saying: They shorten, the reading is according to the language of the one who said: I shortened, I shortened. The Arabs have two dialects for it: I shortened about something and I shortened about it. Surat al-A’raf 7:202 And their brothers prolong them in error and then do not stop.

evidence.text: As for his saying: They extend them, the readings differed in its reading.
Some of the Medinans read it as: (Yamdunhum), with a damma on the ya’, from (Amdadt).
The majority of the Kufians and Basrans read it as: Yamdunhum with the opening of the ya of maddat.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading of this according to us is: Muddudunhum, with the fat-ha on the ya’, because the one who provides the devils with their brothers from the polytheists is an addition of the same type as the extended.
As for his saying: They shorten, the reading is according to the language of the one who said: I shortened, I shortened.

x: God Almighty says: And if you, O Muhammad, do not bring these polytheists a sign from God, “They will say:
h
Why did you not choose it
?” He says: They said:
h
Why did you not choose it
and select it? From the words of God Almighty: But God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills
r
(Al Imran 3:179)
, meaning: He selects and chooses. We have explained this in its places with its evidence. Then the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.

i: Some of them said:
x: It means: Why didn’t you do it yourself and fabricate it?
Meaning: Why didn’t you choose it fabrically? Just as the Arabs say: So-and-so chose this matter and fabricated it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And when you do not bring them a sign
, they say, ‘
h
Why did you not choose it
?’ That is: Why did you not bring it to us on your own! This is the saying of the infidels of Quraysh.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Kathir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying:
h
And when you do not bring them a sign
, they say, ‘Why did you not select it?’ They said: Why did you not summarize it? They said: You extract it from yourself.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when you do not bring them a sign
, they say, ‘
h
Why did you not choose it
?’ They said: Why did you not make it up, you brought it from yourself!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told me, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had I not chosen it
, he says: Had I not received it, and he said another time: Had I not created it and brought it into being.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They said, ‘
h
Why did you not choose it
?’ He said: Why did you not create it?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Why did you not choose it
? He said: Why did you not bring it from yourself?

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Why didn’t you take it from your Lord and accept it from Him?
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Had I not chosen it
, he says: Had I not accepted it from God!

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Had you not chosen it, he says: Had you not received it from your Lord!

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Salman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Why did You not choose it? He said: Why did You not take it and bring it from the sky?

x: The more correct of the two interpretations in this regard is the interpretation of the one who said: Its interpretation is: Why did you not invent it on your own? Because of the evidence of the statement of God: “Say: I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. These are insights from your Lord.” So it is clear that God only commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer them with the report about himself, that he only follows what his Lord sends down to him and reveals to him, not that he invents a statement on his own and creates it and calls people to it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Farra’
m: that he used to say: I selected the speech, “I invented it,” and I improvised it, if you made it up on your own.

c: Al-Harith told me that, he said, Al-Qasim told us,
m: on his authority. Abu Ubaidah said: Abu Zaid used to say: The Arabs only say that when a man begins a speech that he had not prepared in his mind beforehand. Abu Ubaidah said: And I invented it is the same. Say in the interpretation of His saying: “Say, ‘I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. These are insights from your Lord and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.’”

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you, if you do not bring them a sign: Why did you not produce it of your own accord?: That is not for me, and it is not permissible for me to do it, because God only commanded me to follow what is revealed to me from Him. I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord, because I am His servant, and I submit to His command, and I obey Him. These are insights from your Lord, meaning: This is the Qur’an and the revelation that I recite to you. Insights from your Lord, meaning: arguments against you, and clarification for you from your Lord. Its singular is insight, as God Almighty said: These are insights for mankind and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain. (al-Jathiyah 45:20) The reason for mentioning this and singling it out in His statement:
h
These are insights from your Lord is because it was described that what is meant by it is the Qur’an and revelation

And His statement: And guidance, meaning: and clarification that guides the believers to the straight path, and and mercy, meaning: God has shown mercy to His believing servants by it, and saved them by it from misguidance and destruction, for a people who believe, meaning: it is insight from God and guidance and mercy for those who believe, meaning: for those who believe in the Qur’an that it is God’s revelation and inspiration, and act according to what is in it, unlike those who lie about it, deny it, and disbelieve in it. Rather, it is blindness and disgrace for those who do not believe in it.

God Almighty says to those who believe in Him, who believe in His Book, for whom the Qur’an is guidance and mercy: When the Qur’an is recited to you, O believers, then listen to it, meaning: listen to it with your ears so that you may understand its verses and take heed of its exhortations, and pay attention, to it so that you may comprehend and ponder it, and do not be idle in it so that you do not comprehend it, that you may receive mercy, meaning: so that your Lord may have mercy on you by your taking heed of its exhortations, taking heed of its lessons, and using what your Lord has explained to you of His obligations in His verses. Then the people of interpretation differed about the situation in which God commanded listening to the reciter of the Qur’an when he recites and paying attention to him.

Some of them said: That is the situation when the person praying is in prayer behind an imam who he follows, and he hears the recitation of the imam, he must listen to his recitation. They said: This is why this verse was revealed.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, he said:
m: Abdullah used to say: We used to greet one another in prayer: “Peace be upon so-and-so, and peace be upon so-and-so.” He said: Then the Qur’an came:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited

, listen to it and be silent. ... He said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: They used to talk during prayer, and when this verse was revealed,
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, and the other verse, they were commanded to listen.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said:
m: This verse was revealed about a young man from the Ansar. Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited something, he would recite it. So this verse was revealed:
h
And when he recites the Qur’an
, listen to it and be silent.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Bashir bin Jabir, he said:
m: Ibn Masoud prayed and heard some people reciting with the imam. When he finished, he said: Is it not time for you to understand! Is it not time for you to reason?
h
And when the Qur’an is recited

, listen to it and be silent, as God has commanded you. Humayd ibn Masʿadah narrated, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, al-Jariri narrated, on the authority of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah ibn Kurayz, who said: I saw Ubayd ibn Umair and Ata ibn Abi Rabah talking, and the narrator was narrating. I said: Do you not listen to the remembrance and deserve what is promised? They looked at me, then returned to their conversation. I repeated it, and they looked at me, then returned to their conversation. I repeated it a third time, and they looked at me and said: That is only in prayer:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent.

c: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me, he said, my father told me, he said,
m: I heard Al-Awza’i say, Abdullah bin Aamer told us, he said, Zaid bin Aslam told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on this verse:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: It was revealed about raising one’s voice while they were behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim Ismail ibn Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Surat al-A’raf 7:
m: 204 And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. Al-Musayyab:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Laith told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, he said,
m: I heard Humayd Al-Aʿraj say, I heard Mujahid say about this verse:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer. ... He said, Abd al-Samad told me, he said, Shuʿbah told us, he said, Hamid told us, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir and Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when the Qur’an is recited

, listen to it and be silent, he said: in the obligatory prayer. ... He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited

, listen to it and be silent, he said: in the obligatory prayer. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid: regarding the obligatory prayer. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. ... He said, Al-Maharibi and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: In the obligatory prayer. ... He said, Jarir and Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: He said regarding the obligatory prayer.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: They used to talk during their prayers about their needs when it was first imposed upon them, so God revealed what you hear:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And when he recites the Qur’an
, listen to him and be silent. He said: A man would come while they were praying and ask them: How many had you prayed? How much was left? So God revealed:
h
And when he recites the Qur’an
, listen to him and be silent.

x: Another said: They would recognize their voices in prayer when they heard mention of Paradise and Hell, so God revealed:
h
And when he recites the Qur’an

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid and Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reciting, and a man was reciting, so the following was revealed:
h
And when he recites the Qur’an

, listen to him and be silent. ... He said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: They used to talk during prayer, and when the verse was revealed:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: This is during prayer. ... He said, my father told us, on the authority of Harith, on the authority of Amer, who said: In the obligatory prayer.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: When it is recited in prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when he recites the Qur’an
, listen to him, meaning: in the obligatory prayer.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: This is in prayer, in His statement:
h
And when he recites the Qur’an

, listen to him, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: that he disliked if the imam passed by a verse of fear or a verse of mercy for anyone behind him to say anything. He said: Silence. He said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: There is no problem if a man recites outside of prayer and speaks.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy, he said: This is when the imam says the prayer, so listen to it and be silent.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said:
m: Those behind the imam should not recite in what he recites aloud. The imam’s recitation is sufficient for them even if they cannot hear his voice. However, they should recite in secret to themselves what he does not recite aloud. It is not appropriate for anyone behind him to recite with him in what he recites aloud, secretly or publicly. God says:
h
And when he recites the Qur’an
, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He used to say in this: And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear. This is in the obligatory prayer. As for what was of stories or recitation after that, then it is only voluntary. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited in an obligatory prayer, and his companions recited behind him, so they confused him. He said: Then the Qur’an was revealed:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. This is in the obligatory prayer.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by this verse is the command to listen to the imam during the sermon, if he recites the Qur’an in his sermon.
Who said that?

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Saeed bin Masruq, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: Listening to the imam on Friday.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid and Ibn Abi Utbah told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: In the Friday sermon.

x: Others said: He meant listening during prayer and the sermon.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said:
m: I heard Ibrahim bin Abi Hamza narrating: that he heard Mujahid say about this verse:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: in the prayer and sermon on Friday.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: Silence is obligatory in two cases: when a man is reciting the Qur’an while he is praying, and when the imam is delivering the sermon.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, he said: It is obligatory to listen attentively in two cases: in prayer while the imam is reciting, and on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us,
m: he told us from someone who heard Al-Hasan say: In the obligatory prayer, and when remembering.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It is obligatory to listen attentively in two cases: in prayer and on Friday.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Baqiyah ibn al-Walid, he said:
m: I heard Thabit ibn Ajlan say: I heard Saeed ibn Jubayr say regarding His statement:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent, he said: Listening is on the Day of Sacrifice, the Day of Breaking the Fast, and Friday, in what the imam recites aloud in the prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: In prayer and when remembering.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, he said:
m: The reason for obligating oneself to listen on Friday is the statement of God Almighty:
h
And when the Qur’an is recited
, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. And the same applies to prayer.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is the statement of the one who said: They were commanded to listen to the Qur’an in prayer
h
when the imam recites

, and those behind him who follow him hear him, and in the sermon. We said that this is more correct, because of the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said:
h
When the imam recites

, then listen, and the consensus of all that whoever hears the imam’s sermon and is required to attend the Friday prayer, must listen and pay attention to it, with the successive reports ordering this from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and that there is no time when it is obligatory for anyone to listen to the Qur’an and pay attention to the one who is listening to it, from the one who is reciting it, except in these two cases, with a difference in one of them, which is the case of being behind an imam who is being followed.
The report from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) has been authenticated with what we mentioned of his saying:
h
When the imam recites

, then listen, so listening behind him to his recitation is obligatory for whoever is following him and hearing his recitation, based on the generality of the apparent meaning of the Qur’an and the report from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him).

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty says to those who believe in Him, who believe in His Book, for whom the Qur’an is guidance and mercy: When the Qur’an is recited to you, O believers, then listen to it, meaning: listen to it with your ears so that you may understand its verses and take heed of its exhortations, and pay attention, to it so that you may comprehend and ponder it, and do not be idle in it so that you do not comprehend it, that you may receive mercy, meaning: so that your Lord may have mercy on you by your taking heed of its exhortations, taking heed of its lessons, and using what your Lord has explained to you of His obligations in His verses.
Some of them said: That is the situation when the person praying is in prayer behind an imam who he follows, and he hears the recitation of the imam, he must listen to his recitation.
He said: Then the Qur’an came: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent. ...

He said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: They used to talk during prayer, and when this verse was revealed, And when the Qur’an is recited, and the other verse, they were commanded to listen.
Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited something, he would recite it.
And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, as God has commanded you.
I repeated it a third time, and they looked at me and said: That is only in prayer: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent.

Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me, he said, my father told me, he said, I heard Al-Awza’i say, Abdullah bin Aamer told us, he said, Zaid bin Aslam told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on this verse: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: It was revealed about raising one’s voice while they were behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in prayer.

Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim Ismail ibn Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer.

Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Surat al-A’raf 7:204 And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy.
Al-Musayyab: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer.
Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Laith told us, on the authority of Mujahid: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer.

Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, he said, I heard Humayd Al-Aʿraj say, I heard Mujahid say about this verse: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: in prayer. ...

Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir and Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: in the obligatory prayer. ...

He said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: in the obligatory prayer. ...

Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: They used to talk during their prayers about their needs when it was first imposed upon them, so God revealed what you hear: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent.

He said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: They used to talk during prayer, and when the verse was revealed: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: This is during prayer. ...

Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: When it is recited in prayer.

Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy, he said: This is when the imam says the prayer, so listen to it and be silent.
It is not appropriate for anyone behind him to recite with him in what he recites aloud, secretly or publicly.
He said: Then the Qur’an was revealed: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy.

Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Saeed bin Masruq, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: Listening to the imam on Friday.

Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said: I heard Ibrahim bin Abi Hamza narrating: that he heard Mujahid say about this verse: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: in the prayer and sermon on Friday.

Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid: And when the Qur’an is recited, he said: It is obligatory to listen attentively in two cases: in prayer while the imam is reciting, and on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Baqiyah ibn al-Walid, he said: I heard Thabit ibn Ajlan say: I heard Saeed ibn Jubayr say regarding His statement: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent, he said: Listening is on the Day of Sacrifice, the Day of Breaking the Fast, and Friday, in what the imam recites aloud in the prayer.

Ibn Al-Barqi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, he said: The reason for obligating oneself to listen on Friday is the statement of God Almighty: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy.

The report from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) has been authenticated with what we mentioned of his saying: When the imam recites, then listen, so listening behind him to his recitation is obligatory for whoever is following him and hearing his recitation, based on the generality of the apparent meaning of the Qur’an and the report from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him).

x: God Almighty says: And remember, O listener who is attentive to the Qur'an, when it is recited in prayer or a sermon, your Lord within yourself, meaning: Take heed of what is in the verses of the Qur'an and consider it, and remember your return to Him when you hear it, in humility, meaning: Do that in humility and submission to God, and in fear, meaning: and in fear of God that He will punish you for a shortcoming that you may have in taking heed of it and considering it, and heedlessness of what God has made clear in it of His limits. And without speaking aloud, meaning: and supplication with the tongue to God in secret, not out loud.
He says: Let there be remembrance of God when you listen to the Qur'an in supplication if you supplicate not out loud, but in a secret manner, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear and without loudness of speech
, he does not say that out loud.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Saad told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say about His statement:
h
And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear and without loudness of speech
, the verse, he said: They were commanded to remember Him in their hearts in humility and fear.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn al-Taymi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hayyan bin Umair, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And remember your Lord within yourself

, he said: God says: ((If My servant remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself, and if My servant remembers Me alone, I remember him alone, and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in a better and more honorable assembly than them)).

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear

, he said: He is commanded to be humble in supplication and to be submissive, and raising one’s voice, calling out, and shouting in supplication is disliked. As for his saying: in the morning and the evening, he means: in the early morning and the evening. As for al-asal, it is a plural, and Arab scholars differed about it.

x: Some of them said: It is the plural of Aseel, just as Ayman is the plural of Yameen, and Asrar is the plural of Sirr.
Others said: It is the plural of origin, and origin is the plural of authentic.

Others among them said: It is the plural of origin and original. He said: If you wish, you can make origin the plural of original, and if you wish, you can make it one. He said: The Arabs say: The origin has approached, and they make it one.

This statement is more correct in this regard, which is that it is permissible to have the plural of asil and asl, because they can be pluralized as af’al. As for al-asal, it is what is said in the speech of the Arabs: what is between the afternoon and sunset. As for his saying:
h
And do not be among the heedless

, he is saying: Do not be among those who are heedless when the Qur’an is recited, regarding its lessons, morals, and wonders, but rather ponder that and understand it, and make your heart feel it with remembrance of God, submission to Him, and fear of God’s power over you if you are heedless of that.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: in the mornings and the evenings, he said: in the morning and the evening,
h
and do not be among the heedless

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Ma’rif bin Wasil Al-Sa’di told us, he said:
m: I heard Abu Wa’il say to his servant at sunset: Shall we pray yet?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, Mujahid said:
m: His statement, in the morning and the evenings, he said: (The morning) is the end of dawn, the morning prayer, and (the evenings) is the end of the evening, the afternoon prayer. He said: And all of that has a time, the beginning of dawn and the end of it. This is like His statement in Surat Al Imran 3:And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning
r
(Al Imran 3:41)
. It was said: (The evening) is the inclination of the sun to set, and (the morning) is the beginning of dawn.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sharik, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: he was asked about [the dawn prayer, so he said: It is in the Book of God, and no one stands for it]... Then he recited: “In houses which God has permitted to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein. He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings,” the verse (al-Nur 24:36). Surat al-A’raf 7:205
h
And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear
and without being too loud in speech, in the mornings and the evenings,
h
and do not be among the heedless

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear

, until his statement: in the mornings and the evenings, God commanded us to remember Him and forbade us from being heedless. As for in the morning, it is the dawn prayer, and in the evenings, it is the evening.

evidence.text: Abu Ja'far said: God Almighty says: And remember, O listener who is attentive to the Qur'an, when it is recited in prayer or a sermon, your Lord within yourself, meaning: Take heed of what is in the verses of the Qur'an and consider it, and remember your return to Him when you hear it, in humility, meaning: Do that in humility and submission to God, and in fear, meaning: and in fear of God that He will punish you for a shortcoming that you may have in taking heed of it and considering it, and heedlessness of what God has made clear in it of His limits.

As for his saying: And do not be among the heedless, he is saying: Do not be among those who are heedless when the Qur’an is recited, regarding its lessons, morals, and wonders, but rather ponder that and understand it, and make your heart feel it with remembrance of God, submission to Him, and fear of God’s power over you if you are heedless of that.

x: God Almighty says: O listener who listens attentively to the Qur’an, do not be arrogant about worshipping your Lord, and remember Him when the Qur’an is recited in humility and fear and without speaking loudly, for those who are with your Lord from among His angels are not arrogant about being humble before Him and fearing Him, and that is (worship), and glorify Him, meaning: and they magnify their Lord with their humility before Him and their worship, and to Him they prostrate, meaning: and to God they pray - and that is their prostration - so you also pray to Him and magnify Him with worship, as those of His angels who are with Him do.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty says: O listener who listens attentively to the Qur’an, do not be arrogant about worshipping your Lord, and remember Him when the Qur’an is recited in humility and fear and without speaking loudly, for those who are with your Lord from among His angels are not arrogant about being humble before Him and fearing Him, and that is (worship), and glorify Him, meaning: and they magnify their Lord with their humility before Him and their worship, and to Him they prostrate, meaning: and to God they pray - and that is their prostration - so you also pray to Him and magnify Him with worship, as those of His angels who are with Him do.
